## D197 — P9 re-extraction R3: an old citation opens its own extraction with its input stated, reports and owner reviews share one passage-dependency rule, new extractions record the bytes they read, and repair history is backed up and purged only by authorized purge

**Status:** accepted (implemented). Written by gpt-6.1-sol high (its first run stopped correctly on a prompt ambiguity: S1 assumed returned anchor ranges that do not exist; the orchestrator clarified that the stored source-owned `anchor_text` is checked against the returned old passage and no range contract is added; a second run was cut off by a model-capacity error and resumed); plan (docs/product/p9-reextract-r3-prompt.md, by Claude Opus 5.5) reviewed by gpt-6.1-sol medium in 3 rounds (r1 düzeltmeyle hazır, 4 high + 9 medium + 1 low; r2 düzeltmeyle hazır, 3 high + 3 medium; r3 düzeltmeyle hazır, 0 high, 0 medium, 2 low, folded in by the orchestrator without a fourth round); code reviewed cross-vendor by Claude Opus 5.5 in 2 rounds (round 1 "düzeltmeyle hazır", 0 high, 3 medium (the purge closure loaded every asset, extraction, operation and observation row, JSON columns included, once per purged source inside the write transaction; the O7 scan read every frozen record of the library and one unreadable record anywhere blocked every purge; one red-on-old case passed on old code because a live table row still protected the source) and 2 low (backup's import of workflow helpers, kept with a stated reason; a fake report store in the freshness reader), all fixed; round 2 "hazır").
**Owner-level choices:** O1 to O6 proposed by Claude Opus 5.5 and agreed by gpt-6.1-sol medium in plan-review round 1; O7 (frozen JSON records protect their passages' sources) proposed by gpt-6.1-sol medium in round 1 and adopted by Claude Opus 5.5; its research-scoped scan was set by the code reviewer (Claude Opus 5.5) in code-review round 1. The owner was not asked.
**Date:** 2026-10-03, P9 batch R3.

**Context:** D190–D195 preserve old passage occurrences through text retry and file repair, but the document-text route opens only current text. Reports do not compare passage identity, owner reviews duplicate the status rule, initial attachments and ordinary upgrades do not record their parser input, and backups and purges omit parts of recovery history. D176 requires these boundaries to be completed before the R4 interface and R5 compatibility closure.

**Decision:** `workflow/evidence_deps.py` owns the unchanged SQL evidence-status rule and a read-only dependency SELECT, in chunks of at most 500 passage IDs. The Store re-exports the constant. `ReviewReader.evidence_dependency` delegates to the helper while preserving its existing keys and values; snapshot creation and stale reasons are unchanged. Passage occurrence views and report freshness use the same helper. It imports only the standard library and works on pre-0066 libraries.

Reports add `passage_freshness` beside the unchanged `evidence_changes`: `compared: passage_identity`, `semantic_support: not_checked`, distinct dependencies, affected passages, unresolved references, and `file_restored_after`. The reader enumerates effective and restorable citations, snapshot cell evidence, gap basis passages, selected section inputs and citation inputs, and claim equation origins. It sorts identities and uses deterministically and writes nothing. Missing passages become `passage_missing`; unreadable records become `unreadable_record`. Readable older bases and inputs can omit optional passage collections. Markdown and LaTeX add the English or Turkish passage-freshness sentence after the existing evidence-change sentence only when affected or unresolved entries exist; otherwise their output is unchanged. This comparison assesses identity, not semantic support.

Passage views add `occurrence`, null for abstracts. PDF occurrences expose their extraction ID/version/profile/outcome, whether they are current, the current extraction ID, their own recorded input, `input_relation`, and any later completed file restore. Input relations are `input_matched_expected_hash`, `input_differed_from_expected_hash`, or `input_not_recorded`; a mismatch also reports whether a before-restore observation names retained bytes of that digest. The comparison is against the asset's recorded expected identity. It does not hash the present file served by the PDF route. `GET .../assets/{asset_id}/text?extraction_id=...` opens exactly a current or superseded occurrence of that asset, with equations for that version. Foreign and rejected occurrences are refused. Cited replaced assets retain access; the request without the parameter retains its existing access rules and opens current text. No offsets, anchors or highlights are computed; stored `anchor_text` is located in its own passage.

Initial attachments and ordinary upgrades use verified private copies under the hash lock. Copying, hashing, fsync and default PDF parsing run in drained threads; cancellation drains the parser before unlocking. Observations are inserted with their extraction in one transaction, with a null operation ID for these reads. Initial upload, existing-source upload, waiting attachment, both Zotero paths, acquisition and confirmed candidates, run-time fetch, and replacement forward the observation. O1: unverified initial bytes are not parsed; they produce an observed missing/mismatch input and an empty failed extraction with the prescribed repair message. Zotero records a per-item note and continues. Busy reads retain each caller's existing refusal behavior. O2: unverified ordinary upgrades publish nothing; the API returns `409 input_not_verified`, and the CLI counts the outcome and continues with exit 0. Dry runs write no observation. Non-hex hashes and pre-0066 libraries retain direct parsing without observations. Private-copy cleanup errors are logged without hiding the result or original error.

Backups include observation-owned `retained-<observed_sha256>.bin` files, verify name/digest agreement, and refuse contradictory recorded hashes for a single name. Unreferenced retained files and the recovery directory are excluded. O4: each asset file with a lowercase 64-hex hash is copied and verified under its hash lock, waiting at most ten seconds in 0.05-second intervals, then refusing if still busy. Immutable retained files are copied without that lock. Restoration places these files before the database through the existing restore path. Running receipts are preserved in the snapshot and reconciled after restoration without retrying text.

Migration 0069 (renumbered from 0068 at rebase, after P8 B5's `0068_watches.sql`) adds `recovery_purge_authorizations` and delete guards for operations and observations. It drops no existing trigger, index or FK. Both purge paths retain source sharing, citations and B1 owner-review snapshot protection and refusal order. O7 additionally scans surviving step inputs, report snapshots and gap JSON for nested passage references, within researches linked to a candidate source by any corpus membership (including removed memberships), discovery candidate, kill-search query record or kill-search hit. Source-only purge also includes the purging research; research purge has already deleted that research's own records. A passage can reach these frozen records only through its research's corpus, candidates or kill-search records, so unrelated researches need no scan and their unreadable JSON cannot block this purge. Within the linked scope, null passage IDs are allowed; malformed reference shapes or unparsable JSON refuse atomically with `409 frozen_dependency_unreadable`. A referenced source survives research purge; source-only purge refuses it. O5 refuses deletion while a relevant text retry or file restore remains running.

Deleting an unshared source deletes its asset-owned extractions, text retries and input observations. Hash-owned file-restore history remains while any asset holds the same hash. Before deletion, the purge computes the transitive FK closure of outside references, reading only identity, FK and deletion-shape columns for the deleting assets, eligible recovery rows, reverse references into them and dependencies reached from those outside references, to a fixpoint. It does not load extraction math/OCR payloads or unrelated recovery rows. Retained observations keep their owning operations and dependencies; a closure into an asset or extraction being deleted refuses the entire purge. Eligible extractions, observations and operations are deleted in that order under transient hash authorizations, followed by assets. Authorization rows are removed before commit. A deleted retained filename is returned only when no surviving observation names it. The API unlinks it through `remove_retained`, which rechecks references and any running restore under one short `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and unlinks synchronously before commit. Cross-hash reuse therefore leaves the file and reports `files_not_removed`.

O6 adds `deixis recovery-files [--delete]`. It first reconciles stale recovery operations, lists unreferenced retained filenames and sizes, and uses the same guarded unlink for requested deletion. Exit codes are 0 for successful requested deletions, 1 for blocked or failed deletions, and 2 for a schema problem. Referenced files and `.part` staging files are excluded.

**Verification:** Outside the sandbox, by the reviewer: baseline on af9a21e 12,476 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped (`/tmp/reextract-r3-baseline.log`); before the review fixes 12,637 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped (`/tmp/reextract-r3-full-1.log`); after them 12,692 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped, 62 warnings in 465.08 s (`/tmp/reextract-r3-full-2.log`). After the rebase onto bbcf575 (P8 B5, B8a, P7-F2/F3, G1 B5, H9 result) and the renumber to 0069: 13,011 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped in 576.08 s (`/tmp/reextract-r3-rebased.log`). Inside Sol's sandbox 17 socket/process-listing tests fail and pass outside. 216 R3 cases. The 22 red-on-old cases (S1 old-occurrence text route, S3 export notice, S6 over nine initial-attachment writers, S7 torn ordinary upgrade, S8 retained bytes in backup, S10 unshared receipt purge through both routes, S10b frozen-record protection for step input, snapshot and gap basis, S11 live recovery blocking purge, S12 unauthorized delete) were rerun by the reviewer on a clean `git archive af9a21e` copy: all 22 fail at their first behavioral assertion and pass here. Synthetic measurement by the writer (2,000 assets with a current and a superseded extraction each, a 200-source research, 2,000 step inputs of about 34 KB): `purge_research` 14.12 s before the review fix and 0.85 s after; the frozen-record scan 0.126 s and 0.012 s (one machine, one library, not a bound). The implementation report is `/tmp/reextract-r3-impl-report.md`; model-free S1–S16 cases cover occurrence identity, all report dependency kinds, input integrity, cancellation and abandoned copies, backup races and round trips, protected rows, recovery deletion guards, frozen references, FK closure, and current-only retrieval. Existing R1/R2 and owner-review tests form S15. No web surface changed, so no web build, lint or browser acceptance run was required.

**Carried work:** R4 supplies the occurrence interface, current-text comparison, report passage-freshness display, retry action and history, and labels for `input_not_verified`, `frozen_dependency_unreadable`, `process_ended`, `file_busy` and receipts; `.impeccable.md` section 4.6 remains to change then. `input_relation` and `file_restored_after` copy must retain the recorded-expected-identity qualification. Candidate and lineage occurrence/freshness fields follow P8 B8a. R5 supplies the closing compatibility run.

**Limits:** Evidence is from synthetic PDFs and temporary libraries; no real library, model or provider was used. OCR, Marker and arXiv source reads record no input observation (O3). Legacy extractions retain null input and are never backfilled. Advisory locks cannot stop outside processes. A long equation read can exhaust the backup's ten-second wait. A crashed running operation blocks purge until reconciled, normally on the next worker turn. `.part` files are never purged. Abandoned private copies are removed only by a later verified read or text retry, not by startup. O7 prevents source-only purge when surviving model inputs use its passages; its cost depends on the linked researches' frozen records, and purge still runs synchronously inside the write transaction. The report records a before/after measurement on one synthetic 2,000-asset library; it is not a production latency guarantee. Unreadable report snapshots or gap bases still make the existing report view and exports fail as before R3; the new freshness reader reports their unreadability when called directly. Freshness checks no semantic support, and input relation describes recorded input against the expected hash rather than the present served bytes. Candidate, lineage and table views gain no field in R3. Windows is untested.

## D198 — P9 RF: code stamps the package hash, a failing cell anchor is repaired by a model-chosen patch that code applies, and a repaired section cannot lose a claim silently

**Status:** accepted, implemented. Prompt `docs/product/p9-rf-prompt.md` by Claude Opus 5.5, reviewed by gpt-6.1-sol medium in 4 rounds (r1-r3 düzeltmeyle hazır, r4 hazır); decisions 1-3 and the versioning exception agreed with gpt-6.1-sol medium in that review. Code by gpt-6.1-sol high, reviewed by Claude Opus 5.5 in 2 rounds (r1 düzeltmeyle hazır: 1 medium, false hash-stamp provenance on the patch path, and 3 low; r2 hazır).
**Date:** 2026-10-03.

**Context:** D124 stopped at the table; D126 stopped at IV after a passage-id miscopy, addressed by D127's handles; D128 stopped at IV on an unlocatable quote, followed by D129's targeted repair guidance. H9 (`run_YHPhlrH3yeRdPIQwCdoI`, `codex` / `gpt-5.6-luna` / medium) stopped at IV again. The supplied read-only H9 database copy establishes three hash miscopies in 52 sessions, not a rate: IV repair `mss_xhk50S1g0GOlJmHgeH9a`, abstract screening `mss_h5nfepCU8lHyzXZ1W3qz`, and full-text adjudication `mss_IEbEtej7GQuNAUvyNukU`. IV's first output (`mss_HG8MzJk21LAPfYmdMxmF`) had 18 claims, two insufficiency entries and one bad quote at anchor 8, extending past its cell evidence's private-use glyph U+E0A8. Its full repair regenerated 19 claims, lost both insufficiency entries, miscopied the hash and gave all 21 anchors both targets. This corrects the H9 results document's account that those anchors had neither target; that historical document is unchanged. D129's allowed-quote passage_id is a plausible copying cue, not an established cause. V's first output (`mss_AmPVJSuzHvTMLEntGcfu`) had seven anchors quoting the cell's Turkish value text instead of a stored evidence quote. Its repair (`mss_c57ZHZgnqrGFdJNCZhv0`) validated after dropping V.7 and V.8 without insufficiency records.

**Decision 1:** Choose A: omit skill_package_hash from the model-facing output properties and required list, then stamp the StepInput's authoritative hash before canonical validation. This retains step_input_id and scope_revision echoes and their binding checks, model isolation and mismatch refusal, the stored package identity and developer instructions. It loses the model's hash copy, which never established that the model followed the package. Rejected B, a short echo token: it retains a copy check with no stronger evidence and adds mapping machinery. Rejected C, stamping all three fields: it would remove the remaining short binding checks without an observed H9 failure in those fields. Ordinary task outputs through _model_step receive the stamp, including no-repair screening; patch merges rebind the envelope without a hash stamp. Every stamp records its JSON pointer and supplied model value in validation_json.normalised; the raw model output stays unchanged. validate_model_output still checks all three canonical envelope fields. Method instructions echo the short fields and copy the hash only if the supplied output schema includes it; dated provenance entries record this change.

**Decision 2:** A report_section repair uses the patch only when every issue is anchor_not_in_cell_evidence at an exact anchor quote path and every issue has exactly one distinct matching cell pair. Otherwise it uses the full repair. Both consume the existing single schema repair, limiter and budget. The new ReportSectionAnchorRepair v1 contract is registered as a contract, not a task output; its canonical validator resolves common refs and its self-contained adapter schema is sent and stored for the patch attempt. It requires the two short binding fields, numbered anchor choices and affected-claim edits. Allowed-quote pairs expose quote_number and the verbatim stored quote, no passage_id; only the pair cell_id gets a handle. Each associated claim shows its current anchors and failing flags. The guidance distinguishes location from support and asks the model to select a same-cell quote, narrow the claim, or remove the anchor. A claim left without anchors must be explicitly removed with context and reason.

Patch validation fails closed on schema or binding errors, missing/extra/duplicate anchor indices, out-of-range quote numbers, unknown/unaffected/duplicate claim keys, inconsistent removal fields, prefixed context overflow and unremoved claims left without anchors. A validated patch is applied to a deep copy of the failed resolved draft. Code copies only the model-selected stored quote verbatim, removes only named anchors, removes a cited cell only after that claim loses its last anchor on that cell, changes only named claim texts, and removes claims and their anchors only when the patch explicitly requests claim removal. Each removed claim adds the model's reason and context to insufficient_evidence. The claim_key plus `: ` prefix is the only section prose code writes. The merged envelope is rebound to the repair StepInput; the patch itself is never hash-stamped. The merged section passes the unchanged canonical validator before publication. Code never chooses a quote, adds an anchor or citation, or supplies an explanation.

The session keeps the patch as raw_output. Successful patch validation/application records anchor_patch with base_step_input_id and one change per applied anchor or claim item, including old/new quote or text or removal. The session records merged-draft validation and the succeeded step stores the usual merged result plus the same anchor_patch object. Invalid patches have patch issues and no merged draft; invalid merged drafts retain their application record but cannot publish. On patch failure, the returned/stored step issues put the first attempt's anchor issues before patch or merged issues, preserving D129's displayed anchor reason without a UI change.

**Decision 3:** A full report-section repair sees the exact failed raw output in handle form, after the issues, and receives the keep-keys and keep-insufficiency guidance. Other tasks' repair messages and calls without a failed output retain their prior form. After normal validation, code rejects each dropped claim key unless it remains an exact key or has an insufficiency context starting with exactly `<claim_key>: ` followed by a non-whitespace explanation. V.10 cannot cover V.1. Every old insufficiency context/reason pair must remain equal. The two checks independently tolerate readable parts of malformed drafts, count duplicate claim keys once, and add issues without merging any missing content back or making another model call. This establishes key coverage, not preservation of a kept claim's meaning.

**Versioning exception:** The model-facing wire schema drops one required envelope field without bumping the stored task contract's schema_version. Every existing contract file and canonical result shape remains unchanged. step_inputs.output_schema_json records the actual transport schema per attempt, distinguishing earlier hash-echo attempts from stamped attempts. The new patch contract has its own v1 schema version; no migration is needed.

**Verification:** Outside the sandbox, on the reviewed code before rebase: full pytest 12,550 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped. After rebasing onto `bbcf575` (D185, D186, D196, D199): full pytest 12,869 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped. On a clean `581e156` copy the red-on-old tests fail at their first behavioral assertion (E1 for all three tasks, A1, A3, both A5, and A9 `[report-anchor-patch]` with the new fixture server on old product code); the replay-fixture and E3 binding/isolation guards pass there. `npm run build` passed, `npm run lint` 0 errors (baseline warnings). Fresh-build Playwright: 181 passed, 2 failed, 7 not run (the rest of the serial X05 describe); the two failures pass on rerun (candidate report VI alone; whole X05 describe 19/19), and `report.spec.ts` including the bad-anchor case passed. These are synthetic and replayed checks of application behavior, not a real-model or report-quality result. No live service was touched, no model was called.

**Limits:** Only synthetic and replayed stored outputs were used; no real model, provider or network was called. Whether the patch completes a real report remains unmeasured and is H9b's question. H9's own failures shaped the fix, so later success on that corpus would not be independent evidence. A located quote still does not prove support. First-pass wrong-cell-value or overlong-span anchors are not prevented; an evidence-index first-pass contract would require a later report-section v3. Patches for passage-anchor failures and other issue codes, failed-output context for other tasks, repairs for NO_REPAIR_TASKS, new UI labels and H9b are out of scope. Full repairs that merely renumber claims also fail repair_dropped_claim. The canonical-schema scripts in scripts/model_behavior remain unchanged and still request a hash echo; the revised conditional wording's model reliability there is untested. workflow/review/run.py retains its conservative size estimate on the larger canonical schema. The package hash changes from `sha256:8353306cc05cf102609375f89e870c9c0c611d68b7ca528153f27ee612fce93c` (main after D185) to `sha256:1a7e67137173f49fc2acca70edc940a5f0589cf216cf20a2d8f5f606b3b93c4e`; the reviewed pre-rebase version on `581e156` was `sha256:a62dd30eeaa323a2a512741f01cc608a63223cf374759c1e9b3a941f85c5c0e5` (from `sha256:5ba2d214…75ff`), and the rebase only merged D185's `review.md` provenance line.

## D186 — P8 B5: a research can be followed by a manual check that re-reads its frozen queries or the works citing its included sources and announces each new record once, apart from the library

**Status:** accepted, implemented. Writer: gpt-6.1-sol high. Plan reviewed by gpt-6.1-sol medium in four rounds: r1/r2/r3 düzeltmeyle hazır, r4 hazır; corrections folded into `product/p8-b5-prompt.md`. Owner-level choices (A revision 3, B similarity annotates only, C no Add path, D caps, E `watch_reads`, F′ bounded baseline window, G file digest) agreed by the prompt author Claude Opus 5.5 and gpt-6.1-sol medium in plan review. Cross-vendor code review by Claude Opus 5.5: round 1 "düzeltmeyle hazır" (1 high: the nine watch routes were plain `def` and ran in the threadpool on the shared SQLite connection; 2 medium: watch requests dropped the application client's User-Agent, and eight existing test pins broke on the revision bump and the new tables; 2 low: env-driven telemetry writes in a test, an empty OpenAlex `sort` sent as `sort=`), all fixed; round 2 "hazır".
**Reviewer checks outside the sandbox:** full pytest before the round 1 fixes **12,508 passed, 8 failed, 2 skipped** (557.8 s, the eight pins); after them **12,521 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped** (466.4 s). On a clean `30b070c` archive with only `tests/test_watch_old_entrypoints.py` and `tests/watch_helpers.py` copied in, the non-storage selection gives **17 failed** (interface TypeErrors, facade refusal of the new options, revision 2, the runs CHECK and nine missing routes). No web file changed, so no build, lint or Playwright run.
**Date:** 2026-10-03, detached `30b070c`, worktree `DEIXIS-p8b5`.

**Context:** D180 assigns manual follow-up to B5, scheduling to B6 and the interface to B7. Discovery previously ended without a stored follow-up state. A follow-up finding must not become a library source, included work, candidate or research count. D181/B2 supplies the route/run patterns; D194 supplies connector admission and continuation provenance. This batch implements manual checks with synthetic evidence only.

**Decision:** Migration **0068** adds `watch_check` to the runs kind CHECK without changing its columns, other kinds or stage vocabulary. The store assigns stage `discovery`. The rebuild recreates both cross-table run guards; upgrade tests compare all earlier rows, triggers, indexes and foreign keys. Six tables store watches, checks, immutable page reads, the research-level seen set, exact aliases and items. Checks and reads are `WITHOUT ROWID`; conflicting INSERT, REPLACE and upsert are refused with recursive triggers off. Check inputs cannot change; completion observations can be assigned once. Reads cannot change or be deleted outside authorized research purge. Watch rows have no foreign key to a source, passage or asset.

`workflow/watch/{store,check,run,view}.py` separates persistence, pure policy, sequential HTTP reads and read models. Its local `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` wrapper rolls back an active transaction if COMMIT fails. Queueing a watch, check and run is atomic. Completion rechecks the live run, research visibility, enabled flag, scope, bound protocol and state version before publishing anything. It applies persisted records in unit/page/record order, updates seen rows/items/baselines and summaries, finishes `watch_complete`, writes the count event and terminates the run in one transaction. No successful read means `failed/no_provider_read`. Re-executing succeeded completion writes and sends nothing. An exception or failed COMMIT rolls publication back and the worker records `failed/internal_error`; a failed run is not resumable. Recovery after reads but before completion pauses the run; resume retains usage, deadline and reads and publishes once without resending them. A failed payload-file write publishes no immutable read or succeeded page step. Trashed-research cancellation uses a narrow watch run transition because the generic terminal writer's person-reading follow-up requires a visible research.

OpenAlex search and citing helpers accept optional `sort` and `publication_date`; defaults preserve all prior requests, descriptions and outcomes. Watch OpenAlex reads send `publication_date:desc` and select the exact publication date. `publication_date_of` accepts only a real calendar date in exact YYYY-MM-DD form. The default facade endpoint declares the two options and OpenAlex moves from adapter revision **2 to 3**. bioRxiv remains revision 2 with no added options and no date-sorted watch read. An OpenAlex discovery continuation recorded under revision 2 refuses its next page as `adapter_revision_changed` with no send, rather than silently restarting. The regenerated connector freeze changes only OpenAlex descriptor/revision fields within its original 111 cases; every prior request, wait and result is identical. One extra sorted-page case brings the freeze to 112 cases and records direct/facade requests. `product/connector-onboarding.md` records the option change and version consequence; this is not G1 acceptance or lookup binding.

The orchestrator read the OpenAlex provider documents on 3 October 2026: sorting (page dated 28 July), filtering (25 September), paging (18 September), and work attributes (30 September). Sorting documents `publication_date:desc`; paging supports 100 per page and ends at null next_cursor. The date describes the primary location and may not describe earlier locations. Paid created/updated filters and publication-date filters are not used. The citing recipe spells its sort `-publication_date`, unlike the sorting page; this implementation uses the latter's form. These statements are the supplied document record, not an implementer network verification. Cursor-sort persistence and the existing `cites:` adapter path were not verified against a real provider.

Protocol-query units copy the bound protocol's compiled queries in stored order. Unsearchable or unconfigured connectors are retained as skipped units without requests. Citing units resolve included heads to distinct ordered works, take the sorted distinct OpenAlex ids of all source versions, and read one id per unit; missing ids remain explicit. Up to ten citing units roll through the list, prioritizing partial baselines and wrapping without duplication; the position moves only at completion. Unread included works and unread citing ids are counted separately; unread ids still make the check partial when another id of their work was selected. Departed works leave the plan and newly included works receive their first baseline. Legacy researches refuse follow-up; a protocol-query watch requires a current protocol. Only OpenAlex units receive a date sort; all other providers retain discovery options and have unknown temporal coverage, including bioRxiv.

Frozen policy caps are **100** records per page (or the connector's lower maximum), **2** pages per unit, **10** citing units, **80** actual HTTP requests, **3,000** provider-returned records including dropped identities, **2** rate-limit retries per adapter call and **1,800 seconds** from queueing. They are unmeasured policy choices. A full frozen page must fit the records left; a 100-record page is deferred after 2,950 records rather than reduced to 50. Oversized provider responses are stored and counted in full, their excess recorded, and later pages deferred. The watch-scoped HTTP client inherits the application client's default headers, including User-Agent, while provider code retains its per-request timeout. A watch-scoped transport checks run control, visibility, watch/protocol binding, request budget and deadline before every actual HTTP send, then commits usage before delegation. This includes transient retries, adapter-internal rate-limit retries and PubMed EFetch. Refused sends consume no reservation. Interrupted sends keep theirs. Quota defers later units of that provider without sends. OpenAlex and citing reads use the existing host gate; page gaps are respected. Payload and record raw data are sanitized with the sent credential, and citing identities use the same admission/drop rule as facade dispatch. Payload files precede the transaction that records their immutable read and finishes the page step; canonical JSON and actual byte digests are separate.

The baseline window is the same frozen two-page depth used by later checks. This expressly amends design section 15 item 5: its page-limit stop means interruption before the window was read, rather than the window's own depth. A successful two-page window is complete even with a non-null cursor. A partial baseline keeps its cut and last succeeded cursor and continues only its missing pages; failed or skipped providers baseline silently on their first successful read. Changed connector contract/revision restarts a partial baseline at page one with a new cut and a recorded reason, retaining seen rows. In continuation, dated post-cut records can be announced; pre-cut records join the baseline. Undated records become `baseline_undated`, receive no item, and their titles and uncertainty appear in the read model. A unit's success boundary moves only after its read finishes without error; failures and deferrals retain it and expose the unread window. `last_success_at` is only a convenience timestamp for at least one successful unit/page read; unit boundaries remain authoritative.

Identity uses exact version aliases before any similarity comparison: provider-native ids, merge-eligible normalized DOIs, OpenAlex, PMID and PMCID. Neither title nor an arXiv family DOI is an alias. arXiv versions remain distinct; family and named publication DOIs create relations. OpenAlex and bioRxiv records with the same W id share the alias, as the library does; an OpenAlex work can contain several locations and is treated here as one record. Exact alias hits enrich the seen row and do not reannounce. A later DOI joining several seen rows retains the oldest row and oldest item, marks other rows/items merged and preserves dismissals. Library suppression uses `identifier_mappings` only and records every exact matched version. Notice items remain separate from new-paper counts. Late notice classification keeps the first metadata copy, item id and dismissal while recording kind history. Items found through multiple watches/units remain one research-level item with finder history.

Similarity never merges or suppresses a finding. This departs from design section 7's allowance for automatic-merge verdicts to count as already seen/in library. Version, notice and artifact relations are stored distinctly with check provenance. Comparisons are bounded to the research's seen set and own corpus; whole-library comparison is exact alias only. Every item record, including notices and alias hits, reconciles relations, and existing counterpart items receive their side of a later relation even when dismissed or absent from that check. Native-only identity carries an uncertainty line; no publication date is inferred from a year and confirmed version time remains null.

The run supplies queued/running/pause_requested/paused/cancelled/failed state and its reason. A completed check is `succeeded` only when all planned units have acceptable coverage; otherwise it is `partial`. The closed reason list separates provider failure, missing configuration, quota/budget/deadline deferral, unknown outcome/coverage, unreached dates, incomplete baseline, rollover, missing OpenAlex ids and unsearchable units. Exhaustion, requested windows, oldest/newest dates, cap cuts and actual sort provenance remain distinct. Date-sorted coverage can be established by exhaustion or reaching the requested lower date; non-OpenAlex temporal coverage stays unknown. Run controls use the existing routes. The existing research view accepts queued, running and completed watch runs without changing its implementation.

Nine async watch routes provide read-only preview, create, list, Check now, disable, rebind, check detail, item list and dismissal. Their synchronous store calls stay on the application's event-loop thread, where the worker shares the SQLite connection. Mutations retain CSRF, closed request bodies, 1–200-character command keys and expected revisions. Canonical content hashes bind route, research, resource and body. Exact replay precedes stale-state checks, creates no write/send/wakeup, and returns stable original ids with current read models; changed content returns `idempotency_key_reused`. Other named refusals include `scope_changed`, `watch_changed`, `item_changed`, `run_active`, `check_paused`, `watch_follows_old_scope`, `watch_disabled`, `watch_enabled`, `no_protocol` and `interval_not_built`; unknown/trashed research is 404. Rebind atomically disables the old watch and creates a current-scope watch/check with a fresh baseline and the research seen set retained. Interval mode is refused. Preview says “DEIXIS checks only while it is running.” No scheduler, toast or notification is implemented.

The AST guard forbids library writers and library SQL mutation. The real-worker lifecycle authorizer covers baseline, new-item, all-provider-failed and cancelled checks, denying every write outside runs, steps, events and watch tables, with only `researches.updated_at` and `worker_owner.heartbeat_at` allowed. `sqlite_sequence` is allowed for `events.id AUTOINCREMENT`; protected table rows and protected columns remain equal, research counts remain equal, and denied writes are zero. Synthetic libraries contain no waiting person-reading files. Backup records watch payload byte digests, rejects conflicts/missing/corrupt files and restores all six tables and payload hashes. Authorized purge removes watch rows before runs and returns only orphaned payload files, retaining files referenced by other watch reads or library records. Source purge protection is unchanged.

R6 has no screening path for a provider record outside discovery. Library-work and Zotero additions need a new `corpus_memberships.added_by` value and a screening decision, requiring a separate design item and table rebuild. B5 exposes DOI/landing URL and ships only new/dismissed/merged items; `added` is unreachable. B7 must offer Open at publisher/Copy DOI as the add fallback. B6 must add the scheduler, catch-up, interval settings, `next_due_at`, section 15 item 6's superseding rules and item 12's catch-up settings. B7 must add screens, sidebar count, “Not checked between A and B”, native-only identity uncertainty and the prohibition on claiming “up to date”.

The prompt records joint agreement on owner-level choices A–E by its author Claude Opus 5.5 and gpt-6.1-sol medium during plan review; A selects revision 3. F was revised to expose undated continuation records; F′ adopted the equal-depth bounded baseline amendment after frozen page sizing, and G adopted the file digest. Round 3 added counterpart reconciliation; round 4 reported no findings. The code reviewer and outside-sandbox verification remain for the orchestrator to record.

**Limits:** No network, DNS, real provider or model call was made; the planned read-only provider probe was not run. Mocked-provider tests establish application behavior, not recall, provider truth or scientific validation. A bounded page window can miss records; relevance ordering can later raise an older unseen record into view, and a late-indexed old record can be new to the list while retaining its old date. Cross-provider records without a shared DOI/version alias can be announced again. Non-OpenAlex temporal coverage remains unknown. Caps and deadline have not been measured. Similarity covers only the research corpus and seen set. Nothing checks while DEIXIS is closed. No web files, live service, STATUS.md or TODO.md were changed; no commit, push or publication was made. Completion compares each record that gets or keeps an item with the research's live seen rows and corpus inside one transaction, so its duration grows with the seen set; it was not measured. A command key is looked up across all researches (the content hash still binds the research), so one key reused in another research is refused rather than separated. Exact writer checks and sandbox socket failures are recorded in `/tmp/p8b5/impl-report.md`.
## D199 — P7-F2 and P7-F3: PubMed subrequests are counted and bounded, sends are counted apart from reservations, and the authenticated OpenAI embedding route is tested

**Status:** accepted (implemented). Writer: gpt-6.1-sol high. Task prompt `docs/product/p7-f-prompt.md` by Claude Opus 5.5, reviewed by gpt-6.1-sol medium in two rounds: r1 düzeltmeyle hazır (1 high: an adapter that rebuilds its outcome could refund work it sent; 6 medium: trace across retry exits, atomic settlement, scoped equivalence, conformance coverage, excess test sizing, 429 redaction; 1 low: test seam), all folded in; r2 hazır. Code reviewed by Claude Opus 5.5 in two rounds: r1 düzeltmeyle hazır (1 high: six existing tests failed in the full run; 1 medium: kill-search trace held as hidden instance state keyed by query text), both fixed; r2 hazır.
**Reviewer checks outside the sandbox:** full pytest before round 1 fixes 12,559 passed, 6 failed, 2 skipped; after them **12,574 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped** (558.8 s). Frozen fixtures `baseline.json` and `query_baseline.json` byte-identical. No web change.
**Date:** 2026-10-03, detached `41495a8`, worktree `DEIXIS-p7f`.

**Context:** D196 left P7's exit unmet until G1-F1, P7-F2 and P7-F3 land. P7-F2 (acceptance record item 7, ledger e, D174 Q4): discovery counted one base request plus retries per search (`flow.py:2058,2068` on `41495a8`), while PubMed sends ESearch and then EFetch, so a PubMed page that read records charged one request for two and its D89 query share did not bound what it sent; kill-search reserved PubMed's worst case but recorded no observed sends. P7-F3 (item 8): the authenticated OpenAI embedding batch had no test of its own.

**Decision:**

1. `common.send` writes one transport entry per call (URL without query, attempts, sends, retries, status, HTTP status, delivery class) into a context-local collector that `facade.dispatch_search` opens around the adapter and returns as `Dispatched.transport`. The workflow counts only from this collector, so an adapter that rebuilds or drops its outcome cannot refund requests it sent. Every search request must go through `common.send`; the registry-driven conformance replay (566 cases, direct, facade and dispatch) checks collected attempts and sends against the mock transport. `SearchOutcome`, `pubmed.py` and the frozen fixtures are unchanged; an EFetch failure keeps its frozen top-level outcome while the ESearch entry keeps its own completed/200 status.
2. Discovery reserves a dispatch's worst case `R = requests_per_search × (1 + allowed 429 retries)` on the run and the query before sending and, after the reply, settles both to the attempts made and adds observed sends to a new run counter `provider_sends`, in one transaction (`Store.settle_usage`). For a single-request connector the settled count equals the old `1 + retries`; PubMed now pays for EFetch. A crash in flight leaves the reservation (overcount, never undercount).
3. Discovery bound: PubMed's per-page share is `2 × (1 + wait) + transient retries`; D89's send rule (send while the settled count is below the share) stays; a transient connection failure is no longer resent once the share is spent (all connectors). A query's settled count therefore never exceeds `share − 1 + R`; an adapter that exceeds its declared cost is charged and recorded as `over_reservation`. A strict "worst case must fit" check was not adopted, because the retry action adds one request per failed search and would no longer let a retried read send its page.
4. Kill-search keeps its never-refunded per-attempt reservation, adds observed sends to `provider_sends` and charges any excess over the reservation; `provider_sends ≤ provider_requests` holds on both paths. The trace is handed from the request to the recording step explicitly.
5. Every discovery page step and kill-search query step that dispatched carries `output.transport` (reserved, attempts, sends, per-dispatch subrequests, `over_reservation` when nonzero), kept across transient resends and later missing-key or budget refusals. No migration, no `search_runs` column, no `connector_json` change.
6. P7-F3: `tests/test_openai_embedding.py` sends an authenticated OpenAI batch on a mock transport (POST `https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings`, one `Authorization: Bearer` header, model `text-embedding-3-small`, truncation, batching, shuffled indexes, unit vectors), a 401 after one request, missing key with no request, and the keyless Ollama and LM Studio contrast; a direct `ResearchFlow` run stores similarities under `openai:text-embedding-3-small` or ends `embedding_failed` with the key absent from stored rows, events and files. Named change: OpenAI and Gemini embedding errors redact the sent key when a reply echoes it, on 401 and on exhausted 429.

**Limits:** Mocked transports and synthetic keys only; no live provider or OpenAI call, so live error and quota formats remain unmeasured. A stop during a transient backoff writes no step, so that operation's trace is lost while its counts stay; an adapter that raises keeps its reservation and loses its collected entries (ledger d, unscheduled). Lookup (`lookup_requests`) and chaining (`chain_requests`) accounting stay as they were and go with G1-F1; `RetryPolicy` stays descriptive; the OpenAlex count and distribution probes are not counted here; PubMed's top-level `before_send` on an EFetch connection failure is frozen (the entries show ESearch was sent). `provider_sends` has no UI label. Most new embedding route tests are characterizations that also pass on `41495a8`; the redaction cases fail there. P7 exit is still not met: G1-F1 remains.

## D185 — P8 B8a: a candidate version with its finished kill-search can be reviewed by another model; the review reads a stored copy and is marked stale when the candidate, its search or its owner status changes

**Status:** accepted (implemented). Written by gpt-6.1-sol high; plan by Claude Opus 5.5 reviewed by gpt-6.1-sol medium in three rounds (r1 2 high + 5 medium + 1 low, r2 3 medium, all folded in; r3 hazır); the owner-level choices (target rule, frozen assessment passage text, grouping by assessed source, decisions-only candidate accept) were made by the coordinator (Claude) and agreed by gpt-6.1-sol medium in r1. Code reviewed cross-vendor by Claude Opus 5.5 in five rounds (r1 düzeltmeyle hazır: 2 medium (stale review summary line after decisions; the paused-search browser case did not exercise the rule) and 4 low; r2–r4 one medium each, all in the browser spec (missing refresh after an out-of-process seed, an Escape race with the dismiss field, an unrealistic seeded search that crashed the matrix view); r5 hazır).
**Reviewer checks (outside the sandbox):** `candidate-review.spec.ts` 5 of 5 passed in two consecutive runs; `review.spec.ts` and `candidate.spec.ts` passed with the round 1 build (18 tests). Eight screenshots inspected (request and detail, light and dark, 1280 and 390 px). After the rebase onto `41495a8`: full pytest 12,553 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped; build clean; lint 0 errors and 16 warnings (the baseline, no new warning); full Playwright 187 passed, 1 failed, 7 not run: the failure is the X05 keyboard-focus case in `a11y.spec.ts` (the flake D194 recorded); the X05 group alone then passed 10 of 10 twice and failed once on a different X05 case. This batch changes no X05 screen; that flake is not fixed here.
**Date:** 2026-10-03. D185 is reserved by the coordinator.

**Context:** D181 left candidate snapshots and stale tokens for B8. The candidate review envelope existed, but preview and start refused the target and the planner had no candidate group. This batch implements the candidate path with synthetic records and a scripted model. It does not close P8 or execute B8b.

**Decision:** A candidate review targets a candidate version id. The candidate must belong to the research, be outside the Trash and have that version as its current version. Only the version's latest stored kill-search, ordered by `created_at, id`, is read; it must be completed, failed or stopped. A paused or running newer search prevents a review even when an older search completed. A run that has not frozen its queries is not a search yet: a paused kill-search run without a `kill_searches` row does not supersede an earlier completed search or block its review.

One consistent read copies the statement, conditions, critical assumption, nullable nearest simple explanation, ordered elements, kill-search outcome and counts, computed status, latest owner override and assessed-source matrix. The validation plan is excluded. Passages are copied without cutting from each assessed hit's immutable assessment StepInput, preserving the text used to make the matrix. Sources and the evidence manifest retain the existing purge-readable shapes; the manifest digests the live stored dependencies. Abstract evidence with a null passage id maps to the single abstract passage in that assessment input. Every quote must locate exactly or through normalization in its mapped passage; missing, ambiguous, foreign or unlocatable evidence refuses the snapshot rather than dropping evidence.

Snapshot-time markers record the current scope and candidate version, latest search id, a stable hash of the reviewed search's outcome, counts, hits, cells, evidence and query records, and the reviewed version's latest override id. New codes are `newer_candidate_version`, `newer_kill_search`, `kill_search_changed` and `owner_status_changed`, alongside `scope_revised` and the existing evidence codes. Cell quotations associate evidence changes with element refs; whole-claim-only or unquoted passages associate them with sources. Overrides on a later version do not change the reviewed version's owner marker. Model, package and provider changes do not add a stale reason.

The closed review input requires `candidate_context`: null for answers and reports, an object for candidates. It carries the version, conditions, assumption, explanation, counts, status and matrix. Bounds follow the producing decomposition and assessment contracts: six conditions of 300 characters, six cells per source, three quotes per cell or whole claim, eight matrix sources, 400-character source notes, 300-character cell notes and 1000-character quotes; other text is bounded at 4000 characters and owner reasons at 2000. Semantic checks resolve matrix sources, element refs and quote passages against records and allowlists, including passage ownership. D12 handle paths include matrix source ids and both quote passage-id paths. Over-bound owner text is recorded as not reviewed without shortening it.

The review method now distinguishes the owner's candidate from the matrix, which records a prior model's reading. Findings may target an element or the whole candidate; unread works are a context limit. The package hash changes from `sha256:5ba2d214bd1122f9544aaa537226b6234123bf6be82b3e6e1c6d9ff99dcf75ff` to `sha256:8353306cc05cf102609375f89e870c9c0c611d68b7ca528153f27ee612fce93c`. D184 remains tied to its original hash. Existing stored plans are not rewritten; a queued or paused review crossing the package change retains the existing `skill_package_changed` send gate.

Candidate groups pack assessed sources in rank order under the existing full-envelope, 96,000-character and 48-passage bounds, repeating all shared candidate context. An oversized source is omitted with its reason; an oversized shared context refuses the candidate and records `candidate_too_large` plus each measured bound reason, one null-source row per distinct reason; a candidate with no assessed source has one empty-matrix group. Failed groups record one not-reviewed row per source, or one null-source row for an empty group. Preview exposes element and matrix-source counts. Answer and report packing policy is preserved with identical measured envelopes, instructions and package identity; the required null field and new method increase measured request sizes and change preview fingerprints.

Preview and start accept candidates through the existing routes. Read models retain the snapshot's element metadata, candidate version and id, kill-search id, matrix source order and frozen passages. Candidate findings have no live-claim dependency fingerprints. Accept records a decision with `no_change_made`; apply remains report-claim only. This decisions-only candidate accept is an owner-level departure from Q2's prefilled-editor wording, settled by the orchestrator Claude and agreed by gpt-6.1-sol medium in prompt review round 1: mapping free suggested text to the structured candidate would require a guess. The existing card editor writes a new version when the owner chooses to edit it. B8b must list this departure in its closing record.

The candidate detail offers a disabled-with-reason request entry until the latest search is terminal, and exact-version review summaries. A review opens in its own sheet; older-version sheets retain decisions but offer no request. Both entries refresh their review lists after sheet decisions, starts and run controls, and when the sheet closes, without adding backend events. New review runs store `target_kind` and `target_id` in their target JSON; the transcript confirms the run against that target's review list, retaining the previous lookup only for older runs. Its plan note uses lowercase `candidate` (`aday` in Turkish). Candidate evidence opens a narrow second sheet using frozen read-model passages and only the backend-located anchor, without a live passage request or adding corpus membership. Labels distinguish element findings, whole-group source coverage, stale reasons and source omissions, in English and Turkish. Candidate stale labels branch on the four reason codes, so a removed owner override with null status still names the owner status. The scripted `[review-finding]` marker emits an element finding with a matrix quote and an evidence-free whole-candidate finding; `[review-hold]` remains unchanged.

**Evidence:** Synthetic real API/Worker lifecycle tests reuse the unchanged SQLite authorizer and hash checks for normal, internal-error, invalid-output and cancelled cases. Their non-empty protected tables include `research_candidates`, `candidate_versions`, `claim_elements`, `kill_searches`, `kill_search_queries`, `kill_search_query_records`, `kill_search_hits`, `claim_matrix_cells`, `claim_matrix_evidence` and `candidate_status_overrides`. SELECT-only and forbidden-import checks remain unchanged. Tests cover frozen input equality, source grouping, each stale code and evidence target, fail-closed quotes, D12 repair, decisions, historical reads, purge and byte-preserving restoration of the four review tables with search-only assets and payload files. The focused suite passed 1829 tests. The full suite reported 11950 passed, 2 skipped and 17 sandbox socket/process-denial failures; it is not a fully passing suite. The implementation report at `/tmp/p8b8a-impl-report.md` records commands and red-on-old counts. On a clean `ff41701` copy the new and changed tests give 77 feature failures (55 old `NotImplementedError`s and 22 assertions, including the old 422 refusal) plus the 2 expected hash pins; 10 preservation tests pass on both. The browser cases ran in the reviewer's checks above.

**Limits:** No real model has read a candidate input in this batch; that is B8b. The executed pytest tests use synthetic records and a scripted model and establish workflow behavior, not review quality. Browser checks ran in Chrome only, with axe rules and keyboard paths; no other browser or screen reader was tried. A located quote identifies where text occurs, not whether a finding is correct. The matrix is a prior model's reading; the review does not retrieve or re-read sources. Rank-cut and unassessed works are counted, not read. A trashed candidate hides its review entry while GET by review id still answers. Candidate apply is not built. The P8 closing record and T14/T16 matrix rows belong to B8b. No live service was restarted, and no changes were committed or published.

## D195 — P9 re-extraction R2c: a recovery operation left running by an ended process is reconciled by whoever holds its file lock, never re-run; equation and arXiv readers take that lock; crash, limit and full-disk boundaries are tested

**Status:** accepted (implemented). Written by gpt-6.1-sol high (its first run stopped correctly on synthetic fixtures with non-hexadecimal hashes that the reader lock cannot name; the orchestrator resolved it in the prompt: such hashes are read without the lock because no writer or retry can lock or replace their path); plan (docs/product/p9-reextract-r2c-prompt.md, by Claude Opus 5.5) reviewed by gpt-6.1-sol medium in 4 rounds (r1 düzeltmeyle hazır, 5 high + 3 medium + 1 low; r2 düzeltmeyle hazır, 2 high + 2 medium; r3 düzeltmeyle hazır, 1 high + 1 medium; r4 düzeltmeyle hazır, 1 high, folded in by the orchestrator without a fifth round); code reviewed cross-vendor by Claude Opus 5.5 in 2 rounds (round 1 "düzeltmeyle hazır", 0 high, 2 medium (the Marker reader was closed, and so reloaded, after every per-PDF reader error or post-read refusal; the full-disk startup test raced the running worker on one connection) and 2 low (one failing hash stopped a whole sweep; every shutdown logged a cancelled task as an error), all fixed; round 2 "hazır").
**Date:** 2026-10-03, P9 batch R2c.

**Context:** D191 and D192 leave recovery receipts running after their owning process ends. A stale text receipt blocks the next retry; a stale restore receipt does not explain what happened to the file. Equation and arXiv source readers can also publish text from a file read across a concurrent restore. D176 requires reconciliation under the same cross-process file lock, separate file and text outcomes, and evidence at crash, parser-limit and storage-failure boundaries.

**Decision:** `workflow/reconcile.py` uses exclusive ownership of the hash lock as liveness. A busy lock, or a lock acquisition error, leaves the operation running and counts the hash as live; acquisition errors are logged once per hash/errno per Store. Reconciliation runs after worker recovery and legacy cancellation at startup or ownership takeover, before every worker turn selects a queued run, and lazily after a retry acquires its lock. A restore reconciles before its whole-file fast path and again after its writer lock is acquired, covering a holder that died while the writer waited. A failure for one hash leaves its unfinished receipt running, is logged once per hash/exception type per Store, and does not prevent the sweep from reconciling other hashes. Startup and worker sweep errors are logged without preventing work; lazy driver errors propagate through the existing storage-refusal handling.

A stale text retry becomes `interrupted/process_ended`, keeping its recorded input observation. A running text receipt that already owns an extraction is logged and left running as an impossible state. A stale restore without a before observation is interrupted without observing the target. With a before observation and no after observation, reconciliation records the target's present regular-file or missing state, then interrupts; a nonregular entry receives no observation. An existing after observation is retained. Reconciliation never completes a restore as `file_restored`, parses or retries text, creates an extraction or passage, or writes, renames or deletes target or retained files. Each interruption retains the existing terminal event semantics, once per holding research. Failed in-memory interruptions retain their own reason when the flush fails again. Reconciliation writes and pending text flushes use the rollback wrapper that closes a transaction after a failed COMMIT.

Equation and arXiv source reads take the non-blocking hash lock before the first read or write of the attempt and retain it through publication. Only a valid lowercase 64-hex stored hash can name this lock; legacy synthetic identifiers read without it because no retry or writer can lock or replace their path. A busy file returns the unchanged equation state plus `outcome: file_busy`, without an attempt, failure, eligibility row or event. Background reads wait one retry interval; an in-run equation step succeeds with the busy output rather than pausing. Threads are drained through repeated cancellation before unlocking. The arXiv child-owning task is shielded and never cancelled by its caller; it finishes under its own bounds before cancellation is re-raised. Marker shutdown shares one close task per process, waits for termination or kills on timeout, and reaps the child. The Marker service drains close before unlocking when cancellation or another non-`Exception` interruption escapes the reader request; completed per-PDF error replies and post-read publication refusals preserve the shared process. Equation-service shutdown awaits its cancelled tasks without logging normal cancellation as an error. OCR takes no reader lock because its holding research's run already excludes restore and retry.

The no-body extraction POST checks presence and regular-file status before the same-profile `unchanged` shortcut, without hashing. The two CLI messages now say: "The text retry operation stays running until DEIXIS reconciles it (at its next start, while it runs, or at the next retry of this file)." Exit codes, idempotent replay, capability reads and parser defaults retain their existing contracts.

**Verification:** Outside the sandbox, by the reviewer: baseline on 87cee0b 11,856 passed, 2 skipped; before the review fixes 11,947 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped; after the fixes and the rebase onto 30b070c (P7 G1 B4, D194) 12,476 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped, 62 warnings in 409.36 s (`/tmp/reextract-r2c-full-2.log`). Inside Sol's sandbox 17 socket/process-listing tests fail and pass outside. 98 R2c cases. The 29 red-on-old cases (R1 fresh POST and CLI after a crashed retry, R2 startup, R3 restore crashes at six boundaries through startup, worker turn and a later upload, R5 Marker and arXiv busy reads, R6 missing/symlink/FIFO before `unchanged`) were rerun by the reviewer on a clean `git archive 87cee0b` copy: all 29 fail at their first behavioral assertion (operation still running or `operation_running`, parser and reader called under another holder's lock, eligibility row written, `unchanged` answered) and pass here; the two present/torn no-body guards pass on both. Existing tests changed: `tests/test_reextract_r2a_api.py` (a reservation without its lock is now a crash leftover: split into child-held lock → 409 `file_busy` and no lock → reconciled) and `tests/test_reextract_r2a_cli.py` (message text; the `running` refusal case now holds a real child lock); no assertion weakened. No migration. No web change, so no build, lint or browser run. The implementation report is `/tmp/reextract-r2c-impl-report.md`. Required evidence covers real child-process crashes at text and restore boundaries; startup, worker and lazy reconciliation; live owners and pending-interruption rollback; reader exclusion and repeated cancellation; cross-process final-transaction races; real parser timeout, memory, page and character limits; real `SQLITE_FULL` at the writing connection; injected `ENOSPC`; OCR exclusion; and R1/R2a/R2b compatibility. Pre-recovery historical schemas return zero reconciliation counts without querying recovery tables or taking a file lock; the existing migration fixture remains unchanged. These tests use synthetic records and do not establish scientific correctness.

**Carried work:** R3 owns backup and authorized purge of retained bytes, receipts and unreferenced retained files; verified input observations for initial attachments and ordinary upgrades; and provenance views. R4 owns UI labels for `process_ended`, the `file_busy` equation outcome and recovery receipts.

**Limits:** Synthetic PDFs only; no real library was used. Child Python processes are killed on macOS; this does not demonstrate power-loss recovery or filesystem durability. `ENOSPC` is injected; `SQLITE_FULL` is real. Advisory locks cannot stop outside processes. A pending interruption known only to another process may be relabelled `process_ended`. A long Marker read or arXiv read, including its source download, makes retries answer 409 `file_busy`; restores wait up to 10 seconds, then answer 409. Viewer and figure routes take no lock, and the hash-keyed figure cache can retain figures read from torn bytes until restart. A torn same-profile file still answers `unchanged` to the no-body POST. Windows is untested. No live service was restarted; nothing was committed, pushed or published.

Full Playwright under the port lock: 182 passed, 1 failed (`a11y.spec.ts` X05 keyboard focus, `toBeFocused`), 7 not run behind it; the X05 group rerun alone passed 19/19. The new pause texts were not inspected in a rendered browser.
**Date:** 2026-10-03, detached `98f651f`, worktree `DEIXIS-g1-b4`.

**Context:** D174 assigned B4 facade dispatch, integration, capability binding and revision metadata. D178/D179 retained four named changes and the B2 missing-key guard. B3a established request/outcome equivalence; B3b moved query declarations without moving dispatch. This batch implements search dispatch and bounded post-processing; it does not establish G1 acceptance.

**Decision:** The refactor routes discovery and kill-search through `facade.dispatch_search`, using the registry entry, the caller's snapshotted key, the existing request mapper and unchanged `CompatibilityConnector.search`. A frozen `Dispatched` carries the outcome, admission count and connector provenance to writers, with no attribute fallback. Retry loops and consumers read its `outcome` explicitly; flow-made refusals remain `SearchOutcome`, and annotations name both types where accepted or returned. `returned_count` retains the provider-returned count. Pre-send guards, usage, reservations, transient retries and endpoint keywords retain their prior placement. Direct registry/facade outcomes and provider modules remain unchanged.

The four named changes are separate from that equivalence:

1. Search and chain row/step errors and kill-search step errors retain non-null `error_kind`. Quota and temporary limits keep `rate_limited` status; quota pauses as `provider_quota_exhausted`, temporary limits as `provider_rate_limited`. Historical rows are not rewritten.
2. S2 batch answers bind by normalized DOI/ArXiv identifier regardless of position. Request positions sharing a DOI share the matched answer when all answers naming that identifier are JSON-equal, ignoring object-key order. Conflicting answers fail every position for that DOI. Order consistency requires each non-null answer to name exactly the identifier requested at its own position; only an order-consistent null is `not_found` when no answer names that identifier. Unique matches survive inconsistent positions, including `[X, A]`, and matched arXiv answers retain a journal DOI relation. Invalid identifier shapes name nothing. Request shape, length/parse checks and raw response shape remain unchanged.
3. Search payload and admitted record raw data are copied and sanitized with the sent key before storage; the digest covers sanitized JSON. Colliding redacted dictionary keys omit that dictionary with `secret_key_collision`. Chain and keyed lookup writers use the operation snapshot, including when the environment changes before writing.
4. A provider-independent predicate drops non-string, stripped-empty, `"None"` and stringified-container identities. Numeric text remains admitted. Returned counts govern paging/read totals; admitted counts govern stored results. Nonzero drops appear in step output and search provenance, including failed steps; zero adds no step-output field.

Migration **0067** adds nullable `search_runs.connector_json`. Dispatched rows record contract, adapter and query-rule revisions, payload representation and dropped count; flow-made and earlier rows remain NULL. Before a pending page continues from the last succeeded stored page, SQL NULL permits compatibility continuation. Unsupported contracts or changed adapter revisions refuse with `adapter_revision_changed`; invalid JSON/shapes/types, missing required fields or a missing search row refuse with `connector_provenance_invalid`. Both fail the next step with zero results and pause as `provider_adapter_revision_changed`, without request, usage, search row, page-one restart or provider substitution. Completed pages are not rechecked merely on reopening. Query-rule revision is recorded, not compared. Only temporary databases applied the unpushed migration; unique prefix/upgrade checks must be repeated after coordinator renumbering, and branch databases are disposable.

Decisions 8–11 retain explicit boundaries: `RetryPolicy` remains descriptive and policy-driven dispatch is unscheduled (ledger g); local `ValueError` conversion remains unscheduled (ledger d). An unknown stored paged endpoint still raises `KeyError` before usage; S2 kill-search reserves first, then facade `ContractViolation` (a `ValueError` subclass) replaces the module's `ValueError` with unchanged accounting. Lookup capability binding moves to the named unscheduled **Lookup capability binding** owner: this amends D174's B4 row, keeps batched direct helpers and unsupported zero-request facade lookup, and leaves D174 Q3's default unmet. B5 cannot record the original binding as done. Chaining remains on direct helpers. `/api/connections` adds contract ID, adapter revision and sorted capabilities, retaining existing fields and access wording. English/Turkish labels cover quota, missing configuration and changed/unreadable continuation provenance.
