**Limits:** The scan is automated: axe finds the defects it can find mechanically and cannot judge label wording, reading order or whether the focus order makes sense, and says nothing about cognitive accessibility. Chrome only. Records are synthetic and the model is scripted, so text lengths and states are those of the fixtures. The 200% case is the 640 px layout equivalent, not Chrome's zoom, so text-only zoom is not measured. Reduced motion is measured as computed styles and live animations at one moment per screen, not frame by frame; the scan context has reduced motion on, so gradient text such as `.shimmer-text` and styles that exist only in normal motion mode are not measured for contrast. The hand contrast check composites flat colours (no image or gradient) from the paint stack at one point, and applies opacity on ancestors to the text colour only. The focus indicator is compared with a clone of the element, so a style that depends on the element's position among siblings is not reproduced. Tabs not on the list (Activity, Candidates, Artifacts, Waiting for your PDF) were not scanned. The evidence-report table scroll region (`.evidence-report-table-scroll`) is a Tab stop and is labelled "scrolls sideways" even when the table fits and nothing scrolls. The "uncovered" check at 200% reads what is under the control's centre at the scroll position the keyboard focus produced; it tests the centre point, not the whole box, and the three controls that cannot take focus use a scroll check. The "measured" contrast nodes are measured against the paint stack at the centre of the node's own text only (one point per node), 28 are own text only, and 78 are ölçülmedi (named kinds above). Between states the scan does not check that the page is still the intended screen, except 1b, 11a and 11c (which assert their own element); the other screens rely on the waits in their test. The scan switches off transitions and parks the pointer, so hover and transition colours are measured only where a test says so (the default button). A pass of `stable` means no change between two reads around axe, not that nothing changes later. A pass on the frozen list says nothing about other screens or states. The keyboard walk used one column in the evidence flow and the default source scope except in the first case. X07 was not run. The hand contrast measure reads colours through an 8-bit canvas (alpha rounded to 1/255); that rounding was not quantified.

**Sol re-review follow-up (3 October 2026):** gpt-6.1-sol high re-read H6 (read-only) and returned düzeltmeyle hazır with four mediums, all still true on `main`. (1) `focusWhenLost(..., follow)` ended on any key or pointer press, so pressing only Shift while a fill's status line had focus left focus on `body` when the line went away. (2) After Exclude the reason field called `.focus()` unconditionally and took focus back from the "Filter sources" field the person had moved to while the request was pending. (3) `act` swallowed errors, so `.then(toRunStatus)` also ran after a failed Generate answer and sent focus to the previous run's heading. (4) X05's keyboard walk closed toasts with `.click()`, so "every activation by keyboard" was wider than the code. Changed: `focus.ts` ends the wait only when another connected, enabled element other than the one the wait placed (or the control the action started from) takes focus, and a key press that leaves focus in place no longer ends it; it takes the starting control as a fourth argument, which the fill, answer and Resume callers capture before the request, because a started-late wait mistook a control the person had moved to for the starting one (found by mutation: the new delayed-fill test fails without it). Both `act` functions (`ResearchView.tsx`, `EvidenceTable.tsx`) now return true or false; the answer, Resume, add-column and fill handoffs run only on true and are tied to the run id the request returned (`data-run-id` on the table status line and the run strip), and on a failure the pressed control gets focus back once it is enabled, if focus is still lost. `ReasonForm` takes focus only when it is still on the Exclude button or on `body`. `Toast.tsx` was changed too: a pre-fix probe showed that dismissing a focused toast left focus on `body`, so closing it now returns focus to the element that had it before the toast, or to the selected tab or the first available control. In `a11y.spec.ts` the keyboard walk closes toasts by Tab and Enter (`dismissToastsByKeyboard`, which also audits where focus lands and logs it); the clicks that remain in the walk are setup only and are listed in a comment above the helper, and the scan, motion and zoom tests keep the click helper because they do not claim keyboard-only. Nine new tests in the X05 describe: Shift, ArrowLeft and Tab during a fill, a fill answered after the person moved to Export CSV, a delayed Exclude with typing in the filter, a failed fill, a failed answer start (409 and 503), and a keyboard toast dismissal returning focus. Checked by running them against the old code: the Shift test fails on the old `focus.ts`, the delayed-fill test fails without the early-captured starting control. Measured: `npm run build` clean, lint 17 warnings (the baseline), `git diff --check` clean, `a11y.spec.ts` 37 of 37 (was 28; the scan still reports 104 scans, none unstable), the whole Playwright suite 179 of 179 (was 170), `human-queue.spec.ts` alone three times 16 of 16 each; no backend or contract change. Review of this follow-up: Sol (gpt-6.1-sol high), three rounds, 0 high each; the mediums of rounds 1 to 3 that were cheap were folded in (starting control passed to the wait, the failure path's `opener` passed as origin, the Resume fallback to the run strip, the comment on `ReasonForm`). Not folded in, and still open: a wait is still started after the request returns, so a person who moves to another control and loses focus before the response arrives is still handed the status line (the delayed tests blur after the response); the 409 and 503 answer tests answer at once and do not hold the response to prove the button was disabled and focus on `body`; `ResearchView.tsx` finds the run's heading by its position in the transcript list, not by `data-run-id`; the toast's fallback target is not tried again when `.focus()` fails, and the fallback itself has no test; a paused `research_title` Resume has no test. The last three edits (the origin argument on the failure path, the Resume fallback, the comment) were reviewed in round 3 as part of the final diff. Execution: automated browser test; data: synthetic records, scripted model.

## D166 — P9 H5: capacity and performance are measured model-free against thresholds frozen before the first measurement

**Status:** accepted (implemented and measured on 2 October 2026 under parallel load; reviewer: Opus 5.5 high (Sol quota out), Sol re-review pending)
**Date:** 2026-10-02, P9 batch H5.

**Context:** The only capacity evidence before this entry was a statement count (`tests/test_view_scaling.py`) written after one real event: a 7,769-source research whose `research_view` blocked the event loop for 37 s. Nothing measured wall time, loop blocking, memory, first paint in a real browser, a large PDF in the viewer or backup time at size. H5 adds a synthetic-library generator and a measurement script (`scripts/p9/capacity.py`, `scripts/p9/capacity_browser.mjs`), runs them against the real server process and real Chrome, and compares each result with the thresholds below.

**Frozen thresholds and classes (S7, frozen 2 October 2026, before any measurement; never changed after one).** Points: N = 100, 1,000, 5,000, 7,769 (the size of the smoke run that blocked the loop) and 10,000 works in one research. Three repetitions per point; the verdict uses the worst of the three and the median is written beside it. A repetition is a fresh server process on a fresh clone of the same prepared library (cold process, warm OS file cache). `capacity.FROZEN` carries this table and `tests/test_capacity_script.py` holds an independent copy of it.

| Id | What | Threshold (frozen) | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| K01a | N=1,000: research screen ready in Chrome, `K01-ui` (definition below) | worst of 3 <= 2.0 s; the API time of the **first** `GET /api/researches/{id}` the process serves (a separate, earlier call than the browser load) must also be <= 2.0 s | mandatory |
| K01b | N=5,000: research screen ready, `K01-ui` | worst of 3 <= 10.0 s; the first-call API time also <= 10.0 s | mandatory |
| K01c | N=100 and N=7,769: `K01-ui` and API time | none; numbers recorded | measure only |
| K01d | N=10,000: does the screen become ready within 120 s (works / does not work) | none beyond the yes/no and the time | measure only |
| K02a | N=1,000: longest `/api/health` latency among health requests that overlap the first research view request (event-loop block; window defined below) | worst of 3 <= 0.5 s | mandatory |
| K02b | N=5,000: same | worst of 3 <= 1.0 s | mandatory |
| K02c | every other N, and N=5,000 with one event stream open and a second tab loading the screen: same number | none; recorded | measure only |
| K03a | server RSS peak over a repetition (sampled every 100 ms from process start to the end of the browser steps; `ps -o rss=` is KiB, multiply by 1024), judged at N = 100, 1,000, 5,000 and 7,769 and over the large-PDF steps (S7 makes 10,000 a works / does not work record, so it is not judged here; the control run is not judged either) | worst of all points < 2,000,000,000 bytes (S7 says "2 GB altı", taken literally as decimal and strictly below; it is the stricter reading) | mandatory |
| K03c | the same RSS peak at N=10,000, and in the control run | none; recorded | measure only |
| K03b | `library.sqlite` (+ `-wal`) bytes and data-directory bytes per N | none; recorded | measure only |
| K04a | Quick find (Meta+K, typed query) to first Sources result visible, N=1,000, 5,000, 10,000 | none | measure only |
| K04b | source list first paint (navigation to `#/research/<id>/sources` until the first source row is visible), same N | none | measure only |
| K04c | passage panel first paint (click on a source with a stored PDF text until the passage text shows), same N | none | measure only |
| K05 | large PDF in the viewer: first page and jump to a far page (definition below) | none | measure only |
| K06a | `python -m deixis backup` of the N=5,000 library with the server stopped | worst of 3 <= 120 s, exit 0, manifest present | mandatory |
| K06b | backup folder bytes (N=5,000), and K06a-shaped times at N=1,000 and N=10,000, one run per repetition with the server running, and the 45 MiB large-PDF library backed up (server stopped) | none | measure only |
| K07 | the limits table has the four columns filled for each limit (hard limit, watcher threshold, configurable default, measured peak; "not measured" is a filled cell) | complete | mandatory |

Where the code goes beyond or differs from this table: the control run has one repetition instead of three (`capacity.repetitions_for`; K03c is judged on it and the control run's health numbers stay in its raw file); the code's K06b also records the stopped-server backup time at N=1,000, N=10,000 and the large-PDF library, and the running-server backup time and health maximum at N=1,000, 5,000 and 10,000; the code's `what` strings are shorter than the text above; K06a also fails when the manifest's file count differs from the count the formula in `storage/backup.py` gives (the frozen text says "exit 0, manifest present"; the extra check can only make a pass into a fail). No threshold, class or point list differs.

K03a is strict (`<`, "2 GB altı" read as decimal); every other limit passes on equality. A mandatory row that exceeds its threshold is not made to pass: the cause is found and, if the fix is small and safe (an index or a read-path change that leaves the view JSON identical), measured again against the same threshold; otherwise the row stays red and the documented limit ("above N works, X is slower than T") is written for the owner (plan section 4 rule 2). No threshold was added to K04 or K05.

**Shape of the synthetic library** (`generate`, deterministic text and shape from a fixed seed; ids and timestamps are not). Five researches: one big research with N works and four small ones with 12 works of their own each (48 extra works; the home list has rows and Quick find scans several researches). Works go in through `Store.upsert_provider_source` with a `ProviderRecord` each (DOI `10.5555/h5.<n>`, title `SYNTHETIC capacity study <n> on <topic>` over 40 cycling topic words, three authors from 240 surnames, year 2000 to 2025, a venue, a 900-character abstract, `version_label` set); the works with `n % 10 == 0` carry one other version, added to the research with `candidate=False` as `record_search` does. The big research has 20 completed search runs (each with a completed run and finished step so the foreign keys hold); `n % 20` buckets give 15 % included, 55 % excluded, 30 % pending; every 10th included work has a real six-page PDF (PyMuPDF, unique page 1 text) stored with `add_asset_with_pages`, so the viewer, the plain-text view and backup see ordinary files. The generator ends by asserting that no run is queued, running, pause-requested or paused (a server start would execute it), that there are no model sessions or waiting person-PDF requests, that no work lacks a `source_key`, and by checkpointing the WAL away; `measure` refuses a copy where that is not true. `pdf-library` builds one research with one 45 MiB, 500-page PDF (text plus incompressible JPEG noise) attached with a hand-built extraction of pages 1 and 400, because the extractor stops at 400 pages and the upload limit is 50 MiB; no extraction ran. The control run drops the `source_versions.work_id` index from a copy of the N=7,769 library and has one repetition (the other points have three).

**Method.** Per repetition: record `uptime`; start `python -m deixis serve --no-browser --port <8900-8920>` with an allowlisted environment (no model CLI on `PATH`, a temp `HOME`, a temp working directory, no repository `.env`) on a clone of the prepared library; sample the server's RSS every 100 ms; once `/api/health` answers 200, run a `/api/health` poller (25 ms, one persistent connection) around the first `GET /api/researches/{id}` on a fresh connection, then a second warm call (recorded, never judged); the K02 maximum is taken only over health requests whose send-to-receive interval overlaps the first view request. Then one `capacity_browser.mjs` run in system Chrome (fresh context per step, requests to other origins aborted and counted): `K01-ui` runs from the start of `page.goto` until the heading `h1.research-title-text` has the expected `aria-label` (computed from the same rule `ResearchView.tsx` uses) and the Sources tab's `.research-tab-count` equals the response's `sources.length` (the title's typing animation is not counted; waits poll on animation frames); `K04b` until the first `.source-row` is visible; `K04a` from the return of `fill('alpha')` until the first Sources option is visible (the dialog's 120 ms debounce is inside it); `K04c` two paths, "Open PDF" then "Plain text" until the unique page-1 text of the clicked row's own PDF shows (the row's work number selects the marker; every PDF's page 1 carries a different one), and "Read abstract" until `.source-sheet .passage-text` shows; `K02c` with one `events/stream` read held open by the script and a second tab in the same context loading `K01-ui` (the first tab's own EventSource is a second open stream). `K05` clicks "Open PDF" and stops when "Loading PDF…" is gone, the toolbar says `/ 500`, the canvas is not blank (pixel sampling) and its pixel digest has stayed the same for 100 ms (pdf.js draws text first and the image later, so one dark-enough sample can be a partial paint), then sets the page input to 400 and stops when the canvas label names page 400, the pixel digest differs from page 1, the canvas is not blank and the digest has again been stable for 100 ms (the label alone changes before the page is drawn). The 100 ms stability wait is part of the recorded `pdf_first_page_s` and `pdf_jump_s`; the raw record also keeps the first moment the other conditions held, `first_page_first_ok_s` and `jump_first_ok_s` (the recorded time minus the stability wait the browser reports), so the wait's share can be read off. `goto` and the ready wait of `K01-ui` share one 120 s deadline. A screen that is not ready within it is a measured result, not a harness error: the repetition writes `ui_ready_timeout` 1, `ui_ready_ok` 0 and `ui_ready_s` 120.0 (the limit that was reached; the real elapsed time is `ui_ready_elapsed_s`, and the two screen conditions, title `aria-label` visible and tab count equal, are each reported in the error text and in `ui_ready_readiness`), so K01a and K01b fail (120 s exceeds both limits) and K01d reads "does not work" with `ui_ready_ok` 0. Any other failure (no step, a selector error, no JSON from node) is a harness failure: no time and no `ui_ready_ok` are written, the error is in the repetition's `errors` and the rows stay `incomplete`, so a fast failure cannot read as a fast pass. `ui_ready_ok` is 1 only when the step succeeded within 120 s, and its worst of three is the minimum (any 0 is 0). Node prints the result so far after every step and the script reads the last complete line, so a node run that is stopped at its budget, `(120 s + 60 s) x steps`, keeps the steps it had finished. A first view call that does not answer 200 writes no first-call or health time and an error. A backup whose manifest file count differs from the formula is a failed backup. The server is stopped (SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 15 s, only the recorded PID), then `python -m deixis backup` is timed on the stopped data directory and once more against a running server with the poller on; the manifest's file count is compared with the formula `1 + distinct source_assets.storage_path + distinct payload references` (not the data directory's file count). K03b's `wal_bytes` is read after the server stopped (`wal_bytes_running`, read before, is kept beside it). `judge(frozen, results)` is a pure function with the verdict set `pass | fail | incomplete | measured`. Every repetition records `uptime` at its start and its end (`load1`, `load1_end`, `load_high`); the final run starts when the 1-minute load average is below 4, and a result in which any repetition started or ended at a 1-minute load of 4 or more is labelled "under parallel load" and is replaced by a later run under load < 4 (both stay in the raw files). The readiness check opens the library read-only (`mode=ro`, not `immutable=1`, which ignores the WAL and would hide a run queued there) and refuses a prepared library or clone with a non-empty `library.sqlite-wal`. The three `measure` calls (points, `--pdf`, `--control`) either share one `--out` folder or each use their own and are put together with `summarize|table|limits --out A --also B ...` (repetition files are merged by point name, the summary is written to `--out`); K03a needs the `pdf` point and K03c the control point from those calls; a `(point, rep)` held by two folders is refused with an error instead of being pooled twice. The K07 cell "works in one research" shows the largest N that loaded with the time of its slowest successful repetition and "k of 3 repetitions ready".

**Capacity table (final run, 2 October 2026, `.local/p9-h5/final/`, three repetitions per point, worst and median).** Label: **under parallel load.** The wait for a 1-minute load average below 4 succeeded at 3.86 and the run started there, but other batches then ran on the same machine: the 1-minute load was 3.3 to 4.2 during N=100 and N=1,000, 3.9 to 8.5 during N=5,000, 8 to 12 during N=7,769 and N=10,000, and 11 to 13 during the PDF and control runs. N=1,000 and N=5,000 therefore ran at or just above the threshold of 4, the rest above it; every pass below has a wide margin (smallest: K02b 0.40 s against 1.0 s), and a loaded machine makes timings worse, not better, so the verdicts are not expected to turn on a quiet machine, but this was not re-measured. Every repetition had `errors: []` and its library's run states unchanged afterwards.

K07 limits (`capacity.py limits`; kind, value, source line, measured peak): upload 50 MiB (hard limit, `api/app.py:77`; a 45 MiB PDF was viewed, not uploaded, the largest accepted upload is H3's); download 30 MiB (hard limit, `documents/fetch.py:25`; not measured here, H3); extraction 400 pages (hard limit, `documents/pdf.py:57`; a 500-page PDF was viewed, no extraction ran); extraction 3,000,000 characters and 90 s (hard limits, `pdf.py:58`, `:61`; not measured here, H0b); extraction watcher 1 GiB (watcher threshold, `pdf.py:59`; not measured here, H0b, and the server's RSS is not what it watches); `model_concurrency` 6 (configurable default, `config.py:27`; not measured, needs a model); server RSS peak (measured only: 135.3 MB at N=100 to 232.3 MB at N=10,000); works in one research (measured only: 10,000 loaded, screen ready in 1.11 s).

**Before and after the fix (same frozen thresholds).** First run, before migration 0063, under load 14 to 102 (`/tmp/h5-before-fix/`, not kept in the repository): worst `K01-ui` N=5,000 12.0 s (K01b fail), K02a 0.69 s (fail), K02b 7.97 s (fail), first API call median 0.29 / 3.5 / 6.9 / 17.5 s at N=1,000 / 5,000 / 7,769 / 10,000, Sources list first row at N=10,000 23 to 56 s. Final run after 0063: first API call median 0.078 / 0.38 / 0.64 / 0.84 s at the same N, K01b, K02a and K02b pass, Sources list at N=10,000 5.7 s. The fix is indexes only (the statement count did not change, 44,674 at N=5,000); step 2 (batching the per-source queries) was not needed.

**Supported size and documented limits.** Tested up to 10,000 works (11,000 source versions) in one research on this synthetic shape: the research screen is ready in about 1 s and the view API answers in 0.8 s, and no request blocked the event loop for more than 0.83 s; server memory stays near 230 MB; backup takes 1.2 to 1.6 s on libraries of 20 to 40 MB. The frozen thresholds hold at N=1,000 and N=5,000 with a wide margin and nothing was measured above them that fails. What slows with size, as a recorded limit and not a threshold row: the view API grows about linearly (0.38 s at 5,000, 0.84 s at 10,000) and each call blocks the event loop for its whole length (health maximum 0.40 s at 5,000, 0.83 s at 10,000), the Sources list is not virtualized and takes 2.7 s to first paint at 5,000 and 5.9 s at 10,000, and opening a passage from that list takes 2.7 to 3.6 s at 5,000 and 7 to 8 s at 10,000; Quick find stays under 1 s (0.93 s at 10,000, of which the search request is 0.011 s). A library with answers, reports, evidence tables and many run steps is not covered (see Limits). The control run (N=7,769 with the `source_versions.work_id` index dropped on today's code) took 0.64 s for the first call against 0.64 s with the index: it shows that this lookup no longer matters on current code and does not reproduce the 37 s event, which also had the old per-work query pattern that is fixed in code.

**Fix (round 1, after the first full run).** That run, under parallel load (load average 14 to 102), breached three mandatory rows: K01b (`ui_ready_s` at N=5,000 worst 12.0 s against 10.0 s), K02a (health maximum at N=1,000 worst 0.69 s against 0.5 s) and K02b (N=5,000 worst 7.97 s against 1.0 s). The median first view call was 0.29 s at N=1,000, 3.5 s at 5,000, 6.9 s at 7,769 and 17.5 s at 10,000, so growth was faster than linear. Cause: `_research_view` runs about 8 statements per source version (8,994 at N=1,000, 44,674 at N=5,000), and four lookups in that loop had no index on the column they filter, so each one read its whole table every time and the view was quadratic in the number of sources. Migration `0063_view_lookup_indexes.sql` (index only, no row or table change) adds four indexes; `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` before and after on the N=5,000 library:

| Lookup | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `SELECT DISTINCT provider FROM identifier_mappings WHERE source_version_id = ? AND scheme = provider` | `SCAN identifier_mappings` + temp B-tree for DISTINCT | `SEARCH ... USING COVERING INDEX identifier_mappings_view_lookup (source_version_id=?)`, index `(source_version_id, provider, scheme)` |
| `run_steps WHERE operation_key = ? ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 1` | `SCAN run_steps` + temp B-tree | `SEARCH ... USING INDEX run_steps_operation (operation_key=?)`, index `(operation_key, started_at)` |
| the same joined to `runs` (`other_copy:`) | `SCAN s` + temp B-tree | `SEARCH s USING INDEX run_steps_operation (operation_key=?)`, then `runs` by primary key |
| `source_assets WHERE source_version_id = ? AND removal_reason = 'replaced' ORDER BY removed_at DESC` | `SCAN source_assets` + temp B-tree | `SEARCH ... USING INDEX source_assets_replaced (source_version_id=?)`, partial index `(source_version_id, removed_at) WHERE removal_reason = 'replaced'` |
| `passages WHERE asset_id = ? AND kind = 'pdf_page' ... GROUP BY physical_page` (`ocr_state`, once per stored PDF; found by profiling, not in the first list) | `SCAN passages` | `SEARCH ... USING INDEX passages_asset (asset_id=? AND kind=?)`, index `(asset_id, kind)` |

The `passages` scan was 0.29 s of a 1.0 s view at N=5,000 and the only remaining scan inside a loop. `passages_asset` is a fourth index, beyond the three the fix round named (`identifier_mappings`, `run_steps`, `source_assets`): the implementer added it because `ocr_state` scanned `passages`, and the orchestrator accepted it on 2 October 2026 because it is index-only and sits in the same migration. Statement counts did not change (44,674 at N=5,000). Step 2 (grouping the per-source queries in Python) was not done: the in-process timer numbers below were taken at load average 22 to 30 and 0.63 s is above the 0.6 s engineering aim, but the final run passed K01 and K02 with a wide margin, so step 2 was not needed. The view JSON is byte-identical before and after on a clone of the N=100 library and on a library with replaced assets, a failed fetch, another-copy lookup, PDF candidates and discoveries, a second provider's record and another version (`cmp` of `json.dumps(sort_keys=True)` output). In-process timer on a clone of N=5,000, one machine at load average 22 to 30 (an engineering aim of 0.6 s, not a measurement and not a threshold): view wall 3.6 to 5.6 s before, 0.42 to 0.63 s after (CPU 0.38 to 0.42 s); N=1,000 0.07 s after; N=10,000 1.2 to 1.7 s after (CPU 0.93 s). Growth is close to linear now, a little above it from 5,000 to 10,000. `tests/test_view_lookup_indexes.py` (3 tests) holds the plan test on the statements `research_view` really ran (captured with a trace callback, not copied) for the five lookups, with the same statements scanning once the indexes are dropped (the regression test on the old schema), view JSON equal with and without the indexes on a library built from the fixtures above, and the migration applying once on a 0062 library without changing any row. K01, K02 and the load labels after the fix: see the capacity table above.

**Verification:** `tests/test_capacity_script.py` (the frozen table against an independent copy, `judge` with one repetition for the control and three elsewhere, a harness failure of the K01 step staying `incomplete`, a readiness timeout counted as a measured breach (K01a and K01b `fail` at N=1,000 and 5,000, K01d `measured` with `ui_ready_ok` 0 at N=10,000), the worst `_ok` flag being the minimum, the 120 s deadline, the load label, merging folders, the guards, the N=100 generator and its shape, a copy with a queued run and a run queued in the WAL refused before any server starts, the stored-PDF markers, a manifest-count mismatch failing a backup, `cmd_measure` writing its summary after an exception, the manifest-count formula against `backup.create_backup`, the K07 table against the imported constants, the poller and the event stream stopped when a request or a node run raises, a killed node keeping its finished steps and the node budget, a duplicate `(point, rep)` across folders refused, the K07 works cell, `wal_bytes` read before and after the stop, and `first_ok_s`). `tests/test_migrations.py` has a one-element change: the hard-coded list of applied migration numbers gained 63, which every new migration requires; the test's purpose is unchanged. `tests/test_view_lookup_indexes.py` was added for migration 0063. Touched suites (`test_capacity_script.py` 35 tests, `test_view_scaling.py`, `test_view_lookup_indexes.py`, `test_migrations.py`, `test_backup.py`): 71 passed; full suite 8,259 passed, 2 skipped (code-review round 2 fixes included). Smoke of every subcommand (generate at N=100, 1,000, 5,000, 7,769, `pdf-library`, `measure` at 100, 1,000, 5,000, `--pdf`, `--control`, `table`, `limits`) ran end to end under a machine load of 7 to 43, with no leftover process and no port in use afterwards; its numbers are not measurements and no number or threshold was taken from it.

**Limits:** Synthetic text and shape: no answers, reports, evidence tables, model steps, model sessions or `link_records`, so the view of a research that has them is not measured. The server process is cold but the OS file cache is warm; one machine, Apple Silicon, system Chrome only. `K01-ui` runs after the first API call on an already warm server process (that first call carries the cold start). The real research screen refetches the view on every recorded event while a run is active; that is not measured, and neither are real model and provider latency. The health poller and the first view call share one Python process (the view body is received in full and parsed after the poller's window). K02c holds the first tab's own EventSource plus one script-held stream. Stored PDFs in the N-point libraries are small (about 75 files and a few hundred KiB at N=5,000); byte-heavy copying is timed with the 45 MiB library instead. K07 cells for the upload, download, extraction and `model_concurrency` limits say "not measured" with the owning batch or reason; the server's RSS is not what the 1 GiB extraction watcher watches. The control run shows what an unindexed library costs on today's code and does not reproduce the 37 s event (that run also had the old per-work query pattern, which is fixed in code). A smoke run (N=100, one repetition) shows the script works end to end; its numbers are not used.

## D165 — P9 H7: six daily-use defects are closed, none of them reported from real daily use; a torn file under a hash name, a full disk hidden by a savepoint or a Zotero write, and a model stop that said too little now end in a whole file or one sentence

**Status:** accepted (implemented; reviewer: Opus 5.5 high (Sol quota out), Sol re-review pending)
**Date:** 2026-10-02, P9 batch H7.

**Context:** The plan's source for H7 is the owner's daily-use log (`.local/p9-daily-use-log.md`, owner question S9). **That file does not exist**, so no item here comes from real daily use, and nothing in this decision shows what the owner met while using the product. The list was built from section 3.6 of the plan, from the findings and left-open lines of D161 to D164, from `TODO.md` "Carried over from slice 31" (read, not edited) and from five items the main session named. H5 and H6 had no decision on `origin/main` when the list was frozen; their findings go to H8. Each closed item was reproduced on `565c430` first (batch prompt `docs/product/p9-h7-prompt.md`).

**Decision (closed; patch files `.h7-patches/NN-*.patch`, one per item, 07 is this record and the prompt):**
1. **01, severity (a). An upload trusted any file under `papers/<sha>.pdf`.** A torn file left by a version before D162 was kept; the asset row named the hash of the whole file, extraction ran on the torn bytes and came back `failed`, and `deixis backup` refuses such a file. `pdf_files.file_is_whole` (size and hash) is now used by `store_upload` and `store_pdf_file`; a file that is not whole is replaced through `os.replace`. Test fails on the old rule (asset `failed`, file still half).
2. **02, (c). The candidate and lineage savepoint helpers ran `ROLLBACK TO` unconditionally.** After a statement-level SQLITE_FULL SQLite has already ended the transaction, `ROLLBACK TO` raised "no such savepoint" and hid the full disk. Reproduced with a real `max_page_count` limit. `db.rollback_savepoint` acts only while the connection is in a transaction; an ordinary failure still undoes only the helper's own writes (test).
3. **03, (c). Two Zotero routes wrote a PDF, and the import wrote its payload file, with no full-disk mapping.** `disk_full_refused()` now turns ENOSPC and EDQUOT there into the 507 `disk_full` answer of D164; any other `OSError` stays a 500 (test). The second route (`zotero-pdfs`) is covered by an AST test that both `store_pdf_file` calls sit inside the guard, not by a request.
4. **04, (c). The run line of a model stop said too little.** After a restore the line said only that the connection was not ready (D163), and a model quota stop read like any other failure (D164). The run already stored the connection's reason and the model's own error text. Under the unchanged reason line the screen now shows "Open Settings, connect it again, then resume this run." with the connection's reason, or "The connection reported: ..." with the model's words (one line, 240 characters), English and Turkish. DEIXIS does not decide whether the text means a quota or a rate limit; the person reads the connection's words.
5. **05, (d). `tests/test_api_flow.py` defined 35 test names twice.** The 34 first copies were identical to the second ones (AST compared) and the 35th was an older, stale version; 706 lines are gone, no test name is lost, and a test now fails when any test module defines a test name twice. Helpers `attached_research` and `run_to_end` are still defined twice; they are not tests and the guard does not look at them.
6. **06, (d).** `CLAUDE.md` called the README status paragraph out of date; since H1 it is not. The sentence is replaced.

**Not closed, with severity and reason:** pre-D164 password-protected PDFs stay `no_text` and read "PDF has no text layer" (c; closing it needs a version bump that re-reads every PDF, or a change of the D45 rank rule: a product decision); a classifier for quota versus rate limit (c; needs measured error strings of the real connections, no real-model call was allowed); the contact email in the PDF fetcher's `User-Agent` (c; a new disclosure of the person's address); arXiv 406 (b for that provider; needs measurement against arXiv); the `sw` discovery-time short title (c; changes what is shown); the four slice 31 test-debt items (d; each is a test to design, too large for this batch); the report on a real model (D124 to D129; needs a real-model run); leftover `.part` files of cut downloads and restores (d; removing files in the data directory is a new behavior); ENOSPC on other write paths and missing UI text for CSRF and Host refusals (c; D164 avoided a global handler); `TODO.md`'s deferred items (d; not planned); H5 and H6 findings (to H8).

**Verification:** `pytest` 8,357 passed, 2 skipped (baseline on `565c430` 8,343 passed, 2 skipped; +14 new tests in five `tests/test_p9_h7_*.py` files; the 706 deleted lines of `test_api_flow.py` removed duplicate copies only, so no test name is lost). Each fix test was run on the old behavior and failed there: 01 (asset `failed`, file still half), 02 and 03 (the old function or no guard put back by monkeypatch), 05 (the guard fails on `HEAD`'s `test_api_flow.py`); 04's Playwright E line and source check fail on the old code, its two backend tests describe data the old code already stored. `npm run build` ok, `npm run lint` 17 warnings (baseline, none new), Playwright 134 passed in the full run and 8 not passed there (`human-queue.spec.ts:265` failed with `route.fetch: socket hang up` against the fixture server while other worktrees may have used the same ports, the 7 after it did not run); `human-queue.spec.ts` alone: 16 passed, so 142 of 142 passed, one of them on a rerun. Screenshots looked at: the `model_call_failed` line at 1440 and 390 px, light and dark; the not-ready line at 1440 and 390 px light and 390 px dark in Turkish (through a mocked response, not a committed test). `git diff --check` clean. No migration, contract or `methods/` change; `skill_package_hash` unchanged. Review: plan prompt 1 round, code diff 1 round, both Opus 5.5 high, "düzeltmeyle hazır", 0 high (plan: 4 medium and 3 low; code: 2 medium and 3 low; all folded in). The plan round ran after the first implementation draft, not before it.

**Limits:** The list is not a daily-use list: there is no log, and the plan's note stands that a problem nobody wrote down is not covered. Item 01 repairs the file, not a row that already exists: an asset row stored from a torn download keeps its `failed` status and text (no route extracts again for a known hash, and re-extraction answers "unchanged" for the same `EXTRACTION_VERSION`); the file becomes whole, so backup accepts it. `file_is_whole` hashes an existing same-size file inside the async upload route (up to 50 MB, about 0.1 to 0.2 s, event loop blocked). Item 03 keeps what was already imported when the disk fills in the middle of a collection (each item commits on its own); importing again continues. Item 04's not-ready line is covered by a source check and the backend test that the run carries the reason, and was looked at once through a mocked response; the fixture's connection is always ready, so Playwright covers only the `model_call_failed` line. The connection's words are shown as they came: they may be long, in another language, or unhelpful; they are cut to one line of 240 characters. Item 05's guard looks at test functions, not helpers. One machine, one macOS version. Sol re-review of the prompt and the diff is pending (usage limit until 3 October 2026 20:39).

## D164 — P9 H3: every fault class in F05 to F08 now has a named test or a stated reason; a full disk, a busy or damaged library and three kinds of unreadable PDF each end in one sentence and a code instead of a bare 500 or a traceback

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted; reviewer: Opus 5.5 high (Sol quota out), Sol re-review pending)
**Date:** 2026-10-02, P9 batch H3. The number is a placeholder: D161 (H1, H6) and D162 (H2) exist in other worktrees; the main session renumbers.

**Context:** The H3 inventory read the code and tests at `4050a94`, then measured on macOS 27.0.1 arm64 with a 16 MiB HFS+ sparse image. A full disk answered 500 "Internal Server Error" (`sqlite3.OperationalError` at `COMMIT`, `OSError` 28 creating `papers/`), nothing mapped a SQLite error, the worker task ended on a database error, a corrupt library showed as an uvicorn traceback, and a password-protected PDF was stored `no_text` ("PDF has no text layer", OCR offered) while a broken one stored the MuPDF stderr tail.

**Decision:**
- `storage/db.py`: `describe_failure(exc)` classifies by SQLite primary code (`sqlite_errorcode & 0xFF`) or `ENOSPC`/`EDQUOT`: 13 `disk_full` 507; 5, 6 `database_busy` 503; 8 `database_readonly` 503; 11, 26 `database_damaged` 503; anything else is `None`. `transaction` rolled back unconditionally, which after a statement-level SQLITE_FULL raised "no transaction is active" and hid the real error; it now rolls back only `if conn.in_transaction`. `open_problem(path)` opens the library as the app will and returns one sentence for a classified failure.
- `api/app.py`: handlers for `sqlite3.DatabaseError` and a typed `DiskFull` (raised by `store_upload` for ENOSPC, including the `mkstemp` that already fails on a full disk) answer `{"detail", "code"}` and re-raise anything unclassified (a code bug stays a 500). `UploadRefused` and the `local_guard` refusals carry codes `upload_too_large`, `upload_not_pdf`, `upload_size_undeclared`; status codes and English texts are unchanged.
- `workflow/worker.py`: a `sqlite3.DatabaseError` or `OSError` in a turn no longer ends `run_forever`; it is logged once per error class, waits `RETRY_SECONDS` (1 s, stop-aware) and goes on. A run that fails with a disk-full error is stored `failed` with `pause_reason = disk_full`; if recording the failure itself fails, it is kept in memory and written at the top of the next turn. A run that was cancelled or paused while the failure waited is no longer overwritten with `failed` (the check also applies to the first write; before H3 a late exception could overwrite `cancelled`).
- `__main__.py::serve`: one block calls `db.open_problem` after the port check. A classified failure prints one sentence with the path and the SQLite reason ("did not start and changed nothing") and returns 2. A failing migration is not caught: since `open_problem` (connect and migrate) now runs in `serve` before uvicorn, an unclassified failure ends in a traceback from `serve` with exit code 1 (before H3 it ended in uvicorn's lifespan traceback, exit code 3), and migration now runs before the lifespan's `skill.integrity_issues()` check; an unwritable directory is H1's, an unknown migration id is H4's (B03); H4's read-only precheck must run before this block because `db.connect` creates `-wal`/`-shm` and switches the journal mode.
- `documents/pdf.py`: the child states `password-protected PDF` (`needs_pass`), `PDF has no pages`, or `PDF could not be read` (not a PDF, MuPDF cannot open it) as `{"error": ...}` with exit 0; the parent passes only these three through, and any other nonzero exit becomes `PDF could not be read` with the stderr tail going to the log. Statuses, `EXTRACTION_VERSION` and the stored format are unchanged. `extraction_error` is now in the research view's asset dict.

Row verdicts. **F05:** passes on the SQLite and upload half. On the 16 MiB image at 0 bytes free the first create-research is refused 507 `disk_full` with the exact sentence; the upload is refused the same way after a fix found by the process test (it answered 500 on all 5 attempts because `mkstemp` sat outside the `try`; the in-process ENOSPC test missed it because it fails the write, not the file creation). Process files on their own (`-m process -n 0`): 7 passed (5 + 2). `npm run build` ok, `npm run lint` 17 warnings (baseline, none new), Playwright 142 passed. No `hdiutil` image of this batch stays attached, no server of this batch left. On this base the `process` marker does not exist yet (H2 adds it with the default-run exclusion); until then use the two commands above. No existing test was edited; no migration, contract, `methods/` or `skill_package_hash` change.

**Limits:** The `sqlite3.DatabaseError` handler has the same hazard the plan avoided for a global `OSError` handler: a database error raised after a streamed response (an event stream) has started is wrapped by Starlette in a `RuntimeError`; the connection closes either way. - One machine, one HFS+ image. The user's APFS volume is not shown; ENOSPC on a write path that no test hit (any other route that writes a file) stays a 500, because a global `OSError` handler was avoided (Starlette wraps a handled exception raised after the response started).
- Quota and rate limit read the same on screen; a model `client_timeout` and a model quota stop read as the generic "The model call did not complete" / `model_call_failed`. CSRF and Host refusals have no useful UI text (a wrong Host blocks the page itself; `api.ts` refreshes the CSRF token once).

- `tests/test_api_flow.py` defines 35 test names twice; only the later copy runs. Cleanup is outside H3.
- The 404 text in `PdfViewer` relies on pdf.js turning a 404 into an exception with `status`; read in its source, not exercised in a browser.
- No test uses a provider delay near the real 30 s limit (P6).
- The savepoint helpers in `candidates/store.py` and `lineage/store.py` still run an unconditional `ROLLBACK TO`, so a SQLITE_FULL there can still be hidden behind "no such savepoint" and answer 500 (not edited, per the batch prompt).

## D163 — P9 H4: a backup restored into an empty folder matches the source in every table and file; a library written by a newer DEIXIS is refused before anything is written, a cut restore no longer leaves a half file, and a backup of a library the current code has not migrated yet no longer fails

**Status:** accepted and implemented; B02 measured once on the owner's library with their consent (counts only); reviewer: Opus 5.5 high (Sol quota out), Sol re-review pending.
**Date:** 2 October 2026.

**Context:** `tests/test_backup.py` compared hand-picked tables (D34 counted 30 on a library that has since grown to 62 migrations and 85 tables). Nothing compared every table and file after a restore, nothing refused a library written by newer code (`db.migrate` only applies what is missing, and `db.connect` writes `journal_mode = WAL` before anything is checked), and D162's Limits named an open item: `restore` copied straight to final file names. Plan rows F03 (restore part), F06 (unknown version), F10, B01, B01n, B02, B03 (`docs/product/p9-hardening-plan.md`, H4; batch prompt `docs/product/p9-h4-prompt.md`).

**Findings by measurement (each test was run on the old code first and failed as described):**
- **Restore left a half file under its final name** when killed during a copy (process test: `papers/SYNTHETIC-0.pdf`, 460 bytes; the next restore would refuse with "a different file already exists"). Fixed: each file goes to `.restoring-<uuid>.part` in the target folder, its hash is checked, then `os.replace`.
- **A conflicting target file was found in the middle of the loop**, after earlier files and `papers/` had been written, so a refused restore changed the target (B01n "middle" case). Fixed: a pre-pass over all targets before the first write.
- **A manifest of the wrong shape** (a JSON list, no `files`, an entry without `path` or `sha256`) ended in `KeyError`/`AttributeError` and a traceback. Now `BackupError`.
- **No guard against a newer library** (B03): the real launcher started on a library with an unknown migration id (two cases, `Uvicorn running`, 352 connections accepted in the test's probe). Fixed, see the decision below.
- **Found by the B02 run on a real, 22-September library:** `backup._referenced_files` queried tables the old schema does not have (`kill_search_queries`), so `deixis backup` on a library the current code has not migrated yet (checkout updated, first start not yet done) died with `sqlite3.OperationalError`. Each reference source is now its own query and "no such table/column" counts as no references from it; a table that exists with a missing file still fails the backup.

**Decision:**
1. `db.check_schema_known(path)` (new, read-only, before `connect` writes anything): every id in `schema_migrations` that is not among the packaged migrations is refused (set difference, not "highest"), with one sentence naming the ids and saying to update DEIXIS or open the library with the version that made it, and that nothing was changed. No `-wal`: read with `Path.as_uri()` + `?mode=ro&immutable=1` (creates nothing). Non-empty `-wal`: the library and its `-wal` are copied with plain reads to a temporary folder and read there, up to three tries (a checkpoint between the two reads can tear the copy; `SchemaCheckUnreadable` after the third, and for an `OSError` while copying). Probed and the reason for the copy: a plain `mode=ro` open of a WAL library changes `-shm`, and `immutable=1` misses an id that exists only in the `-wal`. `serve()` and `reextract()` call it before the app is built and exit 2 with the message; `db.connect` calls it for every other caller. `backup` is deliberately not guarded (reading a newer library to rescue it stays possible). A corrupt file still raises `sqlite3.DatabaseError` as before (H3).
2. S6, automatic backup before a migration: **not added** (the plan's default); README already tells the person to back up before updating (H1). No new startup message beyond the refusal. The manifest got no new field.
3. `restore_backup`: atomic placement, a pre-pass before the first write, removal of the code's own `.restoring-*.part` leftovers at the start of a re-run, manifest shape checks, `except BaseException` cleanup. The database staging (`library.sqlite.restoring`, then `os.replace`) is unchanged.
4. `scripts/p9/upgrade_check.py` (`copy-live`, `restore-copy`, `open-copy`, `--self-test`): the owner-approved B02 tool. It copies the live library with no SQLite contact that could write (`immutable` when there is no `-wal`, plain byte copy of the library and `-wal` otherwise), copies only the files the copy references, never `codex-home` or keys, refuses the default and `DEIXIS_DATA_DIR` folders without an explicit consent flag, runs the product's own backup and restore on the copy, and opens the restored copy with `create_app(start_worker=False)`, empty adapters, a transport that raises on every request. It prints counts only.

**Verification:**
- **B01** (`tests/test_p9_restore_matrix.py`, default suite): one in-process library built through the API with `FakeAdapter` (attached and academic discovery, selections, upload, answer, answer review, evidence table, trash and corpus removal, candidates and sw queue, report with claim links and edit checks, lineage), tables enumerated from `sqlite_master`: **85 tables, 67 with rows, 18 empty** (each empty table is named in the test with a reason; an unnamed empty table, or a named one that gains rows, fails the test, so a new migration's table is noticed). Backup, restore into an empty dir, before any server opens: all 85 tables equal in row count and canonical digest, 7 file hashes equal, `integrity_check` ok, `foreign_key_check` empty, `schema_migrations` equal. Then the restored library opened with `create_app(start_worker=False)`: 52 view JSONs, 0 differences; 1 answer anchor and 4 report anchors opened and found in their passage text; opening wrote nothing to any table. Allow-list: `generated_at` of the PRISMA-S export, and `worker_owner` only when comparing the live source (a running worker writes a heartbeat every second) with the backup.
- **B01n:** target holds a library, a lone `-wal` or `-shm`, a same-name file with a different hash (first entry and a middle entry), a missing or one-byte-changed file in `papers/`, `provider-payloads/` and the database, no manifest, a wrong format, a truncated manifest, escaping paths (`../x`, nested, absolute, `other/`, `papers/..`, empty), a manifest without the database, six malformed shapes: each `BackupError`, the target tree (names, sizes, hashes) unchanged; a same-hash file is accepted and kept.
- **B03:** unknown ids `0063`, `9999`, `0000` (below the packaged range, which a "highest version" check would miss), two together, and an id present only in the `-wal` (written by a child process with `wal_autocheckpoint = 0` and `os._exit`) are all refused by `db.connect`, `serve` (exit 2, port never accepted a connection) and `reextract`; `library.sqlite`, `library.sqlite-wal` and `library.sqlite-shm` sizes and hashes and the folder listing are identical before and after, also for a path with `#`, `?` and a space. A library from older code (migrations below the last) opens and `migrate` applies exactly the last one. Precheck time on a synthetic 211 MB library: 2 ms without a `-wal`, 0.23 s first and 0.06 to 0.07 s after with one.
- **F10** (`tests/process/test_p9_restore_process.py`): real server with a discovery run held `running` and a writer thread creating researches and uploading PDFs, three real `deixis backup` runs: researches in the three backups 11, 21, 30 (second run 10, 20, 29); each backup `integrity_check` ok, `foreign_key_check` empty, restored with exit 0, and `compare_states(backup, restored)` empty (255 table comparisons and 62 file hashes in all). Shutdown with the held call was forced (exit code 1), as D162 predicts.
- **F03, restore part:** a backup killed after its manifest restores; 85 tables and 5 files equal.
- **Restore killed half way:** killed in the first file, a middle file, the database copy and the database replace: no half file under a final name, no `library.sqlite`; a second real restore exits 0, leaves no `.part`, and equals the backup. The first two fail on the old code; the database copy and replace were already clean (the staging file existed), so those two are regression guards.
- **B02, measured once with the owner's consent (2 October 2026):** a read-only copy of the library at `~/Library/Application Support/DEIXIS` (no `-wal`, so the `immutable` path; the live folder's size, modification time and file list were identical before and after; the service was not running; copy deleted afterwards). Applied schema versions 1 to 36 and 26 pending (37 to 62), none unknown; the product's own backup and restore of the copy worked (222 files); opening the restored copy with `start_worker=False` applied all 26 migrations (1 to 62 afterwards), no worker, 0 outbound requests. Counts before and after the open are equal: 20 researches, 1,206 source versions, 17,448 passages. The views show 17 researches, 1,382 source rows over all researches and 165 distinct passage ids (views leave out trashed researches and removed memberships by design; these are not an equality check). No titles or text were read or recorded.
- **Connections after a restore:** credentials are not in a backup (a test asserts no key or auth file in it). A restored library opens; `/api/connections` reports the Gemini adapter without a key as `ready: false` with "Add a Gemini API key in Settings or set GEMINI_API_KEY ...", and a new run pauses with `model_connection_not_ready`. Gap, not fixed (UI out of scope): the paused-run line says only "The selected model connection is not ready. Nothing was sent to another model."; the "connect again" action exists in the connection settings and on the new-research page, not on the run line. The Codex "not signed in" path could not be run offline; its reason text was read from the code only.
- **Tests:** new default-suite files `tests/test_p9_restore_matrix.py` and `tests/test_p9_upgrade_check.py` (80 tests), `tests/p9_restore_compare.py` (shared `library_state`/`compare_states`); `tests/process/test_p9_restore_process.py` (8) and `p9_restore_driver.py`. `-m process -n 0`: H2's 21 and these 8, 29 passed. Full default `pytest`: 8,300 passed, 2 skipped (baseline 8,215 passed, 2 skipped at `7c197b7`). No web, migration, contract or method change; `skill_package_hash` unchanged.

**Limits:** One shape per scenario, single runs on one machine. Backup and restore equality shows that tables, files and views reproduce on this machine; it does not show that a backup moves to another machine (paths are file names only; that is manual, with I08) or that the owner's library is correct beyond opening, migrating and equal counts. The B01 library is synthetic and 18 of its 85 tables are empty by design of the fixture (reasons in the test); the B02 library had 36 of 62 migrations applied, so it shows the upgrade path from that schema, not from every older one. A cut restore leaves `.restoring-*.part` files until the next restore removes them; nothing removes them otherwise. `backup` on a library with no `schema_migrations` or `source_assets` table now produces a database-only backup (restore then refuses it) where it used to raise; a database that is not DEIXIS's is not detected by `backup`. The schema precheck runs in `connect` for every caller and reads the whole library into a temporary folder when a `-wal` is present (after a forced shutdown that is every next start; 0.23 s on 211 MB, more on a cold disk and for a larger library, not measured). The guard compares ids only: a library whose ids are all known but whose schema was edited by hand is not detected. Windows, cold-cache timings, power loss and a second machine are unmeasured. B02 ran on the owner's library once, on a copy made from a stopped service; a copy from a running service (non-empty `-wal`) is implemented and tested on synthetic folders only. Sol re-review is pending (usage limit until 3 October 2026 20:39).

## D162 — P9 H2: real processes were killed and signalled; a held model call, a Ctrl-C during an extraction and an orphaned extraction child did not end in time and now do, and a torn download file under its final name is no longer possible

**Status:** accepted (implemented; reviewer: Opus 5.5 high (Sol quota out), Sol re-review pending)
**Date:** 2026-10-02, P9 batch H2. D160 is the highest decision on `main` and on the other P9 worktrees today.

**Context:** Before this entry the only process-level kill evidence was the Playwright F case, which stops the backend with SIGTERM on synthetic rows. Plan section 4 rows F01, F02, F03 (kill part), F04 and I06 ask what the next start finds after a real kill. H2 starts real processes, kills them and reads the library, the call log and the process table afterwards. `tests/process/` (marker `process`, left out of the default run, `-m process -n 0`) holds the harness (`p9_harness.py`), the driver (`p9_driver.py`: the production `deixis.__main__.serve` with a scripted model, mocked OpenAlex, fixed SYNTHETIC PDFs and a guard that logs any non-loopback connect or `fetch_file` call; every server test asserts the log has no `network` line) and the tests. Each process has its own OS-assigned port and a data directory under pytest's temp dir; the child environment is an allowlist; the kill is `os.kill(pid, SIGKILL)` on one PID, never a group kill; every descendant is recorded as (pid, start time, command, pgid) before the kill and the teardown signals only a process that still matches its record. Measured on macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Python 3.12.13, uvicorn 0.53.0, load average 30 to 48 from other sessions.

**What was killed and what the next start found** (single runs, one shape per row):
- **F01, model step cut (answer and discovery).** SIGKILL while the `grounded_answer` call was held open: the next process reported `recovered = {runs: 1, steps: 1, model_sessions: 1}`, the run `paused/backend_restarted`, the step and its model session `outcome_unknown`, `integrity_check` ok. After resume the run completed with one row in `answers`; `grounded_answer` was sent exactly twice in total, no earlier task and no PDF fetch again; the step has two sessions (`outcome_unknown`, then `completed`) and the run's `usage` is `{downloads: 2, model_calls: 2}`. The second send is expected behavior: a separate model session and a separate budget unit, not a defect. Discovery run, second `abstract_screening` call held: before the kill 3 `vocabulary_labels`, 3 `criterion_proposal`, 2 `abstract_screening` and 10 provider requests; after resume only 1 more `abstract_screening` call (3 in total), no other task and no provider request again; the run completed. No defect found.
- **I06.** A second process on the same data directory reported `not_owner`; after the owner was killed (a held `grounded_answer` call) it became `owner` 1.03 s later in two runs (limit 10 s), recovered `{runs: 1, steps: 1, model_sessions: 1}`, showed the run `paused/backend_restarted`, and resumed it to one answer. No defect found.
- **F02, download write cut (mandatory row, defect found).** The 2nd write of a downloaded file was cut at half its bytes. On the old code `flow.py` (fetch step), `acquisition._attach_pdf` and the two Zotero routes in `api/app.py` wrote straight to `papers/<sha256>.pdf` guarded by `if not path.exists()`. After the restart the final, hash-named file held 329 bytes of the full file; the resume saw `exists()`, extracted from it and stored a `source_assets` row whose `sha256` is the hash of the full data. The failing test on the old code printed: `after restart: papers/b073bd0b…57a64.pdf is 329 bytes and its content hash is 0b87c056e033, not its name` / `after resume: source_assets row b073bd0b9739 does not match its file` / `backup failed (1): backup failed: file does not match its recorded hash: papers/b073bd0b…57a64.pdf`. With the fix the cut leaves one `tmp….part` file, the resume writes the whole file and the backup succeeds.
- **F02, file complete, row not written.** Held in `extract_pdf` (call 2: call 1 is the attached upload's): the file was whole and hash-named, no `source_assets` row. After restart and resume the file was reused (same size and mtime), the row appeared, one answer, backup succeeded. Same result on the old code. No defect found.
- **F02, passage write cut.** An upload's asset row and two passage rows were inserted inside `Store.add_asset_with_pages`'s `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction and not committed (a TEMP trigger calls a SQL function that sleeps once the second passage is inserted), then SIGKILL. After restart no `source_assets` row and no passage for the cut upload, the first upload's rows digest-identical, `integrity_check` ok, `foreign_key_check` empty. The same file uploaded again returned 201 with the passage count of a fresh upload of it in a second data directory. Same result on the old code. The upload route commits `create_upload_source` in its own transaction before `add_asset_with_pages`, so `works` and `source_versions` each grew by 1 (1 to 2): one source row with no asset, no passage and no membership remains. It is absent from the research's view and from `/api/library` (the library lists only members) and is not a defect of this batch to fix. It meets F02's wording: no `source_assets` row exists without its file, and a write cut inside a transaction is wholly absent. The complete `<sha>.pdf` of the cut upload stays in `papers/` unreferenced (no `.partial` was left); uploading the same file again reuses it. Nothing deletes such files.
- **F03, kill part.** `deixis backup` killed at three points. At the first copy and before the manifest: the folder has no `manifest.json`, `restore` exits 1 with "not a complete DEIXIS backup" and leaves the data directory empty, and a new backup into the same destination succeeds and restores. After the manifest: restore exits 0, the restored library passes `integrity_check`, each manifest file exists with its listed hash, and the research count equals the source's. The B01 comparisons (every table, canonical digests, view JSON) belong to H4 and are not claimed. No defect found.
- **F04, shutdown (two defects).** SIGTERM and SIGINT to the server PID with an event stream open, three cases. On the old code: idle worker, graceful in 3.25 s (SIGTERM) and 3.37 s (SIGINT); a held model call, **no exit in 40 s for either signal** (the shutdown waits for the worker, which waits for the model call; a Codex turn can run 300 s); a real extraction of a 60 MiB-decoded PDF in flight, SIGTERM graceful in 3.19 s but **SIGINT no exit in 40 s** (after the re-raised signal the interpreter waits for the executor thread, which lives as long as its extraction child, up to 90 s; an earlier probe with a patched 25 s extraction measured 24.2 s and exit status 0). Ctrl-C is the normal way to stop `python -m deixis serve`.
- **Orphaned extraction child (defect found).** The 90 s clock and the 1 GiB limit (D138, D159) live in the parent (`pdf._run_watched`) and die with it. With the parent SIGKILLed 1 s after the child started, the child was still alive 13 s after it was first seen, and an earlier probe saw it alive 42 s later (resident 120 to 600 MiB). The OCR, JATS render and arXiv source children share the shape: their parents hold the clocks and all four call `pdf._watch_memory` in the child.
- **Stand-in children (codex RPC, local embedding runner).** `codex_rpc.CodexAppServer` on a stand-in that reads stdin until EOF, and `local_embedding.LocalEmbedder` on the fake runner: after the parent's SIGKILL the child was gone at once when idle (0.01 s) and 2.9 s (`busy:3`) and 2.5 s (`slow:3`) after the kill when it was busy; in both busy cases it was still alive 1 s after the parent was confirmed dead (the child does not die with the parent), and the runner's in-use lock was free afterwards. No defect found in `codex_rpc.py` or `local_embedding.py`; neither was changed.

**Decision (the fixes):**
1. `__main__.watch_shutdown(server, seconds, exit_function, cancel)` runs as a daemon thread started before `server.run()`: it waits until `server.should_exit` is true (uvicorn sets it on SIGINT and SIGTERM), waits `SHUTDOWN_EXIT_SECONDS = 6.0` more, writes "DEIXIS did not finish shutting down in 6 s; exiting" to stderr and calls `os._exit(FORCED_EXIT_CODE)` (`1`). Nothing is cancelled and `api/app.py` is unchanged, so the state at a forced exit is the state after a SIGKILL, which F01 and I06 recover. Measured after the fix over two full runs: a held model call exits forced in 6.05 and 6.08 s (SIGTERM) and 6.12 and 6.09 s (SIGINT), the SIGINT extraction case forced in 6.13 and 6.08 s, the cases that were already graceful unchanged (3.17 to 3.43 s); the next start after the held-call case reports `recovered` runs 1 and steps 1 and the run `paused/backend_restarted`. **The price:** a model call in flight when the person presses Ctrl-C is not waited for and is sent again on resume, as after a crash (a separate session and a separate budget unit, see F01). The watchdog is never cancelled: the executor join it guards happens inside `asyncio.run`'s close, inside `server.run()`, so the thread is simply left running (the cancel event exists for the unit test).
2. `pdf._watch_memory`, shared by the pdf, OCR, JATS and arXiv source children, first arms `signal.alarm(CHILD_LIFETIME_SECONDS)` (100 s, above the longest parent clock of 90 s; `DEIXIS_CHILD_LIFETIME_SECONDS` in the child's environment overrides it with a positive integer; skipped where `signal.alarm` does not exist). SIGALRM keeps its default action, so it ends the child even inside a C call that holds the interpreter lock. After the fix an orphaned extraction child with a lifetime of 8 s was alive 5 s after it was first seen and gone 7.9 and 8.0 s after it (two runs).
3. `documents/pdf_files.py::store_pdf_file(papers_dir, sha256, data)` returns the existing `<sha>.pdf` only when its size and hash match, otherwise writes the bytes to a unique `.part` file in the same folder with `Path.write_bytes` and `os.replace`s it into place (the `.part` file is removed on an exception, a wrong file under the final name is replaced). It is used at the four write sites and nowhere else; uploads already wrote a `.partial` file and replaced it.

**Verification:** `PYTHONPATH=backend:. pytest tests/process -m process -n 0`: 21 passed in 102 s and 98 s on two runs (F01 x2, I06, F02 x3, F03 x3, F04 x6 (idle, held call, extraction; SIGTERM and SIGINT each), children x6 including the constant check). Fast tests added to the default suite: `tests/test_serve_shutdown.py` (4), `tests/test_child_lifetime.py` (2), `tests/test_pdf_files.py` (5). Full default `pytest`: 8,215 passed, 2 skipped (baseline 8,204 passed, 2 skipped at `4050a94`), 430 s under the load above. Before each fix the matching test was run on the old code and failed as described above (F04 held call and SIGINT extraction: no exit in 40 s; F02 download write: the three lines quoted; orphan extraction child: still alive when the 13 s limit ended).

**Limits:** One shape per scenario and single runs on one machine under heavy foreign load; the times are not distributions. SIGKILL is not power loss or a kernel panic: SQLite WAL durability and `fsync` ordering are not shown, and `store_pdf_file` does not `fsync`. The stand-ins are not the real `codex` (H10); a child that ignores stdin EOF is not stopped by anything in DEIXIS, and that case (`deaf`) is not tested (the production `embedding_runner.py` reads stdin the same way as the fake, which is only a reading of the code). The lifetime alarm bounds the orphan's time, not its memory: an orphaned extraction can still pass 1 GiB until it ends, and the extraction child of a forced exit lives until then or until its alarm. A JATS render leaves its temporary folder and a PDF request leaves its placements file when the parent is killed; the Marker runner and the Claude and Gemini CLI children are not covered. `scripts/p9/child_memory_probe.py` (default `--timeout 120`) is now ended by the alarm at 100 s, and `scripts/p9/gil_diagnosis.py` would be ended by it if it ran past 100 s. A torn `<sha>.pdf` already present in a library (made by the old code) is replaced by `store_pdf_file` when the same document is downloaded or added from Zotero again. The paths that do not repair it are an upload (`store_upload` only checks `exists()`) and a restore (`backup.restore_backup` copies straight into `papers/`, so a SIGKILL during a restore can leave a half file that the next restore refuses with "a different file already exists"; for H4). A cut download leaves its `tmp….part` file and nothing deletes it. `store_pdf_file` hashes an existing file in 1 MiB blocks on the event loop each time it is reused, and downloaded files are now created with mode 0600 (`mkstemp`; uploads already were). A process test file run without `-m process` selects nothing (it shows 0 tests), by design. A terminal's Ctrl-C reaches the whole foreground process group; the tests signal the server PID only. A forced exit also cuts a slow `equations.stop()` or `builtin.stop()` without finishing it. Payload files are written with `write_text`, rewritten on resume and not reused, and are not changed. Windows is unmeasured. The process tests are not in the default run. The watchdog starts only when uvicorn's Python-level signal handler has run, so an event loop stuck in a synchronous C call delays it. The graceful shutdown (3.2 to 3.4 s measured) and the forced-exit limit (6 s) leave a margin of about 2.6 s, so a heavily loaded machine can push a healthy slow shutdown into the forced path, and the idle and SIGTERM-extraction process tests assume graceful. Of the four write sites only the answer run's download path is exercised by a process test; the Zotero routes and the rendition path are covered by the unit test and code reading. Sol re-review is pending (usage limit until 3 October 2026 20:39).

**Context:** P9's plan (rows I01 to I05, I07; I08 manual) asks whether the commit works on a clean checkout, not only on the developer's machine, and whether the failures a new user can meet end with an understandable message. The plan also asked for the `PYTHON_KEYRING_BACKEND` isolation to be shown to work on the installed keyring before any harness reads settings.

The harness: exports `--rev` (default `HEAD`) with `git archive` into a work directory that must not exist and that it deletes itself (`--overlay-uncommitted` copies the working tree's changes over the export for a check before a commit and records every path); builds each child's environment from a named allowlist (real `HOME`, `PYTHON_KEYRING_BACKEND` null backend, data and Codex home inside the work dir, empty npm user config, a shim `PATH` of `uv`, `node`, `npm`, `npx` wrappers plus system directories so `claude`, `codex` and `gemini` are not found, proxy variables only for the install steps and a dead loopback proxy for `serve`); runs one launcher for every process that executes DEIXIS code, which refuses to start unless the data and Codex directories are inside the work dir, the keyring is the null backend, no host or port variable is passed and `cwd` is the export; starts every child in its own session and only signals processes it started. Order: `uv sync`, keyring check (two stages, exit 4 before anything else if it fails; the harness itself never reads or writes a secret), `npm ci`, I04 on the not-yet-built export, `npm run build`, I02 with I03b and I07 in one running instance, I03a, I05, a final process and port audit. Port 8871 by default; 8765, 8858 to 8864 and ports below 1024 are refused. Time limits are harness choices: 1800 s for `uv sync` and `npm ci`, 900 s for the build, 60 s to ready, 15 s to stop, 30 s for any other call.

One product change: `backend/deixis/__main__.py::data_dir_problem` and a check in `serve` after the port check. Measured on `89285fe`, a read-only data directory printed a Python traceback ending in `sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file`, exit code 3, the path only inside the traceback and no cause (a missing directory under a read-only parent: `PermissionError`, exit 3). Set DEIXIS_DATA_DIR to a folder you can write to.` (for a missing directory under a read-only parent: `it cannot be created because <parent> is not writable`) and returns 2, before the app is built, creating nothing. README: a paragraph on the clean-install check, an arm64 `python3`/`git`/Node 22 note, a model connection stated as needed for researches and not for installing or starting, a back-up-before-updating sentence, and the false historical sentence "Real model execution, evidence review and production persistence are not implemented." replaced (a reviewer model setting, `answer_review` and `report_review` exist; no route lets a user pick a candidate, snapshot or extra retrieval for a review).
