## D160 — P6 slice 5 X5: the report screen has a "Download LaTeX" button that saves the zip and reports the export note count in one toast; slice 5 is implemented, with no real-model measurement

**Status:** accepted (implemented; reviewer: Opus 5.5 high (Sol quota out), Sol re-review pending)
**Date:** 2026-10-02, P6 slice 5 batch X5. The number is a placeholder after D158 on `origin/main` (`af01d87`); the main session renumbers when it commits.

**Context:** D149 accepts the IEEEtran LaTeX export as five batches. X1 (D153) pinned the Markdown export, X2 (D151) built the text and math layer, X3 (D155) the assembler `to_latex`, X4 (D158) the `format=latex` route with the zip and the `X-Deixis-Export-Notes` header. X5 is the screen: section 8 and Q8 and Q15 of the [design note](product/p6-slice5-latex-export.md), section 11 "X5", and [the X5 prompt](product/p6-slice5-x5-prompt.md). The Codex usage limit ran out until 3 October 2026 20:39, so the Sonnet orchestrator subagent wrote the code and the prompt itself: there was no Sol plan review and no Sol code review. On the owner's instruction Claude Opus 5.5 at high effort reviewed the diff once (0 high; two medium findings, the decision number and this authorship line, and four low ones); the decision number, the authorship line, the LaTeX button's disabled and draft-name checks and a safe-integer guard on the notes header were fixed. Sol re-reviews it when the Codex limit lifts.

**Decision:** `api.reportLatex(id, reportId)` fetches `?format=latex` and returns the blob, the filename from `Content-Disposition` (same strict pattern as Markdown, fallback `report-latex.zip`) and the note count from `X-Deixis-Export-Notes` (digits only, else 0). `ReportView.tsx` gets a third toolbar button after "Download .md": icon `FileCode`, label "Download LaTeX" in `.report-export-label` (the existing 600 px rule hides the label, so only the icon and the `aria-label` remain), disabled by the same condition as the Markdown buttons and while an export runs. **Toast (Q8):** one toast per export. Zero notes: `success`, "LaTeX downloaded: a zip with the .tex and .bib files." One note, 2 to 20 notes, and more than 20 notes: `warning` with the count and "listed in a comment block at the top of the .tex file", and for more than 20 "The first 20 are listed". **Errors:** a 404, 409 or 422 raises `ApiError` before the blob is read, so no download starts and the server's `detail` shows in the existing `error` toast. All strings go through `t()` with Turkish entries. `docs/product/p6-report-design.md` section 12 item 5 gets a status line. No CSS, backend, fixture server, migration, contract, `methods/` or `skill_package_hash` change.

Own judgements: `FileCode` instead of `Download` so that the two download icons differ at narrow width; the shared `exportError(response)` and `saveBlob(blob, filename)` were extracted from the Markdown code and the Markdown path behaves as before; the disabled condition became one `exportBlocked` constant used by all three buttons; a missing or malformed notes header on a 200 counts as 0 notes and shows the success toast; the toast does not describe what the notes are, only how many and where they are; the notes-count test rewrites the real response header with `route.fetch()` and `route.fulfill` instead of adding a scripted fixture case, because the synthetic report produces few or no notes.

**Verification:** `apps/web/e2e/report.spec.ts` (the existing report test gained the LaTeX steps): the real export downloads a file named `report-<slug>-v1-latex.zip` that starts with `PK`, the real header is digits and the toast agrees with it; header values 3, 1 and 25 each give one download and exactly one `warning` toast with the matching text; a scripted 409 gives an `error` toast and no download. `npm run build` clean; `npm run lint` 17 warnings, the same as before; `npm run test:acceptance` against a fresh build 142 passed; full `pytest` 8,199 passed, 1 skipped; `git diff --check` clean. Screenshots read by the orchestrator, saved under `/tmp/x5-shots/` (not in the repository): toolbar at 1440 px (label shown) and 390 px (icon only, the toolbar wraps below the title, no horizontal scroll), keyboard focus ring on the button (light at 1440 px, dark at 1440 and 390 px; light at 390 px was not captured), Enter and Space each starting one download, the success toast, the warning toast with 25 notes at 390 px light, with 3 notes at 1440 px dark, and the Turkish warning toast at 390 px ("LaTeX, 25 dışa aktarma notuyla indirildi. İlk 20’si .tex dosyasının başındaki yorum bloğunda yazılı.").

**Limits:** Sol plan review and code review of X5 are pending because of the Codex usage limit; the main session runs them after 3 October 2026 20:39. Slice 5 as a whole has no real-model measurement: the export is a pure text transform and every test uses synthetic records and a scripted model; the compile test (D158) runs only where TeX is installed and was measured on TeX Live 2021 only. No real report, no other TeX distribution and no Overleaf compile was involved. The note count says how many export notes exist, not what they mean; the person reads them in the `.tex` comment block, and past 20 the block lists only the first 20. The `.tex` and `.bib` content inside the zip is pinned by the X4 backend tests, not by the browser test, which checks only the zip signature and the file name. Not tested: a screen reader reading the button name and the toasts, and browsers other than Chrome.

## D159 — P9 H0c: the 1 GiB memory limit on the arXiv source child did not work and now does; the OCR and JATS render children are stopped by their own in-child watchdog and are left as they are

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-02, P9 batch H0c
**Context:** D138 moved the memory watcher of PDF text extraction from a thread in the child to the parent, because a thread cannot run while PyMuPDF holds the interpreter lock, and left `ocr.py`, `jats.py` and `arxiv_source.py` (still on `pdf._watch_memory` in the child) as an open item. Before this entry D157 was the highest decision at `d65a7ea`.

**Decision:** Each child was run with its production argv at the production 1 GiB limit on scaled synthetic input (`scripts/p9/child_memory_probe.py`; macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Python 3.12.13, foreign load average 4 to 13; raw lines in the main checkout's ignored `.local/p9-h0c/runs.jsonl`; `tesseract` was installed, so OCR was measurable). Verdicts:
- **OCR (`ocr.py`): stopped.** One page whose MediaBox is N points square, rendered at 300 dpi. The in-child thread exits with code 3 ("memory limit exceeded") at 2000, 2500, 3000 (twice) and 4000 pt, in 0.4 to 1.8 s, with kernel peaks of 1073, 1636, 2329, 1856 and 2453 MiB: it stops, but late, up to about 2.4 times the limit, because the pixmap is one large allocation. 1000 and 1500 pt (318 and 635 MiB) finish; from about 5000 pt PyMuPDF refuses the page itself ("Overly large image", 55 MiB). Left unchanged.
- **JATS render (`jats.py`): stopped where the limit can be reached.** Under the 5 MB input cap, five shapes (plain text, one huge table cell, many cells, very many paragraphs, one unbreakable word) never reach 1 GiB (peaks 124 to 577 MiB) and end by the 200-page limit, a recursion error or the 60 s clock. A shape of 1.2 million `a-b` tokens (each becomes a `nowrap` span) crosses the limit and the in-child thread stops it (exit 3), three of three runs, in 7 to 8 s, kernel peaks 1474 to 1585 MiB (about 50% over). Left unchanged.
- **arXiv source (`arxiv_source.py`): NOT stopped.** A tiny archive with one numbered equation and a PDF that decodes to 200 MiB (`match()` reads it with PyMuPDF): three runs reached 1162, 1039 and 1176 MiB and ran until the probe killed them at 60 or 120 s (a fourth run, 672 MiB, ran under heavy load and is not offered as evidence); at a 100 MiB limit with 67 MiB decoded, 3 of 3 runs were not stopped (754 to 912 MiB). The 60 s child clock was the only stop.

`arxiv_source.run_child` now takes `max_memory` and, on macOS and Linux, runs a watcher task beside the stream readers that reads the child's resident size from outside (`pdf._resident_bytes`, every `pdf.WATCH_INTERVAL_SECONDS`) and kills the child over the limit (`failure = "memory_limit"`, the same string as before, so `read_source` still returns `content = "unreadable"`, `error = "memory_limit"`) or, after `pdf.WATCH_LOST_TURNS` unreadable turns in a row with the child alive, with `failure = "memory_watch_lost"`. A finished child is never reported as a lost watch. `read_source` passes `MAX_MEMORY_BYTES`; stdin feed, stdout cap, stderr tail and the 60 s clock are unchanged; the in-child thread stays as a second guard. After the fix, through the real `run_child` with a widened clock: 3 of 3 runs at the production limit with 200 MiB decoded stop with `memory_limit` after 31 to 32 s, kernel peak 1024 MiB; at a 100 MiB limit the child stops in 0.3 s at 102 MiB; a 5 MiB input finishes normally (312 MiB).

**Verification:** `tests/test_arxiv_source_archive.py` (four new tests: a child that holds the lock inside `PyDLL` calls past a 200 MiB limit is stopped fast; a child under the limit and a quick child end normally; an unreadable size gives `memory_watch_lost`; `read_source` passes the production limit; plus an opt-in test at the production limit, `DEIXIS_P9_PRODUCTION_THRESHOLD=1`, about 35 s, which passed); full pytest 8,126 passed, 2 skipped (the opt-in tests). Review: the gpt-6.1-sol reviewer was not available (usage limit until 3 October 2026), so no Sol plan or code review was run; the change was self-reviewed against the D138 watcher (finished child, failure precedence, task cancellation on timeout) and is flagged for review when quota returns.

**Limits:** One input shape per child. OCR and JATS are stopped late (about 2.4 and 1.5 times the limit on the shapes measured), not at the limit; the limit prevents neither allocation, and a parent watcher was not measured on them, so no claim is made that it would stop earlier. The JATS shapes that are slow in C (one unbreakable word or table cell) did not reach 1 GiB in 60 to 90 s, so the lock-holding hole was not shown there either way. The arXiv growth measured is about 30 MiB/s; a faster allocation can overshoot the 50 ms poll as in D138. The watcher reads current, not peak, resident size. Windows has no limit. With this entry all four extraction children have a measured stop at the production threshold on this machine; F09 is shown for PDF text extraction (D138) and the arXiv source child, and for OCR and JATS by their own in-child watchdog. Opus 5.5 high review follow-up (2 October 2026; Sol re-review pending): the first failure written now wins in `run_child`, so a memory stop is no longer overwritten by `timed_out` or `output_too_large`; only the `timed_out` case is pinned by a test, which fails on the old code. A `memory_watch_lost` or `timed_out` result is stored as `content='unreadable'` in `arxiv_sources` until the user resets it, although both depend on the machine rather than the source; this is accepted, unlike the PDF path, which records `EXTRACTION_FAILED` and retries automatically up to `MAX_ATTEMPTS`. Since D159's watcher (not this follow-up), a child that is above 1 GiB at one 50 ms poll is killed and stored `unreadable`, where before it could finish; how often real arXiv sources do that is not measured.

## D158 — P6 slice 5 X4: `format=latex` returns a zip of the `.tex` and the `.bib` read in one snapshot, with the note count in a header, and an optional compile test measures the committed goldens and wide tables when TeX is installed

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-02, P6 slice 5 batch X4

**Context:** D149 accepts the IEEEtran LaTeX export as five batches; X1 (D153) pinned the Markdown export, X2 (D151) built the text and math layer, X3 (D155) the pure assembler `to_latex` and 188 golden pairs. X4 connects it to the existing report export route and adds the optional compile test of section 9 of the note. The number is a placeholder: on 2 October 2026 `origin/main` (`f1a7db0`) stops at D156 (slice 4 E3), `../DEIXIS-e4` holds D156 too and no worktree holds a higher one; re-check when committing. Binding scope: the [design note](product/p6-slice5-latex-export.md) §7, §9, §10 Q9, Q13, Q15, Q19, Q20, §11 X4 and `docs/product/p6-slice5-x4-prompt.md`, which overrides the note where they differ.

**Decision:** New `workflow/report/latex_export.py` with `MEDIA_TYPE = "application/zip"`, `read_bib_sources(store, view)`, `build_zip(bundle)` and `export_latex(store, research_id, report_id) -> (zip bytes, filename, note count)`. **Single read moment (Q20):** inside one `queue._snapshot(store.conn)` it reads `report_view`, the unfinished-report gate, the research title, the corpus snapshot (`NotFound` means `None`, as for Markdown) and the bibliography rows; `to_latex` and the zip are built after the block from values already read. Nothing is written. A transaction the caller has already opened is neither restarted nor committed. **`read_bib_sources`:** one dict per `view["references"]` entry, in that order, from `source_versions` by `id` (title, authors from `authors_json`, year, venue, publication type, DOI, landing URL, version label, volume, issue, pages) and `arxiv_id` from `identifier_mappings` (`ORDER BY id LIMIT 1`, so the choice is deterministic); a version whose row is gone is not returned, which makes `to_latex` raise `RevisionConflict` because `report_view` already left that reference out and the claim citation no longer resolves. No title or author is copied from the view. **Zip (Q9):** exactly `<stem>.tex` then `<stem>.bib`, each the bundle text encoded as UTF-8 without change, written with a fixed timestamp (1980-01-01), `ZIP_DEFLATED`, `create_system` 3, `external_attr` 0o644, no archive comment and no directory entry, so the same bundle always gives the same bytes; an empty `.bib` is still written. IEEEtran class and style are not packaged. **Route (Q15):** the existing `GET /api/researches/{id}/reports/{report_id}/export` takes `format=markdown|latex` (default Markdown); for `latex` it answers 200 `application/zip`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<stem>-latex.zip"` (`report-<slug>-v<n>-latex.zip` or `report-<slug>-draft-latex.zip`) and `X-Deixis-Export-Notes: <total note count>` as ASCII digits; 404 for an unknown research, an unknown report or a report of another research; 409 for an unfinished report ("The report is still being written") and for every `RevisionConflict` from `to_latex` (missing source record, unresolved citation, key collision); 422 for an unknown format; error responses carry no `Content-Disposition`, no `X-Deixis-Export-Notes` and are not a zip. The Markdown branch is untouched: same bytes, content type and headers (no notes header). The `app.py` change is the import, the `Literal` and the `latex` branch. **Compile test (Q13, section 9):** `tests/test_report_latex_compile.py`. `missing_tex()` names missing programs (`xelatex`, `bibtex`, `pdftotext`, `kpsewhich`) and files found with `kpsewhich` (`IEEEtran.cls`, `IEEEtran.bst`, `fontspec`, `cite`, `url`, `booktabs`, `longtable`, `array`, `amsmath`, `amssymb`, `bm`, `xcolor`); the 19 tests that start TeX are skipped with that string when something is missing, and a missing dependency is never a failure. The pure scanners (`scan_log`, `bibtex_failures`, `bbl_keys`, `cite_keys_in_order`, `pdf_contains`, `pdf_regions` and the note-number checks) and their unit tests run on every machine. Each document is compiled with `xelatex -no-shell-escape -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error`, `bibtex`, then `xelatex` twice, in its own `tmp_path`; the final log is scanned for `Missing character`, `Overfull \vbox`, `Overfull \hbox`, `Float too large for page`, `LaTeX Error`, undefined or multiply defined citations, references and labels; the `.blg` for BibTeX errors; the `.bbl` key order must equal the first `\cite` order and the key set the `.bib` set. Group 1 compiles 13 committed goldens as pinned bytes (en and tr; draft with unvalidated sections, missing rows, edit note, review findings, equation labels, two versions of one key, reference order different from the `.bib` order, keyword cite, corpus, 7 columns); the 16 goldens with a known unbroken-value `Overfull \hbox`, the four class-B goldens and `hostile` are left out and pinned as left out. Group 2 builds 8, 13 and 20 column tables (2, 2 and 3 groups, plus a Turkish 13-column table) with 12 rows, unique end markers, cells of 400 and 500 characters, source cells of 200, 201 and 500, headings and option labels of 400, 401 and 500 (the thresholds are read on the final formatted text and a test asserts the sizes), mapped symbols only; expected strings come from the fixture data. The page text is split into table, notes and bibliography regions (a missing, duplicated or reversed heading fails); inline values must be in the table region, every moved value in the notes region under its expected integer note number (derived from the position rule, parsed as integers so note 1 cannot pass as note 11) with its end marker, the cell must point to that number (`pdftotext -raw` also checks header and row order), the caption numerals must all be `I`, at least one per group, and the bibliography copy of a source title is checked separately and never stands in for the table. Group 3 is the single explained exception: one unbroken 150-character token must produce `Overfull \hbox` and nothing else may fail (`allow_overfull_hbox=True` appears only there, an AST test checks it). A real-log negative control compiles a document with a missing glyph (U+6587) and an undefined citation and requires the scanner to report both.

Own judgements: `latex_export.py` is a new module, not an edit of `latex.py` as the note's file list says, because D155's import-boundary test forbids `zipfile`, `Store` and `views` imports in `latex.py` and that test is outside this batch's files; the compile test runs the four commands itself and does not need `latexmk`, so the `latexmk -xelatex` line in the `.tex` header is not exercised; `pdf_contains` applies NFKC and removes whitespace, hyphens and U+00AD on both sides; the Overfull allowance, the golden list and the exclusions are literals in the test; `arxiv_id` uses the lowest mapping id (the Zotero export takes an unordered `LIMIT 1`, so the two exports can differ for a version with two arXiv ids); the 16 unbroken-value goldens, not the 14 that D155 counts: the X3 log lists eight names in en and tr (D155's count was short by two).

**Verification:** `tests/test_report_latex_export.py` (11 tests: real finished report through the route, zip names, bytes and metadata, cite order and key set against the `.bib` and the view, header equals the comment block for zero and for a report whose `source_key` was emptied in the synthetic database, draft and cancelled and paused runs, 404 and 409 and 422 cases with one shared error assertion, a deleted `source_versions` row giving 409 and no write, a trace of exactly one `BEGIN` and one `COMMIT` around every `SELECT` and no write, spies proving the readers run inside the transaction and `to_latex` and the zip outside it, a caller's open transaction kept, `read_bib_sources` from stored rows, Markdown bytes equal to `export_markdown` and unchanged headers, AST import check) and `tests/test_report_latex_compile.py` (66 tests, 47 run without TeX, 19 start TeX). On this machine (XeTeX 3.141592653-2.6-0.999993, TeX Live 2021, IEEEtran.cls 1.8b and `IEEEtran.bst` found) all 19 TeX tests passed: 13 goldens, four wide tables, the unbroken-token exception (log held `Overfull \hbox`) and the negative control; the compile file took about 45 seconds serially. With TeX removed from `PATH` the 19 skipped with `Missing TeX dependencies: xelatex, bibtex, pdftotext, kpsewhich` and the other 47 passed. Full pytest with `PYTHONPATH=backend:.`: 8,194 passed, 1 skipped (a parallel run once failed `test_builtin_embedding_flow` on its 429 wait; the file passed alone, 51 passed). The four X4 files were also copied onto a clean export of `origin/main` `f1a7db0` (slice 4 E3 on top of X3) and the five related test files passed there (973 passed). `git diff --check` clean; no migration, `methods/`, contract, `apps/web`, `latex.py`, `export.py` or `skill_package_hash` change. gpt-6.1-sol high: plan review 1 round (0 high; 4 medium and 3 low folded in: PDF expectations from fixture data instead of the escaped `.tex`, Q19 sizes tied to the final formatted text and `source_key` empty for the long source cases, the golden list pinned with the 16 Overfull files excluded, zip bytes asserted against the bundle encodings, snapshot start state and open-transaction case, error-response headers on every error case, helper import sources), code review 2 rounds (round 1: 0 high, 1 medium, a PDF-wide search that a bibliography copy of a source title could satisfy and moved values whose note number was not checked; round 2: 0 high, 1 medium, a note number check that accepted 11 for 1; both folded in by Sol with region splitting, integer note parsing and negative controls). A third review round could not run because the Codex usage limit was reached; the round 2 fix was checked by the full test run and by reading it, not by Sol.

**Limits:** Synthetic reports only; the compile claim is measured for the 13 committed goldens, these wide-table fixtures and this one TeX distribution (TeX Live 2021) on one day, not for a user report, and on a machine without TeX the compile tests skip and nothing about compilation is measured there. The `latexmk` command in the `.tex` header is not run by any test. The notes header carries the total count; the `.tex` comment block lists at most 20 of them. `latex_export.py` reads one snapshot but the application is single-threaded on one connection, so no concurrent writer was observed; the snapshot test pins the placement of the reads, not a race. No real model, provider or user library was involved. No UI change (X5 adds the button: filename pattern `^report-.*-v1-latex\.zip$` for a first version, header `X-Deixis-Export-Notes`, codes 200, 404, 409, 422).

## D157 — P6 slice 4 E4: a scripted sequence runs edit, citation removal, cell change, source removal, check, restore, backup and purge in one order on synthetic rows; slice 4 is closed as implemented, the real-report measurement moves to P9

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-02, P6 slice 4 batch E4. The number was taken after D156 on main (`f1a7db0`); the slice 5 chat also writes decisions, so the main session renumbers on rebase.

**Context:** E1 (D148) made an edited report checkable by code, E2 (D150) made a claim able to lose citations reversibly, E3 (D156) put a screen on both. Each batch tested its own part; nothing ran the pieces in one order on one report. E2 and E3 also left four interactions to this batch: a removed cell citation opening no staleness mark and reopening one on restore, the removed-source case, the edit check going out of date after a link change, and purge and backup with citation sets and check records present. Binding scope: [the E4 prompt](product/p6-slice4-e4-prompt.md); [the slice 4 note](product/p6-slice4-editing-stale-measurement.md) §9 "E4 senaryo dizisi", §10, §12, §14.

**Decision:** `tests/test_report_edit_sequence.py` (new, the only code file) holds one deterministic sequence of 15 steps on the synthetic report fixture, a fake step input and no model, provider or network (an autouse guard makes any socket or `httpx` send raise): baseline; text edit (banned word on purpose); citation-only removal; a `cell_recheck` proposal that changes nothing until accepted, then accepted (the removed citation opens no mark, the retained citation of another claim does); source removal with a refused read-only `purge_sources`; the edit check and its no-write replay; a second edit that makes the check historical, then a new appended record; a link-only edit that makes the check historical again and leaves the zero-citation claim with explicit skipped rules; "Keep as is" then a new cell change (new key, old key refused); restore of the model's version and of an earlier revision (text and citation set together); restore of the source membership; original links byte-identical to the baseline; export numbering from the effective set; backup and restore of twelve report tables row for row with foreign keys intact; trash, restore and purge with a second research's rows (including an edit-check row and an acknowledgement row) exactly unchanged. Steps collect failures instead of stopping, so one broken step cannot hide the later ones, and the test fails with the list at the end. Three small tests: the sequence is model-free (run and step-input rows are only those the setup and the two proposals created, no adapter or network import in the file), two orders of citation removal and text edit end in the same normalised effective set, and a report-only source stays protected from `purge_sources` through removal and restore of its citation. The sequence found no defect in E1 to E3: no backend, web, contract, method or migration file changed, and `skill_package_hash` is unchanged (`sha256:8e1e4a8453a286ac9da8628dd095dd7796f3a49ae374d7930cb3ef06c546ee76`).

Observed values the test pins: the revision citation counts of the claim after the model restore and the step 3 restore are `[2, 1, 1, 0, 2]` and `[2, 1, 1, 0, 2, 1]` (oldest first, the model's original is not in the list); acknowledging a change leaves `edit_check.current` true; a link-only edit makes the check historical; after a zero-link edit the skipped rules are `phrase_frames`/`human_text` (III.1) and `derived_depth_not_checked`/`no_citation_depth` (abstract.1), the same on a second call; while a source is removed, restoring a membership makes `purge_sources` return three empty lists, so the refusal is only asserted while the membership is removed. Judgements: the removal case uses the fixture source because only sources in the frozen table snapshot produce `source_removed` marks and the report-only helper writes an asset row for a file that does not exist, which backup refuses; a recheck run must be marked completed before a source change, because an active run blocks `remove_sources` and `restore_sources`; a recheck cannot be accepted while its source membership is removed, so step 9 restores and removes the source around the second proposal.

**Evidence:** The E4 prompt had three plan-review rounds (gpt-6.1-sol high: 4, 2 and 1 high; the last folded in without a fourth round); the implementation was written by gpt-6.1-sol in the worktree; code review one round (0 high, 3 medium: the second research in step 15 had no edit-check or acknowledgement row, the abstract marks after the model restore were checked only for presence, and this entry did not exist yet; all three fixed). The new file passes three times in a row and once serially without random order. Full suite on the worktree: see the commit message. No model call, provider request or network use; the live service and data were not touched; nothing was committed or pushed.

**Limits (what slice 4 does and does not establish):** E1 to E4 show, on synthetic rows and a fake model, that the edit check reads the effective citation set, appends one record per input fingerprint, is current or historical as its inputs say, and changes no report state; that citation removal is reversible, never deletes a link, feeds staleness, numbering and export from one definition, and survives trash, backup and purge; that the screen renders the stored state and says "not checked" where the code did not check (D156, scripted fixture model). They do not show that the check finds real errors in a real report (no rate of hits or misses is known), that a removed citation was wrong, that the remaining citations support their sentences, how the screen reads on a real report, or how long any of it takes. No real-model report has been completed under today's code (D124, D126, D128), so the real-report measurement of the slice note §10 (R18 integrity of edits, R19 staleness correctness, R21 time and cost) is a P9 debt, listed in `docs/product/p9-hardening-plan.md` next to the slice 2 and slice 3 debts; R20 (identity stability) is not measurable until a rewrite exists. The sequence does not cover PDF re-extraction or passage change (`not_checked: ["passages"]`), numbers written as words, concurrent writers, the API layer, or a Turkish export.

**Deferred from D147 and still open:** "Publish" and any new `report_version` after an edit, section rewrite proposals with `report_section_revisions` and `claim_match`, stable claim and gap identity with cross-version candidate matching (D143's "slice 4" item, withdrawn from slice 4 and to return only if a rewrite is built), `scope_statement` editing, passage and column staleness extensions, chain-link and candidate staleness, a review of an edit, bulk rewrite, and sentence-level edits inside a claim. The check is never run automatically, and the model's `report_version` and the D118 review still describe the model's base version.

## D156 — P6 slice 4 E3: the report screen shows the edit check and citation removal as stored, and says "not checked" where the code did not check

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-02, P6 slice 4 batch E3 (interface). The number was taken after D154 on main; the main session renumbers on rebase.

**Context:** E1 (D148) made an edited report checkable by code and E2 (D150) made a claim able to lose citations reversibly, both with an API and no screen. The report sheet still said "edited text was not checked again" whatever the stored check said, the edit form could change text only and its toast said the citations were kept, the history showed no citation counts, and a claim that lost every citation read like an uncited sentence. Binding scope: [the E3 prompt](product/p6-slice4-e3-prompt.md); [the slice 4 note](product/p6-slice4-editing-stale-measurement.md) §2, §4, §8, §9 and §14.

**Decision:** The screen renders recorded state only. A check panel in the report head (shown whenever `has_human_edits`, so a draft report with edits has it too) carries the export's three sentences (no check, current, out of date) with a text state label, a "Check edited text" or "Check again" button that is disabled with a visible reason when the run is unfinished or the stored check is current, the result list (severity word and icon, section, rule, stored detail), disclosures for the rules that ran and the rules that did not run for some claims, and one "Not checked" line. The edit form takes per-link citation choices keyed by `link_id` (two links to one source share a reference number), sends `text` only when it changed and `link_ids` only when a box is unchecked, and refuses a save, from the button, the form and Ctrl/Cmd+Enter alike, when nothing changed. History shows each entry's citation count ("Citations: from 2 to 1") and offers Restore only when it would change something (`changes_current`; for the model entry the screen compares text and `removed_links` itself). A claim whose citations were all removed by hand reads "(no direct citation)" in the report and, in the evidence view, "No direct citation.", a type label saying the type is the model's, and a list of the removed citations; a never-cited claim gets only "No direct citation." in the evidence view. A claim resting on an edited claim says so (`edited_basis`), with "This sentence was not changed." only when its own text equals the model's. Three sentences of the sheet follow the export on purpose: the review note says the review covers the model's base version, the anchor sentence handles removed citations and the zero-link case, and the Edit button's disabled reason is visible text. Report state ordering: reads take tickets and apply only if newer than the last applied, a mutation response is stamped on completion, and every mutation outcome other than a 422 form error is followed by one confirming read, so a stale read or another tab's later write cannot leave the screen behind. Focus moves to the claim's Edit button before the form is removed (the modal otherwise pulls it to the sheet). `ReportStore.acknowledge_changes` now finds a trashed research before it writes. The fixture marker `[report-two-citations]` gives each scripted cell claim a second, same-source passage citation.

**Verification:** `apps/web/e2e/report-edit.spec.ts` (16 tests, scripted model and mocked providers): check flow including out-of-date and an unchanged re-check returning the same record, per-link removal and restore with request-body assertions, removal of every citation, a returned citation read as kept, locked fields during a save, two-tab conflicts, the four ordering races, no GET loop, an isolated 422, mocked views for every fallback, Turkish through the header switch, forbidden-word scan of interface text (stored text excluded), keyboard and focus return, 390 px overflow of panel, form and history. One pytest for the `acknowledge_changes` guard. Screens were looked at in light and dark at 1440 and 390 px. Full runs on the worktree: pytest 7,278 passed, 1 skipped (baseline 7,277); Playwright 142 passed (126 before); lint 17 warnings (baseline 17); `skill_package_hash` unchanged. gpt-6.1-sol high plan review 3 rounds (2, 1 and 0 high), code review 2 rounds (0 and 0 high).

**Limits:** Scripted model and synthetic data only: nothing here shows how a real report reads or how often the edit check is right. The check reads a subset of the assembly rules and says nothing about whether a citation supports its sentence; "Current" means the inputs match, not that the text is correct. Only four rule codes have plain-word labels; the rest print their code. The screen's plural wording ("1 error") differs from the export's pinned "1 errors" on purpose. A removed citation can be brought back only through History, with the text of that version. The export buttons and unopenable citation chips still explain themselves through `title` alone. The check is never run automatically.

## D155 — P6 slice 5 X3: `to_latex` assembles the IEEEtran report (`.tex` and `.bib`) from one recorded read model, `to_bibtex` gains `keys` and `latex_report`, and 188 golden pairs pin the output; no route calls it yet

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-02, P6 slice 5 batch X3

**Context:** D149 accepts the IEEEtran LaTeX export of the report as five batches; X1 (D153) pinned the Markdown export and moved the shared bilingual text to `export_text.py`, X2 (D151) built the text and math layer. X3 writes the assembler on top of both: a pure function with no model call, no network, no database and no TeX at run time. The number is a placeholder: on 2 October 2026 `origin/main` (`dc4b19c`) stops at D153, `../DEIXIS-k4` holds D152 (slice 3 K4, uncommitted) and no other worktree holds a higher one; re-check when committing. Binding scope: the [design note](product/p6-slice5-latex-export.md) §3-§9, §10 Q2, Q3, Q4, Q6, Q7, Q10, Q11, Q18, Q19, Q21, Q22, §11 X3 and `docs/product/p6-slice5-x3-prompt.md`, which overrides the note where they differ.

**Decision:** New `workflow/report/latex.py`. Public surface for X4: `to_latex(view, *, title, corpus, bib_sources) -> LatexBundle(stem, tex, bib, notes)` (`note_count` is `len(notes)`; `stem` is `export_text.report_stem`), module constants `MAX_DATA_COLUMNS = 7`, `SOURCE_COLUMN_WIDTH = "1.0in"`, long-value thresholds 400 (cell), 400 (heading), 200 (source). `bib_sources` is one dict per source version with `source_version_id` and the fields `to_bibtex` reads. `to_latex` never mutates the view and imports no `export.py`, `views.py`, TeX, network or database code (an AST test checks the import lines; `bibliography` is imported lazily). **Document:** export-notes comment block (every line `%`, whole line at most 200 characters, at most 20 notes then `% and N more`), `PREAMBLE`, Turkish `\renewcommand` lines after `\begin{document}`, `\title`, identity paragraph, then the unchecked blocks in the note's order (draft line, missing rows, edit note, evidence-changed sentence), the `abstract` and `IEEEkeywords` environments, `\section*{I. ...}` to IX with the Markdown order and empty-section rules, Table I where Markdown puts it, `\section*{Report notes}` (corpus footer, anchor and review note, model findings, Long table values, the traceability sentence of Q21), then `\bibliographystyle`/`\bibliography{<stem>}`; those two lines are left out, with the note `The report holds no citations; the bibliography commands were left out.`, when the document holds no `\cite` (an empty `thebibliography` stops LaTeX, found by compiling). Every stored value reaches the file through one of three escape callables: `fixed` (`escape_text`, for PLAIN words), `line` (`convert_text(cell=True)`, stripped, for every one-line stored value and every `esc` argument of the PIECEWISE functions) and `body` (`convert_text(cell=False)` with labels, for claims and II/VIII `draft.text`). X1's open question has the answer no: no `export_text` signature changed; the long-value threshold reads the final formatted raw text by calling `cell_text`/`source_cell` with an identity `esc`; a test proves the template words of the PIECEWISE functions hold no TeX special and no unmapped character, so their unescaped result is safe. **Claims:** fragments of a paragraph join with a space, or with one LF around a display (`\end{..}`/`\begin{..}` boundary, spaces before the brace allowed); `\cite{k1,k2}` in first-appearance order, duplicates dropped; keywords use `line`, are joined with `, ` and take no `\eqref`. **Equation labels (Q6):** one pass over abstract and I-IX decides per `equation_ref` the first labelable display as target (`eq:EQ<k>`, rank by first appearance, above 999 no target); other labelable displays are `equation*`; a later claim without its own display gets ` \eqref{..}`; one note each, with a count, for refs without a target and for claims that cite a ref and hold a display of their own (the code does not compare the expressions). **Table I:** `\onecolumn`, groups of at most 7 data columns each as `{\scriptsize \begin{longtable}...}`, the source column and all rows in every group, `\addtocounter{table}{-1}` before every group after the first (all captions say TABLE I), `\twocolumn`; a note when there is more than one group; the first cell of every row and the text of every `\item` get a `{}` prefix when they start with `[` or `*` (otherwise `\\`/`\item` read the bracket as an option). Values above the thresholds (strictly greater, on the final formatted text) become `see note k` / `k numaralı nota bakın`, numbered by position (headings, then rows with source then cells), and the full text goes to a `Long table values` list with its position and source label; no value is lost; a count note. **Cite keys (Q3):** `source_key` when it fully matches `[A-Za-z0-9]+`, later holders of the same key `-2`, `-3`, a fallback `ref<n>` with a note otherwise; any case-insensitive collision, a reference number that is not a positive `int`, a claim link whose `(ref_number, source_version_id)` pair does not resolve to one reference, a table row number that does not match its version, a missing or duplicate `bib_sources` row, a non-`int` `edited_after_version`, `errors` or `warnings`, or an invalid stem raises `RevisionConflict`; notes for a reference order that differs from first citation and for an uncited reference. **`bibliography.py`:** `bibtex_with_notes(sources, keys=None, *, latex_report=False, unmapped=None) -> (text, notes)` and `to_bibtex(sources, keys=None, *, latex_report=False) -> str`. With no `keys` and `latex_report=False` the D16 output is unchanged byte for byte. Given `keys` must match the source count, be unique ignoring case and fully match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]*` in both modes. `latex_report=True`: double-braced title (M4), every text field through `escape_text` (symbol table in the same pass), `{` and `}` written `\textbraceleft{}`/`\textbraceright{}` because BibTeX counts the braces of `\{` too, a `year` that is not an `int` dropped before the automatic key is made, and `doi`, `url`, `eprint` omitted with a note when the original value holds a backslash or a character of category Cc, Cf, Zl, Zp, Cs, Co or Cn. Notes are one-line ASCII (non-ASCII becomes `?`), de-duplicated, ordered key and reference notes, equation notes, notes collected while writing, bibliography notes, the one unmapped-character note; `LatexBundle.notes` is the full list.

Own judgements: the `line`/`body`/`fixed` split, with the X2 notes saying "table cell" also outside tables; the unvalidated-section note of the two environments written as `\noindent\textit{<heading>: <note>}` before them; unchecked blocks after the title, identity first (Markdown puts the draft line first); the middle dot through the symbol table (`\ensuremath{\cdot}`); `\item[k.]` for long values; the key regex and the `-n` rule; the `skipped_rules` item writes the stored `claim_key` value as Markdown does (D148 gives the user no other handle); the case classes (normal, noted exception, expected error) that narrow the note's "invariants over every case"; the source column width **1.0in instead of the note's 0.6in**, because the hand compile showed a 17-character key (`floudas2009global`) overflowing 0.6in by 18pt (4pt for a nine-capital word) and 0 overfull boxes at 0.9in and 1.0in; no bibliography commands without a citation.

**Verification:** `tests/test_report_latex.py` (532 tests) and the appended tests of `tests/test_bibliography.py`; 188 golden `.tex`/`.bib` pairs under `tests/fixtures/report_latex/` (en and tr, the Q18 groups and the Q22 sixth group through a `COVERAGE` registry with one predicate per branch, math classes, equation scenarios including 999 and 1,000 refs, reference and key cases, table cases for 0, 1, 7, 8, 13 and 20 columns and every threshold boundary, two kitchen-sink views, a hostile view) written by reading each output against the intended text, and 24 expected-error cases without a golden; independent invariants (no internal id, cite order, cite/bib agreement, labels defined and unique, balanced environments, no empty list, comment header only `%`, no mutation, determinism); a hostile view whose stored fields hold `\input`, `\def`, `\begin {document}`, `^^M`, `%`, braces and a newline then `\input` produced no TeX control word outside `\textbackslash{}`, exactly one `\begin{document}` and one `.bib` entry per reference. The default `to_bibtex` output matched the unmodified module on 300 seeded source lists plus a 30-source and a 40-source suffix series (`cmp` of the before and after dumps exit 0) and a full literal written before the edit. Full pytest after the last change: 7,896 passed, 1 skipped, no failure (7,271 passed before X3). **Hand compile (temporary; the permanent compile test is X4):** all 188 golden `.tex` files with their `.bib` compiled with XeTeX 3.141592653-2.6-0.999993 (TeX Live 2021, IEEEtran.cls 1.8b and IEEEtran.bst 1.14 found), `xelatex -no-shell-escape`, `bibtex`, then two more `xelatex` runs. 184 compiled without a LaTeX error; the four with an error are the two class-B kitchen-sink and math-class cases in both languages (`\R` is undefined, as the note says) and, before the fix above, the two no-citation cases in both languages (now compile). Zero `Overfull \vbox`, zero `Float too large`, no undefined citation or label; the only font message is the known IEEEtran `Font shape TU/ptm undefined`. `Overfull \hbox` appeared in 14 files, all from fixtures holding one 400-character token or an unbroken plain-text array (`table_cell_400/401`, `table_heading_400/401`, `table_source_200/201`, `table_parenthetical`, `table_math`), which the note expects (§5, "Kalan risk"). Tables of 8, 13 and 20 columns compile to 2, 2 and 3 groups with every caption "TABLE I" and the header row on each; Turkish documents print Özet, Dizin Terimleri and Kaynaklar; the hostile document prints its payload as inert text; one BibTeX error in the hostile document is the stored author name ending in a comma (`has a comma at the end`), not an injection. gpt-6.1-sol high: plan review 3 rounds (round 1: 4 high, bibliography `year` written raw, a key-suffix rule that contradicted the collision error, invariants that the expected-error cases cannot meet, the `claim_key` value against the no-internal-id rule; round 2: 3 high, escaped braces unbalancing a BibTeX field, `year` reaching the automatic key, a link number accepted without its source version; round 3: 1 high, given keys checked only in `latex_report` mode; every finding folded in, no fourth round by the limit), code review 1 round (0 high, no finding; verdict hazir) after the orchestrator's two fixes from the compile run.

**Limits:** Synthetic views only; no real report, no model and no provider were involved, and no route calls `to_latex` (X4). The hand compile shows these 188 files compile on one TeX distribution on one day; it does not show that a user report compiles, and no test requires TeX. D59 keys longer than about 21 characters still overflow the 1.0in source column, and a word wider than a data column (about 14 lowercase letters at 7 columns) overflows into its neighbour; both are readability limits, not data loss. The scan behind `convert_text` bounds what saved text can make TeX do; it checks neither argument counts nor meaning, so `\R` and `\frac{x}` style spans may stop compilation. The X2 notes say "table cell" for display math written inline in any one-line context. A table caption ends with a full stop before the group suffix (`... 8 columns). (columns 1-7 of 8)`). The stored author name ending in a comma makes BibTeX print an error (the entry is still written). The two class-B goldens that contain an unmapped character (U+6587) stopped at the undefined command before it, so the "Missing character" log line was not exercised by this run; a minimal IEEEtran document with the same character does log it. `Long table values` and the Report notes are English or Turkish text written by this module and the number of notes shown is capped at 20 in the comment block only. No migration, model call, contract schema, `methods/`, route or `skill_package_hash` change; no `apps/web` change.

**Evidence** (gpt-5.6-luna through the Codex connection, one attempt per case, results in the ignored `.local/p6-slice3-k5/results.json`; 4,953 to 5,683 input and 273 to 774 output tokens per case, 41,716 tokens in total; all seven completed, were structurally valid, needed no repair, and every behavior screen read true):

| Case | Expected | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| CB01 same result, other terminology | `explicit_support`, aligned | `related`; all three element cells `explicit_support`, `aligned`, one quote each; `states_whole_claim` true with the sentence as whole-claim evidence (the text does state all three) |
| CB02 wall pigments | `unrelated`, all `no_match_in_supplied_text`, whole claim false | exactly that; summary says the passages concern pigments, no novelty or absence claim |
| CB03 buffering alone | one supported element with a quote, rest no match or uncertain, whole false | `related`; buffering cell `explicit_support` with `unclear` alignment and a quote; the other two cells `no_match_in_supplied_text`; whole false |
| CB04 biological analogy | no `explicit_support`, limits described | `unrelated`; all cells `no_match_in_supplied_text`; summary says the text is about an animal storing food |
| CB05 opposite result, unbounded bursts | `different_conditions`, no plain contradiction | `related`; buffering `explicit_support`/`different_conditions`, bounded arrivals no match, delay `partial_match`/`different_conditions`; notes name "unbounded rather than bounded" and "increased rather than reduced delay"; whole false |
| CB06 elements stated separately | whole claim false, empty whole-claim evidence | `related`; three cells `explicit_support` (alignment unclear, aligned, unclear), each with its own passage quote; whole false; summary says the passages do not state that buffering reduces delay under bounded arrivals |
| CB07 owner sentence, empty basis | one formulation, no explanation, empty id lists, owner framing | claim restated with three elements (mechanism, condition, outcome), `nearest_simple_explanation` null, empty `source_ids` and `passage_ids`; rationale says the elements restate the owner's sentence and no literature explanation is derived |

End-to-end development trial (isolated copy of `library.sqlite` at `/tmp/k5-data`, port 8873, Codex home of the live connection; the live service and library untouched; research `res_IXBsnzhYZsKByEdTpSJo`, wireless sensor networks, which has no report and so no VI gap rows, hence an `owner_text` candidate): the owner sentence was "choosing the packet size of each link from its measured bit error rate increases network lifetime compared with one fixed packet size optimised for the whole network". Decomposition: 1 model call, 5,725 tokens, 13 s, four elements (two mechanism, one parameter, one outcome), `nearest_simple_explanation` null. Kill-search (plan: 5 providers, 6 queries, 20 records, keep 8, ceiling 54 model calls and 54 provider requests): 6 model calls (1 query, 5 assessments), 38,238 tokens, 18 provider requests, 101 s, completed. The model wrote one block pair; the compiled query was the same for all providers: ("wireless sensor networks" OR "link bit error rate") AND ("adaptive packet size" OR "network lifetime"). Five queries succeeded (openalex 20 records, semantic_scholar 20, arxiv 20, biorxiv 0, pubmed 20), 80 found, 12 duplicates, 8 kept, 60 cut by rank. Of the 8 kept, 5 had an abstract and were assessed, 3 were `metadata_only` and got `insufficient_access`. All 5 assessed works were `unrelated`, all 20 cells `no_match_in_supplied_text`, no evidence; the notes say the abstracts concern clustering, UAV data collection, tree routing and lifetime surveys, not per-link packet size, measured bit error rate or a fixed-size baseline. Derived status: `undecided`, reason `insufficient_access`. None of the 68 stored hits has "packet", "frame size" or "payload" in its title.

**Limits:** One attempt per case and one claim: no rate, no generalisation. The seven cases are easy by construction and the screens are heuristics (CB07's null-explanation and empty-id screens are also enforced by the validator). The trial shows the whole path runs with a real model and real providers; it does not show that the search finds prior art. Read honestly: the compiled query joins the terms inside each block with OR, so any lifetime paper matches the second block, and the search returned generic lifetime and clustering papers and no work on packet size at all; the 60 works cut by rank were not read, so whether work on the claim was among them is not known. This is a query-shape and recall finding, not fixed here (a change would alter `compile_block_queries` or the method file, which K6 and the H9 rule want frozen); it is recorded as open, together with the 3 of 8 kept works without an abstract that made the status `undecided`. Quotes were located, no semantic support was verified. The research and the sentence are burned for K6. No generated-sentence quality, validation-plan quality or speed claim is made.

**K6 moved to P9 (debt):** the frozen independent measurement of section 13 (S1 to S5, six fresh claims, one run, `p6-slice3-expectations.md` frozen and reviewed before the run) is not part of slice 3 and is listed in `docs/product/p9-hardening-plan.md` next to the slice 2 lineage debt. Until it runs, nothing says how often kill-search finds the nearest work, how often it wrongly reports `open` or `closed`, or how it behaves on budget.

**Deferred from D143 and still open:** chain-end candidates, forward-citation check, report write-back of `kill_search_status` and the VII takeover (needs `workflow/report/*`), stable gaps across report versions (slice 4), PDF acquisition and full-text assessment, adding found works to the corpus, alternative claim formulations, candidate file export, concurrent assessment calls.
