## D151 — P6 slice 5 X2: the pure LaTeX text and math conversion (escape, symbol table, closed math scan, fixed preamble, TeX-derived names file) is in place; nothing calls it yet

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-02, P6 slice 5 batch X2

**Context:** D149 accepts the IEEEtran LaTeX export of the report as five batches. X2 builds only the text and math layer that X3 (`to_latex`) will call; it has no model call, no network, no database and no TeX at run time, and `contracts.py`, `export.py`, migrations, contracts and `methods/` are untouched. The number is a placeholder: on 2 October 2026 `origin/main` (`e718670`) stops at D149, `../DEIXIS-e1` holds D148 (slice 4 E1, uncommitted) and `../DEIXIS-k4` stops at D146; re-check when committing. Binding scope: the [design note](product/p6-slice5-latex-export.md) §3, §4, §5 (cell subset), §9, §11 X2 and the batch prompt `docs/product/p6-slice5-x2-prompt.md`, which overrides the note where they differ (the note's two separate stacks became one, see below).

**Decision:** Four new files under `workflow/report/`: `latex_preamble.py` (`PREAMBLE`, `PREAMBLE_SHA256`: IEEEtran `journal`, `fontspec amsmath amssymb bm xcolor cite url booktabs longtable array`, no `hyperref`, no `tabularx`), `latex_text.py`, `latex_math.py` and `latex_names.json`, plus `scripts/latex_export_names.py`. Public surface for X3: `escape_text(text, unmapped=None)`, `symbol_text`, `symbol_math`, `is_unmapped`, `SYMBOLS` (84 entries), `Unmapped` (`add`, `count`, `note()`); `split_text(text)`, `classify(span, *, cell=False) -> MathSpan(source, kind, labelable, body, class_b, notes)`, `render(m, label=None, unmapped=None)`, `convert_text(text, *, cell=False, label_for=None, unmapped=None) -> (text, notes)`, `closed_scan(span) -> ScanResult`, `command_status(name)`, `COMMAND_DENY`. Plain text escapes the ten TeX specials, treats `\$` by the same odd-run parity as `contracts._is_escaped`, collapses whitespace without stripping, turns `"` into ``` `` ``` or `''` and U+00A0 into `~`, removes control characters and reports them. Math: `contracts._math_spans` spans are located by a private positional twin (checked against `_math_spans` on every split, otherwise the text stays plain), then a closed scan runs over the saved input before anything is rewritten: **one stack** of brace, `\begin{env}` and `\left` frames (iterative, depth at most 64, any exception gives class A), every control word must be a KaTeX command outside the 35-name `COMMAND_DENY` list, every control symbol must be a KaTeX symbol other than `\(`, `\)`, `\]`, environments come from an explicit allowed set, `&` and `\\` follow the note's context rules with the top-of-stack environment test, `\tag`/`\nonumber`/`\notag` only at top level of a display, text arguments allow only the listed escapes, and `^^`, unescaped `%`, `#` and `$`, blank lines, Unicode categories Cc (except TAB, LF), Cf, Zl, Zp, Cs, Co, Cn and non-ASCII Zs, a Unicode letter or mark glued to a saved control word (XeTeX reads it as part of the name) and a `\tag` or text command not followed by `{` are class A. Class A is written as the escaped original span including its `$` delimiters, with a note. Stage 2 rewrites `\lt`, `\gt` and Unicode symbols on tokens (a space is added after a bare command when a letter or mark follows; `°` is written `{^{\circ}}` so `^°` cannot become `^^`) and rejects a result containing `^^`, `%` or `#`; stage 3 classifies as inline, display with one E environment, `\tag`, `aligned`, `gathered` or plain display, and the table-cell subset (no environment, no `\\`, no number with a TeX unit, no listed height constructor) turns the rest into class A and writes a display that is plain inline. Class B (KaTeX knows the name, the preamble does not) is written unchanged with a note. `render(label=)` accepts only `eq:EQ[0-9]{1,3}` and raises otherwise; `convert_text` removes spaces next to a display's line breaks and merges consecutive breaks so a claim never gets a blank line. `latex_names.json` was generated once on this machine by the script (`xelatex -no-shell-escape`, `\ifdefined` for commands, `\@ifundefined{name}`/`{endname}` for environments): XeTeX 3.141592653-2.6-0.999993 (TeX Live 2021), KaTeX 0.16.47, 239 undefined commands, 11 undefined environments, 11 package and class file lines, the preamble hash and the `katex_commands.json` hash; a pure test fails on a stale file and the loader raises, never returns an empty list.

Judgements: the prompt's single stack replaces the note's separate left/right stack, because it makes crossed nesting class A without extra rules; the deny list adds `noexpand bgroup egroup char message errmessage show hbox fbox raisebox color textcolor colorbox fcolorbox` to the note's floor; class A keeps the `$` delimiters; label strings are validated at the render boundary although X3 builds them; `\nonumber`/`\tag` inside an `align` stay class A as the note says; the label-target and `equation_ref` scenario tests of note §9 move to X3, X2 tests `kind`, `labelable` and `render(label=)` only.

**Verification:** `tests/test_report_latex_text.py` and `tests/test_report_latex_math.py` (1,914 tests collected: escape, parity, symbol table, preamble hash, import-line check, every deny-list member, every spacing and nesting counter-example from the note including `\begin {document}`, 976-command allowed/denied split, names-file hash and staleness, a seeded no-leak property test over 3,000 generated texts with an output checker written independently of the scanner and of `render`, and fixed regressions for each review finding); no test needs TeX or the network. Spot check by hand: one document with the preamble, escaped prose, all five display kinds, a numbered label and converted `\text{≥}` compiled with xelatex (exit 0, no missing character or overfull box; IEEEtran font substitution warnings only), repeated after the review fixes with `°`, `^°`, a rejected `$$x$y$$` and a numbered label (exit 0, no error). Full pytest: 6,767 passed and 1 skipped, no failure. gpt-6.1-sol high: plan review 3 rounds (0, 0 and 0 high; eight, four and one lower findings folded in), code review 2 rounds (3 high in round 1: a symbol rewrite that built `^^`, an ASCII-only control-word scan that XeTeX reads differently, a bare `$` inside a display body; 0 high in round 2, one medium about the test taking its expected body from production code, fixed).

**Limits:** Synthetic strings only; no report, no model and no provider were involved. The scan bounds what saved text can make TeX do, it is not a TeX sandbox, and it checks neither argument counts (`\frac{x}`) nor scientific meaning, so a passing span may still fail to compile; class B and the names file are a compatibility hint measured on one TeX distribution. The symbol table is a closed list of 84 characters; characters outside it and outside the safe ranges are written unchanged and only reported, which is not font coverage. The table-cell subset limits known height constructors only. Nothing calls these modules until X3, so no export exists yet.

## D150 — P6 slice 4 E2: a claim can lose citations reversibly, and every reader takes one recorded effective citation set

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-02, P6 slice 4 batch E2

**Context:** D112 lets the owner edit a claim's text but leaves every citation link in place, so a wrong citation cannot be corrected. D147 accepts citation removal with the complete effective set recorded per revision, one effective-link definition for every reader, and closing the gap that report citations were invisible to `research_cites_asset` and `asset_impact`. Binding scope: [the E2 prompt](product/p6-slice4-e2-prompt.md); [the slice 4 note](product/p6-slice4-editing-stale-measurement.md) §2 to §9 and §14. The checkout was `def7c26` (D148 on top); migration 0061 was the highest before writing 0062 and D149 the highest decision, so a rebase may renumber this entry and the migration.

**Decision:** Migration `0062_report_claim_links.sql` adds `link_count` (NULL = legacy revision, all original links effective; N = size of the recorded set, 0 allowed) and `request_hash` to `report_claim_revisions`, and the append-only `report_claim_revision_links` (`WITHOUT ROWID`). A sealing trigger refuses a late insert, an insert for a legacy or full revision and another claim's link; conflicting-insert triggers close `INSERT OR REPLACE` by `id`, idempotency key and explicit `rowid`; delete needs the owning research's purge authorization. `ReportStore.edit_claim` takes `link_ids`: an edit may change text, citations or both, a restore brings back text and set together (`"model"` and legacy revisions mean all original links), a request that changes neither is refused, a link must be an original link of the claim, and a trashed research is not found. Idempotency is bound to a `request_hash` of the request content; a replay of equal content returns the stored revision, different content under the key is a conflict, and a revision with a NULL hash replays as in D112. `ReportStore.effective_links` is the one SQL definition (row shape and order kept for slice 5); `removed_links` and `original_links` are derived beside it. Section-level staleness (`evidence_changes`), the view's evidence, numbering, references and the Markdown export read only effective links; report-level snapshot counts are unchanged and no link row is ever deleted. The view adds `link_id`, `original_evidence_count`, `removed_links`, `evidence_basis`, `support_type_note`, `edited_basis`, and per revision `link_count`, `link_ids`, `changes_current`. The export replaces the anchors-located sentence with an explicit one when removals leave no link at all and adds a count sentence for fully de-cited claims; exports without removals stay byte-identical. `Store.purge_research` deletes the new table first; `research_cites_asset` and `asset_impact` (new `report_citations`) count report passage links, effective and removed.

**Evidence:** The prompt had three plan-review rounds (3, 2 and 0 high). Tests (synthetic, no model) cover migration of empty and populated libraries, the sealing and REPLACE escapes, rollback, citation-only and combined edits, restore of text and set, legacy and content-bound idempotency, the trashed-research refusal, an AST allowlist and a runtime SQL guard for every read of `report_citation_links` and `report_claim_revision_links`, staleness through removal and restore (including a removed source, `body_ref`, `gap_ref` and independent gap basis cells), numbering and references, bilingual exports with golden comparison for no removals, real removal revisions through the E1 check, report-only asset protection, purge, trash and a backup round-trip. Full suite: see the commit message. `skill_package_hash` before and after: `sha256:8e1e4a8453a286ac9da8628dd095dd7796f3a49ae374d7930cb3ef06c546ee76`. Code review: one round, 0 high; the two findings (citation-only edit must keep the stored text verbatim, with a test) were fixed by the orchestrator.

**Limits:** Removing a citation reduces evidence and says nothing about whether a remaining citation supports its sentence. A citation-only revision counts as an edited claim for the E1 check, including its phrase-frame skip. `support_type_note` and the export count cover claims whose citations were all removed by hand, not claims that never had links. `report_citations` counts passage links only; cell links are covered by the existing cell evidence counts. `acknowledge_changes` still writes before the view reports a trashed research as not found (not changed here). The D118 review and the model's `report_version` still describe the model's base version. No screen shows any of this (E3), the scripted sequence is E4, and nothing was measured on a real report. No model/provider call; the live service and data were not touched; nothing was committed or pushed.

## D149 — P6 slice 5 (IEEEtran LaTeX export of the report): accepted for implementation as five build batches with golden-file tests as the evidence; no migration, no model call, no measurement

**Status:** accepted 2026-10-02 as a design (docs only, no code, no model call, no product measurement). Decided jointly by Claude and gpt-6.1-sol (high, read-only) on the owner's instruction; the owner was not asked. The number is provisional: on 2 October 2026 `origin/main` (`878281f`) stops at D147 (D146 slice 3 K3, D147 slice 4 design), the `DEIXIS-e1` worktree already holds an uncommitted D148 (slice 4 E1) and `DEIXIS-k4` stops at D146, so D149 was taken after those. Re-check all of them when committing. Authority for scope: [the design note](product/p6-slice5-latex-export.md) §10 (Q1 to Q22) and §11 (X1 to X5).

**Context:** The slice 5 note was drafted on 17 September 2026, before slice 1 code, and called itself D60. Re-checked against `58676f1`, it was out of date in ten places (note §0). The report is now read through `report_view`, exported as Markdown by `report/export.py` (D120), and slice 4 (D147) adds edit and citation-removal wording to that same export. The note also needed TeX evidence: twelve measurements on TeX Live 2021 (note §2) show that XeLaTeX drops `≥` and `α` without an error, that a float taller than the page loses table rows with exit code 0, that a 13-column table with 500-character cells loses 12 of 13 cell ends even in `longtable`, and that `IEEEtran.bst` lowercases titles. These shape the design.

**Decision:** (1) A pure text transform `to_latex(view, *, title, corpus, bib_sources)` beside `to_markdown`, with no intermediate document model; the shared bilingual "not checked" sentences move to `report/export_text.py` and the Markdown output stays byte-identical. (2) The download is a zip of `<stem>.tex` and `<stem>.bib` through the existing route with `format=latex`; XeLaTeX, `IEEEtran[journal]`, BibTeX with `IEEEtran.bst`; no `hyperref`, no pdfLaTeX; no class or style is bundled. (3) Citation keys are `works.source_key` (D59), `-2`, `-3` for later versions of one work, `ref<n>` with a warning when missing; the table's first column is plain text so the `.bbl` order equals the screen order. (4) Stored math passes a closed scanner (an allowlist of commands and environments, `^^`, `%`, `#`, blank lines and control characters rejected, context rules for `&`, `\\`, `\tag`); what fails becomes escaped plain text with a warning. Accepted math gets a lossless rewrite, a closed Unicode symbol table and a write class (`equation`, `equation*`, `aligned`, `gathered`, or a single top-level display environment as is); one label target per `equation_ref` across the report. (5) Tables use `\onecolumn` and `longtable`, in column groups of at most 7 data columns with `\addtocounter{table}{-1}` so every group reads TABLE I; oversize cells move to a "Long table values" list in the report notes. (6) `to_bibtex(..., latex_report=False)` keeps the Zotero export byte-identical; with `True` it double-braces titles, applies the symbol table once and drops `doi`, `url` and `eprint` values that contain a backslash or control character, each with a note. (7) Notes go in a `%` block at the top of the `.tex` (at most 20), the header `X-Deixis-Export-Notes` carries the count, the UI shows one warning toast. (8) One read snapshot through `workflow/queue.py::_snapshot`; a missing source record returns 409. (9) Slice 4's three-state edit sentences, `has_human_edits`, skipped rules and effective-citation set are written from the shared text module, so X1 starts after slice 4 E1 and E2 and X5 after E3 (Q22). (10) Five batches: X1 pins Markdown with golden cases and extracts `export_text.py`; X2 builds the preamble, text and math modules and `latex_names.json`; X3 the assembler, bibliography parameters and golden `.tex` and `.bib` files; X4 the wrapper, route, zip, header and the optional compile test; X5 the button, strings, Playwright test and design-note status. No migration, run kind, model contract, `skill_package_hash` or `contracts.py` change.

**Evidence:** A code comparison against `58676f1` with file and line evidence (note §0 and §1), the TeX measurements M1 to M12 with reproducible inputs under `/tmp/x0-tex/ref/` (note §2), a question round for Q1 to Q22 (Sol rejected the first proposal of Q5 and added Q17 to Q21), and six design-review rounds by gpt-6.1-sol high with 11, 7, 1, 1, 1 and 0 high findings; the last verdict was "hazır". Findings of the first rounds corrected the note itself (a wrong M9 claim, an unbounded class A scanner, a wrong D146 claim). This entry records a design decision: no export code, compiled PDF of a real report or journal-submission check is established.

**Limits:** A design decision, not a verified implementation. The TeX measurements come from one distribution (TeX Live 2021) and a few synthetic tables; the claim that the output compiles without lost content is untested until X3 and X4 build golden files and the compile test, and the new width formula, the 400 and 200 character thresholds and the table-cell math subset are designs, not measured results. The optional compile test (`tests/test_report_latex_compile.py`) is skipped when `latexmk`, `xelatex`, `bibtex`, `pdftotext`, `kpsewhich` or a required package is missing, and any report that quotes a green run must say whether it was skipped. The math scanner is a closed allowlist, so valid LaTeX outside it is written as plain text with a warning; `latex_names.json` needs one run of `scripts/latex_export_names.py` on a machine with TeX. The current report contract has no real-model-completed report (one full report from 18 September, `4582b64`, predates later contracts, and the P16 series did not complete), and the real shape of `index_terms` is unseen. The output is "an export that uses IEEEtran", not a checked journal submission; quotation passages, cell evidence and located anchors stay in DEIXIS and the report notes say so.

## D148 — P6 slice 4 E1: edited report text can be checked by code, with an append-only result whose currency follows its inputs

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-02, P6 slice 4 batch E1

**Context:** D112 preserves human claim revisions, but the fourteen assembly checks read the model's base text. D147 accepts a separate check of current text without publication or a model call. Binding scope: [the E1 prompt](product/p6-slice4-e1-prompt.md); [the slice 4 note](product/p6-slice4-editing-stale-measurement.md) §5 and §14. The checkout was `878281f`; local `main` and this checkout both had D147 at the top immediately before this entry was written. Migration 0060 was the highest before writing 0061.

**Decision:** Migration `0061_report_edit_checks.sql` adds `report_edit_checks`, unique per report and input fingerprint, with an update refusal and a delete refusal except under the owning research's purge authorization. `assembly.run_current_checks` reads claim revisions while `run_assembly_checks` retains its signature, outputs and raw citation reads. Every current-mode citation read goes through `ReportStore.effective_links`, which returns all original links in E1. Current checks recount only edited sections, preserve structural checks, list count claims without integers and derived claims without complete citation depth as skipped, omit human claims from phrase frames and exception matching while retaining lexical diagnostics, and apply the existing VIII digit test to edited VIII claims.

`workflow/report/edit_check.py` records checker version `edit-check-1`, deterministic result version 1 and a canonical JSON dependency manifest. The fingerprint covers section ownership of claims, current text, frozen structure and snapshot content, selected section inputs and citation-linked inputs separately, effective links, passage ownership/kind/text source/text, bibliography fields, gap bases, latest phrase repairs, report language, scope-language fallback and phrasebank text. Missing records have explicit absent markers. `ReportStore.check_edits` evaluates and inserts with one event in one synchronous transaction; identical inputs return the prior row without writes. It changes no report, section or claim row. Currency is derived when read: a matching fingerprint takes precedence over the latest historical row. The bodyless CSRF-protected POST route returns `report_view`, which adds `has_human_edits` and `edit_check`. English and Turkish Markdown exports distinguish absent, current and historical checks, retain the exact prior versioned no-check sentences, cover edited drafts, print skipped rules and limits, and identify an accepted D118 review as a review of the model's base version.

Judgements: rule-family names follow the existing fourteen function names in their existing order, followed by the VIII number rule; results sort by section/rule/detail and skipped entries by section/claim/rule/reason. The current section word-count formula mirrors `sections._word_count` without editing or importing that execution module. Historical selection uses insertion order (`rowid`), so equal timestamps remain unambiguous. Missing or unresolved body-ref depth prevents comparison of a partial subset while the support-strength check still runs. The store action returns record metadata plus the decoded `result`; the view exposes the specified state shape. The base-version review clause is attached only to an accepted `reviewed` record, because a failed review has no accepted coverage. Fingerprint tests disable immutability triggers only in temporary synthetic databases to prove that dependency hashing does not rely on them. Existing migration coverage changes one expected migration list to include 61; backup code needs no change because SQLite's backup API copies the table.

**Evidence:** Before editing assembly, clean, error, warning and malformed-record fixtures were run on `878281f`; their exact outputs are literals in `tests/test_report_edit_check.py`, compared again after human edits. Separate cases filter one effective link for each of bibliography, anchors, VII cell-link basis, equation origin, derived depth and one-source plural diagnostics; a SQL trace guard forbids current-mode raw link reads outside `effective_links`. Synthetic tests cover dependency changes (including moving a claim to another section and changing only its selected section input), deterministic bytes, replay, checker-version changes, current/historical state, transaction rollback, unchanged report/section/claim rows, draft edits, route conflicts/CSRF, bilingual export, empty/populated migration, trash/restore/purge and identical backup/restore rows. Final focused command: `PYTHONPATH=backend:. UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/deixis-uv-cache UV_OFFLINE=1 uv run pytest tests/test_report_edit_check.py tests/test_report_assembly.py tests/test_report_flow.py tests/test_report_review.py tests/test_report_api.py tests/test_report_export.py tests/test_migrations.py tests/test_backup.py tests/test_corpus_removal.py tests/test_contracts.py tests/test_report_review_methodology.py -q` — 549 passed, 60 deprecation warnings (SWIG and Starlette/AnyIO). The three existing assembly/flow/review test files are unchanged. `git diff --check` passes. `skill_package_hash` before and after: `sha256:8e1e4a8453a286ac9da8628dd095dd7796f3a49ae374d7930cb3ef06c546ee76`.

**Limits:** Structural and lexical code checks only: no semantic support validation, no number-word check, no scientific validation of passages, no measured real-corpus hit rate. An anchor location or a current fingerprint does not establish support. No model/provider/network call or measurement was made. The live service and data were not touched or restarted; nothing was committed, pushed or published. Full-suite and browser acceptance remain with the orchestrator; no web file changed. The pending r2 plan review was not performed in this batch. E2 still owns citation removal, effective-set persistence, staleness/view numbering and report-citation asset protection; E3 owns the screen; E4 owns the scripted sequence and P9 debt. The Turkish note's §4 names `finalize` as an assembly caller, but code calls assembly in `sections.py` and `revert_repair`; neither caller changed. Its historical-check wording refers only to later edits, while the binding E1 wording correctly refers to all current inputs. Those sections remain unchanged under E1's §14-only documentation scope.

## D147 — P6 slice 4 (edit check and citation removal, narrow version): accepted for implementation as four batches without any model call; publish, section rewrite, stable identity and the closing measurement are deferred

**Status:** accepted 2026-10-02 as a design (docs only, nothing implemented, no model call, no measurement). Decided jointly by Claude and gpt-6.1-sol (high, read-only) on the owner's instruction; the owner was not asked. The number was taken after D145 on `main` at `58676f1`; parallel batches write D146 and maybe D147, so re-check when committing. Authority for scope: [the design note](product/p6-slice4-editing-stale-measurement.md) §0, §12 and §13.

**Context:** Slice 4's note was drafted on 17 September 2026, updated on 29 September (small version, D112) and mostly built under D112 and D113 (claim edit with history, read-time staleness, "Keep as is", the report screen, export). Re-checking the 17 September draft against `58676f1` found it wrong in several places: slice 1's report is in code, "Publish" and section rewrite do not exist, assembly rules read the model's `report_claims.text` and never an edited revision (so the screen and export say "edited text was not checked again"), a citation cannot be removed from an edited claim, `edited_after_version` is null on a draft report, `research_cites_asset` and `asset_impact` do not count report citations, and the stable-identity layer has nothing to match without a rewrite. The earlier "first complete real-model report" (`4582b64`, 18 September) is real, but the frozen P16 series never completed a report (D124, D126, D128) and the first report predates D118, D127 and the eight assembly rules. The owner asked for the narrowest close, four or five batches, deferring anything that depends on unbuilt work or on a real-model report that has never completed.

**Decision:** (1) The slice adds one read-only, model-free action, "check edits": a current-text mode of the assembly rules (glossary order, banned words, count numbers, word budgets recomputed, equations, own-work and plural-source diagnostics, VIII number restatement; phrase frames and exceptions stay off for human text; rules that cannot run are listed as skipped, not clean) whose result is stored in an append-only record keyed by a fingerprint of the checker version and every input the check reads, and shown on screen and in the export as current or historical. It never changes report status, `report_version`, section status or the D118 review. (2) The slice adds citation removal from an edited claim: every revision records its full effective citation set, sealed at insert (`link_count`, `report_claim_revision_links`, `request_hash`), a citation-only edit is valid, restore brings back text and citations together, a claim with no citations shows "no direct citations" (not a refusal, since body or gap refs and counts may still support it), idempotency for new requests is bound to the request content (a D112 replay behavior is superseded, old keys keep it), and one effective-link definition feeds checks, section-level staleness, numbering, view and export while the report-level snapshot counts stay independent of removals. The lifecycle gap (report citations missing from `research_cites_asset` and `asset_impact`) is closed in the same batch. (3) Deferred: Publish and any new `report_version`, section rewrite proposals, stable claim and gap identity and cross-version candidate matching, `scope_statement` edit, passage and column staleness extensions, chain-link and candidate staleness (slices 2b/2c and slice 3 K3 unbuilt), review of an edit. Slice 4 no longer fulfils the identity matching that D143 left to it; it returns when a rewrite exists. (4) The closing measurement (R18 to R21, real model, held-out question) moves to P9 as a debt, consistent with slice 2's measurement and slice 3's K6; a deterministic fake-model sequence stays in the slice as tests (E4). (5) Batches: E1 check edits (M), E2 citation removal and the recorded effective set with lifecycle (M-L), E3 interface (M), E4 scripted sequence, closing and the P9 debt entry (S-M); no batch calls a model and `skill_package_hash` does not move. Joint answers: Q1 agree, Q2 changed by Sol (wider rule list, mandatory persistence), Q3 changed by Sol (restore recovers citations too, zero citations is a state), Q4 to Q7 and Q9 agree, Q8 changed by Sol (sizes); X1 to X4 added.

**Evidence:** Read-only comparison of the note with `main` at `58676f1` (code, migrations, `docs/decisions.md`) by Claude and, separately, gpt-6.1-sol; the decision round and three design-review rounds (4, 1 and 0 high findings; the last found none) are recorded in the note's header. This entry records a design decision: no check, citation removal, migration or test exists yet, and no model call or measurement was made.

**Limits:** A design decision, not a verified implementation. The check re-runs code rules on edited text; it shows nothing about whether a sentence is supported by its cited evidence, does not see numbers written as words or a count claim without integers (listed as not checked), and its coverage of real edits is unmeasured. Removing a citation reduces evidence and cannot add one. An edited report keeps the model-written `report_version` and the D118 review, both of which describe the model's text. PDF re-extraction and passage changes are still not detected. The sentences in an edited, never-rechecked report stay unchecked. No real-model report completed under today's code is on record, so the real-corpus behavior of editing, checking and staleness is a P9 debt.

## D146 — P6 slice 3 K3: the flow and the API for claim candidates and the claim-specific kill-search run end to end with a fake model and mocked providers; no screen shows them yet

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-02, P6 slice 3 batch K3 (flow, then API, one commit)

**Context:** D143 accepts the slice, D144 gave storage and pure code, D145 the contracts and method file. K3 joins them with the database and the network. The number was taken after D145 in the K3 worktree at `58676f1`; re-check when committing. Binding scope: the [design note](product/p6-slice3-kill-search.md) §2, §5, §6, §9, §12 and §17 K3, and the batch prompt `docs/product/p6-slice3-k3-prompt.md`.

**Decision:** `workflow/candidates/run.py` (pure) builds the `candidate_target` of each task from stored rows, the frozen kill-search plan with its preview fingerprint, the reading depth and shown passages of a work, and the candidate-scoped evidence reader. `ResearchFlow` gets explicit dispatch for `claim_decomposition` and `kill_search` (stage `candidate`; the fall-through into `_table_columns` is closed). A decomposition run makes one model step and publishes one `model_decomposition` version through `add_version` after a synchronous run, scope and candidate re-check; a candidate with a version is not decomposed again (a human edit is the revision path). A kill-search run asks for two term blocks, compiles them, freezes the search (blocks with backups, rendered queries, skipped terms, selection), sends at most six logical provider queries of at most twenty records with no paging or enrichment, merges and cuts to eight works through `query_records()` read back from the store, freezes the shown passages per work in a plan step, assesses the works one by one (no model call for a work with no text; its hit is `insufficient_access`) and publishes cells and quotes only through `claim_assessment_evidence`; an unlocated quote fails the run. Nothing touches `corpus_memberships`, candidates, selections, search runs or `selection_revision`. Ceilings: model attempts computed from the constants (6 for a decomposition, 54 for a kill-search, 60 together; checked before every send, rate-limit resends included, resume never renews them) and a separate transport ceiling from a new `Connector.requests_per_search` (PubMed 2): each attempt durably reserves its whole possible cost before it is sent and is never refunded; a refused query is recorded `failed/transport_budget` and the search finishes `failed` at the end, never `completed`. An answer is recorded before any stop is honoured, and an `after_send_unknown` answer is `outcome_unknown` and never re-sent. Terminal invalid steps are never re-sent, the repair history survives a pause, a stored successful assessment is published from its stored input, a changed frozen passage makes the whole unassessed hit `insufficient_access`, the frozen `skill_package_hash` is enforced, and a terminal `failed` search is carried to the run by the failure code written to the summary step before it was finished. The search outcome follows the run (`sync_search_outcome`, also called by the read endpoints and run control, an idempotent write on read). Resume of any run kind is refused while another run of the research is active. API under `/api/researches/{id}/candidates`: open (gap or owner text), list, card, human edit, decompose, kill-search plan and start (preview fingerprint, replay first, scoped `Idempotency-Key`), matrix view with a status derived for that search, candidate-scoped evidence reader (the text the model really received, from the stored StepInput), owner decision (reason required, append-only, beside the computed status). Human text is refused with 422 when it holds NUL, an unencodable character or only whitespace.

Judgements: a failure before the freeze (invalid or failed terms step, no compiled query is the exception) means the search did not start and writes no search record; no compiled query freezes an empty search and fails it (`undecided`, `search_failed`); an invalid, oversized or unreached assessment leaves its hit `pending`, which K1 reads as unassessed (`not_assessed_budget`), the exact reason is in the `kill_search_summary` step (`assessed`, `insufficient_access`, `invalid_output`, `message_too_large`, `not_reached_budget`); the terms step is optional-wrapped, so a transient model failure there fails the run instead of pausing it; the ceilings are conservative (a reservation is the whole attempt cost); `fixture_server.py`, trash/restore routes and report integration were left out.

**Verification:** `tests/test_candidate_run.py`, `tests/test_candidate_flow.py` (real `_model_step` with `FakeAdapter`, mocked `httpx`, crash and stop windows, ceilings, isolation, frozen passages) and `tests/test_candidate_api.py` (both origins, replay, conflicts, evidence access, text safety, CSRF), plus the existing suites. Full pytest outside the implementer's sandbox: 4,853 passed, 1 skipped. gpt-6.1-sol high: plan review 3 rounds (7, 3 and 1 high, all folded in; the third folded in without a fourth round), code review 2 rounds (1 high in round 1, an uncertain delivery lost to a pause, fixed; round 2 0 high).

**Limits:** Synthetic data, a fake adapter and mocked providers only: no real model or provider call, so nothing shows that the terms find prior work, that eight works are enough, or that a model reads an abstract correctly; a located quote is not proof of support. Reading is title, abstract and stored passages only. The hash check runs before the terminal-failed resume branch, so a run resumed after a package change fails with `skill_package_changed` while the search summary keeps its earlier code. A read endpoint writes (idempotent outcome sync). The skill hash and frozen model triples are not re-checked against later setting changes beyond the hash. No screen exists (K4); report integration, trash and restore routes and the fixture scenario wait for K4 or later. `skill_package_hash` is unchanged (`sha256:8e1e4a84...`).

## D145 — P6 slice 3 K2: the contracts, citation handles, validators and method file for the three candidate tasks are in place; nothing calls them yet

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-01, P6 slice 3 batch K2

**Context:** D143 accepts three model tasks for the claim-specific kill-search (`claim_decomposition`, `kill_search_query`, `claim_assessment`); D144 gave them storage. K2 builds only the road a model step travels, in the pattern of D133 (lineage) and D127 (per-field handles). The number was taken after D144 in the K2 worktree at `0e2aa80`; re-check when committing. Binding scope: the [design note](product/p6-slice3-kill-search.md) §5, §8, §12 K2 and §17 K2, and the batch prompt `docs/product/p6-slice3-k2-prompt.md`.

**Decision:** Three strict output schemas (`claim-decomposition`, `kill-search-query`, `claim-assessment`, each v1) registered in `SCHEMA_FILES`, `SCHEMA_VERSIONS` and `TASK_OUTPUTS`. `step-input.schema.json` gains the three task types, an optional closed `candidate_target` (candidate id, origin, gap kind, origin text, basis items, a closed `candidate_version` with 2 to 6 elements, assessed source), root `$defs` `candidate_version` and `candidate_element`, and the allowlist key `element_ids` for assessment. `check_step_input` gets `_check_candidate_target` (target iff candidate task, one task-specific shape, exact allowlist, basis only for decomposition and empty for an owner's sentence, one assessed source with at least one passage of that work, at most 24 unique passages, element positions 1..n, conflicting repeated records refused). `KillSearchQuery` reuses `_check_search_query` unchanged; `_check_claim_decomposition` and `_check_claim_assessment` enforce the §5 consistency rules (relevance against cell relations, alignment against relation, support cells need a quote, exactly one cell per element, whole-claim flag needs related relevance and a quote, a non-null nearest explanation needs a shown basis, a surface list of experiment-design words in the validation plan). Quotes are located by `locate_anchor`; because that match is fuzzy, `claim_assessment_evidence` returns the located passage words (never the model's raw words) and maps an abstract passage to `evidence_kind = abstract` with no passage id, and K3 must store evidence only through it. Candidate outputs additionally reject whitespace-only, NUL-containing and UTF-8-unencodable text (`blank_text`, `text_not_encodable`), because K1 would refuse them after the step had succeeded; issue paths and messages are escaped for the same reason. Handles follow D127: `CANDIDATE_INPUT_ID_FIELDS`/`CANDIDATE_OUTPUT_ID_FIELDS`, numbering passages, sources, then version elements, `ele_E` added to `PADDED_HANDLE`; the decomposition's `e1`..`en` are model labels nothing resolves. `flow.py` changes are plumbing only (`HANDLE_TASKS`, a `candidate_target` parameter, `element_ids` in the assessment allowlist, handle resolution on the output). Method package: `RUNTIME_FILES` for the three tasks = (`SKILL.md`, `references/candidate-check.md`); `candidate-check.md` is new; `SKILL.md` gets a scoping paragraph and keeps the two existing prohibition sentences verbatim; `provenance.json` records the file and the seven prepared, not-run cases in `tests/model_behavior/candidate_cases.json`. ## D144 — P6 slice 3 K1: claim candidates, kill-search records and the status derivation have durable storage and pure code; nothing calls them from the flow yet

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-01, P6 slice 3 batch K1

**Context:** D143 accepts the slice as K1 to K6. K1 builds only storage and pure computation. The number was taken after D143 in the K1 worktree at `9ae16fb`; D142 belongs to the slice 2 fix batch running in parallel, so re-check when committing. Binding scope: the [design note](product/p6-slice3-kill-search.md) §5, §7, §9 items 1 and 5, §12 K1 and §17 K1, and the batch prompt `docs/product/p6-slice3-k1-prompt.md`.

**Decision:** Migration `0060_candidates.sql` rebuilds `runs` (0059 pattern, `claim_decomposition` and `kill_search` added to the kind CHECK, every old row kept) and adds ten `WITHOUT ROWID` tables: `research_candidates`, `candidate_versions`, `claim_elements`, `kill_searches`, `kill_search_queries`, `kill_search_query_records`, `kill_search_hits`, `claim_matrix_cells`, `claim_matrix_evidence`, `candidate_status_overrides`. Candidates copy their origin as plain text (no foreign key to `report_gaps`, reports, tables or cells) with a content fingerprint, so a rewritten gap row becomes a second candidate. Versions, elements, cells, evidence and owner decisions are append-only; a search's frozen columns, terminal outcome and a hit's assessment cannot be rewritten; cell and evidence integrity (element of the search's version, kept assessed hit, passage of the same source, whole-claim quote only for a whole-claim hit) is enforced by triggers; every CHECK is NULL-safe; deletes need the research purge authorization. `workflow/candidates/status.py` derives the five statuses from stored rows by the §5 table (no prose), `hits.py` merges provider results round-robin, deduplicates by work and cuts at eight, `terms.py` builds the two-block vocabulary and compiles it with `compile_block_queries`; all three are pure and purity-tested. `CandidateStore` opens candidates from a gap snapshot or the owner's text (replay-safe), adds immutable versions with `expected_version`, records the search, its queries (sources only through `upsert_provider_source`), merged hits and per-work assessments in one SAVEPOINT-protected transaction with the §5 consistency rules, refuses writes to a terminal search and a `completed` search without a recorded merge, and computes `candidate_status` (latest search of the version whatever its outcome; an earlier finished one only as `previous`; the owner's recorded status beside it). Lifecycle: `purge_research` deletes the candidate tree and the sources only a kill-search held, `purge_sources` and the research purge keep a source another research's kill-search holds, payload files stay while a search run, a source version, a kill-search query or an abstract passage names them, `cited_source_versions`, `research_cites_asset` and `asset_impact` (new key `candidate_quotes`) see assessment cells and quotes, backup carries query payload files and abstract-passage payload references.

Judgements: a new table `kill_search_query_records` makes the merge input durable and lets a purge find sources of a run that died before writing hits; a `completed` search with an `outcome_unknown` query is `undecided` (`query_outcome_unknown`), a pending hit in a finished search is `not_assessed_budget`, an empty hit list with `found > 0` is never `open`; `kept = 0` with `found = 0` is `open`; the K1 store does not locate quotes (K2 and K3 do); candidate trash and restore exist with an active-run guard; every candidate write emits one `candidate_changed` event; `idempotency_key` columns on candidates and versions bind a replay to its content; `create_run`'s stage mapping for the new kinds was left to K3.

**Verification:** `tests/test_candidate_status.py`, `tests/test_candidate_store.py`, additions to `tests/test_migrations.py` (every old run kind and dependent row survives, empty pre-0060 database, vocabularies equal the CHECK lists), `tests/test_backup.py`, `tests/test_corpus_removal.py`, and the exact `asset_impact` expectation in `tests/test_asset_replacement.py`. Full pytest: 4,240 passed, 1 skipped. gpt-6.1-sol high: plan review 3 rounds (2, 1 and 0 high; the first round's isolation finding became a documented limit), code review 2 rounds (1 high in round 1, a `completed` search without a merge giving `open`, fixed; round 2 0 high).

**Limits:** Synthetic storage only: no flow, route, view model, model call or provider request uses it, and no real output was stored. `upsert_provider_source` is the shared-library write path discovery uses, so for a source another research already holds it can fill metadata, add an abstract or re-check arXiv eligibility exactly as that research's discovery would; K1 claims only that the research-scoped tables (corpus memberships, candidates, selections, search runs, counts) stay unchanged. Sibling `other_versions` rows and the payload files they name can survive a purge and enter backups. Stored quotes are as given, not located. Status is computed from stored rows and is only as right as the assessments; `open` still means no match in the assessed subset of supplied text.

## D143 — P6 slice 3 (claim-specific kill-search and candidate card): accepted for implementation as four build batches, one development-behavior batch and one measurement batch; chain-end entry, report write-back, PDF reading and export are deferred

**Status:** accepted 2026-10-01 as a design (docs only, nothing implemented, no model call, no measurement). Decided jointly by Claude and gpt-6.1-sol (high, read-only) on the owner's instruction; the owner was not asked. The number was taken after D141 on `main` at `06a146d`; D142 belongs to another batch running in parallel, so re-check both when committing. Authority for scope: [the design note](product/p6-slice3-kill-search.md) §0, §15 and §16.

**Context:** The slice 3 note was drafted on 17 September 2026, before slice 1 and slice 2 code. Re-checking it against `06a146d` found it wrong in several places: the slice 2 tables it relied on (`chain_end_uncertainties`, `citation_expansions`, `field_baseline_selections`) do not exist because slice 2 2b and 2c were deferred in D130 and never built; `Store.record_search` writes the research's own candidates and corpus memberships, so reusing it would put kill-search records into the research's pool, the opposite of what the draft required; the `SearchPlan` contract is gone and discovery uses a model-written two-block query (D92); `report_gaps.kill_search_status` has a SQL CHECK without `undecided`; `save_gaps` updates a gap row in place, keeping its id while text and basis change; no report has completed on a real model (D124, D126, D128). The owner asked for a slice narrower than slice 2, which had nine batches and took about fifteen hours.

**Decision:** (1) A candidate is a versioned, one-claim card opened from a snapshot of a stored `report_gaps` row of the three existing kinds, or from the owner's own sentence (`owner_text`); chain-end entry, the fourth gap kind, forward check, citation expansion and field baseline are deferred with slice 2b/2c. The candidate copies the gap's text, basis and a content fingerprint and has no foreign key to live report rows. (2) Kill-search never touches the research's corpus: it uses its own hit table and `upsert_provider_source` only, and calls none of `record_search`, `add_search_run`, `add_to_corpus` or `link_records`. (3) One formulation per version; every model decomposition or human edit creates an immutable version, and matrix cells belong to one `kill_search_id`. (4) Three model tasks (`claim_decomposition`, `kill_search_query`, `claim_assessment`) and two run kinds (`claim_decomposition`, `kill_search`, stage `candidate`); screening is folded into the per-work assessment. The query is two bounded term blocks compiled by `compile_block_queries`, with D92's field-count probes, backup substitution and companion code query left out and the compiler's provider filtering and endpoint routing kept; a logical query is a provider's one search operation and multi-request operations such as PubMed's are counted by their real requests. (5) Fixed visible budget: one decomposition, one query, at most six logical provider queries of at most twenty records, the first eight works by cross-provider order assessed one call each, sequentially; a model-attempt ceiling of 60 for both runs and a separate transport ceiling; timeout resends are not enabled. (6) Status is computed on read from the latest search record of the version, whatever its state, with five values (`not_run`, `undecided`, `narrowed`, `closed`, `open`): `closed` needs one work that states the whole claim explicitly under aligned conditions and cannot come from inference; unresolved, unreadable, budget-skipped or unclear evidence gives `undecided`; `open` only means no match in the assessed subset of read text, with reading depth and the number of unread results stated; anything unclassified fails closed to `undecided`. `not_run` means no search record exists; a running or paused search is `undecided` unless its published partial cells already give `closed`, and an earlier finished result is shown separately and never decides the status. `undecided` exists only in candidate tables. (7) Reading is title, abstract and already stored passages; no PDF acquisition. (8) The owner may record a status with a reason beside the computed one; it satisfies no searched-evidence gate. (9) Nothing is written to `report_gaps` and `workflow/report/*` is untouched; report VI/VII status badges, banned-word loosening and VII inheritance wait for report integration or slice 4. (10) Batches: K1 storage and pure functions, K2 contracts and method package, K3 flow and API, K4 interface, K5 development behavior cases with a real model, K6 independent frozen measurement (owner-started, not required for closure, uses `owner_text` with a frozen human-written claim version). Joint answers to the ten draft questions: Q1 agree, adding that a search that was attempted and read nothing is `undecided`, not `not_run`, Q2 agree, Q3 agree, Q4 agree with cells per search, Q5 changed by Sol (logical-query definition, two ceilings, 60 attempts), Q6 agree, Q7 defer, Q8 agree, Q9 single formulation, Q10 defer; X1 abstract reading changed by Sol, X3 query rendering changed by Sol, X6 lifecycle and safety additions by Sol.

**Evidence:** Read-only comparison of the note against `main` at `06a146d` (code, migrations, `docs/decisions.md`) by Claude and, separately, gpt-6.1-sol; the decision round and four design-review rounds (4, 2, 1 and 0 high findings; the last found none) are recorded in the note's header. This entry records a design decision: no candidate implementation, live-provider run, model call or scientific validation is established.

**Limits:** A design decision, not a verified implementation. Assessment reads titles, abstracts and passages already stored for a work: an abstract may not reflect a whole work and stored passages are not a full-text reading, so `closed` is a positive finding of the supplied text's statement and `open` is not evidence that nothing exists. Recall (providers, term blocks, eight works) is unmeasured. The report-gap entry has never been exercised with a real-model section VI, and slice 2's real-model link production is unmeasured (D140, D141). The budget numbers (eight works, twenty records, six queries, 60 attempts) are borrowed and unmeasured. A result stays with its candidate version; changing the claim means searching again. A reopened gap whose row was rewritten becomes a second candidate; there is no cross-report-version matching. The skill package hash will move when K2 lands, and the slice 3 batches must stay out of any measured H9 checkout window.

## D142 — P6 slice 2 closed as implemented, usefulness of link production on a real corpus not shown; two medium findings of the cross-batch review fixed (restore cannot re-activate a cycle, whitespace `what_changed` goes to repair)

**Status:** accepted (slice closing statement and two fixes implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-01, P6 slice 2 fix batch (D138 and D139 belong to P9 H0)

**Context:** A gpt-6.1-sol cross-batch review of all slice 2 code (L1 to L8) ended "düzeltmeyle hazır" with two medium findings. (1) A model link A->B turns stale when a role column is removed and so leaves the cycle graph; a human can then add B->A; restoring the column makes A->B current again and both links are active, a directed cycle that bypassed the check (reproduced in memory, `has_cycle=True`). (2) `what_changed="   "` passed the L3 semantic check, but L4 `_shape` rejects it with `strip()`; publication runs in one transaction, so the exception became `lineage_publication_failed` for the whole run and every valid decision of that run was lost (reproduced: two stable outputs closed without repair and the other valid decision was rolled back). Separately, L9 (D141) stopped at the corpus gates and the slice needed a closing statement; it was decided with gpt-6.1-sol on the owner's delegation (option A).

**Decision:** Fix 1: `TableStore.restore_column`, for a column with a `lineage_role`, compares the stale set before and after the UPDATE in the same transaction and refuses the restore (`InvalidTableInput`, nothing written, column stays removed, no event) when a link re-activated by the restore lies on a directed cycle of the active, non-stale, non-`independent_parallel`, live-endpoint graph. A cycle that existed before and that the restore does not touch does not block it. `LineageStore` shares one edge filter (`_graph`) between `_cycle` and the new re-activation check. No revision is rewritten or marked stale. Fix 2: `domain/lineage.py` holds `MAX_WHAT_CHANGED` and `valid_what_changed` (a string with non-whitespace text, 1 to 500 characters on the raw text); L3 (`what_changed_empty` issue, bounded repair) and L4 `_shape` both use it. No schema, fixture, method or migration change; `skill_package_hash` is unchanged (`sha256:371fcecb7977fec6cce031f101a68cba9e4688383118951fe663614f342b2e8c`).

**Closing statement.** Slice 2 (Chain of Ideas, D130 to D137 and D140 to D142) is closed as: **implemented; usefulness of link production on a real corpus not shown; L9 stopped at the corpus gates, R12 to R15 not measurable.** This does not mean the screen and human-edit path are verified with real model output.

**Evidence:** full pytest 3,939 passed, 1 skipped (baseline before the fix 3,906 per D141); the focused lineage and evidence-table suites passed; regression tests: restore refused for the cycle scenario with real node inputs, allowed for no-cycle, no-role, remaining scope/evidence stale reasons, `independent_parallel`, non-live endpoint, three-node cycle and diamond; whitespace `what_changed` yields the L3 issue, runs through repair and publishes both decisions; L3 and L4 agree on a value table. gpt-6.1-sol plan review 1 round (0 high, 4 medium and 1 low folded in), code review 2 rounds (r1 düzeltmeyle hazır, 0 high and 1 medium: the first restore check refused any restore while an old untouched cycle existed, now only restore-reactivated edges are tested, with two added regression tests; r2 hazır, 0 findings). The restore check compares the stale set before and after the UPDATE and refuses only when a re-activated edge lies on a directed cycle.

**Limits:** What is verified across L1 to L9: deterministic behaviour with synthetic data and a fake or scripted model (candidates, edges, contract, store, plan, flow, view, screen, behaviour-case runner); eight synthetic real-model cases and one 7-work trial (D140), each structurally valid, one attempt, no rates; the fresh-corpus measurement did not run (D141). What is not verified: real-model link production on a real corpus (how often links are found, right or wrong), the finder's recall, the screen and human-edit path with real output, R12 to R15. Open debts: (a) numbered citation styles are missed by the mention finder; (b) reference-list-only mentions are not detected as such (the model is told not to count them); (c) a budget-paused lineage run cannot progress by resume alone (D135); (d) a head change of a work is a display flag, not stale (D136); (e) real-model link production is unmeasured; the independent lineage measurement is an open debt to plan as a separate L9 job at the start of P9 (H9 covers the report only); (f) the discovery finding of D141 (the default flow included 1 of 99 works on an NLP question, 69 left pending, 25 of them waiting for a PDF): a separate product finding, not proof that screening is too strict, to be examined in P9 with found, pending and not found counted apart. The fix guarantee is limited to column restore: other ways to re-activate an old link (for example re-including an excluded row after a cycle was closed around it: A->B->C, C->A added while B is excluded, B re-included) can still create a cycle. A `succeeded` step output stored before this fix is reused without re-validation, so a whitespace output stored earlier could still fail publication when a paused run resumes. If `restore_column` is called inside an outer transaction whose caller swallows the refusal, rollback is that caller's business.

## D141 — P6 slice 2 L9: the fresh-corpus development-lines measurement stopped at the corpus gates after one preparation attempt; no lineage run was made and R12 to R15 are not measured

**Date:** 2026-10-01, P6 slice 2 batch L9 (frozen in `62812a1`; D138 and D139 belong to P9 H0)

The freeze (`p6-slice2-expectations.md`, `p6-slice2-chain.json`, kit `measure_lineage.py`) passed three gpt-6.1-sol rounds (8, 3, 0 high). Two choices in it need recording here: (1) the quota-resume rule deviates from D130 section 14.4, which allows one resume only when every root cause is `client_timeout`; the freeze keeps that and adds a quota/load-only rule frozen before the run (same run, at most two resumes for the lineage run and three per preparation run, only on the main session's "connection is back", eligibility by root-error class only); it was not used. (2) The owner approved, in chat on 1 October 2026, the read-only product backup of the live library into the run folder for the K0 independence check; nothing was written to the live data directory and the service on 8765 was not touched.

**Decision:** Record what happened. Question: `How did pretrained language representation models for natural language understanding develop, ...` (`res_SQ8KMWIzxERpBxeSWceO`), `codex` / `gpt-5.6-luna` / `medium`, `standard`, default `sw` flow, protocol approved as proposed. Discovery (17 sessions) and adjudication (53 sessions) completed; the product included 1 of 99 unique works (a 2022 ICD-coding paper using contextualized language models), excluded 29, left 69 pending (25 waiting for a PDF in the review queue). Of the frozen chain G the search returned ELMo, BERT and ALBERT, none included, RoBERTa not found. K0 passed (no overlap). Table of 1 row filled (1 session). Totals: 71 model sessions, recorded tokens from 70 of the 71 sessions (the failed one has none): 677,824 input and 64,669 output, 13.0 minutes from the research record to the filled table, 0 `started` sessions and 0 non-terminal runs at the end; product trees and `skill_package_hash` unchanged and the five freeze files matched their recorded sha256 at the end.

Nothing is known from this run about the finder, the lineage task or the links on an author-year corpus, and it is not evidence that development lines are useless there; the L8 open items (reference-list-only mentions, numbered citations) stay open. ## D140 — P6 slice 2 L8: the lineage task was run once on eight synthetic cases and once on a development corpus with a real model; every output was valid, nothing in either run shows that development lines are useful

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-01, P6 slice 2 batch L8 (D138 and D139 are taken by the parallel P9 H0 batch; renumber on rebase if needed)

**Context:** D130 to D137 built the `lineage_links` task, its contract, flow and screen with a fake or scripted model only. L8 is the first real-model contact: the eight cases of note section 11 (LB01 to LB08, defined in L3) and one end-to-end development trial. Neither is the L9 measurement.

**Decision:** `scripts/model_behavior/run_lineage_cases.py` builds each case from `I_lineage_links`, sends it through the production message path (handles, `resolve_citation_handles`, `normalise_output`, `validate_model_output`) with one attempt, no repair and no fallback, and writes the results incrementally to a directory of choice. It passed gpt-6.1-sol review (plan 2 rounds: 1 and 0 high; code 2 rounds: 2 and 0 high; one of the two round-1 high findings, "the Codex home is writable state", was answered with a `--codex-home` option and the unchanged use of the connection's own home, as every earlier runner does) before any model call. Screens are booleans next to separate observations; a human reads the text. The L3 catalogue test was relaxed (added fields allowed, a runner may exist) and the catalogue status is now `run_once_2026-10-01`.

**Evidence** (gpt-5.6-luna through the Codex connection, one attempt per case, results in the ignored `.local/p6-slice2-l8/results.json`; about 7,500 tokens per case; all eight completed and were structurally valid; no repair was needed):

| Case | Expected | Observed for candidate A |
|---|---|---|
| LB01 citation, relation unclear | no_relation or insufficient_evidence | no_relation; the `present` edge made no link |
| LB02 chronology only | no_relation | no_relation |
| LB03 one table version | decides the shown versions only | `extends` (source_stated, quote from the mention passage that says "we extend"); no comparison of the unshown published version |
| LB04 opposite results, different conditions | corrects_or_contradicts only with the condition difference in what_changed | corrects_or_contradicts, what_changed names the heated and cooled conditions and says they differ |
| LB05 abstract-only cells | no invented method difference; analyst_inference or insufficient_evidence | no_relation, no method terms; this differs from the literal expectation (see Limits) |
| LB06 coincidental match | no_relation | no_relation |
| LB07 bibliography entry only | insufficient_evidence | insufficient_evidence |
| LB08 embedded instruction | instruction ignored | no_relation, instruction passage not quoted, not echoed |

Candidate B (the fixture's "comparator, no dependency" mention) was `no_relation` in every case.

End-to-end trial (isolated copy of the library at `/tmp/l8-data`, port 8871, Codex home of the live connection; the live service and data untouched): research `res_jAMb1nXLwfrRdC3D8Miq` (underwater sensor networks), a new table `tbl_MA9Z8LgHoIfmKWzuSfYC` of seven works that have stored PDF text, development columns added, filled by a `table_fill` run (7 model calls, 21 values, about 125,000 tokens, 35 s), then one `lineage_links` run from its plan (ceiling 24, 4 calls used, 4 chunks, 9 candidate pairs, about 43,900 tokens, 13 s). Result: 9 pair decisions, all `insufficient_evidence`, 0 links, 0 rejected proposals, 0 failed pairs, 3 works without a candidate, 7 works unplaced. Reading the stored inputs: every one of the 9 mention passages is a reference-list passage of an IEEE paper (numbered citations in the body are the known blind spot of the mention finder, note section 17), and every candidate's edge state was `not_read` (42 of 42 pairs; no stored reference lists for this corpus). The model's notes (in Turkish, the research language) say the passages are only bibliography entries, which is what the method file asks for. This corpus and research are burned for L9.

**Limits:** One attempt per case and one corpus: no rate, no generalisation, no claim that development lines are useful. The cases are easy by construction: in LB01, LB02, LB06 and LB08 the passage itself says that no dependency or relation exists, so `no_relation` follows the text; LB03's mention passage states an extension, so the link there is the source's own statement. LB05's passages say "states no development relation", which makes `no_relation` a faithful reading and the case cannot tell it from insufficient evidence; rebuilding LB05 without that sentence needs a second run and was not done (one run per case was the brief). Structural validity and located quotes do not show that a link is true. The trial found no link, so the publication of real links, the screen on real data and the human edit path were not exercised on model output. The trial shows that on a numbered-citation corpus the mention finder hands the model nothing but bibliography lines (9 of 9 pairs); whether to drop reference-list passages from candidates, or to cover numbered citations, is not decided here. Python tests used synthetic data only.

**Open for L9:** pick a different corpus (this one is burned) and one whose later works name earlier works in body text (author-year style or titles); decide, before the measurement is frozen, how a reference-list-only mention is counted in R14; consider reading and storing reference lists so `edge_state` is not `not_read` everywhere; LB05 wording; the trial used `language_hint: tr`, so notes are Turkish and a keyword screen would need that.

## D139 — P9 H0a: baseline on a clean copy of `8091d62`, the supported environment written into the repository, a harness gap found, and the feature inventory

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-01, P9 batch H0a (done with H0b, one commit)

**Context:** P9 (plan `docs/product/p9-hardening-plan.md`, §5 H0a) needs the starting numbers, the supported environment fixed in the repository, the list of what the code implements and the first isolation check (§4 rule 5). Before this entry D138 was the highest number in this worktree; another worktree may take D137 in parallel.

The load average at each start is in `.local/p9-baseline/baseline.log` (4 to 7 before the first run, which followed the H0b measurements; other worktrees ran no pytest, Playwright or Vite at the start of any step but did at the end of the serial run). **The timings are not clean**: the serial run in particular (28 min against 8 min 42 s measured on 22 September, before the suite grew) overlapped my own reviews and test runs and one 90 s timeout of the known failing test (a second one is in the `-n auto` run); how much each cost is not known, so do not use it as a speed baseline. Environment: `apps/web/package.json` gets `engines` (`node >=22.12.0 <23`, `npm >=10 <11`), `.node-version` holds `22.23.2` (observed: Node 22.23.2, npm 10.9.8, uv 0.11.24, macOS 27.0.1 on arm64, Chrome installed), and the README Quickstart gets one supported-environment sentence. `package-lock.json` is not touched: regenerating it with the new `engines` would also add unrelated bundled-package entries (npm drift), and `npm ci` passes on the committed lock.
