## D138 — P9 H0b: the 1 GiB memory limit on PDF text extraction did not work and now does; the watcher moved from the extraction child to its parent

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-01, P9 batch H0b (done with H0a, one commit)

**Context:** The P9 plan (F09, mandatory) says the memory watcher must stop a PDF extraction that passes the production 1 GiB limit, and the red test `tests/test_documents.py::test_extraction_is_stopped_when_it_exceeds_the_memory_limit` had never been diagnosed (the 17 September handoff called it broken for an unrelated reason). Before this entry D136 was the highest decision at `8091d62`. The only memory control was `pdf._watch_memory`: a thread inside the extraction child that polls `ru_maxrss` every 50 ms and exits with code 3.

**Decision:** Product bug, not a test fault. Measured on macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Python 3.12.13 with `scripts/p9/memory_probe.py` (a one-page PDF whose Flate content stream decodes to N MiB, so the file stays small): before the fix the child was never stopped at the 100 MiB test limit (6 of 6 runs, 67 MiB decoded, peak resident size 951 to 1195 MiB until the probe killed it at 90 s) and never at the production 1 GiB limit (3 of 3 runs with 200 MiB decoded, peak 1223 to 1312 MiB, over the limit, killed by the probe at 90 s; three runs with 67 MiB decoded peaked at 938, 1025 and 903 MiB, so only one crossed 1 GiB and they are not offered as evidence). The pytest test alone passed once in 3.7 s and failed the next time with "extraction timed out" on the same code, and the serial baseline run failed it too, so it is not specific to `-n auto`; load as a contributing factor is not excluded or shown. Observed cause (`scripts/p9/gil_diagnosis.py`, saved output): the main thread sits inside `pymupdf.extra.page_get_textpage`, a C call that holds the interpreter lock, and neither the watchdog thread nor a second ticker thread ran for 8 s. A thread in the child cannot be relied on; the 90 s timeout was the only, late, stop.

`pdf.py::_run_watched` now runs the child under a watcher in the parent: `Popen` with stdout and stderr to temporary files, a wait of at most 50 ms (never more than the time left) per turn, the child's current resident size read from outside (`proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDTASKINFO)` through `ctypes` on macOS, `/proc/<pid>/statm` on Linux, no new dependency), SIGKILL over the limit with return code 3 and the old error text `extraction exceeded the memory limit`, `TimeoutExpired` past 90 s as before. A finished child is never reported as a lost watch. Fail-visible: on macOS and Linux, 20 unreadable turns in a row (one second) with the child alive kill it and `extract_pdf` returns `failed` with `extraction memory limit could not be watched`; a single unreadable turn is tolerated. The in-child thread stays as a second guard because `ocr.py`, `jats.py` and `arxiv_source.py` still use it. Limits, timeout and `MAX_MEMORY_BYTES` are unchanged. Windows still has no memory limit.

After the fix (extract mode, saved lines in `.local/p9-h0b/runs.jsonl`): 3 of 3 runs at the production 1 GiB limit with 200 MiB decoded stop with the old error text after 27, 32 and 36 s, sampled peak 1023.5 to 1023.7 MiB, kernel peak (`RUSAGE_CHILDREN`, one process per run) 1024.1 to 1024.4 MiB, i.e. stopped within about a MiB of the limit; 5 of 5 runs at the 100 MiB test limit stop in 0.3 s; a 20 MiB input (573 MiB peak, below the limit) finishes `succeeded` in 22 s. F09 passes with process evidence at the production threshold. The known red test passes and was stable in the runs kept in `.local/p9-h0b/test-runs.txt` (the known test alone 5 of 5, 0.5 s each; `tests/test_documents.py` 25 passed in three serial runs and one `-n auto` run; the opt-in test passed). New tests: the parent stops a child that holds the interpreter lock inside `PyDLL` calls past the limit, output and exit code survive without a pipe stall, a timeout kills and reaps the child, the deadline is not stretched, a lost watch is visible, a single unreadable turn and a child that ends mid-read are not failures, and an opt-in test at the production limit (`DEIXIS_P9_PRODUCTION_THRESHOLD=1`, about 30 s; the F09 run sets it and passed).

Judgements: the watcher reads current, not peak, resident size (a peak of another process is not available without privileges; macOS can compress pages, so a reading can fall below an earlier peak; the limit still reads "shortly after the size crosses it"); the 50 ms poll and 20-turn loss window are chosen values, not derived; `_libproc` caches a failed library load for the life of the process (no silent loss: the loss window turns it into a visible failure).

**Verification:** `tests/test_documents.py` (25 passed, 1 opt-in skipped, repeated in `-n 0` and `-n auto`, kept in `.local/p9-h0b/test-runs.txt`); the opt-in test passed; full pytest in the isolated environment: 3,781 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed (after the review fixes, 2 min 59 s at load 2 to 3) (the baseline on the clean export had the known failure; 3,772 passed + 1 failed + 2 skipped, plus 8 new tests and the formerly red one); Playwright 112 passed, lint 17 warnings, build ok; gpt-6.1-sol high plan review 2 rounds (round 1: 2 high, 6 medium, 1 low, all folded in; round 2: 0 high, 4 medium, 1 low, all folded in), code review 1 round (0 high, 3 medium and 2 low, all folded in: deadline checked on every exit path, record wording and decimals, raw-record validity, missing test records added).

**Limits:** Only `extract_pdf` was measured and fixed. `ocr.py`, `jats.py` and `arxiv_source.py` start their own children with the same in-child thread and probably have the same hole; not measured, not changed, so a 1 GiB limit on them is NOT established (open follow-up; if confirmed unenforced it is a P9 closing item under plan §4 rule 2). One input shape (one huge content-stream string) was used; other shapes, the claim that the limit prevents the allocation (it stops shortly after, within a MiB here, measured with slow growth of about 30 to 40 MiB/s on this machine) and Windows are not shown. Timings depend on this machine; the load average is recorded per run, and runs after the first of the final batch were taken under heavy foreign load (load 10 to 11) without a visible effect on the stop point. Growth figures come from single inputs, not a model.

## D137 — P6 slice 2 L7: the Development lines screen shows the stored read model, starts the link-finding run with its call ceiling, and lets a human remove, edit and add links

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-01, P6 slice 2 batch L7

**Context:** D130 to D136 built role columns, candidates, the contract, durable decisions, the flow and the read and edit API; nothing showed them. Before this entry D136 was the highest decision at `8091d62`. The [slice 2 note](product/p6-slice2-chain-of-ideas.md) §4.6, §13, §19 L7 and the batch prompt `docs/product/p6-slice2-l7-prompt.md` bind the scope.

**Decision:** The Evidence tab gets a "Table | Development lines" switch; the sub-view (`apps/web/src/lineage/`) renders the whole `GET .../lineage` read model with no list hidden and an explicit "None." for empty ones: status and counts (citation-list states kept apart from link counts), lines with roots, branches and merges and links as year-ordered rows that open `PassageSheet` at the stored anchor, cross relations, works without a placed link with all reasons and recorded details, proposals not accepted with fixed rejection sentences, the two citation-edge lists, run outcomes (`step_outcomes`, `not_sent_budget`, `failed_pairs`, shown whole and as filtered lists), stale and out-of-scope history in disclosures whose summaries always show counts, and a separate field-baseline panel. "Find development links" shows the plan (works, calls, ceiling, unselected, unsent, carried failures) and starts the run only from that plan's fingerprint; Start is disabled only when nothing is selected, a zero-call scan can start, and "Retry failed pairs" is always available. Human remove, edit and add use the pair `version` from `pair_decisions` (0 for a new pair) and the current revision id; the evidence picker offers current PDF passages of the later work from the asset text and sends the quote as typed; 409 and 422 show the server's message and keep typed text. Currency of old negative facts prints from `current`, `stale_reasons` and `unchecked` and never reads "current" for unchecked input. The view refetches on the research event cursor (a cell save does not bump the table version), on table version, run end and manual refresh, with one ordering guard shared by reads and writes. Run kind `lineage_links` shares the table-run controls; EN and TR strings and fixed maps for the eleven unplaceable reasons, stale reasons and rejection codes were added; forbidden words ("foundational", "founder", "novel", "original", "verified" for a quote) are absent from every DEIXIS string while stored titles, quotes and notes are shown byte for byte. `ConfirmDialog` gained an optional content slot. The fixture server has `[lineage]` (six synthetic works A to F: A to B and A to C linked, D `no_relation` on its mis-matched candidates, E `no_candidate`, F an unassessed stored edge) and `[lineage-reject]` (a second run rejects B to A as a `cycle`).

**Verification:** `apps/web/e2e/lineage.spec.ts` (real fixture server: scan, branching, anchor sheet, durable remove, add, edit, 422 and 409 handling, baseline, keyboard, forbidden-word scan, reduced motion, 1440 and 390 px light and dark; a mocked read model covering merge, history, all eleven reasons, all currency states, every list and long strings; plan and retry cases) plus `lineage-columns.spec.ts`; build, lint (17-warning baseline) and the full suites as recorded in the commit message. gpt-6.1-sol high: plan review 2 rounds (4 high folded in, then 0 high), code review 2 rounds (4 high fixed in round 1; round 2 0 high, 1 medium fixed by the orchestrator).

**Limits:** Synthetic data and a scripted model only: nothing shows that real corpora give useful lines or that the wording helps a reader. A stored quote is located text, not proof of support, and the screen says so. The Evidence page's sideways scroll on a phone is unchanged (D131); the new sub-view itself does not overflow at 390 px. A quote picker based on typed or selected text is the only evidence input. The pair CAS value can still go stale between opening a sheet and saving (409 handled). No report integration, no graph drawing. `skill_package_hash` unchanged (`sha256:371fcecb...`). No live service was touched; nothing was committed, pushed or published.

## D136 — P6 slice 2 L6: development lines are assembled and read from stored decisions, and a human can add, edit and remove links through the API; no screen exists yet

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-01, P6 slice 2 batch L6

**Context:** D130 accepts lines read at view time from the current decisions, with a human decision that a model run never overwrites. D131 to D135 built role columns, candidates, the contract, durable decisions and the flow. Nothing read the decisions back. Before this entry D135 was the highest decision in this checkout at `90ff783`. The [slice 2 note](product/p6-slice2-chain-of-ideas.md) §3, §4.1, §4.3 to §4.5, §12 "Montaj ve insan düzenleme" and "Alan tabanı", §19 L6 and the batch prompt `docs/product/p6-slice2-l6-prompt.md` bind the scope.

**Decision:** `workflow/lineage/assembly.py` is pure: from plain link records it builds weakly connected components of development links (roots with in-degree 0 and out-degree above 0, branches, merges, per-node neighbours, a `has_cycle` flag that reports and terminates on cyclic input), never lets `independent_parallel` build an edge, and maps per-row facts to the closed reason list (`not_run`, `no_pdf_text`, `no_candidate`, `no_relation`, `insufficient_evidence`, `rejected`, `not_sent_budget`, `step_failed`, `human_removed`, `cross_relation_only`, `stale_only`); a live row with no applicable reason gets `not_run`, meaning only "no recorded decision for this work". `workflow/lineage/view.py` reads one table in one synchronous transaction, with no write, model or provider call, and returns the components, the cross relations, `history.stale` and `history.out_of_scope` (kept apart, never rewritten), every live row that is not placed with all its reasons and a `details` list, every rejected proposal with `superseded` and the pair state, `pair_decisions` for every stored pair with its `version` (the CAS value a client needs to add a human link over a `no_relation`, `insufficient_evidence` or removed pair), `unassessed_edges` (a present citation edge into a scanned target with no mention found by a fresh model-free scan), `edges_into_unscanned_targets` as a separate list (no mention scan has run there, so no mention claim is made), the four citation-list states counted apart from link counts, and `step_outcomes`. Step outcomes (failed pairs, unsent pairs, failed or skipped chunks) are chained across all finished runs of the table, so a failure carried by a later run keeps its original time; an outcome is open until a later model revision or a current human decision closes the pair, and a chunk stays open until all its planned pairs are closed. Every historical negative fact carries `current` (true, false or null), `stale_reasons` and `unchecked`; a check that could not be made is never reported as current. `run.py` gained `stale_link_reasons` (the L5 active-link rule, now with reasons; `stale_link_revisions` is a wrapper with unchanged results) and `decision_currency` for negative and rejected model decisions (scope, node snapshots, mention passage ids). The field baseline (`GET .../lineage/baseline`) uses the live rows, stored counts and registered types only, the D132 representative (membership creation time), five shown entries and all entries, unknown counts never zero. Routes: `GET .../lineage`, `GET .../lineage/baseline`, `POST .../lineage/links` (201), `PUT` and `DELETE .../lineage/links/{id}`, each returning the fresh view; add and edit pass the current stale map to L4, remove does not; errors keep L4's mapping (version or revision mismatch and re-adding over an active link are 409, a quote not located in the later work's passage, a cycle, a non-live end and shape errors are 422). `apps/web/src/api.ts` gained the types only.

Judgements: a link end that no longer heads its work gets the display flag `not_head_ends` and is NOT stale. This knowingly relaxes note §3 and §12, which ask for re-evaluation or a `stale` mark on a head change: a decision does not store which version headed the work, so "the head changed after the decision" cannot be told from "never the head" without a migration; L6 has none. The note is aligned. `scanned` means recorded as a target by a finished run and live and eligible now; `no_candidate` is recomputed from today's passages with no pair exclusion, never read from an old record. Components and reasons are read-time only and have no persistent identity. The L5-dependent test "a model run does not overwrite a human decision" is closed end to end through the routes and a real run with the fake adapter.

**Verification:** `tests/test_lineage_assembly.py` (pure), `tests/test_lineage_view.py` (real database: components, diamond, cross relations, every stale reason, out-of-scope, every unplaceable reason, carried failures, currency, pair decisions, read-only SQL trace, baseline) and `tests/test_lineage_api.py` (routes, CAS, 409 and 422 mapping, CSRF, idempotency, the human-survives-a-run test, the PDF kept by evidence created through the POST route), plus the existing lineage suites; `tests/test_lineage_mentions.py` purity test now lists `assembly` as pure and `view` as database-reading. Full pytest by the orchestrating session: 3,774 passed and 1 failed (the known `test_extraction_is_stopped_when_it_exceeds_the_memory_limit`); web build passed, lint 17 warnings (baseline), Playwright 112 passed. gpt-6.1-sol high: plan review 3 rounds (round 1 ran twice: 4 and 3 high; round 2: 3 high; round 3: 0 high), code review 1 round (0 high, 1 medium and 2 low, all fixed by the orchestrator).

**Limits:** Synthetic data and a fake adapter only: no real-model call, no measurement, so nothing shows that real corpora give useful lines or that the reasons help a reader. Stored quotes are located text, not proof that a passage supports the relation. Currency checks compare recorded inputs; failure and unsent records that hold no send record are reported unknown, and negative revisions record mention passage ids but not their text, so text changes under an unchanged id are unchecked. Head change is only a flag. The mention scan behind `unassessed_edges` and `no_candidate` is redone at read time over scanned targets and is unmeasured on large tables. No screen, fetch function or copy exists (L7). `skill_package_hash` is unchanged (`sha256:371fcecb...`). No live service was restarted; nothing was committed, pushed or published.

## D135 — P6 slice 2 L5: the flow that scans, plans, asks and publishes development links runs end to end with a fake model; no route shows its results yet

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-01, P6 slice 2 batch L5 (L5a model-free, L5b fake adapter, one commit)

**Context:** D130 accepts per-pair development links decided by a model step over mention candidates; D131 to D134 supplied role columns, model-free candidates, the contract and durable storage. L5 joins them. Before this entry D134 was the highest decision in this checkout at `8162c8b`. The [slice 2 note](product/p6-slice2-chain-of-ideas.md) §4.3, §9, §12 "Akış", §19 L5 and the batch prompt `docs/product/p6-slice2-l5-prompt.md` bind the scope.

**Decision:** `workflow/lineage/run.py` builds, from one synchronous read, a snapshot of the table's live rows (live = non-removed table row, active corpus member, selection `included`; L4's rule), the three node cells of every row from the CURRENT cell revision only (a pending proposal is never read as the value; a row with no current revision is `missing`), and the `lineage_target` of a chunk. A run reads at most 25 eligible targets (a live row with a current `pdf_page`; stored text, not reviewed text). Targets are classified before any scan by a cheap target fingerprint (`new`, `changed`, `retry`, or `settled` and skipped), scanned with L2's `find_candidates`, and their pending pairs packed with the REAL message size (the StepInput after handle conversion, at most 48,000 characters, 8 candidates, 24 passages, three calls per target; the planning measure is an upper bound because the stub run's budget has the most digits). A pair is pending unless its latest `model_propose` revision carries its current pair fingerprint and is accepted or rejected with `anchor_not_found`, `same_work` or `cycle`; known-failed pairs (a terminal failure recorded for the same sent fingerprint with no later revision) are left out until their fingerprint changes or the request says `retry_failed`. Pairs that do not fit one call alone and candidates beyond three calls are recorded as `not_sent_budget`, never as "no relation". The plan (rules, selected targets, chunks, not-selected and not-sent lists, budget) is frozen in `runs.target_json` (new run kind `lineage_links`, stage `synthesis`, no migration); `GET .../lineage/plan` previews it with the call ceiling `C * (1 + repairs) * (1 + rate-limit retries)` (today `6 * C`) and `POST .../lineage/runs` (202, `Idempotency-Key` per research and checked against the table, a preview fingerprint that must still match or the request is 409, `retry_failed`) queues it. A paused lineage run of the same table blocks a new one. A plan with selected targets but no call is allowed, otherwise the same first 25 works would be offered forever.

`ResearchFlow._lineage_links` sends one job per planned chunk through the shared limiter. A step that already succeeded is used as it is (its output holds the send record) and is judged at publication; a chunk is sent only without one. Publication happens only when every planned chunk is terminal, in one transaction that re-checks the run is `running`, the scope revision and the table, then calls `LineageStore.apply_model_proposals` over all chunks (so `(to, from)` order is global), and writes a `lineage_publication` record (published, `step_failed`, `failed_pairs`, per-target `settled` or `incomplete`, `not_sent_budget`, skipped). A pause, cancel, scope change or budget pause publishes nothing; stored outputs are used on resume; a failed or unsent pair never becomes `no_relation`. L4 gained `input_stale` (a proposal whose sent fingerprint, or any cited or mention passage digest or currency, no longer matches the database is stored rejected with `stale_input`). `stale_link_revisions` names the active links that must leave the cycle graph: any link, human or model, whose evidence passage is no longer current; a model link whose node snapshots or scope changed; deliberately not the selection revision. `_model_step` gained four opt-in hooks (`max_message_chars`, `resend_guard`, `send_gate`, `attempt_record`); with none passed every other task behaves exactly as before.

Three identifiers are kept apart, which refines the note's single "input fingerprint": the planned chunk key (the step `operation_key`, stable for the run), the pair fingerprint (selection and reuse key, stored by L4 as the revision's fingerprint, computed from the StepInput payload so planning, sending and publication agree) and the send record of an attempt (what was really sent: pair fingerprints, link versions, shown-passage digests, the selection revision). The note's selection-revision rule is kept literally: any inclusion change re-asks every pair, a stated cost.

Judgements: stage `synthesis` (the schema allows it, `i18n.ts` labels it); no migration; model-free "no candidate" outcomes are stored in the publication record, not in new tables; a budget pause cannot progress by resume (the counter and ceiling do not reset), cancel and a new preview is the way; fixture-server scripting and web kind labels are left to L7 (the current web would describe a lineage run as an answer run; nothing in L5 changes apps/web, so build, lint and Playwright were not run); the three-round plan-review limit ended with one open high (the send record taken from the real payload) which was folded in without a fourth round.

**Verification:** `tests/test_lineage_plan.py` (model-free planning: node builder, eligibility, real-message packing, selection classes and the 25 limit, fingerprints, plan content and budget, request and API errors) and `tests/test_lineage_flow.py` (fake adapter and real `_model_step`: publication, T11 integration, chunks and budget checks before every send, stops and recovery, order and atomicity, in-flight changes recorded as rejected revisions, send records, second runs, stale edges), plus the existing suites. Full pytest run by the orchestrating session outside the implementer's sandbox: 3,636 passed and 1 failed (the known `test_extraction_is_stopped_when_it_exceeds_the_memory_limit`); the implementer's sandbox run showed further failures from denied loopback binds and process access, which are not results of this change. gpt-6.1-sol high: plan review 3 rounds (7, 4 and 1 high, all folded in), code review 4 rounds (round 1: 2 high, 1 medium; round 2: 1 high, 1 medium; round 3: 1 high, 1 medium; each fixed; round 4: hazır, 0 findings).

**Limits:** Synthetic data and a fake adapter only: no real-model call, no provider request, no measurement, so nothing shows that a model produces useful links, that the 25-work and eight-candidate bounds fit real papers, or that the call count and time are acceptable. Stored quotes are located text, not proof that a passage supports the relation. A `cycle` rejection is not retried until the fingerprint changes. Any inclusion change re-asks every pair. The mention finder's recall is still unmeasured. No route shows lineage results or edits links (L6), no screen exists (L7), and the web does not label the new run kind. `skill_package_hash` is unchanged (`sha256:371fcecb...`). No live service was restarted; nothing was committed, pushed or published.

## D134 — P6 slice 2 L4: development-link decisions, their evidence and the human edits have durable, append-only storage; nothing calls it from the flow yet

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-01, P6 slice 2 batch L4

**Context:** D130 accepts per-pair development-link decisions; D131 to D133 supplied role columns, model-free candidates and the contract. L4 adds only the durable layer. Before this entry D133 was the highest decision in this checkout at `93e2d2c`. The [slice 2 note](product/p6-slice2-chain-of-ideas.md) §4.3, §5, §12 "Depolama", §19 L4 and the batch prompt `docs/product/p6-slice2-l4-prompt.md` bind the scope.

**Decision:** Migration `0059_lineage_links.sql` rebuilds `runs` (0046 pattern, `lineage_links` added to the kind CHECK, every old row kept) and adds `lineage_links`, `lineage_link_revisions` and `lineage_link_evidence` as `WITHOUT ROWID` tables with the CHECKs of §5. Eleven triggers: evidence only from the later work; revisions and evidence cannot be updated and can be deleted only under a research or table purge authorization; identity columns of a pair cannot change; a pair's pointer must name an accepted, structurally valid revision of the same pair, with at least one evidence row when it is a link; and insert guards so no conflict clause (`INSERT OR REPLACE`, upsert, an explicit rowid, which is why the tables have no rowid) can rewrite history. `workflow/lineage/store.py` (`LineageStore`) records and publishes model proposals in a fixed rule order (same work, live endpoints, human precedence, stale input, located quotes, directed cycle); a rejected proposal is stored with its code and changes nothing else; an accepted one becomes the pair's current decision only when the pointer is empty or the current decision is a model's with a different input fingerprint; batches apply in `(to, from)` order inside one savepoint-protected transaction; replays return the stored revision. Human add, edit and remove need the pair's `version` and, for edit and remove, the current revision id; an active human link needs a located quote from the later work; a human removal is never reactivated by a model run. Six lifecycle hooks: `_delete_tables` (pointers to NULL, then evidence, revisions, pairs), `cited_source_versions`, `research_cites_asset`, `asset_impact`, `table_impact` and `trash_table` (blocked while a lineage run is active).

Judgements: the input fingerprint lives inside `inputs_json` as `{"fingerprint", "inputs"}` (the note's §5 has no column); the cycle graph is the current active links with live endpoints minus edges the caller names as stale by revision id (L4 cannot know node-input staleness; a refreshed link re-enters the graph); `independent_parallel` needs `source_stated` for humans as for the model; removal has no endpoint condition; a revision's `created_at` is bumped by one millisecond when needed so a pair's history keeps insertion order; `rejection_code` has no SQL enum (the note gives none); `table_impact` gained `lineage_links` and `lineage_human_edits`, `asset_impact` gained `lineage_links`; the L2 purity test now skips `store.py`; `active_links` is unfiltered and L6 filters it.

**Verification:** `tests/test_lineage_store.py` (checks, append-only and pointer guards, every REPLACE and rowid variant, every rejection code and the rule order, parameters, fingerprint rules, diamond and cycle cases, stale-by-revision, batch order, atomicity inside an outer transaction, replay, the human primitives, the six hooks), migration tests (every old run kind and the rows pointing at runs survive; empty pre-0059 database; vocabularies equal the CHECK lists), backup restore identity, corpus protection and the PDF route. Full pytest: 3,462 passed plus the known memory-limit failure. gpt-6.1-sol high: plan review 3 rounds (round 3 clean; 1 high each in rounds 1 and 2, fixed), code review 3 rounds (high in rounds 1 and 2, REPLACE and rowid bypass, fixed; round 3 0 high, 1 medium insertion order, fixed).

**Limits:** Synthetic storage only: no flow, route, view model or model call uses it; no real model output was stored. Node-input and extraction staleness are not detected here (the caller must name stale revisions or the graph counts them). Stored quotes are located text, not proof that a quote supports the relation. The evidence union branch of `cited_source_versions` cannot be isolated under the same-source trigger, so it is tested combined. Wrong-file PDF removal still denies access even when lineage cites the file (unchanged route behavior). SQLite backup carries the tables whole; restore identity is tested on synthetic data.

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-01, P6 slice 2 batch L3

**Context:** D130 accepts a model step that decides, per candidate pair, whether the later work's own passages state a development relation to an earlier work. D132 supplies the model-free candidates. L3 builds only the road such a step travels, in the pattern of D127 (per-field handles). Before this entry D132 was the highest decision in this checkout at `2f85f6c`. The note left several shapes open; closed as follows: exactly three cells per node, `cell_id` a nullable `cel_` id, nullable revision fields, `value` at most 500 characters, `state` the seven cell states plus `missing`, `flags` a closed object of five required booleans, `evidence_quotes` a string array with no count or length cap. `check_step_input` gains `_check_lineage_target` (target present iff the task is a lineage task; the plain `candidates` list, `candidate_ids` and every other target or `claims_under_review` absent; the allowlist carries exactly `candidate_ids` (empty), `source_ids`, `passage_ids`; `to` and every `from` are shown in `sources` and allowed; same source id or same shown `work_id` never pairs; every passage belongs to the later work; at most 24 unique passages; each mention passage is shown and unrepeated; each node has the three roles once; a `missing` cell carries no stored content; conflicting repeated source or passage records are refused). `_check_lineage_links` checks that every candidate is answered once (duplicates counted), the field shape of `link` against every other decision, `independent_parallel` only with `source_stated`, evidence passages from the shown later-work passages, each quote located by `locate_anchor`, a duplicate located quote inside one decision (the seen-set resets per decision because the later evidence key is per pair), and for `source_stated` at least one of that candidate's own mention passages. The best-effort pass that reports an unknown ID beside a schema error now covers lineage tasks. `flow.py` changes are plumbing only: `lineage_links` in `HANDLE_TASKS`, a `lineage_target` parameter in `_step_input` and `_model_step`, and handle resolution on lineage output; no eligibility, selection, packing, run kind or store call. ## D132 — P6 slice 2 L2: model-free mention candidates, citation-edge states and the field baseline are pure functions

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-01, P6 slice 2 batch L2

**Context:** D130 separates text-mentioned candidate pairs from stored citation edges and accepts two corpus lists over stored values. D131 supplies node roles, but L2 needs no role columns or database access. Before this entry, D131 was the highest decision in this checkout at `7cd6820`. The [slice 2 note](product/p6-slice2-chain-of-ideas.md) §19 L2 and the batch prompt specify pure calculations over snapshots supplied by later callers.

**Decision:** Add `workflow/lineage/{__init__,mentions,edges,candidates,baseline}.py` with frozen snapshot/result dataclasses and deterministic functions. Imports are limited to the standard library, `workflow/source_keys.py` and other lineage modules. Nothing reads or writes the database, starts a process, calls a provider or model, or changes flow, API, persistence, contracts or web code.

`prepare_passages` normalizes later-work passages once using `_ascii`, casefold and alphanumeric tokens separated by one space. The first usable author surname follows `family_name`'s selection, particle and suffix rules without its ten-character truncation; hyphenated parts remain consecutive tokens. Each surname occurrence followed within 60 normalized characters by an accepted four-digit year (any century, optional lowercase suffix) counts once. Accepted years include the record's own year and supplied same-work version years. Title matching removes the same stopwords from both sequences and counts maximal runs of matching 5-grams. `mention_rules` records normalization, text definition, gap, year direction, stopwords and limits. A mention retains every passage hit and selects at most three passage IDs by count descending, page ascending with abstract first, then passage ID.

Edges derive the four states from read-list flags and normalized OpenAlex identifiers. Only `absent_in_read_list` sets the unexpected-missing-edge warning. A present edge enters `unassessed_edges` only when its target was scanned and its pair is neither a mention candidate nor human-excluded. Unscanned targets remain distinct from scanned targets with no mention. Candidates require a mention, reject same-work pairs, keep the first duplicate source-version row, retain reversed-year warnings, and honor an explicit excluded-pair parameter. Target order is table position; candidate and packing order is match count descending, earlier-row position ascending, then source-version ID. There is no 25-target limit here.

Packing defaults to count-only limits of eight candidates per chunk and three chunks per target. An explicit fit predicate may split sooner. Empty chunks use no quota; a candidate that cannot fit alone is recorded as `too_large_for_one_call`, and remaining candidates after the call limit are `beyond_call_limit`. No candidate is silently lost. `passage_budget_fits` is an explicit proxy counting unique mention passages and their text lengths; missing lengths fail rather than count as zero. L5 will record these reasons under `not_sent_budget` and enforce its real StepInput message budget.

The caller supplies all current included baseline versions. Each work's representative follows D48: head, active asset, membership creation time, source-version ID. Count, count date and type come only from that representative. `versions_considered` records source-version IDs in this priority order. Known counts sort descending with work-ID ties; unknown counts are counted separately. Registered review types sort by work ID ignoring case for type comparison. Both lists retain every entry, expose their first five and total, and carry included-citation denominators. Target identity is the union of its included versions' OpenAlex IDs; this resolves identity without filling representative metadata. Only read versions contribute references, and each other work counts once. Unresolved targets or no read other-work lists produce `count=None`; otherwise the count applies only to the read lists, with `lists_read` and `other_works` reported.

**Verification:** All 51 requested named tests and two additional guard tests are present: 11 mention, 9 edge, 18 candidate/packing and 15 baseline tests, all on synthetic snapshots without a database or network (they pin the rules record, check the import allow-list with AST, patch socket/subprocess to fail, and check deterministic results and unchanged inputs). Final run of the orchestrating session outside the implementer's sandbox, in the worktree: full pytest 3,203 passed and 1 failed (the known `test_extraction_is_stopped_when_it_exceeds_the_memory_limit`), 62 warnings; the implementer's own sandbox run showed further failures from denied loopback binds and process access, which are not results of this change and are not repeated here. gpt-6.1-sol high: plan review 2 rounds (1 high fixed: the year rule had been limited to 19xx/20xx; 4 medium fixed), code review 1 round (0 high, 0 medium).

**Limits:** Nothing reads these functions yet; database snapshot construction and use belong to L5 and L6. Synthetic data only, no real-model or provider call, no measurement. The mention finder's recall on real passages is unmeasured; numbered citations are missed, shared surnames can produce false candidates, and reference-list passages may match. A candidate is not a link; a citation edge creates no candidate. The 60-character gap is measured in normalized text and the year must follow the surname, a recorded judgement. Titles with fewer than five significant tokens are never searched. Packing defaults to count-only; the explicit passage-text proxy does not enforce the real 48,000-character StepInput message limit, which is L5's responsibility. The `O(|T|·P·R)` cost is unmeasured. "review" is the registered type and its provider is not stored: `Registered type: review. Which provider wrote the type is not stored.` Counts are stored numbers, not quality, and no "foundational" claim is made. No live service was restarted; nothing was committed, pushed or published.

## D131 — P6 slice 2 L1: node columns carry a stable lineage role added only by an explicit action

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-10-01, P6 slice 2 batch L1

**Context:** D130 accepts three visible node columns in the P5 evidence table. Later batches need to identify their roles after a user renames or moves them. This batch implements only the role marker and its explicit addition action. The highest decision on local `main` was D130 when this entry was allocated.

**Decision:** Migration `0058_lineage_role.sql` adds nullable `table_columns.lineage_role`, restricted to `problem`, `change` and `uncertainty`, with at most one active column per role per table. Existing columns remain unmarked. `TableStore.add_development_columns` appends only missing roles in that order, using the names and verbatim instructions from the slice 2 note §6, as ordinary `text` columns with `origin='user'`. All inserts, the one table-version bump and one change event share a transaction. Replay precedes the expected-version check and includes removed-column history. Revision keys are `lineage-columns:{research_id}:{table_id}:{key}:{role}`; the leading prefix separates them from the research-prefixed ordinary column and template writers. Another table or research may use the same client key independently. If all roles are already active, the action writes nothing and bumps nothing.

The role lives on the column row, outside its append-only definition revisions. Renames, moves and instruction edits preserve it; definition changes retain the existing stale-cell behavior. A role column cannot change to a non-text format. Removal retains the role, and restoring it is refused with a plain 422 conflict when another active column holds that role. Ordinary user columns, model-suggested columns and templates never receive or copy roles. The API exposes the role and adds `POST /api/researches/{research_id}/tables/{table_id}/lineage/columns`, with the existing CSRF and expected-version checks, optional bounded idempotency header, and a 200 table view. It queues no run. The Evidence tab offers the action beside Add column and in the first-column prompt, hides it when all roles are present, and locks the role column's answer-format control with a visible explanation. Existing components and styles are reused; copy has English and Turkish entries.

**Verification:** 19 new synthetic backend cases (18 L1 cases including parameter variants, one migration case) and one new Playwright case. The implementer's own sandbox could not run the browser suite (it refused loopback ports and Chrome) and its full pytest run showed five sandbox failures; those runs are not results of this change and are not repeated here. Final run of the orchestrating session, outside that sandbox, in the worktree: full pytest 3,150 passed and 1 failed (the known `test_extraction_is_stopped_when_it_exceeds_the_memory_limit`), 62 warnings; all existing `test_report_*.py` and `test_evidence_tables.py` cases passed unchanged. `npm run build` passed (large-chunk warning); `npm run lint` 17 warnings (baseline) and no errors; fresh-build Playwright 112 passed (111 before, plus `lineage-columns.spec.ts`), run as `DEIXIS_ACCEPTANCE_DIR=/tmp/deixis-acceptance-l1b npm run test:acceptance`; `git diff --check` passed. The new control and the locked format control were screenshotted at 1440 and 390 px in light and dark and looked at: the button sits in the toolbar row and stays inside the viewport at 390 px; the column sheet shows the disabled format control with its one-line explanation. The Playwright case's 390 px assertion covers only the new button: the Evidence page already scrolls sideways on a phone (the long fill-button label and the wide grid), which this batch did not change and does not claim to fix. Existing test changes: `tests/test_migrations.py` (an applied-migration list pin extended to 0058) and one line in `tests/test_arxiv_source_migration.py` (`== 57` became `>= 57`, because 0058 exists; its row, link, trigger and search-index assertions are unchanged). No live service was restarted; no real model was called; nothing was committed, pushed or published.

**Limits:** The role feeds nothing yet. Synthetic data only, no real-model call, no measurement; the quality of the three columns' cells is unmeasured. The three columns are ordinary columns to the report, so adding them changes `report_ready` and the snapshot, recorded rather than mitigated as accepted in D130. A template does not carry roles. No route removes a role. Restoring a removed role column can conflict and is refused. A no-op with all roles present stores no idempotency record: if a role column is later removed, repeating that previously unused key adds its replacement. The skill package hash is unchanged at `sha256:cef7c08662f102f5e7dd56f5203ecb142fc28b91eebeddbfb5b3bb0bbad3b6bb`, pinned in the synthetic L1 test consistently with the existing report test. No live service was restarted, and nothing was committed, pushed or published.

## D130 — P6 slice 2 (Chain of Ideas): evidence-linked development lines are accepted for implementation as a core of nine batches; the zero-continuation marker, forward check and report entry are deferred

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-30 as a design (docs only, nothing implemented, no model call, no measurement). Decided jointly by Claude and gpt-6.1-sol (high, read-only) on the owner's instruction; the owner was not asked. The number was taken from `main` at `4eb0b87` (D129 was the highest); re-check it before committing. Authority for scope: [the design note](product/p6-slice2-chain-of-ideas.md) §18 and §19.

**Context:** The owner chose Chain of Ideas as the synthesis method on 14 September 2026. The slice 2 note was drafted on 17 September, before slice 1's code, D95 citation chaining and D127 handles, and waited for ten owner questions. Re-checking it against `4eb0b87` found stale statements: a `chain_links` table already exists (migration 0050, D95), reference lists and OpenAlex identifiers are already stored (`record_references`, `identifier_mappings`), `legacy` discovery is gone, the report schemas are already v2, there is no column role marker, and the report has never completed on a real model (D124, D126, D128).

**Decision:** Build a core and defer the rest. Naming uses `lineage_*` so it cannot be confused with D95's citation chaining. (1) The three node cells are visible `text` columns with a stable `table_columns.lineage_role`, added only by an explicit action, at most one per role per table; their meaning lives in each column's `instruction`. (2) The citation edge is derived at read time from `record_references` and `identifier_mappings` with four states (`present`, `absent_in_read_list`, `unresolved`, `not_read`); it never creates a link and never reaches the model as a candidate. (3) The field baseline is computed on request from stored counts and recorded types of the included works, two short lists, with no new queries and no word "foundational". (4) Six relations; `independent_parallel` is a cross-relation outside chains. (5) Analyst-inference links are distinguished on screen; report entry waits. (6) A person may add a link only with an anchor located in a stored passage of the later work. (7) The view is a list under the table in the Evidence tab; no graph. (8) One run takes at most 25 works with stored PDF text; candidates go to the model in calls of at most eight. (9) and (10) The "no continuation in corpus" marker, the user-started forward check, bounded expansion and the promotion record are slice 2b; report sections III, VI and VII are slice 2c. A link is stored per table and per source-version pair as append-only revisions with `link`, `no_relation`, `insufficient_evidence` and `removed` decisions and a rejected disposition with a stored code; chains, components and the baseline are computed on read and not stored. A link needs a quote located in the later work's passage; the code checks location, direction, directed cycles and same-work ends, not meaning. The model step is a new task `lineage_links` with its own schema (v1), D127-style handles and method file `synthesis.md` (`skill_package_hash` will move). Nine batches, seven without real-model calls; the real-model measurement (R12 to R15) is the last batch with its own freeze rule and a corpus never used in development. The measured H9 checkout stays fixed in product code, methods, schemas and validators from freeze through final recording; slice 2 batches run before or after that window, or in a separate fixed checkout.

**Evidence:** Read-only comparison of the note against `main` at `4eb0b87` (code, migrations, schemas, `docs/decisions.md`) by Claude and, separately, gpt-6.1-sol; corrections from Sol's decision round and two review rounds (the second ended with no high finding) are in the note. One public OpenAlex request on 2026-09-30 showed that `type:review` exists (1,031,211 works, first result the PRISMA 2020 statement). This entry records a design decision: no lineage implementation, live-provider run, model call or scientific validation is established.

**Limits:** A design decision, not a verified implementation. Mention finding misses numbered citations, and common surnames can produce false candidates; its recall is unmeasured. Budget numbers (25 works, 8 candidates per call, 24 passages and 48,000 characters per step) are borrowed and unmeasured. The node columns are ordinary columns to the report, so adding them changes `report_ready` and the snapshot; this is recorded, not mitigated. A located quote does not prove the model's relation. Whether the real Codex connection runs concurrent turns in parallel is unmeasured. The slice 3 note still names tables from the earlier draft (`field_baseline_selections`, `citation_expansions`, `chain_end_uncertainties`); it must be aligned when slice 3 closes.

## D129 — Report sections: the one repair pairs each failing cell anchor with its own cell's quotes, and a failed section's reason is shown

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-09-30, P6 slice 1 batch P19

**Context:** D128's last P16 run stopped at section IV on `anchor_not_in_cell_evidence` in both calls. The existing repair sent the issues and the StepInput but did not pair a failing anchor with its own cell's stored quotes. D121 retained section reasons without displaying them; D122's assembly-only draft header counted zero invalid sections without naming the refused rule.

**Decision:** Specialise the existing single schema repair for `report_section` only. Code builds per-anchor context from the stored StepInput and the failed, ID-resolved draft: anchor index, claim key, cell, failed quote, that cell's stored evidence quotes and passage IDs, and claims citing it. Only allowlisted cells and `anchor_not_in_cell_evidence` issues at an anchor's quote path qualify. The message uses D127's cell and passage handles and adds fixed guidance: a located quote does not establish support; the model must rewrite an unsupported claim or remove its cell citation and anchor, and removing a claim without remaining support requires a visible `insufficient_evidence` entry naming its `claim_key`. Code never chooses, replaces or deletes a quote, citation or claim. Validators, evidence sets, allowlists, repair count, failure persistence and report resume behavior are unchanged; no report salvage is added. `references/report.md` records the support boundary beside the cell-anchor rule, with dated P19 provenance.

The timeline reads the first stored reason for each failed or must-be-rewritten section from the run; the report section notice reads its own first validation issue. English and Turkish phrases use the code only, with a code-with-spaces fallback; raw identifiers, quotes and model-written messages/details are not rendered by these notices. Missing reasons retain the existing copy. The report read model exposes the run's error only when it is an assembly issue list. An assembly-only draft names the first three distinct refused rules in order, then the remaining count, excluding only rules ending `_warning` whose detail starts `WARNING:`. Markdown follows the same rule; a nonzero invalid-section count retains its existing line. `[report-bad-anchor]` makes scripted section IV fail its cell anchor in both calls.

**Verification:** 43 new synthetic backend cases (32 anchor/repair, 11 API/export). Final run of the orchestrating session, outside the implementer's sandbox, in the worktree: full pytest 3,131 passed and 1 failed (the known `test_extraction_is_stopped_when_it_exceeds_the_memory_limit`), 62 warnings; `npm run build` passed; `npm run lint` 17 warnings (baseline) and no errors; fresh-build Playwright 111 passed (109 before, plus a label test and the bad-anchor case), run as `DEIXIS_ACCEPTANCE_DIR=/tmp/deixis-acceptance-p19 npm run test:acceptance`. The new failed-section and assembly-only draft states were screenshotted at 1440 and 390 px in light and dark and looked at: the timeline line `IV failed: a cited quote was not found in that table cell's stored evidence`, the sheet notice with the same reason, and the header `DRAFT: the assembly check refused the report (banned word)`. The implementer's own sandbox could not launch Chrome or bind loopback ports (its pytest run showed six sandbox failures, its Playwright run failed before page creation); those are not results of this change. Existing test changes are limited to D125's package-hash pin and the report-flow helper's optional distinct synthetic cell quotes. No live service was restarted; no real model was called, and no change was committed, pushed or published.

**Limits:** Synthetic fake and scripted models only, no real-model call, no measurement. The repair guidance changes a prompt; whether it lowers real-model anchor failures is unmeasured. A later success on the known corpus would not be independent validation, because this fix was developed after seeing that corpus's failure. A located anchor still does not prove the claim is supported: assembly and deterministic validation of the model review check location and wording, not meaning. The runtime review method explicitly asks the model to read for meaning; that remains a fallible assessment, not verified support. `anchor_not_in_passage` and all other codes receive no specialised guidance. The series closed by D128 stays closed; this is not a fourth attempt. Real-model acceptance for the report remains an open question. The package hash changes from `sha256:52775258f530aa6a51513488f2aea37d0b7e609ffebe23d06451fd8ef0ae81ac` to `sha256:cef7c08662f102f5e7dd56f5203ecb142fc28b91eebeddbfb5b3bb0bbad3b6bb`.

## D127 — Show per-step citation handles in all four report tasks and reject output IDs outside the shown evidence

**Status:** accepted (implemented, uncommitted)
**Date:** 2026-09-30, P6 slice 1 batch P18

**Context:** D126's second P16 run stopped because section IV copied a long passage ID with two characters missing, twice. D12 already gives answer and cell steps short IDs. Report steps lacked both display conversion and output resolution; section anchors, count members, gap bases and nearest matches also lacked membership checks and could reach citation-link construction with unknown IDs.

**Decision:** `report_plan`, `report_section`, `report_phrase_repair` and `report_review` use report-specific, field-by-field mappings in `domain/contracts.py`, dispatched through the existing handle functions and both model-step paths. Passages, sources, cells and columns use `psg_P0000001`, `srv_S0000001`, `cel_L0000001` and `col_C0000001`. Numbering restarts per step and is recomputed from its stored StepInput: passages and sources in record order, cells in target order, columns in target order followed by allowlist, cells, gap candidates and plan axes. Glossary-only passages follow the shown passages; failed-row sources follow the shown sources, then review count sources in section/claim order, numerator before denominator. Remaining plan-role and review-count columns follow the primary column order, in explicit input-field order. First occurrence wins. Display-only references acquire handles without acquiring citation, count or matching permission. The stored input, succeeded result and evidence links retain real IDs; messages and raw sessions retain the handles sent and received. Quotes, prose, revision IDs and envelopes are untouched. Resolution is restricted to the field's ID kind, with the existing leading-zero rule extended to cells; correct real IDs remain accepted. Unknown IDs are repaired once and then fail; D56 salvage remains answer-only.

Every section output passage, cell, column and source field is checked against the real step allowlist (sources also include the source versions of shown cells). Plan IDs retain their existing membership checks and issue codes. For wrong-kind strings, report validation records the unknown-ID issue alongside the schema issue, even at the same path; non-string values remain schema errors. Phrase repair retains its existing runtime input: empty sources, passages and cells, plus the frozen plan, columns and flagged sentences. It receives no new evidence. `references/report.md` requires exact handle copying, allowlisted use and no citation to a glossary-only passage; its provenance records P18. No schema, fixture or migration changed. The runtime package hash changes from `sha256:08f1bdeadc63b809bdf6d123a1e77889cada14d64d3e851c3d9fe25bfb2704ee` to `sha256:52775258f530aa6a51513488f2aea37d0b7e609ffebe23d06451fd8ef0ae81ac`; no hash manifest exists or is required by integrity checks.

**Evidence:** The requested contracts/StepInput/report-flow check passed 189 tests. P18 adds 61 synthetic cases covering each output ID field, display-only references, wrong-kind IDs, leading zeros, stored messages/results/links, phrase-repair evidence boundaries and a section that stops after one repair without salvage. The full backend suite ran: 3,083 passed and six failed, with 62 warnings. The accepted document-memory test reported `extraction timed out`; four arXiv fetch tests could not bind a temporary loopback socket (`PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted`), and the embedding-service orphan-runner test could not enumerate processes for `pkill`. The five sandbox failures repeated in a serial run (five failed, six warnings); none was parallel-only. Package integrity and `git diff --check` passed. Three existing test functions changed: the displayed report StepInput expectation, the invalid anchor's additional membership issue, and D125's pinned package hash.

**Limits:** This deliberately narrows scripted section outputs: a count or nearest match that names a source from the frozen snapshot but absent from the step's shown evidence now fails here, although assembly previously accepted such count members. Failed-row and review-count display handles do not expand that source set. Existing `_step_input` construction already allowlists columns named by cells, gap candidates and plan axes; this batch preserves those permissions and adds none through display conversion. Synthetic tests establish mapping, membership, persistence and bounded-failure behavior; no real model was called and no reduction in model copy-error frequency or report-quality improvement was measured. Targeted report browser acceptance was attempted but stopped at `playwright: command not found`; this checkout lacks `apps/web/node_modules` and `apps/web/dist`, and no dependencies were installed. Live services were not restarted.

## D125 — A report can be written with recorded failed rows, only by an explicit choice, and those rows stay out of its evidence

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-30 as P6 slice 1 batch P17 (prompt `docs/product/p6-slice1-p17-prompt.md`). The number was taken from `origin/main` (D124 was the highest); re-check it before committing. Scope decided jointly by Claude and gpt-6.1-sol after D124.

**Context:** D124 stopped at the table: 21 of 175 cells were missing because three of 25 included sources had failed (two with no stored text, one extraction that failed after its repair), so `report_ready` was false and no report could start. `report_ready` already had a `continue_with_failed` parameter that nothing passed, and the design note (section 6) foresees the owner continuing with failed rows.

**Decision:** `POST /reports` takes `continue_with_failed` (default false); the choice is stored in the run target (only when true) and passed to the runner's own readiness check and to `save_snapshot`. Continuing is allowed only when every missing cell comes from a recorded failure (an `inaccessible` revision, or a failed or outcome-unknown extraction step of this scope revision) and at least one included row is complete; an untried cell, a row outside the table, or all rows failed still block. The snapshot keeps every included source in `rows`, drops a failed row's cells from `cells` (so selection, gap candidates, assembly and review cannot see them), and freezes `failed_rows` (id, source key, title, missing columns with reasons `no_stored_text` or the step's error code, the existing `inaccessible` revision ids) and `row_counts` (included, completed, failed, cells missing of total), only when failed rows exist; older snapshots and the default path are unchanged. No value, anchor, evidence link or cell revision is created for a cell without a revision. Assembly changes only the three source sets (completed rows). The plan's word budget uses the completed-row count. Resume of a flagged run uses the stored snapshot without re-checking the live table. Section II states included sources, completed rows, failed rows and missing cells separately (the found, unique, screened, included and full-text figures keep the included-source denominator); section VIII gets an eighth item naming the failed sources with reasons (the `limitations_core` sub-schema in `contracts/research/step-input.schema.json` was widened backward compatibly to allow it); the table summary reports `can_continue_with_failed`, and the panel and table toolbar say how many rows and cells are missing and offer "Write the report with missing rows" instead of "Write report"; the report header and the Markdown export carry the same note and list the failed sources. No migration; `methods/` unchanged.

**Limits:** Synthetic fake and scripted models only: this shows that the choice, the freeze and the exclusion work, not what such a report is worth; the P16 measurement was not re-run (that is a separate step, and its results are conditional on a table whose fill result is already known). A failed row's other, successfully filled cells are excluded too, on purpose (a row is failed as a whole). A failed source leaving the table still counts as a corpus change in evidence-change detection. One test (assembly's absence-basis rule with a failed cell) is rejected for a weaker reason than the failed cell, because it stores no VI step input; the exclusion itself is proved at the snapshot and gap level. Failure reasons are the step's stored error codes, shown with underscores as spaces.
