## D123 — Report behavior cases and a seeded-fault review set, run once against gpt-5.6-luna

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-30 as P6 slice 1 batch P15 (prompt `docs/product/p6-slice1-p15-prompt.md`). Files: `tests/model_behavior/report_cases.json`, `scripts/model_behavior/run_report_cases.py`, `tests/test_report_behavior_cases.py`. One real run on 2026-09-30 with `--model gpt-5.6-luna` (Codex, requested and resolved model equal in all 18 cases, no tool items, one attempt each, no repair, no retry); raw results in ignored `.local/report-behavior-2026-09-30/results.json`.

**Context:** Plan 1m and design section 4.1 ask for behavior cases for the report tasks, and R10 for seeded faults. The plan's case list was written before the report steps existed, and its RS cases were written as writing tasks, which cannot test a review.

**Decision:** Eighteen synthetic cases, each one `StepInput` built in the runner from the `C_report_*` fixtures. Five RB cases (`report_section`: summary-only absence, abstract-only method detail, empty axis in VI, equation in words, embedded instruction) and twelve RS cases plus one control RC01 (`report_review`, one small report each, one seeded fault: meaning-changing repair, abstract-only method detail, two wrong denominators, incomparable conflict, VII claim with unsupported citation, novelty implication, simulation as demonstrated, development from citation, same result under other terms, `not_found` as "did not consider", abstract stronger than body). The runner copies the production call shape (`REPORT_PHRASEBANK_SECTIONS` for section and repair steps, no citation handles, schema enforced by the adapter), stops on the first quota, rate-limit, overload, tool-item or model-mismatch result, never overwrites an earlier results file, and exits non-zero unless every case ran, completed and validated. Checks are split: keyword screens (`screen_` prefix, wrong in both directions, only a human reading decides) and, for RS, `flagged` (a finding sits on the seeded claim; for the repair case also the sentence id and `support_broken`).

**Result of the one run (measures gpt-5.6-luna on synthetic inputs, one attempt per case):** 18 of 18 completed, 17 structurally valid. RB02 failed validation (`anchor_not_in_cell_evidence`: the model quoted a phrase that is not the cell's stored quote). RB03 returned an empty section with no `insufficient_evidence` entry (its own screen `insufficient_evidence_present` is false). RB01, RB04, RB05 passed every screen. RS: 12 of 12 flagged on the seeded claim, all 12 with an accepted code; 4 flags on other claims (three in RS05, one in RS12); the control RC01 had no findings. Whether each RS flag names the seeded fault, and whether RB01's wording ("unknown whether reported" for the full-text row) is the intended "not reported in the inspected text", is a human judgement not yet made by the owner; the implementing agent's reading of the finding texts agrees with the flags for the cases it read.

**Limits:** Not R10: R10 is one valid stored report with 12 to 14 seeded faults and separate review and assembly counts; this is twelve small reports, one fault each, `assembly_would_catch` not measured (the assembly checks need a stored report). RS03 and RS11 cite every count member's cell, which the real review input does not carry, and assembly rejects those faults before a report can be valid. RS05 tests only the citation support of a VII direction: VI gaps and VII `gap_refs` are not in the review input, so a wrong candidate is invisible to the review (a design gap for a later batch). RS12 needs content matching because `body_refs` are absent from the review input. RS05's clean VII claims are not direction claims and drew three flags, a fixture weakness. One attempt per case is no reliability estimate; twelve of twelve does not show the review catches faults in a real report. No migration; `methods/` untouched, `skill_package_hash` did not move (`sha256:08f1bdea...`). Full pytest before the last small fix: 2,887 passed plus the known memory-limit failure; the P15 file alone afterwards: 194 passed.

## D122 — Scripted browser cases for assembly refusal and an empty report section

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-30 as P6 slice 1 batch P14 (prompt `docs/product/p6-slice1-p14-prompt.md`). P13 (D121) was written in parallel and landed first; it stores failure reasons only in the run's error and shows none, so the empty-section case asserts the stored reason through the research API and no screen display.

**Context:** The two existing `report.spec.ts` cases cover a readable report, edits, export, and one model review finding. They did not drive a report that assembly refuses or a section that leaves its run paused.

**Decision:** The scripted model recognizes two markers in the research question. `[report-banned-word]` puts "research gap" in section IV's source-stated cell claim, so assembly reports only `banned_word` for IV. `[report-empty-section]` returns section IV with no claims, anchors or insufficient-evidence entries and skips its usual cell claim. Two Playwright cases (ports 8802 and 8803) start their own research from the UI. The first checks a completed report run whose stored `error` holds the `banned_word` issue, a `draft` report with no version, the entry text `Evidence report · draft`, the `DRAFT` header, and a Markdown copy and download that carry the draft line and no `-v1`. The second checks a paused run (`section_must_be_rewritten`, `error = {sections: [IV]}`), the timeline line `IV: must be written again` (under the collapsed "Report sections" row), the sheet's `Paused: ...` header and section notice, disabled Copy and Download buttons, a 409 from the export route called directly, and Cancel leaving the run cancelled and the report unfinished. Resume is not clicked. Eight named screenshots were taken and looked at.

**Limits:** Synthetic records and a scripted model: this shows workflow and screen states, not report quality, real-model behavior, or a section rewritten after Resume (resume replays the stored empty step; that is P13 and later work). The draft header for an assembly-only refusal reads `DRAFT: 0 sections not validated`, seen in the browser: the screen counts invalid sections, not assembly errors, so it does not name the refused rule and the count reads as if nothing failed. The tests do not pin that wording; the rule is visible only in the research API's run `error`. Left for a follow-up in `apps/web/src`/`views.py`, not changed here. Results: `report.spec.ts` 4/4, full Playwright 108/108 (106 before), lint 17 warnings unchanged, pytest 2,678 passed plus the known `test_extraction_is_stopped_when_it_exceeds_the_memory_limit` failure. No migration; `methods/` untouched, so `skill_package_hash` did not move.
## D121 — Report sections stop before applying late results, and run errors retain each section's stored reason

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-30 as P6 slice 1 batch P13 (the 1k interruption tests). D119 remains reserved for slice 31.

**Context:** A report section could finish a model call after cancellation, a requested pause, or a question revision and still write claims, gaps, or phrase-repair rows. A failed or draft section kept its issues in `report_sections.validation_json`, but the paused run's error named only section IDs.

**Decision:** Each report section checks the run and scope after its model call and after phrase repair, before applying the result. Phrase repair also checks immediately after its own model call and on its optional-step failure path, before writing repair rows. A section checks for an already `paused` run because another section in the same round may have converted `pause_requested` to `paused` first. A stop leaves the section row `running` and any saved model-step output available for resume. The round still waits for all siblings, then re-raises `RunStopped`. `pause_reason` remains `section_failed` or `section_must_be_rewritten`; `error_json` keeps `sections` and adds ordered `reasons` from the stored validation issues (`section_id`, `code`, `detail`). Failed sections contribute their first issue; draft sections contribute up to three; a missing issue uses `unknown`. A string detail and string values one level inside a dict are capped at 300 characters. The wrong-model case remains a failed optional section with `model_mismatch` in `reasons`, with no claims or gaps applied. A step left `outcome_unknown` by recovery is sent again on resume because its result was never stored; a `succeeded` step reuses its stored output.

**Limits:** Tests use fake and scripted models only; they do not measure a provider's real quota or crash behavior, or report quality. The crash test leaves simulated interrupted state and calls the real `Worker.recover()`; it does not kill a process. An `outcome_unknown` step is sent again on resume. The UI still shows only "A section could not be written." The reason is available in the run's `error`, and displaying it on the screen remains open. The plan's `model_mismatch` pause wording was not built: the run pauses as `section_failed`. These checkpoints guard the tested interruption points; they do not make the separate report-table writes atomic against an external process changing run state between synchronous writes. The phrase-repair checkpoint now also stops when a sibling has already converted `pause_requested` to `paused` while the call was out, closing that late repair-row gap.

## D120 — The report exports as one Markdown file built from the screen's own read model, with the screen's "not checked" limits written into it

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-30 as P6 slice 1 batch P12 (prompt `docs/product/p6-slice1-p12-prompt.md`). D119 is reserved for slice 31 (legacy removal), which lands later.

**Context:** The report had numbered citations on the screen (D113) but no way out of the app. The plan's 1j asked for `numbering.py`, `export.py`, a `reportMarkdown.ts` copy of the format, and Copy/Download buttons.

**Decision:** `report/export.py::to_markdown` is a pure function over the dict `report_view` returns, so numbers exist in one place. There is no `numbering.py` and no TypeScript copy of the format: Copy and Download both fetch `GET /api/researches/{id}/reports/{report_id}/export?format=markdown` (a direct `Response` with an attachment name, `report-<title slug>-v<n>.md`, `-draft.md` for a draft). The route answers 409 "The report is still being written" while the report is `in_progress` or its run has not finished, 404 for an unknown or cross-research id. The file follows the screen: a DRAFT line for a draft (no version number), II and VIII `draft.text` always written, claims grouped by paragraph in first-seen order with `[n]` markers and ` (k)` equation numbers, Table I as a Markdown table, numbered References, a corpus footer read from the frozen snapshot, and one provenance paragraph carrying the screen's sentences (edited by hand, evidence changed and passage text not checked, anchors located or not, the review note as the screen words it, model findings listed as flags). English or Turkish by the report language. `report_view` changed in one place: sections are visited in the screen's display order (`DISPLAY_ORDER` in `report/store.py`: index terms second, not last) and claims are ordered by paragraph first-seen before numbers are assigned, so citation and equation numbers follow reading order; two old assertions in `tests/test_report_api.py` that encoded the old section order were updated. Stored text (claims, titles, reference fields, column names, cell values, findings) is neutralised: whitespace collapsed to one line, `\ [ ] < > \` and `|` escaped, a leading `#`, `-`, `+`, `*`, `>` or `n.` escaped, math spans kept except that `< > [ ]` inside them become `{\lt}`, `{\gt}`, `{[}`, `{]}` and, in a table cell, `|` becomes `{\vert}` (`\|` becomes `{\Vert}`). The screen has Copy Markdown and Download .md buttons (icon only at narrow width); a failure (409, 404, refused clipboard) shows an error toast and downloads nothing.

**Limits:** Fake and scripted models only: this shows the file's structure and that it carries the screen's limits, not report quality. Table I's `[n]` row labels are the screen's numbers for the frozen rows, so a label can name a source that only a later section cites; the first-appearance rule holds for the citations in the body. The escaping over-protects a little (a literal `[2]` in a claim reads `\[2\]`) and does not neutralise a backtick inside a math span. DOI and version label in References are additions the screen does not show. LaTeX export (slice 5) is not built. pytest 2,722 (2,721 passed + the known memory-limit failure), Playwright 105/105, lint 17 unchanged. gpt-6-sol high: plan three rounds (3, 2, 2 high fixed; round 3's fixes not re-reviewed), code three rounds (1, 1, 0 high fixed).

## D119 — Remove `legacy` discovery execution and preserve stored records

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-30 as SW slice 31, implementation left uncommitted. The authority for the scope is [the reviewed plan](product/sw-slice31-legacy-removal.md). D117's owner decision selects `sw`; D114's measured medicine limitations remain.

**Decision:** New researches and scope defaults use `sw`; there is no executable `search_plan` or `screening` discovery step, unpaged `_search`, legacy screening batch, legacy model contracts, or new legacy protocol body. The runtime method package hash is `sha256:08f1bdeadc63b809bdf6d123a1e77889cada14d64d3e851c3d9fe25bfb2704ee`. Stored `legacy` researches still expose plan and screening notes. A fake-model answer test completes on an old research; Store tests verify that PDF collection, OCR, table, title and report runs may be queued and marked running. Discovery, full-text fetch, full-text adjudication, scope revision, and seed replacement raise 409 `legacy_research_read_only` from the stored scope revision; run creation checks before idempotency return. The UI reads `research.read_only_reason`, hides its two search controls, revision form and seed selector, and keeps the queue tab limited to `sw`.

After `Worker.recover`, before a run is picked, the owner cancels each queued, running, pause-requested or paused legacy discovery-side run with a `legacy_workflow_removed` event in the same transaction. `DEIXIS_SEARCH_WORKFLOW` is ignored; its presence produces one warning on each CLI startup, including `serve`, `backup` and `restore`. The database column and old migrations remain; no migration or `uv.lock` change was made.

**Entry audit:** `rg -n "start_run|queue_run|requeue" backend/deixis/api` found `start_run` at `api/app.py:979`; the route audit also found `/scope` (942), `/seed` (972), `/runs` (978), `/runs/{run_id}/protocol-approval` (1046), `/term-suggestions` (1072), `/search-query-choice` (1107), and `/runs/{run_id}/{action}` (1124: resume and retry). All take the store guard; run actions use the run's stored scope revision. `create_research` is the only scope revision insertion exempted. The other insertions are `Store.revise_scope` (450) and `Store.set_seed` (576), both guarded.

**`runs.status` SQL audit:** `Store.create_run` (695, `queued`), `update_run` (740, dynamic `queued`/`running`), `queue_failed_search_retry` (776, `queued`), `request_term_suggestions` (971, `queued`), `submit_approval` (993, `queued`), and `choose_code_query` (1014, `queued`) all check stored legacy discovery scope before writing. `Worker.recover` (76) writes only `paused`; startup cleanup (94) writes only `cancelled`. `Store.add_usage` (796) and `start_model_session` (1062) update usage only. Migration `runs_new` insertions in 0019, 0022, 0028, 0032, 0035, 0045 and 0046 copy existing rows during schema migration; they do not queue new work. A direct `update_run(..., status='running')` and an idempotency-key hit are covered by tests.

**Test boundary:** Deterministic and fake-model tests exercise the 409 routes, direct Store guards, historical plan and note rendering, answer-side concept reading, answer execution, recovery order and event rollback, and obsolete environment warning. They do not validate scientific support or live providers. The final `PYTHONPATH=backend:. uv run --no-sync pytest -q` run had 2,678 passes and the known extraction memory-limit failure in `tests/test_documents.py` (timeout reported instead of the expected memory-limit error). Web build passed; lint reported 17 warnings and no errors. The final full Playwright run passed 106/106, with 0 failures and 0 did not run; it uses synthetic records and a scripted model. No live service was restarted and no real model was called.

**Judgment and limits:** I treated records written directly into historical test fixtures as stored old data, not as a way to run old discovery. I migrated generic API, backup and Zotero tests to explicit `sw` user selections; removed tests whose sole assertion required execution of the deleted path. The provider record tests reconstruct historical selection rows without calling the deleted `apply_screening_proposal`. The browser fixture approves `sw` proposals automatically for unattended A–G cases. The `build_protocol` signature retains an unused `plan` parameter for callers; it writes only the `sw` body. The worktree was rebased onto P12 (`545745c`, D120) before commit. Playwright captured desktop and narrow screenshots, but they were not separately reviewed by eye. **Discovery-time short title (D39) now depends on the user:** `_research_title` runs at the end of discovery only when `included_works` is non-empty, the same gate as at `545745c` for both workflows. Legacy screening included sources by itself, so a legacy research always got the title; in `sw` sources are included by the user, so a research with no user inclusion yet keeps the question as its header until the user includes a source and asks for a title, or an answer renames it. The trash and rename acceptance tests therefore request the title through "Suggest a short title" instead of expecting it at discovery end. This is `sw` behavior since D117, not new in this slice; changing it (a title from the question alone, or after the first inclusion) is left to a later decision (TODO.md). Code review: gpt-6-sol high two rounds (round 1 hazır, three medium test-coverage notes kept as backlog; round 2 raised this title point as high, judged pre-existing `sw` behavior and recorded here, and one medium: the table test includes its three sources through the API, not the UI).

### D119 Playwright failure causes and fixes

- `acceptance.spec.ts:138` — `sw` does not auto-name a research during discovery; the test requests a short title through the UI before checking Trash, restore and permanent deletion.
- `acceptance.spec.ts:189` — the rename test expected the removed discovery title step; it requests the short title through the UI, then checks both rename paths and persistence.
- `acceptance.spec.ts:311` — `sw` has no legacy screening override label; the test checks the user's exclusion and reason after reload.
- `acceptance.spec.ts:508` — `.search-summary` also names the flow block, while another provider can legitimately have zero results; the test checks the OpenAlex row for `rate limited` and absence of `zero results`.
- `acceptance.spec.ts:555` — explicit `sw` selection includes three works, not four legacy-selected works; table rows and fill budget now check those three selected sources.
- `acceptance.spec.ts:716` — the fill button and progress expected four legacy-selected works, so the test stalled; pause, resume, cancellation and kept values now check the three `sw` selected works.
- `arxiv-source.spec.ts:75` — `sw` left the arXiv work undecided, so the answer action was unavailable; the test includes that source in the UI before generating and inspecting the cited PDF.
- `builtin-embedding.spec.ts:216` — with the uploaded PDF already in hand, the answer action is labelled `Generate source-linked answer`; the test uses that action and still checks the failed ranking's disclosure.
- `human-queue.spec.ts:116` — a new research defaults to `sw` even on the second server; the test opens an explicitly stored historical `legacy` fixture and checks the queue tab is absent there.
- `report.spec.ts:43` — `sw` had no included source for the first table; the test includes a source in the UI before filling and checking the report lifecycle.
- `report.spec.ts:207` — the second report case had the same empty `sw` selection; it includes a source before checking the recorded model review flag.
- `acceptance.spec.ts:523` — a paused error sentence appeared twice, and the resumed `sw` run has no legacy selection proposal; the test targets the exact sentence, then checks retained sources, completion and the same model.

## D118 — The report is read once by a model after assembly, and only a `support_broken` finding on a kept repair can put original wording back

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-30 as P6 slice 1 batch P9 (prompt `docs/product/p6-slice1-p9-review-prompt.md`). D117 (sw default) and D114 are on main; this number follows them.

**Context:** `run_report` ended after assembly with no review, and the screen said the report was not reviewed by a model or a person. The plan's 1f asked for a single `report_review` call and a rollback of repairs that break support. Repairs (`report_phrase_repairs`) are append-only and every reader takes the latest row per sentence.

**Decision:** After assembly and `finalize`, one optional `report_review` model step reads the claims of the sections that fit a 30,000-token estimate (II is never shown; claim-less sections, sections with an unresolvable cited passage and sections over the budget are recorded in `sections_not_reviewed` with their own reason). Cited passages are resolved by the exact stored passage id. The record is stored in `reports.review_json` (migration 0057) as `reviewed` or `not_reviewed` (reasons include `input_too_large`, `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exhausted`, `model_mismatch`, `model_call_failed`, `invalid_model_output`), the omitted-section list is written in the same transaction as the step result so a resumed run rebuilds an equal record, and the review never changes report status, version or section status. A `support_broken` finding with a sentence id restores the sentence's original wording only if the latest repair row is `kept`, both `report_claims.text` and `draft_json` still hold the repaired sentence, and assembly checks show no error before and after; it is one transaction per sentence that appends a `reverted_exception` row and an event, and otherwise lands in `not_reverted` (`not_kept`, `text_changed`, `report_has_assembly_errors`, `would_break_assembly`). Sentences of `insufficient_evidence` reasons are outside the review's scope. The report run's model-call budget formula gains one step (still floored at 50; the handoff's open question 3 is closed). The screen's closing note says a model read the claims of n of m sections in an extra call by the same model that wrote the report, that it is not peer review, and lists findings as flags. The method file `report.md` gained one paragraph, so `skill_package_hash` changed (sha256:1122205c... to sha256:de30bf07...).

Own judgement: the batch prompt said "a second model"; Sol's code review round 1 found this false (the step uses the research model), so the wording was changed. Tests `test_migrations.py` and `test_arxiv_source_migration.py` were edited only for the new migration version. When nothing can be shown, each section keeps its own reason and the record reason is `nothing_to_review` unless size excluded one.

**Limits:** Fake and scripted models only: this shows workflow behavior, not how many errors a real review catches (P15/P16). Code does not check that a passage supports its claim. Findings other than `support_broken` are shown, never acted on. One review per run; Markdown export is P12.
## D117 — `sw` is the default search workflow by the owner's decision, and `legacy` is to be removed

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-30, the owner's decision after reading D114 ("bizim sw default olmalı", "artık legacy vs olmamalı"). It supersedes D114's "the default stays `legacy` for good" and D105's and D108's default clauses. It is not a measured pass: D114's gates stand as recorded.

**Context:** Slice 30 (D114) passed only gate 3 on medicine: `sw` cited fewer reference trials than `legacy` (mean 1.0 vs 4.5) and one `sw` answer stayed `unverified_draft`. On quantum `sw` passed all four gates in slice 24a. The owner chooses `sw` as the product's only search workflow anyway.

**Decision:** `Settings.search_workflow` and `DEIXIS_SEARCH_WORKFLOW` default to `sw` (`config.py`). `legacy` stays selectable with `DEIXIS_SEARCH_WORKFLOW=legacy` only until a removal slice takes it out. The tests that exercised `legacy` through the old default now set `search_workflow="legacy"` explicitly (`test_api_flow`, `test_backup`, `test_protocol_record`, `test_provider_flow`, `test_zotero`); `test_the_default_search_workflow_is_sw` replaces the old default test. The removal slice gets its own plan; by default, researches already stored as `legacy` keep opening and answering, and no new `legacy` research can start.

**Limits:** What D114 measured still holds: on the medicine question `sw` reached fewer reference trials, mostly for lack of open PDFs, and a standard `sw` research opened about 124 model sessions against `legacy`'s 10, so model quota use rises. `Store.create_research` and the Playwright fixture server still default to `legacy` until the removal slice. pytest: 2,680 passed plus the known memory-limit failure; three script-importing test modules need `python -m pytest` to find `scripts` (unchanged by this decision). Playwright was not re-run.

## D114 — The last medicine measurement at `a04eaa0` passes only gate 3; the default stays `legacy` for good in this track, 24b closes undone and the SW track ends

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-30 as the recorded result of slice 30 (plan `docs/product/sw-slice30-medicine-final.md`, commit `a04eaa0`; resume prompt `docs/product/sw-slice30-resume-prompt.md`). The plan named D112; P6 took D112 and D113 first, so this is D114. Run folder `.local/sw-slice30-medicine-final-2026-09-28/`; results `docs/product/sw-slice30-results.md`. No product file changed; no migration.

**Context:** Slice 27 (D108) failed gates 2 and 4 on medicine. D109 then changed how full-text reading judges the comparator. Slice 30 re-ran slice 27's seven medicine researches, protocol, reference set (|R| = 12, the post-hoc BMI widening, Cienfuegos 2020 as two units) and gates unchanged at `a04eaa0` (`skill_package_hash` `sha256:1122205c…`), with a cap of 1,000 model sessions. The plan fixed the consequence in advance: all four gates pass → 24b unblocked; any gate fails or is unreadable → the default stays `legacy` for good, 24b closes as not done.

**Decision:** All seven researches ran (Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` medium, 898 counted model sessions). The verdict rests on the owner's decision of 30 September to leave the 145 sessions in the five folders of four researches that first ran without provider keys (`invalid-noenv-*`) out of the cap. Counted with them the total is 1,043, and the frozen cap rule would have stopped the campaign with no verdict. Each verdict joins two commits (quantum from `65a7ec8`, medicine from `a04eaa0`), and the medicine half rests on a reference rule chosen after the numbers were seen.

- *Gate 1, completion:* **fails**, 9 of 10. `qtre-sw-standard-r2`'s answer stayed `unverified_draft` (`anchor_not_in_passage`, not fixed by the bounded repair).
- *Gate 2, workflow comparison:* **fails**, unreadable on medicine because one of the four `standard` runs has no valid answer. Its arithmetic fails too: pool mean `sw` 12.0 vs `legacy` 9.5 (passes), cited mean `sw` 1.0 (2 and 0) vs `legacy` 4.5 (4 and 5), below 3.5; the one-unit reading (|R| = 11) gives the same.
- *Gate 3, evidence integrity:* **passes**.
- *Gate 4, analyst reading:* **fails**, unreadable on medicine: 6 unique includes across the two `sw` `standard` runs (8 needed), 8 `sw` claims. None of the 6 includes, 8 `sw` claims or 10 `legacy` claims was read as serious by the run session, and the blind Sonnet second reader agreed on its 5 seeded units.

The default stays `legacy` for good in this track. 24b is closed as not done, and the SW track ends; the `sw` workflow stays available behind its flags.

**Limits:** One run per research on one machine and one model; the two readers are models, not a human check. The medicine reference rule is post hoc, so gate 2's medicine verdict is descriptive. No quantum research ran at this commit. The run deviated from the plan in ways recorded in the results file: `detailed` restarted after a `serverOverloaded` stop, the run moved to a worktree at `a04eaa0` and back, four researches first ran without provider keys and were re-run by the owner's decision (their folders are kept as `invalid-noenv-*` and not counted), the driver did not run the per-research diff check the plan named, and the last four researches ran on the owner's VPN while the first three did not, so the two `standard` repeats of each workflow were measured on different networks (effect not measured). How often `anchor_not_in_passage` leaves an `sw` answer unverified was not measured.

## D116 — The other eight assembly rules are in code, and rule 7 compares the stored numbers of II and VIII with the frozen corpus instead of reading label words in prose

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-30 as P6 slice 1 batch P7 (prompt `docs/product/p6-slice1-p7-prompt.md`). Structural checks only; no report review (P9) yet.

**Context:** `assembly.py` had rules 1, 2, 3, 4, 7 and 10. Rule 7 searched the prose of II and VIII for `found`/`bulunan`-style label words and read the number beside them, so a differently worded label slipped past silently. D115 now stores the numbers those texts are rendered from in `report_sections.validation_json["numbers"]`.

**Decision:** Rule 7 no longer reads prose (its regexes are deleted). For II and VIII it requires the structured numbers (version 1, the right `kind`, integer corpus counts, finite ratios) and compares `found, unique, screened, included, full_text` with the frozen snapshot (`corpus_numbers_missing`, `corpus_count_mismatch`); the derived ratio (II) and share (VIII) must follow from the counts, and VIII's `draft["text"]` must equal `render_limitations(numbers)` (`limitations_text_drift`). Rules added, all errors unless noted: 5 count fields (members, snapshot cells, mixed depth or value, integers in the text); 6 banned words in model-written text (claims, headings, gap texts, insufficient-evidence reasons); 8 citation source in the frozen corpus, complete reference record, source owns the cited passage or cell; 9 VII links (`gap_ref` or a cell of the plan's future-work column; an inference needs a gap) and VI gap bases (stated limitation from what VI was given and the limitations column; corpus absence equal to all applicable full-text cells of one column, at least three, matching the stored code candidate); 11 well-formed math, equation origin present, cited by the claim, in the section's own step input, holding math, its `text_source` equal to the passage's (OCR or Marker origin is the one warning, `equation_text_source_warning`); 12 an unmatched anchor is an error, not `NULL` (handoff decision 1), and each anchor is re-located in the passage or the frozen cell quotes; 13 a conflict gap names V claims; 14 a sentence that follows no frame needs a matching recorded exception (its `before` or `after` equals the sentence), and own-work and plural-source phrases are errors that cannot be excepted. Malformed stored JSON or step inputs give `stored_record_malformed`, never an exception. `sections.py` now treats any `*_warning` issue with a `WARNING:` prefix as non-blocking.

Own judgement: the list is narrow for "first" (only novelty phrases) and leaves out Turkish "yeni"; `band gap` and `energy gap` style compounds are exempt; II and VIII's code-written prose is exempt from the word list (VIII's template itself says "research gaps"); rule 14's language comes from the section's stored step input, falling back to report language, scope hint, then `en`; a language with no frames skips only the frame part.

**Limits:** Structure, not meaning: a cell that holds a generic sentence is not shown to be a source's own limitation, math is not checked for correctness, and count words ("four of six") are not parsed. II's prose is not re-rendered (it needs search provenance). A report whose VIII was written before D115 has no numbers and fails rule 7 if resumed. Open: VI's evidence selection carries the limitations column only, while code corpus-absence candidates come from plan axes, so their basis cells may not reach VI's input (not changed here; rule 9 does not require them in the input). Synthetic data and fake models: pytest 2,680 passed plus the known memory-limit failure; this shows workflow behavior, not report quality.

## D115 — Section VIII's numbers are written by code from the frozen snapshot and stored as structured data; the model writes only claims around them

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-30 as P6 slice 1 batch P6 (prompt `docs/product/p6-slice1-p6-prompt.md`). Assembly rule 7 still reads label words in prose; batch P7 can now read the stored numbers instead.

**Context:** VIII was an ordinary model section with no numbers of its own, `selection.py` had no branch for it, and the handoff's "truncation record" had no decided place. II's numbers existed only inside its prose.

**Decision:** Before VIII's model call, `review_methodology.limitations_core` computes a core from the snapshot and stored records and sends it in `report_target.limitations_core` (new required field; an object only for VIII, `null` elsewhere, checked as `limitations_core_mismatch`; `flow._model_step` defaults it to `null` so other callers are unchanged). Keys: recall (`null`, no known-set measurement exists), open-access bias, `no_full_text_share` (renamed from the plan's summary ratio: it counts included sources with no PDF text, not sources read from an abstract), analyst-inference share over valid III-VII claims, kill-search `not_run`, phrase-repair outcomes (latest row per sentence, as of the VIII write), the truncation record, and seven numbered `items` the model may cite as "item N". After the model call code sets `draft["text"]` (the numbered paragraph, in the report language) and stores the same numbers in `report_sections.validation_json["numbers"]` (also when the step fails; then there is no text). II now stores its printed counts the same way (`kind: review_methodology`). Both texts are rendered from the stored dict by one function each. The truncation record stays in `validation_json["truncated"]`, already written per section; no table, no migration; VIII counts it, budget cuts apart from cells whose evidence passage was missing. `selection.py` gives VIII no passages or cells (limitation claims from sources belong to VI). VIII may write only `analyst_inference` (`ALLOWED_SUPPORT`), and a VIII claim may contain no digit except in "item N" (`limitations_number_restated`, `source_stated_without_evidence`), checked on the model output and again after phrase repair; a violation after repair leaves the section a draft and pauses the run. The report view shows VIII's paragraph like II's. No `methods/` change, so `skill_package_hash` did not move.

**Limits:** Fake and scripted models only; nothing here measures report quality. Rule 7 is unchanged and P7 has not yet switched to the stored numbers. A number written in words in a VIII claim is not caught. The phrase-repair counts are as of the VIII write; a later `report_review` revert (P9) does not update them. `report.md` still says "summary-vs-full-text ratio" where the code says "no PDF text"; fix it in a later methods change. The stored truncation count can over-count: `select_evidence` may append the same omitted passage more than once (dictionary, ranked and per-source passes), so the figure in VIII is an upper bound, not a count of distinct passages (found in the last code review, not fixed). The code-written paragraph is not in `word_count`, so assembly's word budget does not cover it, and it reads as one run-on numbered paragraph. gpt-6-sol high: plan three rounds (2 high, 1 high, 1 high fixed; the third ended "düzeltmeyle hazır", folded in without a fourth), code two rounds (1 high fixed, then "düzeltmeyle hazır" with one medium left open).

## D113 — The report is on screen: written from a ready table, read as an article with numbered citations, edited by claim, marked when its evidence changed

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-29 as P6 slice 1 batches P10 and P11 (prompt `docs/product/p6-slice1-p10-p11-prompt.md`), with slice 4's editing and staleness API (D112) wired in. P6 (VIII's numeric core), P7 (the other eight assembly rules), P9 (`report_review`) and P12 onward are still not built; none of them blocks the screen, which renders what the report stores.

**Context:** The report run, claim editing and the staleness marker were in code, but `apps/web` had no report screen and no report types, so the owner could not see or use a report.

**Decision:** The "fourth state" is a separate component (`report/ReportReadiness.tsx`) on the Answer tab, not a branch of `PdfReadiness`, because `PdfReadiness` disappears once an answer exists. It shows table-fill progress with Pause/Resume, or one "Write report" button per ready table; readiness comes from the backend (`GET …/tables` items gain `report_ready` from `tables.report_ready`), never from the client. The Evidence toolbar has the same action, disabled with its reason. A report is a card labelled "Evidence report · V{n}" (so it is not confused with the answer's "Report" card) that opens a sheet: sections in display order with headings in the report's language, claims joined into paragraphs, IEEE numbers and a reference list numbered by the backend in first-appearance order, TABLE I from the frozen snapshot (under IV's heading when no claim carries `table_ref`), a report-level "Evidence changed after this report" band, a per-section marker with "Keep as is", and an evidence view with the claim's support type, links, Edit form (409 keeps the draft and re-bases it on the version now shown) and history with Restore. The closing line says anchors were located, that semantic support was not checked, and that no review ran. Report runs appear in the timeline with plan, sections and assembly phases.

A report citation anchor is now checked like an answer's: `_check_report_section` raises `anchor_not_in_passage` / `anchor_not_in_cell_evidence` (each cell evidence quote tried separately) into the bounded repair, and `_citation_links` stores the located source text, not the model's quote. The screen highlights only a located anchor; a cell citation opens the frozen evidence passage whose quote holds the anchor. An older stored link without a located anchor opens without a mark.

**Limits:** Synthetic data, fake and scripted models only: pytest 2,558 passed (the known memory-limit test failed), Playwright 104/104 including the new `e2e/report.spec.ts`; screenshots checked at 1440 px and 390 px, light and dark. No real-model report was opened on this screen. Deferred: Markdown export and copy (P12), publish, section rewrite, removing a citation from a claim, a model name in the closing line (the report view does not return the run's model), equation display beyond the printed number. A citation marker opens the source sheet, never the cell panel. gpt-6-sol high: plan one round (4 high, fixed before implementation), code two rounds (3 high fixed, then "hazır").

## D112 — A finished report's claim can be edited with its history kept, and the report says which evidence changed after it was written

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-29 as the small version of P6 slice 4 (`docs/product/p6-slice4-editing-stale-measurement.md` §0, prompt `docs/product/p6-slice4-prompt.md`). The owner did not choose among the note's §12 options ("I don't know, let's continue"); the coordinator took the note's own fallback for every question (1a, 2a, 3a, 4a, 5a, 7c, 8b, 9a) and deviated on 6. Backend and view model only: there is no report screen yet (slice 1 batch P11), so nobody can use this from the UI until P11 lands.

**Context:** Slice 1's report run is in code and produced a valid real-model report on 18 September, but a finished report could not be corrected, and nothing told the reader when the evidence table changed after the report froze its snapshot. AGENTS.md asks for revisions to be kept and stale work to be marked rather than silently rewritten.

**Decision:** The editing unit is the claim. `report_claims.text` stays the model's text; a person's edit or a restore (to the model's text or an earlier edit) is a new row in the append-only `report_claim_revisions` (migration 0056; update and delete refused by trigger except under a research purge authorization), the claim carries `current_revision_id` and a `version`, and an edit needs `expected_version` (409 on mismatch) and honours `Idempotency-Key`. Edits are refused until the report's run has finished; citations always carry over; the phrasebank check does not run on human text; malformed math and an edited `count` claim give warnings, never refusals. `save_claims` refuses to replace a section that has a human edit. Editing does not change `report_version`, the section's `draft`/`validation`, or the report status (2a: a separate publish step will re-check and number an edited report; not built).

Staleness is computed when the report is read (the deviation from 6a): the frozen snapshot is compared with live records. The report level counts changed cells, removed and added rows (active table rows that are included sources, the snapshot's own rule), and revised columns; each section lists the changed cells and removed sources its claims cite, and one level further through `body_ref` and `gap_ref`. Write-time flags were rejected because a cell changed between the snapshot and the claim save would never be flagged, and because every mutation path would need its own hook. "Keep as is" stores the acknowledged change keys in append-only `report_stale_acknowledgements`; a key carries the cell's live revision or the timestamp of the source's departure, so a later change opens a new marker (4a), and a key that is no longer open gives 409. `purge_research` now deletes report rows; it could not purge a research with a report before.

**Limits:** Tested with synthetic data and the fake model only (pytest 2,551 passed; the known memory-limit test failed, and one arXiv archive test failed under parallel load and passed alone); no real-model run, no measurement. PDF re-extraction and passage changes are not detected at any level (`not_checked: ["passages"]`). Two source departures in the same millisecond share a key. Deferred: the publish step, section rewrite proposals (S3/S4), stable claim and gap identities (§5), `scope_statement` edits, chain-link and kill-search staleness (slices 2/3 are not built), removing a citation from an edited claim, the optional review of an edit, the UI and Playwright, and the P6 closing measurement (R18–R21). `purge_table` still fails on a table a report points at. Backlog from review: an acknowledge → restore → remove-again test for the exclusion and research-removal paths, and an HTTP-level idempotency test. gpt-6-sol high: plan one round (4 high, fixed before implementation), code one round ("hazır", no high).

## D111 — `standard` keeps its full-text limits of 100 fetched and 50 read works; 75% of the quantum gain is reached only at `detailed`'s limit, at about `detailed`'s cost (estimated)

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-28 (owner's answers to slice 29: A1, B1, D1; C does not apply because nothing changes; the owner answered "Ok" to "limit stays 100, record as D111, close SW24"). Plan `docs/product/sw-slice29-fetch-limit.md`. No code change, no migration; the dated comment above `FULLTEXT_WORK_LIMIT` that the plan's A1 outline proposed was not added. Closes SW24 as measured and not changed.

**Context:** SW24 (slice 24a) found that in quantum `standard` the full-text work limit loses more reference works than any other stage: 10 and 12 of 31 were routed to full text but not planned under `FULLTEXT_WORK_LIMIT["standard"]` = 100, while `detailed` (limit 300) planned 23. The same runs took 17.7 and 19.9 minutes from create to answer (a third took 29.2 with a 10-minute timeout wait) against the 15-minute `standard` target (D88, as revised by the owner on 2026-09-22).

**Decision:** Both `standard` limits stay: 100 works fetched, 50 read (`backend/deixis/domain/rules.py`). The basis is a model-free replay (`.local/sw-slice29-fetch-limit-replay-2026-09-28/`, protocol frozen before any number) of the 12 stored `sw` libraries of slices 24a and 27: quantum `standard` r1, r2 and embedding plus `detailed`, and medicine `standard` r1, r2 and embedding plus `detailed` from each of the two slices. The replay reproduced every stored fetch plan exactly. For quantum `standard` (31 reference works, mean of three runs, read limit at half the fetch limit):

| fetch / read | reference works planned | est. read | est. added min per run |
|---|---|---|---|
| 100 / 50 (today) | 13.0 | 10.3 | 0 |
| 150 / 75 | 16.7 | 14.0 | 4.3 (2.8–6.0) |
| 200 / 100 | 18.7 | 17.0 | 8.6 (5.6–12.0) |
| 300 / 150 | 22.7 | 20.3–21.0 | 17.2 (11.2–24.0) |
| 300 / 50 | 22.7 | 10.3 | 4.6–4.8 |

The frozen rule said: change only if the gain at 300 is at least 3 works, then take the smallest limit reaching 75% of that gain whose added time is at most 5.0 minutes. Each step up plans more reference works (+3.7 at 150, +5.7 at 200, +9.7 at 300), but even 300 plans 22.7 of 31, not all of them. Only 300 reaches 75% of the 9.7 gain (150 gives 38%, 200 gives 59%), and 300 adds about 17 minutes, so the rule gives no change. At 300 / 150 `standard` would plan what `detailed` plans and take about as long as `detailed` takes today (35.9 minutes); a user who wants those works can choose `detailed`.

The read limit binds: with it held at 50, a fetch of 300 leaves the estimated reference works read at a mean of 10.3 (per run 10 → 10, 10 → 11, 11 → 10, so the run mix shifts but the total does not rise), because the reading already stops at 50 with text left over in r1 and r2 (the embedding run had 47 works with text, so its estimate reads three more works, while its reference works read go from 11 to 10). So a fetch change without a read change is estimated to add no reference works read on average, though it changes which ones are read (B1: no read-only change either; at fetch 100 a larger read limit could reach at most 3 / 1 / 0 more quantum reference works, about a minute, seen after the numbers). Medicine gains little at any limit: planned reference units go from 9, 5, 5 (slice 27) and 8, 8, 4 (slice 24a) at 100 to 11, 9, 8 and 10, 11, 8 at 300, but only 3 of the 12 units got a PDF in any stored medicine run, so the lower bound of units read stays at 2 (slice 27) and 0 (slice 24a). More room adds planned medicine units but leaves that lower bound where it is: medicine's loss is the missing open PDF (D108), not room.

The 15-minute `standard` target stays a target (D1). `standard` misses it by about 3–5 minutes today (17.7 and 19.9 minutes in slice 24a, not counting the run with a timeout wait), and no fetch or read change estimated here brings it closer: every step up adds estimated time (from stored stage durations, not measured at the higher limits).

**Limits:** Measured: the fetch plan at each limit, replayed exactly on stored candidates. Measured: the stored create-to-answer times quoted here (17.7, 19.9, 29.2 and 35.9 minutes), each from one earlier run. Estimated, not measured: which added works would get a PDF (from each run's own PDF yield and from other stored runs), the reading's reference works, and every added-time figure, which comes from the stored stage durations of the same runs (per added fetched work about 0.023 minutes of wall time, per added read work 0.08–0.19 minutes; r1's rate includes a 5-minute call that ended `outcome_unknown`). The fetch time is an upper bound: none of it is credited to the overlap with discovery. No live run was made, so none of the estimates was checked against a real `standard` run at a higher limit. Two questions only, three stored runs each, all one model (`gpt-5.6-luna` · medium); run-to-run variation beyond that is unknown, and so is any third field. Whether a read reference work would be included or cited was not measured. The quantum reference list is a model-derived subset of earlier runs, not a human truth, and the medicine list rests on a rule widened after the fact. The rule's 3-work floor, 75% share and 5-minute ceiling were picked by hand, not derived; 150 / 75 is the only step under 5 minutes on average (+3.7 planned, about +3.7 read) and was seen only after the numbers.

## D110 — The user-approved code gate (slice 23) is not built

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-27 (owner's choice A3, the coordinator's recommendation, confirmed explicitly: "önerdiğin şekilde yap"). Plan `docs/product/sw-slice23-code-gate.md` kept as the record of the measurement; no Sol plan round ran, no code, no migration.

**Context:** SW15.6 and SW16.2–4 allow a code gate that closes a work without a model call, only with a rule the user approved and that made no false close on held-out verified records. The slice 23 plan designed a close-only gate (one criterion part plus plain phrases; a read text of at least 4 pages with none of them is closed as `criterion_not_met`; opening needs at least 20 verified `include` and 5 verified `criterion_not_met`, zero false closes, at least one correct close).

**Decision:** The gate is not built. Measured offline on the 15 stored `sw` libraries of slices 24a and 27 (`.local/sw-slice23-plan-2026-09-27/`, read with `immutable=1`): at the planned threshold the gate could open in 1 of 15 researches and there it closes 0 works still waiting to be read; with each part's frozen phrases, 19 of 55 part rules close at least one verified `include` (worst: 32 of 42 in one quantum `detailed` research); of rules that pass on a random half of the verified records, 24% (662 of 2,762 draws, 7 researches with at least 10 includes, 300 draws each) close an `include` in the other half. The saving would come only from readings after approval and cannot be shown on stored data, while the false-close risk is measurable now.

**Limits:** Every "verified" record here is a model reading (two agreeing runs with verified quotes); none of the 15 libraries holds a human decision. The phrases tried were the frozen cue phrases, not rules a user would write. Two questions only. SW16 stays an accepted design direction without an implementation; a future gate would need human-verified records to validate against.

## D109 — The full-text reading judges a marked comparator part by what the comparison group receives, and code no longer excludes on a comparator criterion: kept by the owner's choice although the effect gate failed

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-27; implemented and closed in slice 28 (Sol · high code r2: r1 findings closed; its one new high finding, that the record claimed an owner choice without an explicit answer, was resolved by the owner's explicit answer) (plan `docs/product/sw-slice28-comparator-reading.md`, commit `d5a78ef`, A1, B1, C1, D1 and E1 as proposed). The first dry run did not pass the plan's effect gate (condition (ii) failed). The code is **kept by the owner's choice although the effect gate failed** (option 1, recommended by the coordinator; the owner confirmed it explicitly on 2026-09-27 after Sol code review r2: "önerdiğin şekilde yap"); Sol code review r1's two high findings are fixed (below) and the reading part of the dry run was measured again. No migration (highest stays `0055`); `skill_package_hash` becomes `sha256:1122205caf88fe87b4baad10dc529df93e391150b9b6ea0502e018a380baa2d8` (the first build's `48a1c41e…` is superseded by the r1 fix). Outputs in `.local/sw-slice28-acceptance-2026-09-27/`.

**Context:** Slice 27 (D108) failed gate 4 on medicine: 3 serious errors in 10 sampled includes, each a trial whose comparison group followed the same calorie restriction as the time-restricted-eating group, while both reading runs labelled the comparator part `present` (14 of 14 stored runs). The reading step never saw the criterion proposal's comparator sentence and did not know which part was the comparator (new SW27).

**Decision:**

- *Method.* `fulltext-adjudication.md` gains one line: a part marked `"role": "comparator"` is `present` only when a passage shows the comparison group receives what the part names; the group is judged by everything it receives; a shared added treatment, restriction or regimen that makes the group something the part does not name gives `absent` (unrestricted or usual X is not met when both groups follow the same restriction of X), a shared addition that leaves it as named does not matter; with several arms, one arm receiving what the part names against one receiving the thing sought meets it; otherwise, when no passage shows that the comparison group receives what the part names, `unclear`. A group described only as not receiving the thing sought does not show what it receives (Sol code r1: the first build's line let such a group meet the part unless shown otherwise). No field word.
- *Criterion rule 8.* `criterion-proposal.md`: the comparator's definition names what the comparison group must receive, in the question's words, adds no alternative the question does not name, and says that a group also receiving an addition that makes it something other than the named comparator does not meet it; the hard case adds "or the same added treatment or restriction as the intervention group". Consensus, checks and contract unchanged.
- *Marker.* `adjudication.mark_comparator` gives `"role": "comparator"` to the part a `comparator` question element names, only when `comparator` is a required role, comparing part names with `criterion.norm` as the criterion check does (Sol code r1: an element naming "Usual Diet" as "usual diet" lost the role and kept the automatic exclusion); `flow._adjudication_plan` applies it; the StepInput schema allows an optional `role` (`enum: ["comparator"]`) on reading parts. The output contract does not change.
- *Guard.* `adjudication.with_comparator`: on a criterion with a marked comparator part, `criterion_absent` becomes `comparator_exclusion_withheld` (full text, `unresolved`, decided by code, next step the queue) with note `comparator_exclusion_withheld:criterion_absent:<part>`; every other code passes through. `_close_adjudication` applies `combine` → `with_comparator` → `with_title`. Queue kind `confirm_absent`, question naming the comparator part; English reason text and its Turkish.

**Measured (one M1 Pro, Python 3.12 arm64):** replay (a), offline on stored data through the product helpers: slice 27 284 of 294 reading codes equal, exactly the 10 stored `criterion_absent` becoming `comparator_exclusion_withheld`; slice 24a 452 of 455 equal, exactly the 3 known `protocol_title` changes in `qtre-sw-detailed-r1`; quantum 304 of 304. Replay (b): 625 quantum and 305 slice 24a medicine reading StepInputs byte-identical under the marker, 614 slice 27 medicine StepInputs with exactly the comparator part marked. Dry run, Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` medium, 24 model sessions (22 planned calls plus 2 schema repairs; cap 25), one run of each call, no stop rule fired:
- *Errors (3):* Cell Reports Medicine 2024 run 1 comparator `absent` ("both groups received isocaloric caloric restriction"), run 2 no valid output (it echoed run 1's `step_input_id` twice: `envelope_mismatch`), so no code; TREATY `fulltext_runs_disagree` (run 1 `present` on "daily-calorie-restriction group without time restriction", run 2 `absent`: "all participants followed the same 25% calorie reduction"); APT 2025 still `all_parts_verified` (both runs `present` on "consumed meals throughout the day without time restrictions"). Stored: 3 of 3 `all_parts_verified`.
- *Controls (4):* Kotarsky 2021, `nu16142187`, `nu13041155` and the quantum work unchanged, every part `present` with a verified quote in both runs; the quantum target carried no role.
- *Edge:* TRIM `fulltext_runs_disagree` (run 1 comparator `absent`: both arms received controlled isocaloric study meals; run 2 `present`): a queue row, not an exclusion.
- *Criterion (6 calls):* medicine consensus `required_roles` `["comparator", "population"]`, each proposal's comparator definition names what the group receives and carries an exclusion clause; quantum 0 of 3 proposals with a question element, consensus roles `[]`. The word-list screen passes 3 of 3 new definitions (reported only).
- *Effect condition (i):* 2 of 3 errors leave `all_parts_verified` with the comparator not `present` in a run, **if** the Cell Reports Medicine pair counts with one valid run; counted strictly (two valid runs), 1 of 3.
- *Reading part again after Sol code r1* (new method line and marker, 16 sessions, cap 18, no repair, fresh copies, one run of each call, no stop): Cell Reports Medicine `fulltext_runs_disagree` (run 1 comparator `present` on "instructed to follow their usual eating regimens", run 2 `absent`: "the control group received the same isocaloric caloric restriction"); TREATY `part_without_evidence` (comparator `absent` in both runs: "followed a prescribed 25% calorie reduction"), a `confirm_absent` queue row; APT 2025 still `all_parts_verified`. Controls 4 of 4 unchanged per part and combined; TRIM stays `all_parts_verified` (comparator `present` in both runs). **Condition (i) now holds: 2 of 3 errors** leave `all_parts_verified` with the comparator not `present` in a run, each with two valid runs. The definition gate was not re-run.
- *Effect condition (ii):* **fails.** Two blind Claude Sonnet readers (separate subagent sessions, the same packet shuffled with seed `2809270`) both PASS all 3 new definitions, but each matched only 3 of the 6 frozen calibration verdicts (both passed `standard-r2`, frozen fail; both failed `standard-r1` and `standard-emb`, frozen pass), so both readings are invalid, and by the plan an invalid reading is not repeated and counts as the condition failing.

**Tests:** first build, full pytest 2531 passed and 2 failed: the known `tests/test_documents.py::test_extraction_is_stopped_when_it_exceeds_the_memory_limit` and `tests/test_arxiv_source_archive.py::test_links_devices_and_unsafe_names_are_never_read_and_nothing_is_written_to_disk` (stray files of other processes in the shared temporary directory under parallel load; the file re-run alone passed 29 of 29). After the r1 fix, full pytest 2536 passed and 1 failed (the known one). Playwright 103 of 103 both times; lint 17 warnings; replays (a) and (b) unchanged after the fix.

**Limits:** The comparator rule is the model's reading of a marked part, measured in one dry run on one medicine question (3 errors, 4 controls, 1 edge, one run each); the marker and guard are code and leave quantum byte-identical. On a criterion with a comparator part the guard withholds every automatic full-text exclusion (10 of 294 stored slice 27 codes) and never excludes. No lexical check on the quote, because on stored data it withheld 24 of 29 correct includes. The isocaloric edge is not special-cased; TRIM moved to the queue in the first run and stayed included in the second. The effect gate failed on condition (ii), and keeping the code does not change that record. The failed condition (ii) says the readers and the frozen calibration disagree on what the rule means for three stored definitions; it does not show the new definitions are wrong, and it was not re-run. One machine, one model.

## D108 — The medicine re-measurement at `142dfa1` passes gates 1 and 3 and fails gates 2 and 4; the default still stays `legacy`

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-27 as the recorded result of slice 27 (plan `docs/product/sw-slice27-medicine-remeasure.md`, commit `bc64236`, the owner's (b) decision, A1, B1, C1, D1, E1 and F1 as proposed). Run folder `.local/sw-slice27-remeasure-2026-09-27-043237/`; results `docs/product/sw-slice27-remeasure-results.md`. No product file changed; no migration.

**Context:** 25b stopped before any research because the frozen medicine reference rule gave |R| = 7. The owner then chose to count BMI as body weight in condition (b), after 25b's stop and after seeing a what-if estimate: a post-hoc widening. Rebuilt from 25b's copied decisions plus the plan's pre-work, R has 12 trials, 8 with a different comparator and 4 unknown (25.0%, the paper-check limit with no margin). Cienfuegos 2020 is counted as two units (E1: its sleep report and its main report share no registration number); counted once, |R| = 11 and the unknown share 26.7% would have stopped the paper check.

**Decision:** The seven medicine researches ran at `142dfa1` (`skill_package_hash` `sha256:a633e9c7…`), Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` medium, one at a time; all seven answered. The quantum half of every gate is carried from slice 24 (`65a7ec8`), so each verdict joins two commits.

- *Gate 1, completion:* **passes**. 10 of 10 `sw` researches answered `structurally_valid` (5 medicine here, 5 quantum from 24a); two medicine researches used the one allowed `client_timeout` resume.
- *Gate 2, workflow comparison:* **fails** on medicine, a descriptive verdict conditional on the post-hoc rule. Two units (|R| = 12): pool mean `sw` 11.5 vs `legacy` 8.0 (passes, threshold 2); cited mean `sw` 1.0 vs `legacy` 3.5 (fails: 1.0 < 2.5). One unit (|R| = 11): pool 11.0 vs 8.0, cited 1.0 vs 3.5, the same failure. Quantum passed in 24a.
- *Gate 3, evidence integrity:* **passes** (0 bad links, 0 isolation violations, 0 other-model sessions in the five medicine `sw` answers; quantum from 24a).
- *Gate 4, analyst reading:* **fails** on medicine: 3 serious errors in 10 sampled includes (limit 1), all three a comparator that was the same calorie restriction in both arms; one of the three is serious only because the blind second reader disagreed. 0 serious in 10 `sw` claims. Quantum 0/10 and 0/10 from 24a.
- The default still stays `legacy`.

**Measured (one M1 Pro, Python 3.12 arm64, one run per cell):** 766 Luna calls, 8.26 M input / 0.77 M output tokens, 2 h 58 min wall time including two 10-minute resume waits. Every `sw` criterion named population and comparator (5 of 5); the code query kept `time-restricted eating` and `body weight` apart (0 of 256 search rows carry the welded phrase); none of 24a's three protocol works was included. The gate 2 loss sits at the PDF stage: of R's 10 units without a PDF in the `sw` runs, only one is in Europe PMC's open-access subset, so the loss is outside that subset.

The analyst reading is two model readings, the first not blind. A full quantum research at `142dfa1` was not run (F2 open). Two runs per side make gate 2 a descriptive rule, not a statistical test.

## D107 — A result part needs a reported result, a study-protocol title keeps a work for a person, and the code query cuts an inverted question at its verb

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-27; implemented in slice 26 (plan `docs/product/sw-slice26-protocol-results-and-phrases.md`, commit `2c3acf2`, A1, B1, C1, D1, E1 and F1 as proposed). Not yet reviewed by Sol at the time of writing; no migration (highest stays `0055`); `skill_package_hash` becomes `sha256:a633e9c7091ed3338b0a51d3c7bdb99e524678f5cc4bdb60e1049d8b4a68028a`.

**Context:** Slice 24a's medicine `detailed` research included three trial protocols that report no results: both reading runs labelled the outcome part `present` on an outcome the trial only plans to measure (SW26). In all five medicine `sw` researches the code query searched `"time-restricted eating reduce body weight"`, the question's words run together through a verb (SW25).

**Decision:**

- *SW26, method.* `fulltext-adjudication.md` says that a part about a result, an effect or a measured outcome is `present` only when a passage reports that result, or an analysis of it, as a finding of this paper, whatever its source (an experiment or trial, a re-analysis, a review's pooled estimate, a derivation or a simulation). A result the paper only plans to measure is not reported: `absent` when the passages show no result is reported yet, `unclear` when they cannot tell.
- *SW26, code.* `adjudication.protocol_title` matches one English, hand-written pattern (`study|trial|review|research|clinical|intervention protocol`, `protocol for/of a|an|the … trial|study`, `protocol overview`, `rationale and design`, `design and rationale`). `with_title` turns `all_parts_verified` and `criterion_absent` into the new code `protocol_title` (full text, `unresolved`, decided by code, next step the queue) when the read version's own title matches, with the note `protocol_title:<combined code>:<matched words>`; every other code passes through. `_close_adjudication` applies it after `combine`; `combine` and `verdict` are unchanged. The queue shows the row as kind `confirm_results` with no part asked: "The title names a study protocol. Does this paper report results for every part, rather than only planning to measure them?"
- *SW25, the cut.* In a clause the question inverted with an auxiliary (a token of the clause, or the last word of the stripped question frame; punctuation ends the clause), `vocabulary._phrases` cuts a candidate phrase once at its last listed effect verb that has a word on each side: the verb is dropped, the left part keeps the phrase's position, the right part is `outcome`. The lists (`AUXILIARIES`, `EFFECT_VERBS`) are in `vocabulary_words.py`.
- *Notes, no code.* Code writes no spelling variant. `providers.env.example` records what OpenAlex's keyless budget did once (2026-09-26, 14 researches: HTTP 429, `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, reset in about 8.4 hours).

**Measured in 26 (one M1 Pro, Python 3.12 arm64):** replay (a), offline on slice 24a's 10 `sw` libraries: 455 of 455 stored reading codes reproduced from their stored proposals (quantum 304, medicine 151); with `with_title`, exactly 3 change, the three protocols of `qtre-sw-detailed-r1`, `all_parts_verified` → `protocol_title`; 0 in quantum; no stored `criterion_absent` changes. Replay (b): the 13 questions of the plan's `verb-split.json` through the product's extraction give its phrases and positions byte for byte, 4 changed and 9 unchanged (both quantum questions unchanged). Dry run with `gpt-5.6-luna` · medium over Codex, one run of each call, 19 model sessions of a cap of 22, no repair, no re-send: the model alone kept 3 of 3 protocols out of `all_parts_verified` (two `fulltext_runs_disagree`, one `part_without_evidence`); the outcome part was `absent` in 4 of the 6 protocol runs, each rationale saying the protocol reports no result yet, and in one PCOS run the design part was also `absent` ("a study protocol that will conduct the trial"). The 5 controls (3 medicine, 2 quantum) stayed `all_parts_verified` with every part `present` and every quote verified in both runs. The labelling put `time-restricted eating` in `task` and `body weight` in `outcome` in 3 of 3 runs. These are model readings; no person checked them.

**Limits:** The title rule is English and hand-written, measured on two fields plus packet in stored data; it withholds both an automatic include and an automatic exclusion and never excludes. A protocol whose title does not say so still depends on the method sentence, which the dry run measured on 3 works, one run each. The sentence can also move a design part to `absent` on a protocol (seen once in 6 runs). The cut covers inverted clauses only; a declarative "X reduces Y" stays one phrase. Spelling variants are not written. Undoing a person's answer restores `protocol_title` with the restore note, as for every code, not with the original note. One machine, one model.

## D106 — The criterion names the question's population and comparator, an sw answer with nothing included says so, and Europe PMC's open text is drawn as a labelled PDF

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-26; implemented in slice 25a (plan `docs/product/sw-slice25-pico-criterion.md`, commit `e142c7a`, G2 by the owner's choice, A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1 and H1 as proposed). Not yet reviewed; measured live in 25b.

**Context:** Slice 24a (D105) failed gate 4 on the medicine question with 3 serious errors in 8 includes, two of them a population or a comparator the criterion never asked about (SW23). Its built-in-embedding medicine run included nothing and the answer was refused with 422 (SW22). 83 of the 112 works one medicine run planned to read had no open PDF (SW21).

**Decision:**

- *SW23, population and comparator.* `criterion_proposal` moves to v2. Each proposal lists `question_elements` (0 to 2; role `population` or `comparator`, the question's own words, and the part that asks for it). Code checks each element: the part exists, the words are in the question or in the person's steering, no role twice, no part shared (`question_element_unknown_part`, `question_element_not_in_question`, `duplicate_question_element`, `question_elements_share_part`). The consensus makes a role required when at least two of the valid runs list it and picks the base run only among runs that hold every required role; the criterion carries `question_elements` and `required_roles`. With no role required the consensus is byte for byte the one before this slice. The method file says setting is a system, domain, material or environment, and that the people a study is done in belong to the new population part (rule 8).
- *SW22, no include.* An `sw` answer asked for after discovery completed, with no work included at full text, ends as `no_evidence` with reason `no_includable_source`, the start snapshot's counts and no model call. Its notice reads "No work was included at full text when this answer started". The 422 stays for every other case.
- *SW21, Europe PMC.* The PDF route does not work from this machine (Europe PMC's PDF address 8 of 8 Cloudflare 403, `oa.fcgi` 33 of 33 404, NCBI PDFs `not_pdf`), so the text comes from REST `fullTextXML`. Europe PMC is asked once, only after the four PDF lookups and their fetches leave the record without a file, by DOI; a candidate needs the same DOI, a PMCID, `isOpenAccess = Y`, `inEPMC = Y` and `authMan = N`. The XML is drawn into a PDF with PyMuPDF `Story` in a bounded child process (5 MiB input, 60 s, 1 GiB, 200 pages, 30 MiB output, entity declarations refused) and attached through the existing extraction as `<PMCID>.europepmc.pdf`. Every surface that names one of its pages says "Europe PMC text, rendered p. n" through one formatter, and the passage sheet says its pages are not the publisher's. A Europe PMC candidate cannot be attached by hand as "same version" (422). Migration `0055` adds `europepmc` to the PDF provider lists and `wrong_type` to `pdf_candidates.access_status`.

**Measured in 25a:** replay of the three stored proposals of the ten 24a `sw` libraries through the new consensus: 10 of 10 byte-identical, both new fields `[]`. Dry run with `gpt-5.6-luna` medium, two questions twice, three proposals each (13 calls, one schema repair for a pre-existing phrase-length check): medicine `required_roles = ["comparator", "population"]` in both consensuses, words "adults with overweight or obesity" and "unrestricted eating or usual diet"; quantum `[]` in both, and 0 of its 6 single proposals listed a role, so the 24a quantum results stand. Europe PMC live check on the frozen sample of 7 PMCIDs: 7 of 7 attached with paged passages, title and first abstract sentence found and the rendered flag on every passage, drawing 0.16 to 0.20 s, child peak RSS 56 to 62 MiB, 8 to 19 pages. The first attempt passed 6 of 7: the drawing broke "quality-of-life" at a hyphen and extraction joined it into "quality-oflife"; hyphenated words up to 40 characters are now kept on one line and the second attempt passed 7 of 7.

**Limits:** A proposal set in which no run names the population or comparator is not caught by code; code only refuses a base run that lacks what the majority named. Only two roles. The full-text reading sends a missing part to the queue, it does not exclude. An answer with no include records the state when it started, not a finding that no source exists. Europe PMC covers only its open-access subset, no author manuscripts; the drawn page is not the publisher's page and MathML markup is lost. The gain (upper bound 30 of 83 PDF-less planned works) was counted on one run; how many become includes is not measured. One machine, one model, two questions.

## D105 — The default search workflow stays `legacy`: three of the four slice 24 gates did not pass

**Status:** accepted 2026-09-26 as the frozen consequence of the slice 24a measurement campaign (plan `docs/product/sw-slice24-measurement-campaign.md`, commit `65a7ec8`, decision 11); the owner decided on 2026-09-26: a fix slice 25 (SW23 population and comparator in the criterion, SW22 an answer when nothing is included), then the medicine question re-measured with a widened reference rule (SW18), then 24b if the gates pass; Sol reviews for this path stop only on high-severity findings, at most 3 plan and 4 code rounds. Part B (24b) did not run, so no default, test, fixture or document changed. **Date:** 2026-09-26.

**Context:** Slice 24 was to decide, by gates frozen before any run, whether `sw` replaces `legacy` as the default. Part A ran 14 researches on one Apple M1 Pro with `gpt-5.6-luna` (Codex, effort `medium`) on two questions, a quantum-networks question with a 31-work reference set and a time-restricted eating (TRE) question with a reference set built from meta-analysis tables: `sw` `quick`, `standard` twice, `detailed` and `standard` with the built-in embedding, and `legacy` `standard` twice, per question. Results: `docs/product/sw-slice24-results.md`; evidence `.local/sw-slice24-campaign-2026-09-26-134050/`.

**Decision:** `Settings.search_workflow` keeps its default `legacy`. The gates, as applied by the frozen `gates.py`:

- *Gate 1, completion:* **not passed.** 9 of the 10 `sw` researches ended with a `structurally_valid` answer. The TRE `standard` run with the built-in embedding read 24 PDFs and included none, and the answer run was refused with 422 ("Include at least one source") (SW22).
- *Gate 2, workflow comparison:* **not passed.** Quantum passed: pool mean `sw` 29.5 (29, 30) against `legacy` 8 (11, 5), margin 4; cited mean 5 (6, 4) against 5 (5, 5), and both `sw` runs cited a reference work. TRE was unreadable: the frozen reference rule gave |R| = 4 unique trials, below 10 (SW18), and unreadable counts as not passed. This is a descriptive decision rule on two runs per side, not a statistical non-inferiority test.
- *Gate 3, evidence integrity:* passed. 0 unresolved links or unlocated anchors in the nine `sw` answers, no `model_isolation_violation`, no output from another model.
- *Gate 4, analyst reading:* **not passed.** Quantum: 0 serious errors in 10 unique `include`s and 0 in 10 cited claims. TRE: 3 serious errors in 8 unique `include`s (a population without obesity; a 12:12 TRE comparator; an individualised dietitian programme as comparator, where the blind second reader disagreed and the rule counts it serious), 0 in 10 claims. Two or more serious errors stop Part B. The common cause is that the proposed criterion carried neither the population nor the comparator as its own part (SW23).
- *G1, arXiv source:* the rule held (642 placed blocks, 0 KaTeX 0.16.47 errors, 40 of 40 image-checked blocks from 26 papers read as correct), so `arxiv_source = auto` would be justified; it is not switched, because 24b did not run.

The campaign's other findings are SW18–SW25 in `docs/product/search-workflow-review-2026-09-18.md`: the reference-set rule, the two code findings (SW19, SW20), no open full text in medicine and Europe PMC (SW21), the no-answer case (SW22), the criterion's missing PICO parts (SW23), the full-text work limit and time targets (SW24), and a welded code-query phrase (SW25).

**Limits:** One machine, one model at one effort, two questions, one run per cell except gate 2's two per side. The reference sets are not ground truth: the quantum set comes from our own earlier OpenAlex-based runs, and the TRE set is an analyst's set of 4 trials read from three meta-analysis tables. Elicit is not a correctness criterion and its "Balanced" setting is not an equal budget. The analyst readings are two model readings, the first not blind, not human verification. G1's 40-block image sample is not a general reliability bound. OpenAlex's keyless daily budget ran out after the runs, so the check of whether stored OpenAlex queries cover missed works today was not done (one research only, partly). The gate verdicts say the frozen rule did not allow the switch; they do not say `legacy` answers better on a clinical question, which the campaign did not measure.

## D104 — An arXiv PDF read without Marker takes its numbered display equations from the authors' LaTeX source, matched to the page by their numbers, behind a flag that is off

**Status:** accepted; implemented and closed 2026-09-26 (slice 22). Implementation review: `gpt-6-sol` · high fourteen rounds (5, 4, 3, 2, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1 findings, r13 "düzeltmeyle hazır" with one low finding, r14 "hazır"). Round 1 said "hazır değil" with 5 findings (1 high, 3 medium, 1 low), all fixed with tests: macros are expanded with the definition in force at each group's position (a `\renewcommand` after an equation had changed that equation); the 20,000 cap counts every macro use and the length limit is checked while a group is expanded; a re-extraction that hits `pdf.py`'s time or memory limit is stored as `extraction_failed` with its attempt count and tried again like a failed Marker read (it had been stored as `nothing_placed`); the stamp read and the stored file's hash, durable write and read run in a worker thread; the citation chip carries a visible origin mark. Round 2 found the five closed and said "hazır değil" with 4 new findings (1 high, 2 medium, 1 low), all fixed with tests: the archive's `.sty` files are read where the main file loads them (`\usepackage` / `\RequirePackage`, in TeX's order, each once), not in archive order before the main file; the eligibility reads the record after the stamp thread returns; the stored file's check and its repair transition run under the version's locks from the row read then; a PDF already waiting for its source gets its `read_equations` step recorded in the next answer run. Round 3 said "hazır değil" with 2 findings and a test gap, all fixed with tests: a load inside a conditional or a brace group (a macro body, `\@ifpackageloaded`) no longer counts as run; the eligibility's row check, record read, decision and insert are one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction, so another process cannot enrich the record in between; `SourceStore.read`'s lock-budget timeout is tested to end `rate_gate_busy` with the PDF still `pending`. Round 4 said "hazır değil" with two counterexamples to the load rule (a `.tex` `\input` that may not run was read; `\verb` content was read as a load or a comment). Both were fixed, and the whole class was closed with a safety net rather than more TeX constructs: any definition of a macro anywhere in the archive that differs from every definition certain to run makes that macro ambiguous, and no group using it is placed (`macro_ambiguous`).
