Round 5 said "hazır değil" with counterexamples to that net (a body inside `\iffalse` repeated after the equation, a local group, `\let`, a delimited `\def`). The timing model was dropped for one rule that can only take placements away: a macro is safe only when every definition of it in the archive has one body and nothing else could redefine it (see *Archive*). Round 6 said "hazır değil" with two counterexamples (LaTeX3's `\cs_set:Npn` read as `\cs`; a `\def\alpha` inside `\begingroup … \endgroup` applied to the next equation). A source with LaTeX3 code is now unbounded, groups and environments count as depth, a definition of any name below the top level makes it unsafe, and an unbounded source places only groups without a control word. Round 7 said "hazır değil" with one counterexample: `\newcommand{\startlocal}{\begingroup}`, then `\startlocal\input{defs}\endgroup`, hid the group from the scan. Round 8 said "hazır değil" with one more (`\newcommand{\pass}[1]{#1}`, then `\pass{\begingroup}\input{defs}\endgroup`). Position is no longer modelled: a known name is never trusted and a user name needs one body everywhere (see *Archive*); rounds 6 and 7's group checks were removed. Round 9 said "hazır değil" with one counterexample (`{\newcommand{\foo}{x}}` then a bare `\csname foo\endcsname`, which makes `\foo` `\relax` outside the group): any name a name-building construct gives is now unsafe. Round 10 said "hazır değil" with the same class (`\@nameuse{\pick}` with `\def\pick{foo}` builds `\foo`): an argument holding a control sequence or `#` is now computed and makes the source unbounded, unless it is plain letters followed by `#n`. Round 11 said "hazır değil" with `\@nameuse{\pick{foo}}`, whose nested braces the scan skipped; every place the scan cannot read now fails closed. Round 12 said "hazır değil" with `\myop[{x]y}]{z}`, whose optional argument ended at the first `]` inside braces: braces in an optional argument now refuse the group. Round 13 said "düzeltmeyle hazır" with one low item (a brace after `\\` was read as escaped), fixed by reading escapes pairwise. Plan `docs/product/sw-slice22-arxiv-latex-source.md` (commit `ef1e788`), reviewed by `gpt-6-sol` · high over nine rounds (11, 5, 4, 4, 3, 3, 2, 2 findings, then "hazır"). The owner asked to proceed without questions and the coordinator took A1, B1, C1, D3, E1 and F1 as proposed; D's proposal moved from D1 to D3 after Sol's first round. **Date:** 2026-09-25.

**Context:** SW10 point 6 (a) asked for text and equations from an arXiv copy's LaTeX source, point 7 for a source equation to be used only once it is matched to its PDF page, and point 8 for the arXiv version to be carried. Marker (D52, D62) is an optional 4.4 GB component, so a person without it gets the text layer's broken display equations. The plan measured the live library read-only on one Apple M1 Pro (`.local/sw-slice22-plan-2026-09-25/`): 56 arXiv PDFs (53 versions), 45 of the 53 sources carrying `.tex`; in 43 versions, 873 of 1,520 equation-number lines passed the final matching rule as prototype candidates; 118 matches were read from page images and the 77 that fall under the final rule were all right, with the rule chosen after those images were seen.

**Decision:** A1: the route runs only while Marker is neither installed nor installing, and only for a PDF whose current text is not a Marker reading. D3: no page leaves Marker; with Marker installed nothing changes. C1: a PDF Marker has read is never read by the route, even after Marker is removed. F1: `DEIXIS_ARXIV_SOURCE` (`auto` | `off`) is off by default; the route is POSIX only (`fcntl`) and says "not available on this system" elsewhere. E1: the route runs where equations are read today (the background reader, an answer, a table, a cell); an answer run's `read_equations` step records the route's outcome and never pauses the run.

- *Version (decision 1).* The arXiv version comes from the PDF's address and from the arXiv stamp printed on pages 1–2. A conflict between them is refused (`version_conflict`), and so is no version at all (`no_version`). The record must carry the same arXiv identifier; if it carries none, several, or another version, the PDF is refused as `record_identity_unknown`, `record_identity_conflict` or `record_version_conflict`. The result is stored once per PDF in `asset_arxiv_versions`. `enrich_source` checks the record again when a landing address arrives, and a refusal withdraws a source reading and makes the previous extraction current again.
- *Fetch (decision 2).* `https://arxiv.org/e-print/<id>v<N>` goes through `fetch.fetch_file`, with every redirect hop gated. Requests reach the server at least 3 s apart across the processes of one data directory, by `arxiv-sources/.rate.lock` and a durable `.rate` stamp; a start stamp with no end waits start + 33 s. There are 3 attempts 10 minutes apart and one repair after a stored file fails its sha256. Files are written through `.part-<pid>`, fsync and `os.replace`, and a `Content-Disposition` naming another version is `version_mismatch`. State lives in `arxiv_sources`. No request carries an e-mail address or other identity.
- *Archive (decision 3).* The archive is read in memory in a bounded child process: 64 MB unpacked, 1,000 members, 5 MB of text, include depth 5, macro depth 8, 20,000 expander calls and 4,000 characters per group. The five definition forms are expanded, including control-symbol names such as `\1`, only for safe names (below). The archive's own `.sty` files are inlined where the main file (or another of them) loads them with `\usepackage` / `\RequirePackage`, once, in TeX's load order, and only when the load is at the top level of its file: one inside a TeX conditional (`\iffalse`, `\ifdefined`, `\if@…` … `\fi`) or a brace group (a macro body, an argument of `\@ifpackageloaded`) is not counted as run and reads nothing, and a file whose conditionals do not balance leaves every later load undetermined; a `.tex`, `.def` or `.sty` file counts only where such an `\input` reaches it; `\verb|…|`, `\verb*|…|` and verbatim-like environments (`verbatim`, `Verbatim`, `lstlisting`, `minted`, `comment`) are blanked before comments are stripped, so their content is never a command or a comment. **Name rule (round 8):** where a definition is in force is not modelled; every text file of the archive, loaded or not, and the flattened text are scanned whole, inside conditionals, groups and macro bodies or not. A known name is never trusted: any definition anywhere of a name that the web app's KaTeX knows (its commands and symbols) or that is defined in the document body of `\documentclass{article}\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}` under pdfLaTeX (`latex_kernel_names.json`, 3,742 names from TeX Live 2021's kernel, `article.cls`, the AMS packages and LuaTeX's primitives, written by `scripts/latex_kernel_names.py`), by any definer, `\let` or built form, makes it unsafe, since the paper may use it where that definition is not in force (after a group or a macro-opened group closes). A user name is safe when it is unknown in that sense, every parsed definition of it has one and the same body, none of them is `\providecommand`, it is not `\renewcommand`ed without a `\newcommand`, `\def` or `\DeclareMathOperator` of it, it is never named by a name-building construct anywhere (a bare or targeted `\csname … \endcsname`, `\ifcsname`, `\expandafter\ifx\csname`, `\@ifundefined{…}`, `\@nameuse{…}`, `\@namedef{…}`, `\@ifdefinable\x`, etoolbox's `\cs…` / `\ifcs…` / `\letcs` with a name argument), and nothing else targets it: `\let` and its forms, `\gdef` / `\edef` / `\xdef`, a `\def` with delimited parameters, `\DeclareRobustCommand`, the document-command forms, a `\csname … \endcsname` or etoolbox `\cs…` target, or any definer not parsed (a word ending in "def" or "let", containing "command" / "Command" / "cmd", or starting with "Declare"; a test such as `\ifdef\x` also marks `\x`). The invariant is: a safe name is a user name with one body, never named by a name-building construct, and never a known name. It is expanded with that body wherever the group is, if it is defined in a file the main file reads. The tests show the forms listed below; the invariant is not a proof that no other construct changes what a name means where the equation stands. In every name-building construct, bare or as a definer's target, an argument of plain characters (no `\`, `#` or brace) is that one name; plain letters followed by `#n` (`\@namedef{keycolor#1}`) make every name with that prefix unsafe; any other argument holding a control sequence or `#` (`\@nameuse{\pick}`, `\csname\pick\endcsname`, `\csname fo\pick\endcsname`, `\@ifundefined{,#1}`), and a control sequence given where a name is expected (`\@nameuse\pick`), is computed and makes the source unbounded; `\@ifdefinable\x` and `\letcs\x` name `\x` itself; a declaration with a plain-text argument (`\DeclareGraphicsExtensions{.pdf,.png}`) marks each letter run in it. A name built any other way, a target reached through `\expandafter`, or LaTeX3 code (`\ExplSyntaxOn`, `\ProvidesExpl…`, `\cs_new…` / `\cs_set…` / `\cs_gset…` / `\cs_generate…`) makes the source unbounded: there any name may have been redefined, so every group holding a control word or symbol is refused. A group that uses an unsafe name, directly or through another macro, is refused as `macro_ambiguous` and never placed. This trades round 1's timeline for safety: a `\renewcommand` between two equations gives the macro two bodies, so both equations are refused; an identical duplicate anywhere is harmless and expands. Rounds 6 and 7's group depth and macro-opened-group checks were removed. What the tests show: each of Sol's round 4 to 12 counterexamples (the `\alpha` ones because `\alpha` is known: `\begingroup`, `\bgroup`, `{…}`, an environment, `\startlocal` holding `\begingroup`, `\let\startlocal\begingroup`, `\pass{\begingroup}` with a definition or an `\input` inside), `\gdef`, `\edef`, `\DeclareRobustCommand`, `\NewDocumentCommand`, `\global\let`, a literal, prefixed or computed `\csname` / `\csdef` / `\@namedef`, `\expandafter\let`, `\cs_set:Npn`, `\tl_set:Nn \alpha`, `\cs_new:Npn`, `\providecommand`, a renew-only name, a local user definition followed by a bare `\csname foo\endcsname`, `\@ifundefined{foo}`, `\ifcsname foo\endcsname`, `\expandafter\ifx\csname foo\endcsname`, `\csuse{foo}`, `\ifcsdef{foo}`, `\@nameuse{foo}` or `\@ifdefinable\foo`, the computed forms `\@nameuse{\pick}`, `\@nameuse\pick`, `\csname\pick\endcsname`, `\csname fo\pick\endcsname`, `\ifcsdef{\pick}`, `\@ifundefined{,#1}` and `\@ifundefined{f9#1}` (unbounded), the unreadable inputs `\@nameuse{\pick{foo}}`, an unclosed `\@nameuse{foo`, `\@ifundefined` with no argument, a stray `\endcsname`, a `\csname` never ended, an unclosed `\verb` or `comment` environment (unbounded), a truncated `\def\foo` or `\newcommand{\foo}`, a body naming `#2` with one parameter, `\def\foo #1{…}`, a body never closed (the name unsafe) and a macro use whose argument is missing, whose `[` never closes or whose optional argument holds braces (`\myop[{x]y}]{z}`, `\myop[a\\{x]y\\}b]{z}`; the group refused), and a known name defined once (`\alpha`, `\vec`, `\a`, `\label`) ends in a refusal, not a wrong equation; the LaTeX3, group, macro-opened group and prefixed forms are tested both directly and through another macro; a user macro defined once inside a group and used there, and an identical duplicate, place. The scan fails closed: wherever it cannot read its input (a name argument it cannot match, a `\csname` without its `\endcsname` or a stray `\endcsname`, a definition body never closed or naming a parameter it lacks, a definition form it does not parse, a `\verb` or verbatim environment never closed, a macro use whose argument it cannot read or whose optional argument holds an unescaped brace, `\\{` included), the name involved is unsafe (the group, for a macro use), or the source is unbounded when the name cannot be known. A form not in that list is guarded only by the broad definer match, the name-builder scan and the LaTeX3 check. Not seen: a user name that a package or class outside the archive also defines (the archive's one body is then expanded though the paper may use the package's meaning where the archive's is not in force), what a command derives from a name (`\newtheorem{thm}` defining `\thethm`), names that other classes and packages define beyond the kernel list, and catcode or mathcode changes. A file loaded no other way defines nothing, so a group using its macros fails the KaTeX gate. Every macro use counts toward the 20,000 per paper: the group that passes it is left out, and so is a later group that still needs an expansion; a group passing 16,000 characters is stopped while it is being expanded. Layout commands are removed and the seven-rule rewrite table applied. A group is left out when it carries `\ref`/`\cite`, is too long, uses a command, control symbol or environment the web app's KaTeX does not know (`katex_commands.json`, KaTeX 0.16.47, written by `scripts/katex_commands.mjs`), or is numbered on its first row and continues unnumbered.
- *Matching (decision 4).* Every equation-number line of the PDF gets a region of at most 12 non-prose lines above it, and regions are scored against the numbered source groups by letter multisets. An order-constrained assignment maximises the summed F1 − 0.5. A number passes when recall ≥ 0.90 and either the paper margin ≥ 0.20, or the window margin ≥ 0.20 with the paper margin ≥ 0, so the order never overrules letters. The region is then trimmed, vertically overlapping parts are absorbed, and a region holding a word foreign to the group's LaTeX is refused. Table-caption and OCR pages get no placement.
- *Placement (decision 5).* In `pdf.py`'s child, a passing region's lines are replaced by `$$\n<latex>\n$$ (n)`, Marker's format. Offsets are in `normalize_page_text` space, and `chunk_page(keep_display_math=True)` never cuts a block. A region line that never reached the page text, or two regions that overlap, are refused.
- *State (decision 6).* The version string is `…+arxiv-latex-v1`, and the target and state follow four precedence rules. The last-write guard runs inside `reextract_asset`'s `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction and refuses a removed asset, a record change, a newer extraction and a Marker install. Nothing placed and offsets not resolved are D45 rejections. A re-extraction stopped by `pdf.py`'s time or memory limit is `failed` with reason `extraction_failed` and an attempt count: the background reader tries it again after 10 minutes up to 3 attempts, an answer run while attempts are left, and the person's retry at any time. The stamp read, the downloaded file's hash and durable write and the stored file's read and hash run in worker threads; the rows are written on the event loop. A caller that finds a not-settled row decides under the locks, so it waits for another task's attempt in flight instead of reporting it as waiting. The person's retry is the existing equations retry.
- *Label and contract (decision 7, B1).* The label is set per chunk: `text_source = 'latex_source'` for a chunk holding a placed block; the rest of the page keeps `text_layer`. Migration `0054` rebuilds `passages` with the new CHECK value and keeps rowids, FTS and the `cell_evidence_same_source` trigger. `step-input.schema.json` gets the value, and `report_section_draft` moves to v2 with the `equation_origin` check (`unknown_passage_id`, `equation_origin_not_cited`, `equation_origin_mismatch`). The method package's two reference files say what `latex_source` means, and `skill_package_hash` moves from `sha256:7d4e238c…6fca` to `sha256:1700eb6e55e963a61c569cc0374588cab71f20318bf5061ef493c67d87cb9cc6`.
- *Version label and UI (decisions 8, 9).* `math_json.source` carries the arXiv id, version, where the version came from, the record label, sha256, placements and reasons. The source row says "Equations from the arXiv source (v2) · n matched to p pages by their numbers". The passage view names the chunk's own equation numbers and says the rest is the PDF's text, a citation chip carries a Σ mark named "arXiv source", and a reference shows an "arXiv source" pill. The words are "matched to the page by its number" and "the authors' LaTeX source", never "verified", "exact", "reliable" or "correct".

**Departures from SW10:** (1) prose is not taken from the source: passages stay tied to PDF pages (D27), and only numbered display equations come from the source; (2) Marker's page selection is not narrowed and no page leaves Marker (SW10.6 (c) and SW10.7's speed point; D3); (3) inline mathematics is not taken from the source, and D62's path is unchanged; (4) the route runs only without Marker, so a number that fails the threshold stays in the text layer rather than going to Marker; (5) the order constraint is not counting and never overrules letters; (6) the route does not run in the full-text fetch or reading runs (E1), so D85's reading run and D98's fetch arm see source equations only once the PDF was read in the background or by an answer.

**Acceptance (2026-09-25, one M1 Pro, `.local/sw-slice22-acceptance-2026-09-25/`, no model):** (a) The live library was copied with SQLite's backup API (opened read-only; schema `0036`, 17,448 passages) and migrated to `0053`, then to `0054` in 0.35 s. Rowid/id/text_sha256/text_source were equal, the FTS query and `integrity-check` passed, `foreign_key_check` was empty, and the DDL differed only in the CHECK; the trigger SQL was the same and the new tables empty. On the 56 PDFs (53 versions, all eligible; 45 `tex`, 5 `pdf_only`, 3 `no_tex`) the product's code found 1,521 number lines and 882 candidates in 45 versions (plan: 1,520 and 873 in 43; 866 shared, 17 only in the product, 6 only in the prototype, from the product's own line extraction). It placed 787 blocks on 225 pages of 44 versions; the plan has no placed count to compare. Candidates not placed: 53 table or OCR page, 31 `not_in_page_text`, 9 `katex_unknown`, 2 `ref_or_cite`, 0 `offsets_unresolved`. Against Marker's stored reading, with the method of the plan's number 7, 725 of 796 candidates with a Marker equation of the same number agree (91.1%), and 644 of 708 placed ones (91.0%); the plan's 94.1% was for r1's rule on Marker's pages. (b) The first render with the web app's KaTeX found two errors, a trailing control space that ate `\end{aligned}`'s backslash and an undefined `\1` macro. Both were fixed in code before (f) (control-symbol macro names, a control-symbol KaTeX gate, the trailing backslash dropped), and after the fix 787 of 787 placed groups render with 0 errors. (c) A real reading on the copy, flag `auto`, Marker not installed in the scratch data directory: `2410.08980v2` (text layer only in the live library) went to `+arxiv-latex-v1` with 1 `latex_source` chunk; `1910.05310v1` was `no_source` (`pdf_only`); `1511.06344v1`, whose earlier text-layer extraction was made current again in the copy to stand in for a person without Marker, got 35 placements and 23 `latex_source` chunks. All old passages stayed, and its 2 evidence links still resolve as `text_superseded`. (d) Three live fetches through `SourceStore.ensure` made six requests (each e-print redirects once), 3.17–3.61 s apart, with only the product's User-Agent; the three files' sha256 equal the plan's. (e) The child process took a median of 0.46 s per paper and at most 0.81 s (45 papers; the run before the round 1 fixes gave 0.50 and 0.84 s). After the round 1 fixes, again after the round 2, 3 and 4 fixes (5 of the 45 `tex` sources carry 13 `.sty`/`.def` files, 10 of which the main files load), (a) and (b) were run again on the same copy: the same 1,521 number lines, 882 candidates and 787 placements with the same LaTeX, 0 KaTeX errors; the most macro uses in one paper is 805, no group reached `macro_limit`. After round 4: 10 of the 45 sources have ambiguous macros (mostly internal `\@…` names and layout macros), 9 display groups (7 numbered, in 3 sources) are refused as `macro_ambiguous`, none of them a matching candidate, so candidates (882), placements (787) and their LaTeX are unchanged. After rounds 9 to 12, (a) and (b) on the same copy: 1,521 number lines, 885 candidates, 776 placements on 221 pages of 42 versions, 0 KaTeX errors, the same set and LaTeX as after round 8 (rounds 10 to 12 changed no count). Every placement is one of round 4's 787 with the same LaTeX, so no new block needs an image check. The 11 dropped since round 4 are 6 in `1403.0001v1` and 4 in `2104.02783v1` (bundled `algorithm2e.sty` and `enumitem.sty` build names with `\csname`, so both stay unbounded) and 1 in `2005.00948v1` (`\DeclareMathOperator*{\argmax}`, a name KaTeX knows). 37 of the 45 sources have at least one unsafe name; 27 display groups (23 numbered) in 5 sources are refused as `macro_ambiguous`, 16 of them matching candidates; the name-builder scan added 2 groups in `1911.00745v1`, neither placed before. Not placed: 53 table or OCR page, 31 `not_in_page_text`, 16 `macro_ambiguous`, 7 `katex_unknown`, 2 `ref_or_cite`. Against Marker, 729 of 799 candidates agree (91.2%) and 633 of 697 placed ones (90.8%). The child took a median of 0.47 s and at most 0.87 s in the round 11 run. Round 7's group check had left 658 placements and round 6's 777. (f) After code and constants were frozen, 40 placements were drawn (seed 104, at most 3 per paper, 24 papers, none from the plan's samples; 20 by paper margin, 20 decided by the order) and read by eye from 150 dpi crops with the region drawn: 40 of 40 groups right, and no region took another text line (four tall boxes checked by their line lists and in the page text). After rounds 8 to 12 all 40 are placed with the same LaTeX, and no placement is new, so (f) was not repeated.

**Limits:** One computer (Apple M1 Pro), one library, three fields. The rule was chosen on this data after its image sample was seen, and there is no held-out set. The images had one reader in the plan (its author) and one in acceptance (the implementer, the same model family); neither 77/77 nor 40/40 is an accuracy bound for other data or readers, and acceptance (f)'s placements come from the same papers. 873 is a count of prototype candidates, not of placements. The route is POSIX only, and the 3 s rate holds only across the processes of one data directory. The r1 complete-page rule was not checked, since D3 does not use it. Marker's reading is a reference, not a ground truth. There is no speed gain (D3). The macro rules are a text scan, not TeX: they cover the forms the tests name; a user name that a package or class outside the archive also defines, names defined by classes and packages beyond the kernel list, and catcode or mathcode changes are not seen; twelve review rounds each found a new construct, so another one may exist. The rules are chosen to refuse rather than place when unsure, which costs 11 of round 4's 787 placements on this data. The kernel list is TeX Live 2021's, from one computer. The product's placement was measured only in acceptance (a) and (f), and whether a person reads a placed block better than the text layer was not measured. `export.arxiv.org` answered httpx with 406, for an unknown reason, so the route uses `arxiv.org`. Acceptance (c)'s third PDF was a Marker-read PDF set back to its text layer in the copy, because the live library has only one text-layer arXiv PDF with a `.tex` source. The flag is off by default, and the live library did not change.

## D103 — Semantic search gets a keyless built-in model installed on request, embeds batch by batch with partial results and a bounded HTTP 429 wait, and reads an English sentence for a question not in English

**Status:** accepted; implemented 2026-09-25 (slice 21). Implementation review: `gpt-6-sol` · high five rounds (9, 5, 3, 3 + 1 low findings, then "hazır"). The owner asked to proceed without questions and the coordinator took the plan's proposals A1, B1 and C1. `gpt-6-sol` · high reviewed the plan over seven rounds (11, 5, 4, 3, 3 + 1 low, 2 findings, then "hazır"). Its first implementation round said "hazır değil" with 9 findings (2 high, 5 medium, 2 low), all fixed: uploaded-PDF text counted when the request goes out, a request that failed kept apart as unconfirmed; a provider's 200 reply checked for one vector per text, index, dimension and finite values; `fcntl` imported only after the platform check; a removal that leaves files fails and says what stayed; a 429 wait charged the time that really passed; the install's clean-up run off the event loop; a sentence for a question read as English refused; the transcript reads whether the model was installed from the step, not from today's Settings; the runner reads `onnxruntime`'s version from package metadata and imports only the standard library and `fastembed`. The second implementation round said "hazır değil" with 5 findings (2 high, 3 medium), all fixed: every batch's vectors must have the dimension of the step's query vector, kept in the step output across a resume, else `bad_reply`; a cancelled install waits for its deleting thread to end before it releases the locks; the transcript says the built-in model "was not installed when this step ran" and the removal dialog says stored similarities may still be used for the same question revision; the uploaded-PDF counts are split into attempted (a request carrying the text was issued: a reply came back, or it failed after the connection was made) and confirmed (vectors came back), and a connection never made counts nothing; the wait budget is checked after every wake and a refused batch is never sent again once the step has waited past 180 s. The third implementation round said "hazır değil" with 3 findings (1 high, 2 medium), fixed in the computation: a stored passage vector whose dimension differs from the step's query vector is left out of the similarity and counted (`stored_other_dimension`), its passage taking the keyword order; the persisted wait budget is checked before every request, so a step paused by the late wake that passed 180 s sends nothing after its resume; a batch's uploaded ids are written as pending before its request is awaited. The fourth round found that the counts and the transcript still overstated two of these, and corrected them: `from_store` counts only the stored vectors the similarity used, and a step left with none comparable fails and says it continued with keyword search; ids still pending when a step stops are counted as unknown, apart from attempted. Later rounds are recorded in row 21 of `docs/product/sw-status.md`. **Date:** 2026-09-25.

**Context:** SW8 made the embedding a fifth ordering signal with no authority, and D79 built that signal on `sw` researches. Semantic search still needed a Gemini or OpenAI key or a separately installed Ollama or LM Studio (D29), which most people who will use DEIXIS do not have. SW8 asked for a keyless built-in model, Settings that say how to get a free Gemini key and what the free tier means, and an English sentence for a question in another language. SW8's status line also named two gaps for every provider: a failed batch threw away the whole result, and an HTTP 429 was not waited out. The plan (`docs/product/sw-slice21-builtin-local-embedding.md`) measured `fastembed` 0.8.1 with the quantised `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` on one Apple M1 Pro (`.local/sw-slice21-plan-2026-09-25/`). The environment took 145 MB installed and the five model files 67,179,163 bytes. On the SW7 pool, cutting at 256 tokens halved the time (51 s for 1,369 records) and kept the five-signal median (104 / 10 in the top 100) and both rescued positives. None of the 46 stored `sw` libraries had ever run the embedding.

**Decision:** A1: the person writes the English sentence and no model proposes it, so the model contract and `skill_package_hash` (`sha256:7d4e238c…6fca`) are unchanged. B1: the built-in model runs outside DEIXIS's own environment. It is installed on request under `<data dir>/tools/` (uv, Python 3.12, `fastembed==0.8.1`, uv's cache and Python and Hugging Face's home all inside the data directory), with the model files from the pinned revision `aa8f8b0` of `Qdrant/bge-small-en-v1.5-onnx-Q`, each checked for size and sha256. `installed.json` is written last. `documents/embedding_runner.py` runs in that environment and answers one JSON line per batch. `uv.lock` and `pyproject.toml` are unchanged, and the DEIXIS process never imports `fastembed`, `onnxruntime` or `numpy`. The install job lives in a job file and is owned by an `fcntl.flock` install lock; runners hold a shared in-use lock that install and removal take exclusively. Recovery after a crash deletes only when it holds both locks. The option is POSIX only in this slice. The stored model name is `builtin:bge-small-en-v1.5@aa8f8b0:256`, and `chosen()` never picks it by itself. C1: the whole pool is embedded before the ranking (about 4 minutes on the largest stored pool on the M1 Pro). For every provider, the query is embedded first, then the texts batch by batch. Each batch is written in its own transaction and followed by a checkpoint, so a pause waits at most one batch and a resumed run embeds only what is missing. A failed later batch ends the step `partial`. The step opens with the provider and stored model frozen in its output, and the ranking reads the model from there. Stored similarities of the same revision and model are read even when the model is not installed now. Passages always embed the query and fall back to keyword order. An HTTP 429 is waited out from `Retry-After`, then Gemini's `retryDelay`, then 10 / 20 / 40 s: at most 3 times per batch, and only when the wait fits in what is left of 180 s per step. The wait is kept in the step output across a resume and taken in one-second slices that a pause, cancel or new revision interrupts. It counts the time that really passed and is checked after every wake and before every request, a resumed step's included: an event loop that wakes late can take a step past 180 s by at most one slice, and the step then sends nothing more. Every batch's vectors must have the dimension of the step's query vector; a stored passage vector of another dimension (a local server that changed its model under the same name) is left out of the similarity, counted as `stored_other_dimension` and not in `from_store`, and not embedded again; the step is `partial` when some passages could still be compared and `failed`, with the keyword order, when none could. Stored source similarities are numbers, not vectors, and have no such check. The English sentence lives in `scope_english_questions` (migration `0053`). It is written once per scope revision, opens no revision and makes no decision stale, and is carried to a new revision whose question text is unchanged. With no sentence and a question not read as English, the built-in arm is off and says why (`english_question_missing`); the other providers take the question as written. Settings lists Gemini, built-in, OpenAI, Ollama, LM Studio, Off. The research view shows the English-sentence line and form, and a conditional line under the answer and table buttons when Gemini or OpenAI will rank passages. The passage step records the uploaded files and passages whose text went in an issued request (`uploaded_files_attempted`, `uploaded_passages_attempted`) apart from those vectors came back for (`…_confirmed`). A batch's uploaded ids are written as pending before its request is awaited: a request cut off in flight (a cancelled task, a forced shutdown) leaves them pending, and whether the request even started is not known, so a resume moves them to `uploaded_files_unknown` / `uploaded_passages_unknown`, not to attempted; an id later sent again is counted as attempted, and a failure before any connection clears the pending ids. The transcript shows attempted but not confirmed as "went in a request that brought no vectors back; whether {service} received it is not known", and unknown as "was being sent when the step stopped; whether {service} received it is not known", on a failed or partial step as on a finished one; these names depart from the plan's `uploaded_files_sent` / `uploaded_passages_sent` so that a failed request is neither hidden nor called received. The transcript's line for stored similarities says the built-in model "was not installed when this step ran", read from the step, where the plan wrote "is not installed now". Named departures from SW8: Off stays last; no "Recommended" badge on Gemini; no model proposal (A1); the 256-token cut; the measured disk sizes ("about 212 MB", runtime about 145 MB installed, model 67 MB, plus about 74 MB if uv downloads Python) instead of "about 130 MB"; the free-tier sentence shown with every Gemini use and the uploaded-PDF line shown without a count, both conditional, because the tier cannot be read from the key and the passages to be sent are not known when the button is pressed.

**Limits:** One computer (Apple M1 Pro) and one topic: the 256-token cut was chosen on one pool of 1,369 records with 20 positives, and the acceptance timed 50.8 s there and 243.4 s on the largest flow pool (6,217 records). Passage-level retrieval with the local model was not measured, so its use in the answer step is a design intention. Gemini's free-tier rate limit and 429 behaviour were not measured live, and the wait constants were picked by hand. A full research on a Gemini key without billing was not run; this is an open acceptance limit, and the 429 rule was tested only against a fake endpoint. No stored research had ever run the embedding: all 46 stored `sw` libraries had semantic search off. The language rule has two known failure modes: a question in another language written without accents is read as English and embedded; an English question full of accented names can be read as not English, and "The question is already in English" is the way out. The arm's switch-off (SW8.7) is still open. DEIXIS cannot tell a free-tier key from a paid one. The acceptance on migrated copies showed the four code signals' rows byte-for-byte unchanged and listed the records the embedding rescued (31 and 14), with no claim that they are better.

## D102 — An sw research shows where each of its works stands, keeps the flow of an answer's start, counts how often the person changed a machine decision, draws a small audit sample, and exports its search against the PRISMA-S items

**Status:** accepted; implemented 2026-09-25 (slice 20); `gpt-6-sol` · high reviewed the implementation over four rounds (5, 1, 2 findings, all fixed; fourth round "hazır"). Sol birinci tur: düzeltmeyle hazır, 5 bulgu, hepsi düzeltildi (the waiting bucket now shares D99's rule; a list edit is timed by the row that set the head's selection; a query group ends on its highest page; the abstract audit cards send the person to the source list; the Markdown names every group's stored pages). Sol ikinci tur: düzeltmeyle hazır, 1 bulgu, düzeltildi (the abstract audit card opens the source list at its work by id, not by title). Sol üçüncü tur: düzeltmeyle hazır, 2 bulgu, düzeltildi (the PDF filter and leaving the Sources tab end the single-work focus; "Show all sources" resets every filter). Sol dördüncü tur: hazır. The owner answered the plan's questions the same day, both as proposed: A = A1 (the two full-text strata of the audit sample are answered through separate audit endpoints; the two abstract strata are for viewing and a manual selection and do not repair an abstract-stage exclusion; a person's abstract-stage code is a separate slice), B = the export is in English only. `gpt-6-sol` · high reviewed the plan over six rounds (8, 4, 3, 2, 2, 1 findings, all folded in). **Date:** 2026-09-25.

**Context:** SW11 points 8, 12 and 13 asked for the queue's size and reasons in every research, a small audit sample of works decided outside the queue, flow counts beside an answer given before the queue is empty, and a count of how often the person overruled code or the model. SW9 and the main plan's row 20 asked for PRISMA-style counts and a search report. The plan (`docs/product/sw-slice20-flow-audit-prisma.md`) measured 46 stored `sw` researches read-only (`.local/sw-slice20-plan-2026-09-25/`): a provisional bucket rule put every work in one place (46 / 46) and agreed with D101, D96 and D99 in the same snapshot; the person had 4 open decisions in 2 researches, none of which changed a machine decision; 23 of 24 stored answers were written with a non-empty queue and none kept the flow; 129 of 390 keyword query groups did not end completed or with zero results.

**Decision:** `workflow/flow_counts.py` puts every work of the current revision in one of 18 buckets, the person's decision first by D101's rule (confirmed, criterion not met, excluded, to look at again), then the work's outcome, reason code and next step, with `waiting_for_pdf` read from D99's own rule (`fulltext.waits_for_pdf`); the buckets add up to the works (asserted), and the five counts of SW11.12 and the queue by reason sit beside them. PRISMA 2020-style boxes (rows returned by searches and by citation requests, works found, works, abstracts the model read, out of scope by the model runs and by code, full text sought, not retrieved and read, criterion not met, queued, included) all carry `flow_status: "incomplete_no_human_screening"`, are never added up and draw no diagram; works found reads `null` ("not counted") before D93's hit rows. An `sw` answer run opens a `code:answer_start_snapshot` step at its start that stores the flow, the scope and selection revisions and the included works whose only text is the person's unread file; a resumed run keeps it, and the view says "the state of the included sources changed" when the answer's own selection revision differs. Answers stored before this slice say the flow was not recorded. `workflow/overrides.py` classifies each of the person's decisions against the machine decision it closed (for a queue or audit answer, the rows strictly before the human row by `(created_at, rowid)`; for a list edit, as of the `selection_history` row that set the head's current selection, a selection a new head copied followed to its source version's row, a same-millisecond decision giving `time_unknown`) as `overruled`, `agreed`, `settled_open` or `time_unknown`, by path (queue, audit, list), decider and direction; "not sure", "wrong PDF" and "to look at again" are counted apart. The screen says "Of your N decisions, you changed a decision of code or the model runs in M", never a rate. `workflow/audit.py` draws, per stratum (F1 two agreeing includes, F2 two agreeing "criterion not met", A1 out of scope at the abstract stage by the model runs, A2 by a code rule), the `AUDIT_PER_STRATUM = 3` works with the smallest `sha256("{research}|{revision}|{criterion hash or 'none'}|{stratum label}|{work}")`, the label being the plan measurement's stratum name so the product draws the works the plan measured. A work the person answered in the audit stays in the stratum of its fresh prior machine decision. Nothing is stored. F1 / F2 rows are answered through `POST …/audit/{svid}/decision` and taken back through `…/undo`, which share D96's answer writer and mark the `stage_decision_recorded` event `via: "audit"`; inside the write the work must still be in its stratum's current sample, the version's current decision must still be the token's machine decision, and the token must match, else 409 and nothing is written. D96's undo now checks the origin of a person's decision first: an audit decision is refused (`audit_decision`), an event with any other `via` or no event is `origin_unknown`; audit decisions are left out of the queue's decided list. `GET …/prisma-s?format=md|json` exports the 16 PRISMA-S items with the statuses `reported`, `incomplete`, `not_performed` (with the protocol record or a load-pinned code source that shows it) and `not_recorded`, a `trace` of resolvable row ids per item, aggregate counts apart, a search table by query group (a group's end state is its highest page's; the Markdown lists every group's stored page ids) and the flow counts; its opening statement says it is not a PRISMA-compliant review. `GET /api/effort-limits` gives Home the `sw` depth numbers from `rules.py`. All of it is read in the research view's one snapshot; the view writes nothing. No migration, no new reason code, protocol body and `skill_package_hash` unchanged.

**Limits:** A person's decision at the abstract stage and "send back to full-text reading" are an open requirement: an A1 / A2 work the person includes (the audit card opens the source list at that work by its id, and the list's own controls decide) goes straight into the answer input, and the event that reopens it is a person wanting to overrule an abstract-stage exclusion for reading, or slice 23's code gate. The audit gives counts, not rates. The sample is stateless and drifts when a later reading run puts a work with a smaller digest in a stratum; the screen keeps the current sample and the earlier answers apart and draws no rate from either, and a frozen cohort (the drawn ids and the moment in a table) is an open requirement. Stored data holds 4 person decisions in 2 researches and no answered audit row, so the override classes other than `settled_open` and every audit answer are covered by synthetic tests only. PRISMA-S item 15 reads `incomplete` in all 40 of the plan's researches with works (a keyword query group that did not end completed or with zero results in each; in 33 a group read nothing because of a rate limit, in 37 one read nothing for any reason) and item 9 in all 40 (the limits have no stored justification). The export was not checked by a journal or a librarian. A work whose code says it waits for a PDF while another version already has PDF text is off D99's list and counted "text in hand, not read yet"; a person's own list decision still comes first, so such a work is counted under the person's decision while D99 may list it. Acceptance on migrated copies of the plan's 46 libraries (`.local/sw-slice20-acceptance-2026-09-25/`): buckets equal the plan's in 46 / 46, the audit sample the same works in 46 / 46, the override classes `settled_open:queue` 2 in the two slice 16 libraries and empty elsewhere, 575 traces all resolving, 390 keyword and 294 chain groups with 129 not complete, and no table's row count changed by the view or the export. On the four largest, measured again after the review's fixes while another project held four cores, the derivation given the context took 0.016–0.018 s (budget 0.05; 0.019–0.075 s when the queue scan and the waiting list it shares with the tab counts are recomputed too), `GET …/audit` 0.13–0.15 s (0.5), the export 0.15–0.24 s in either format (1), an audit answer and its undo 0.32–0.37 s each (0.5), and `research_view` moved from 4.32–9.54 s to 4.35–9.62 s; that view was already slow before the slice. Whether a person reads the flow line, answers the audit rows, or finds the export useful, and anything live, were not measured.

## D101 — An sw research shows what each search arm and ranking signal brought, counted against the person's own decisions; comparative signal contribution, the stopping rule and the costly-signal switch-off stay out of the product

**Status:** accepted; implemented 2026-09-25 (slice 19). The owner answered the plan's questions A–E as proposed the same day. `gpt-6-sol` · high reviewed the plan over three rounds (9, 3, 3 findings) and the implementation over three rounds (4 findings; 3 findings in the check of the fixes; "hazır" in the third). **Date:** 2026-09-25.

**Context:** SW13, SW1.8, SW7.6 and SW8.7 asked for a probe set of verified works, a table per search arm and per ranking signal in every research, a signal switched off after it adds nothing, and a stopping rule for repeated rounds. The plan (`docs/product/sw-slice19-probe-tables.md`) measured 43 stored `sw` researches read-only (`.local/sw-slice19-plan-2026-09-25/`). A person had confirmed a work in 2 of them (1 each). The works two agreeing model runs included are chosen by the order itself: in quantum 90% of them (308 of 343) sit inside the abstract read limit of the stored order against 37% of the reference list's works, and dropping one signal from the order pushes an included work out of that limit 200 times for 35 pulled in (5.7 : 1; the reference list gives 180 : 120). Measuring a signal against the research's own includes would make every signal look useful. TF-IDF and the embedding ran in none of the 43. No arm repeats, so a stopping rule has nothing to stop.

**Decision:** The probe set is derived on read, never stored (`workflow/probes.py`), over the current revision's works with one precedence rule on the head's current selection: a selection that is not the person's is no probe; one linked to a queue answer (`human_selection_links`) follows that answer, and a stale answer leaves the probe set and counts as `look_again`; otherwise it is the person's own list edit (`included` a confirmed positive, `excluded` a negative of kind `not_recorded`; a list edit is not tied to a criterion and does not go stale). Works the person brought (upload, import, library, the scope seed) are not positives. Only a person's decision is a probe positive (A). Works that two agreeing runs include (`work_outcome`, D100 included, `decided_by = model_agreement`) are a separate column, never called verified; the head's selection is no column. No "out of scope" answer exists for the person, and the report says "out of scope not recorded" (E). D93's round × source rows keep their shape; beside them (`source_counts.arms`) each row gets rows returned, included and confirmed counts with "only" in D93's universe (no other source's search, for the chain row no search), a model / code query split read from the step index against the approved query list, and "full text not read yet" before any reading. An arm-kind line (keyword, data expansion, chain) gives works, new works, included and confirmed, with no threshold. Confirmed or brought works that no search or chain request of any discovery run of the revision found are listed by name; a stored hit anywhere counts as found, a run with missing hit records makes the rest `unknown`, a revision with no traceable run says "not counted". The signal table is descriptive: whether each signal ran and why not, and for the person's positives the top-100 and top-200 captures over the rows the signal scored (`available = true`), with ties at the cut counted apart, the denominator and a "too few to decide" state below 30 (`PROBE_JUDGE_MIN`, a display constant); agreement includes on a separate row with a fixed note that they were read because they ranked high; the embedding's moved-up records and, observationally, those included or confirmed after the ranking step (a same-millisecond stamp is `unknown`). Comparative contribution with paired bootstrap intervals is `scripts/probe_report.py`, read-only, against a reference-set file that must name its origin and completeness, refusing duplicate keys and conflicting roles, every interval labelled "given this pool and this reference set" (B). Ordinary signals are never switched off; the costly-signal switch-off (C) and the stopping rule (D) are open requirements, with the events that reopen them: the embedding running in slice 24 or becoming the default; any arm able to run a second round. All of it is in `research_view` from one read snapshot and one `DecisionStore.facts()` derivation; nothing is written. One API change: a selection reason equal to the reserved text the head-copy writes is refused (422), so the selection history tells a copy from an edit without a migration. No migration, no new reason code, protocol body and `skill_package_hash` unchanged.

**Limits:** The tables are numbers for the person, not a judgement on any signal: with 0–1 confirmed works per research every signal row reads "too few to decide" today. The acceptance reproduced the plan's measurement, not a signal's worth: 237 arm rows on 25 libraries with no difference, the script's 120 leave-one-out results and intervals equal to the plan's (28 single-signal `blocks` cells differ, all from records tied at the cut), `research_view` writing nothing on 25 libraries; the new derivation took 0.029–0.039 s on the four largest (budget 0.25 s) and `research_view` moved by 0.03–0.06 s. The reference sets are model-derived and incomplete. TF-IDF, the embedding's moved-up records and the stale and list-edit probe cases are covered by synthetic tests only. Selection history rows stored before this change whose person-typed reason equals the reserved copy text are read as copies, so their work's time reads as unknown. Whether 30 positives is enough, whether a person reads these lines, and anything live were not measured.

## D100 — A PDF the person attaches in an sw research gets a code at once, a reading request that outlives runs, the front of the reading order, and once read it decides its work

**Status:** accepted; implemented 2026-09-24 (slice 18b); `gpt-6-sol` · high's review (5 findings: an unread file could reach the answer through the head fallback, and again after a question revision; cancelling a reading run closed files attached after its plan froze; closing a failed run's files was a separate write; stale quotes shown for a re-extracted file), its check of the fixes (3 findings, 2 fixed: the view could not tell "the head is read" from "nothing is read", and the `human_pdf_wrong` exception had moved the fetch plan; 1 rejected, see Limits) its third check (1 finding: the PDF readiness panel offered an upload for a work whose attached file is not read yet) and its fourth check (2 findings: that work was in no progress counter during a collection, and a fourth counter wrapped alone on desktop) fixed the same day; a file's page digest now reads its passages through the version index (a full scan of about 10 ms per file before; `answer_versions` 30–38 ms against 25–30 ms on HEAD on a 3,839-source library). Accepted live the same day with one publisher PDF (see Limits). **Date:** 2026-09-24.

**Context:** After D99 a confirmed file was attached and nothing else happened: the work's stored decision stayed the old `no_fulltext`, the work left the waiting list and showed up nowhere, the reading plan skipped a work with a fresh model decision on another version, and only the end of a fetch or discovery run queued a reading run. `create_run` refuses a second run while one is active, so the file's reading could not simply be started at attach time. The plan is `docs/product/sw-slice18-waiting-for-pdf.md`, section "Dilim 18b", decisions 1–10, reviewed by `gpt-6-sol` · high over five rounds.

**Decision:** The confirmation (`POST /waiting/uploads`) and, in an `sw` research, the upload on a source row write, in the same transaction as the file, a full-text code on the chosen version: `not_read_yet` when the file has text, `text_unreadable` when it has none. The note names the file (`person_pdf:<asset_id>`), and a different file writes a new row even when the code is the same. The code replaces a code or model decision given before the file; a reading decision given after it is not overwritten (`should_write`). The person's own decisions are never overwritten. A `human_pdf_wrong` is never withdrawn and speaks only for its version: a file on another version of the work is read, and while it waits the work is `unresolved`, so no earlier model decision based on the wrong file comes back. Any other decision of the person stands: the file is added, and no code and no request are written. A file with text on a work eligible for reading (`group_of` with that exception, a frozen criterion, reading `auto`) gets a row in `person_pdf_requests` (migration `0052`): `waiting` → `planned` (in the transaction that freezes a reading plan, with the run) → `read` (in the transaction that writes that file's reading decision, whichever run writes it, provided the plan carried the file's asset, page digest, scope revision and criterion digest) or `unread` (its run ended without a decision on it). A request under an older scope revision or criterion digest is stale: it is not rewritten and not queued again. One helper, `ResearchFlow.queue_person_reading`, opens the reading run (`fulltext_adjudication:person:<scope>:<criterion>:<digest of the waiting assets>:<attempt>`) when a request waits and the research has no active or paused run. The attach calls it, as do the worker after every run and at start, and the API's pause and cancel. A paused run holds the reading; the view offers to resume or cancel that run. A run owns the requests its plan made `planned`, plus every waiting request while its plan is not frozen. When it ends, those become `unread` in the same write as its status (`Store.update_run`). A file attached after the plan froze stays `waiting` and is read next. Retry is the person's: "Read again" sets an `unread` request back to `waiting` and raises `attempt`, so a new run really opens; there is no automatic loop. In `read_plan` the works with a waiting request come before every group, in the order their files were added, and count against the same limit (40 / 50 / 150). The frozen plan stores each work's version, asset and page digest; before each call and before the write the file must still be in use with the same pages, otherwise the work is `not_reached` in that run and its request `unread`. **D48's exception for a person's file:** until the file is read, `answer_version` and `answer_versions` skip the version carrying it, falling back to a version whose PDF text is safe, else to a version with no PDF text (abstract only), else leaving the work out of the answer input. The same rule applies to a stale request, until a reading under the current criterion has read that file. Once read, and while the file is in use with the same pages, the file's decision is the work's outcome in `work_outcome` (the person's own decision still comes first) and the answer reads that version. Another version's different outcome is kept and shown with its version label, and no `versions_disagree` row opens for the work. Works without a person's file, the fetch plan (which keeps the pre-18b `group_of` rule) and `legacy` are unchanged. A section "Your files" under the waiting list shows each file's state from stored decisions and steps: waiting to be read, being read, included (with its verified quotes and pages), criterion not met (no quote shown, as `criterion_absent` carries none), waiting for your decision, not read (with "Read again"), changed since it was read, model off, and your decision stands. The PDF readiness panel does not count a work whose answer reads nothing as full text in hand. No new reason code; `skill_package_hash` unchanged.

**Limits:** Two limits are recorded as the plan chose them. A work waiting because of its own file (`text_unreadable`, or `human_pdf_wrong` for that file) that has no other version cannot take a new file in 18b: D99's `pdf_in_use` refusal stands, and D45's replace and D50's library-wide removal are neither changed, called nor suggested. When a person's read file is removed library-wide from another research, its precedence drops and the old rule returns, but this research's answer revision does not change: that is D50's current limit, not changed here. With full-text reading off, a person's file is not tracked as unread and the answer may read it as before 18b (a reviewer finding rejected on purpose: nothing is read against the criterion for any work while reading is off). A single-version work whose only text is the person's unread file gives the answer nothing, not even its abstract, until it is read. The strict-cue code gate is not built, so there is no "closed by code" response and SW11 point 9 stays partly implemented. The tests use a scripted model and synthetic records; they show workflow behaviour, not reading quality. Live acceptance, one work, not a generalisation (`.local/sw-slice18b-acceptance-2026-09-24/`): on a copy of the 18a acceptance library the owner's IEEE PDF of the first waiting work (10.1109/jsac.2024.3380080, 14 pages) was matched by DOI to its only version, confirmed, and the reading run was queued 0.13 s and its plan frozen 0.73 s after the confirmation; the list went from 65 to 64. The server had been started without the Codex home, so the run paused on its first model step; it was resumed through the paused-run action, the file was being read 4.3 s later and settled 17.2 s after the resume (the two `gpt-5.6-luna` calls took 12.6 s in parallel). The result was `fulltext_runs_disagree`: both runs quoted the same verified passage for the model proposal, and on the optimization-model part one quoted the objective and constraints while the other called it unclear, so the work waits for the person's decision. A second run on a fresh copy with the Codex home set (the first pause was "Not signed in to the DEIXIS Codex home": the copied data directory had no login) went through without a pause: the reading run was running 0.9 s after the confirmation's response, the file was being read by 3.6 s and settled 20.3 s after it (two parallel calls, 13.7 s and 16.3 s), with the same disagreement on the same part.

## D99 — An sw research lists the works waiting for the person's PDF in reading order, opens their links through the institution's proxy in the browser, and attaches a dropped file only to the version the person picks

**Status:** accepted; implemented 2026-09-24 (slice 18a), committed on the owner's decision before the publisher-PDF acceptance; `gpt-6-sol` · high's review (4 findings: the manual choice offered only listed works, a fragment in the proxy address, the order of two decisions written in one millisecond, a race test that matched again), its check of the fixes (2 findings: a work included in the same millisecond as the plan, a malformed proxy address answered 500) and its third check (1 finding: a removed version's inclusion kept its work a match candidate) fixed the same day; its fourth check found nothing. The part after the file is attached (a code for it, the reading request, version outcomes) is slice 18b and not built. **Date:** 2026-09-24.

**Context:** A work of an `sw` research that no route found a PDF for ends `no_fulltext`, `unresolved`, with `next_step = waiting_for_pdf`, and no code read that step: the work was listed nowhere. A read-only look at 15 stored libraries (`.local/sw-slice18-plan-2026-09-24/`) found 56–173 such works on the current path, mostly IEEE, and put the file matcher at 2 wrong of 633 open copies, both put down to a first page naming another candidate work's DOI. The plan (`docs/product/sw-slice18-waiting-for-pdf.md`, section "Dilim 18a", decisions 1–6) was reviewed by `gpt-6-sol` · high before it was split into 18a and 18b.

**Decision:** The list is derived on each read, never stored (`fulltext.waiting`, `workflow/waiting.py`). A work is on it when its current full-text decision (`DecisionStore.work_outcome`'s rule: the person's newest, else the best fresh one) is fresh, carries a code whose next step is `waiting_for_pdf` (read from the reason table: `no_fulltext`, `text_unreadable`, `human_pdf_wrong`), and no version has PDF text; for `human_pdf_wrong` the judged version's text does not count. A stale decision lists nothing, whoever wrote it. The order is the newest stored retrieval plan of the question revision, then an older plan's for a work settled before it, then the head; a work is found in a plan through any of its versions. No plan, no list. A row carries title, year, venue, DOI, the reason in plain words, its place, and links opened in a new tab (`noopener noreferrer`): the DOI's resolver and a landing page that is an http(s) page other than the DOI; stored links that are not http(s) are never shown. "Find PDF" on a row is today's action (D4), run only on the person's click. The institution's proxy address lives in `app_settings` (`institution_proxy`): `https` only, no user name or password and no `#` fragment, either a template holding `{url}` (the target percent-encoded in its place) or a prefix (the target appended as it is, percent-encoded when it holds `&` or `#`); empty means links open directly. DEIXIS sends no request through it. In an `sw` research `/uploads/match` proposes a work among the latest plan's works, the listed works, and the works the person included after that plan; a first page naming the DOIs of more than one candidate work lets the title decide, and without a single title nothing is proposed (`identity.propose`; `identity.check` and the legacy match are unchanged). The answer carries the file's `sha256`, the scope revision, the proposed work with every version (label, year, type, whether it already has a PDF, which one the file named) and a digest of its version list; when nothing is proposed, every candidate work comes back with its versions for the person to choose from. The person picks the version; none is preselected. `POST /waiting/uploads` refuses (409, with its reason) a file whose digest differs from the match's (`file_changed`), a revised question (`scope_revised`), a version no longer in the research or not of the work (`not_a_member`), a work no longer a candidate (`not_a_candidate`), a changed version list (`versions_changed`) and a version with a PDF in use (`pdf_in_use`); it checks before extracting the text and again in the write, then adds the file as a person's upload (`origin = user_upload`) with the event `waiting_pdf_attached`. No code and no run is written for it. The screen is a tab "Waiting for your PDF" beside the human queue with the list's count; a file dropped on the PDF panel of an `sw` research goes there. No migration, no new reason code, `skill_package_hash` unchanged.

**Limits:** The live acceptance with a real publisher PDF is not done: on 2026-09-24 the machine was off the institutional network (Scopus check `none`), IEEE Xplore sent its login and a bot challenge and ScienceDirect answered 403, and no publisher file of a waiting work was found among the stored libraries. It was run instead on a copy of the stored 17a quick library (`.local/sw-slice18a-acceptance-2026-09-24/`): 65 works listed, the first ones IEEE, the proxy link shape `…/login?url=https://doi.org/10.1109/jsac.2024.3380080`, a stored open copy matched by title in 0.6 s. The multi-DOI rule was measured again on the 15 stored libraries (`.local/sw-slice18a-acceptance-2026-09-24/waiting_after.json`): the two wrong matches of the plan were one file seen in two libraries, a repository copy of a paper the library holds as two works (a DOI-less accepted version and the published record); its first page names only the published record's DOI, so the rule does not apply and the match is still counted wrong, though it names the same paper. The rule turned one right match into no match (a preprint and its article held as two works, both DOIs on the first page, one shared title). No case was found where the rule closed a real wrong match; the rule is the plan's and was kept. The proxy flow itself was not tried (no institutional account). How often a publisher file names its own DOI, the length of the list outside quantum and the wireless-sensor question, how many files a person drops, and anything of slice 18b were not measured. The count adds about 30 ms to a research view of 3,600 sources whose view already takes 2–5 s.

## D98 — The full-text fetch of an sw research runs inside its discovery run, from the abstract code step on, for the works already certain to be in the plan

**Status:** accepted; implemented 2026-09-24 (slice 17a); `gpt-6-sol` · high's review (4 findings), its check of the fixes (no findings) and its last check (4 findings: the separate-path estimate, the test helpers' default, the acceptance wording, two stale doc lines) fixed the same day. **Date:** 2026-09-24.

**Context:** D83 queued the retrieval run after the whole discovery run, a named deviation from SW10.1, because the
worker runs one run at a time and a research holds one active run. A model-free replay of 13 stored libraries
(`.local/sw-slice17a-plan-2026-09-24/`) put the gain at 1.5–2.1 min (`quick`), 2.2–4.8 (`standard`) and 4.3–4.4
(`detailed`), with no early work outside the final plan. Eight choices were settled by Claude and `gpt-5.6-sol` ·
medium (`docs/product/sw-slice17a-fetch-overlap.md`, "Ortak kararlar" and "Kalıcı koordinasyon sözleşmesi").

**Decision:** An `sw` discovery run queued with the setting `auto` carries `fulltext_fetch: {"mode": "overlap", …
fetch_budget(effort)}`. After its abstract code step it writes `fetch_baseline` (the works holding a fresh code of this
stage and the works with PDF text, by `work_id`, with the revision, criterion digest, room and keyword ranking step,
and a digest that does not depend on order) and starts a fetch arm beside the model arm (abstract batches and
citation chaining). A work is claimed when it is safe: its own abstract decision is final and it is inside the plan in
which every work of an open batch is counted a candidate, computed against the baseline, so the fetch's own codes and
texts never move the plan (`fulltext.safe_to_fetch`). The chain group is claimed from only once this run's chain order
and its works' code decisions are written. A claim opens `fulltext_work:<work_id>` with its time; it is never taken
back and counts against its group's room. When the model arm ends, `fulltext_plan` is written once (the D83 plan
against the baseline, with `claimed_early`, `deviations`, `conditions_held` and the `fetch` list), the rest is claimed,
and once written it is the only source of claims, on a resumed run too. At most four works are in flight
(`host_gate` unchanged). A settled work's step output, its `fulltext_work_settled` event and its code are one
transaction; a person's full-text decision on the version stands (`code_written: false`, `held_by: "human"`, the
event's code empty); a file that arrives after a question revision decides nothing (`cancelled` / `scope_revised`).
Only the coordinator writes a stop: under the overlap `_checkpoint` reads it, `_pause` and `_fail` note theirs, both
arms drain, and the stop is written once; a work stopped between two routes is closed `cancelled` / `run_stopped` and
sent again on resume. A step a crash left `outcome_unknown` is sent again, and after three starts closed
`fetch_not_settled` (delivery is at least once). The run completes and queues its reading run
(`fulltext_adjudication:after:<discovery run>`) in one transaction; no retrieval run is queued. A discovery run
queued before this carries no mode and keeps D83's separate run; a retrieval run the user starts is unchanged. The
timeline shows the fetch as the discovery turn's PDF phase ("Retrieving the full text: N of M") beside screening.
No migration, no model contract change (`skill_package_hash` unchanged), no new reason code.

**Limits:** Two live quantum runs (`.local/sw-slice17a-acceptance-2026-09-24/`, `gpt-5.6-luna` · medium): every
gate held (fetch started at the code step, 92 and 112 works all claimed before the model arm ended, no deviation, the
work list recomputed after the reading run equals the stored one, the reading opened once; equality at the moment the
plan was written was not measured); the fetch ended 0.6 and 0.9 min after the last model batch, and the same works with
their measured durations, four at a time in the final plan's order from the moment the model arm ended, would have
ended 1.6 and 2.4 min later.
That is an estimate from one run each, not a measured causal gain. End to end the runs took 7.9 and 14.0 min, but
model-call counts and durations differ from slice 15's runs. Event-loop delays over 0.5 s occurred inside and outside
the overlap window, the longest outside it; `host_gate` waits reached 57 s. Not measured: `detailed`, topics other
than quantum, how often a person changes a work while discovery runs, whether the event-loop delays come from the overlap, and whether
overlapping reading with the fetch (17b) is the larger gain.

## D97 — The human queue screen: its own tab, a list and one row's detail, the PDF opened on the row's page by one action, only the backend's anchor marked

**Status:** accepted; implemented 2026-09-24 (slice 17, `89ce03d`); `gpt-6-sol` · high's review (11 findings) and its check of the fixes (5 open points) and its last check (5 more) fixed the same day. **Date:** 2026-09-24.

**Context:** D96 put the queue in the back end with no screen; `research_view.counts.queue` was only a number. A
model-free read of 13 stored libraries (`.local/sw-slice17-plan-2026-09-24/`, `shape.json`) found 346 rows: 155
`find_part`, 98 `confirm_absent`, 51 `choose_run`, 25 `confirm_quote`, 17 `confirm_pdf`, no `choose_version`; 243 rows
with no cue sentence for their question part; 47 unverifiable quotes, a closest passage for 40 of them; a PDF on every
row. The API returned neither the passage of a quote nor, outside identity rows, the file. Seven choices were settled
by Claude and `gpt-5.6-sol` · medium at the owner's request (`docs/product/sw-slice17-human-queue-screen.md`, "Ortak
kararlar").

**Decision:** An `sw` research gets a tab, "Awaiting your decision", after Sources, with the pill `counts.queue +
counts.look_again`; the latest reading run's timeline turn carries one line "N works await your decision · Open". A
legacy research has neither. The tab (`HumanQueue.tsx`) is a listbox of rows in the fused order, `look_again` rows last
under their own heading, filter chips by kind and a reason filter, and the selected row's detail: its one question and
the part's definition, why it is in the queue with the code in small type, the two runs side by side (label, quote,
"found on the page" or "not found in the text", page link, rationale), for an unverified quote the model's quote beside
the closest text with its match ratio, the question part's cue sentences or "This part's phrases do not occur in the
text", an identity row's first page beside the work's title and DOI, and for `choose_version` both versions in the
place of the two runs. Answers sit in a footer pinned under the detail: four equal buttons, and on an identity row "PDF
is right, let the model read it" first and primary; an optional note of at most 1,000 characters; no confirmation
dialog. A 200 removes the row (never before), moves the selection on, reloads queue and research view, and shows a
toast with Undo; "Your decisions" lists every work a person decided, with Undo where `undo` would take it back and the reason where it
would not (a PDF confirmation whose reading has begun). An answer is sent with the
list row's token, and only on a detail whose row token is that same token; until then the buttons are off and the
detail says it is being read again. The row token also moves with the text of the file in use (its extraction version
and that extraction's passages; a rejected extraction's kept passages do not count), so a new extraction or OCR text makes a shown detail stale. A detail that still disagrees with the list
after two list reads says so and waits for "Read it again". Of overlapping list reads only the newest is applied, and a
caller whose read was overtaken gets the newest list. A
409 reloads all three; the detail says whether the row changed or left the queue, and a note being written survives,
under its row, or in the notice with its work's title when the row left. The queue reloads on every event of the
research's stream. A `look_again` row names the earlier answer beside its label, in the list and in the detail. At 760 px and below the detail replaces the list, with "Back to the list".

**Deliberate departure from SW11.6.** SW11.6 says selecting a row opens the PDF at its page. Here selecting fills the
detail, and Enter or "Open page N in the PDF" opens the source sheet on that page, in the PDF view at full width.
Opening a full-width sheet on every selection would cover the context the answer needs, break row-by-row keyboard
work (every arrow key would load a PDF), and carry a queue action into the source sheet. The page is the question
part's verified quote page (run 1, then run 2), else the closest passage's page, else the first cue sentence's page,
else the first page the run was shown; an identity row opens page 1.

**Evidence rules.** The PDF view is a canvas and marks nothing. In the plain-text view only `anchor_text` is marked:
the page's own text a verified quote was found as by `locate_anchor`, `exact` or `normalized` only, computed when read
and never stored. The mark is shown only when it is exactly that text: a match that falls in a title, heading, table
or figure (marked whole there), cuts a formula or an in-text link, or starts or ends inside a word leaves the page unmarked, with the
amber strip saying the quote could not be marked exactly (`marksExactly`). The mark's accessible name is "The model's
quote, as found in the page text", not the answer citation's. A model quote, a fuzzy match, the closest passage and a
cue sentence are never marked; a page opened for an unverified quote has an amber strip saying nothing is marked. The screen never says an answer is right.

**Back end, reads only.** `row_detail` parts gain `passage_id` (the verified quote's page passage, else the passage
the model named) and `anchor_text`; `closest` and cue sentences gain their page's `passage_id`; the detail gains the
version's current `asset_id` and, for `choose_version`, `versions` (each version with a fresh full-text decision, the
named one first, with its label, file, decision and runs). `GET …/queue` gains `decided`: one entry per work whose
outcome is a fresh human decision or a fresh PDF confirmation, from the same snapshot and the same `_classify` path, with
a typed `answer` and the undo token `_state_of` computes; a confirmation is listed only while its file is still the
one in use; a confirmation whose reading has begun is listed with no undo token and `undo_blocked: "reading_started"`,
the same rule `undo` applies, and the detail's `decision.undoable` says the same; a confirmation's internal note is not returned; a stale decision is a `look_again`
row, not an entry. An identity row's first page is the text of physical page 1, or none. A source row's selection gains
`queue_answer`, read from every stored `human_selection_links` row of an open decision whose selection nobody changed
since (after a head change both heads keep theirs), and the Sources list says "Your answer in the queue: …" from it, never from the reason text a person can type. The queue endpoints' 409 is `{"detail": {"reason": "row_changed" |
"reading_started", "message": …}}`, the reason set where the conflict is raised (`QueueConflict`); other 409s keep one
sentence. No migration, no model contract change, no new reason code, nothing written on read.

**Limits:** Case J passes on four SYNTHETIC works of two fields with a scripted reading model; it shows application
behavior, not whether a person reads well. The visual check on a copy of the slice 16 live library
(`.local/sw-slice17-acceptance-2026-09-24/`) saw `choose_run`, `confirm_absent` and `find_part` rows; that library has no
`confirm_quote`, `confirm_pdf` or `choose_version` row, so those were seen only in the fixture, and `choose_version` in
neither (its data is covered by a back-end test). After the review a second copy (slice 16 `data-q1-quick-luna`,
port 8772) showed two `confirm_quote` rows and one `confirm_pdf` row: five verified quotes opened with one exact mark
each, the unverified one unmarked, and the `pdf_confirmed` round with its undo matched the API at each step (15 → 14 →
15 rows, `decided` 2 → 3 → 2). A `look_again` row's earlier answer is not in case J (it has no scope revision). At 900
px the sidebar leaves the list 278 px and the detail 318 px, and the answers wrap to two lines. Minutes per row, whether cue sentences and closest passages help, the
correctness of any decision, and a usability trial with a person were not measured. At 390 px the pinned answers take
about a third of the screen height.

## D96 — The human queue: rows derived from stored decisions, a person's answer written as a stage decision and the user's selection in one transaction, and no model call for a decided work

**Status:** accepted; implemented 2026-09-24 (slice 16, back end only; the screen is slice 17). **Date:** 2026-09-24.

**Context:** Since slice 12 five reason codes and `pdf_identity_unconfirmed` routed works to `human_queue`, and
nothing read them. A model-free count on 16 stored libraries (`.local/sw-slice16-queue-measure-2026-09-24/`) found the
queue would hold 8–21 / 15–40 / 90–100 rows for quantum `quick` / `standard` / `detailed` and 1–4 for the packet
question; 223 of 315 rows were `part_without_evidence`, mostly because the model's criterion carried a topic part
(SW15.1). A sample of 74 rows found about a third to be real questions. Seven choices were settled by Claude and
`gpt-6-sol` (one high, two medium rounds) and approved by the owner on Sol medium's approval
(`docs/product/sw-slice16-human-queue.md`).

**Decision:** The queue is not stored. `workflow/queue.py` derives it on each read from `DecisionStore.work_outcome`:
one row per work whose outcome routes to `human_queue` (the six codes of the reason table) or is `versions_disagree`,
named on the version that decision is written on; no code is closed by a rule. A work whose selection the user set
from the source list is not listed (counted as `user_selected`); a person's decision that went stale under a new
revision or criterion is listed at the end as `look_again` whoever set the selection, and still counts. Each row has
a `kind` (`confirm_quote`, `choose_run`, `choose_version`, `confirm_pdf`, `confirm_absent`, `find_part`), one question
(the first criterion part the two runs did not settle), its place in the fused order (keyword works by the latest
keyword ranking, chained works after them by the chain ranking; ties by head) and a `row_token`. The row detail adds
each run's labels, quotes, checks, pages, passages and rationales, the pages each run was shown, the closest passage
to an unverified quote on those pages only (`locate_anchor`), the question part's cue sentences with pages (only that
part's phrases), and for an identity row the PDF's first page. Reading writes nothing and opens no step.

An answer (`include`, `criterion_not_met`, `not_sure`, `pdf_wrong`) is a `human` stage decision on the row's version.
`include` and `criterion_not_met` also set the work head's selection `included` / `excluded` with origin `user`, and
an append-only `human_selection_links` row (migration `0051`) records which head and selection version the decision
wrote; `_settle_work_head` adds a row when it copies that selection to a new head. Undo (`undo_human`) restores the
earlier code decision and releases the selection only while the link's head is still at that version; any list edit
since, to the same state too, keeps it the user's. The fifth answer `pdf_confirmed` marks the file
(`source_assets.identity_confirmed_at`, migration `0051`) and closes the identity code with `not_read_yet` (note
`pdf_confirmed:<asset>`, no step); `_user_supplied_pdf` exempts a confirmed file, and its undo is refused once a later
reading plan opened a step for the work. The token carries the revision, criterion digest, every current full-text
decision of the work, the row's reason, the head and its selection version, membership and the current file; it is
